title: Next Generation Technology for Epidemic Prevention and Control: Data-Driven Contact Tracking
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to epidemics prevention and control, namely the use of next generation technology for data-driven contact tracking. Data driven contact tracking involves building a system that uses advanced algorithms and big data analytics to trace infectious disease outbreaks in real time by recording the identity, geographical position and contacts of infected individuals. The proposed system would provide public health officials with enhanced surveillance capacity and allow them to rapidly anticipate emerging trends or new pandemic threats. It would further enable prediction-based intervention strategies such as targeted testing, quarantine procedures or visualization outputs of risk levels around particular geographic points which can help prevent wide-spread out breaks before they happen. This project also explores potential privacy issues related to this type of technology suggesting concrete methods for overcoming these roadblocks successfully while empowering healthcare workers globally with solutions for better decision-making capabilities in order to minimize disease transmissions throughout various populations through responsible means.

title: Isolation and study of the properties of an interferon-like inhibitor of viruses from normal human blood serum
abstract: A protein with a molecular weight of 17,400 daltons and an isoelectric point at pH 4.9 has been isolated from the blood serum of healthy donors by successive ion-exchange chromatography of QAE-Sephadex A-50, affinity chromatography on DNA-cellulose, and polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, in the presence of sodium dodecyl sulfate. The protein isolated, like interferon, suppresses the development of the cytopathogenic action of the viruses of vesicular stomatitis and murine ecephalomyocarditis in cultures of human cells of the L-41 and M-19 lines. The amino acid composition of the protein isolated differs from those of various fractions of human interferons.

title: Triple combination therapy of favipiravir plus two monoclonal antibodies eradicates influenza virus from nude mice
abstract: Prolonged treatment of immunocompromised influenza patients with viral neuraminidase (NA) inhibitors is required, because the immune system of such patients fails to eradicate the viruses. Here, we attempted to eradicate influenza virus from the respiratory organs of nude mice, which is a model of immunocompromised hosts, by using combination therapy of the viral polymerase inhibitor favipiravir and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the receptor-binding site (RBS) and stem of viral hemagglutinin (HA). Although monotherapy or combination therapy of two antivirals (two mAbs or favipiravir plus a mAb) suppressed virus replication, they failed to eradicate viruses from nude mice. In contrast, the triple combination therapy of favipiravir plus anti-Stem and anti-RBS mAbs completely stopped virus replication in nude mice, resulting in virus clearance. Triple combination approaches should be considered for the treatment of human immunocompromised patients with severe influenza.

title: Global Surveillance of Emerging Influenza Virus Genotypes by Mass Spectrometry
abstract: This article aims to investigate the use of mass spectrometry as a viable tool for global surveillance of emerging influenza virus genotypes. Over the past decades, influenza epidemics have resulted in an enormous burden on global health, claiming up to 5 million lives annually. With intensifying international travel and increasing opportunities for animal-human transmission, new flu viruses are rapidly spread across boundaries and become endemic in many parts of the globe. To combat this potential risk, there is therefore a need for effective web-based strategies capable of quickly identifying any changes in flu genotype composition at high throughput screening levels. This study seeks to assess mass spectrometry (MS)-based technologies as a means of achieving accurate detection rates while providing real-time monitoring over several influenzaviruses within multiple species microcosms across different regions worldwide. The results from this work could verify MS’s validity as one component within an improved oil sampling protocol and offer deeper insight into existing challenges encountered when attempting an expensive multi pronged approach towards comprehensive pandemic preparedness arrangements.

title: Exploring resveratrol dimers as virulence blocking agents – Attenuation of type III secretion in Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of resveratrol dimers on virulence blocking using Gram-negative bacterial pathogens Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Type III secretion system (T3SS) is a crucial upholder of pathogens' intracellular activity and has been employed by myriad pathogenic bacteria as an apparatus for counteracting host immune response. This paper aims to investigate whether resveratrol dimers may attenuate T3SS in these two significant microbes so that they cannot establish an effective foothold for infection, thus reducing their ability to cause illnesses. Through our experiments, we ascertained that resveratrol substantially prevented the expression levels of many genes related to excretion systems with reports from previous studies supporting this concept. Our results exemplify that novel strategies involving such simple compounds can yield marked progress in curbing microbial resistance faced by certain diseases posed by Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, while providing new therapeutic solutions across numerous disciplines. title: On the challenges associated with the study of police use of deadly force in the United States: A response to Schwartz & Jahn
abstract: This article examines the challenges associated with the study of police use of deadly force in the United States, in response to Schwartz & Jahn's examination of poor data collection as a non-trivial aspect. The study is an analysis of current research and existing literature, which aims to assist scholars by highlighting factors that limit access to accurate information and understanding when studying this politically fraught topic. As mass demonstrations have shined a spotlight on police violence and calls for reform have risen throughout society, this paper seeks to bring clarity and direction concerning the difficulties in trying to understand systemic issues engrained within law enforcement culture.

title: Global trends in research related to social media in psychology: mapping and bibliometric analysis
abstract: This paper examines the global trends in research related to social media in psychology. Through bibliometric mapping and analysis, major trends, topics and citations have been identified that have advanced our understanding of the psychological aspects associated with using social media. The results revealed numerous opportunities for further exploration into the development of empirical evidence from existing research evaluating both positive and negative outcomes from usage of these digital communication platforms. As such a rapidly changing field, an improved comprehension of how social media is shaping human behavior both online and off-line can serve to inform practitioners as well as policy makers when crafting solutions for some of society’s most pressing issues of today. Furthermore, this study contributes significantly to an up-to-date assessment on how this topic is playing out within academia globally.

title: The avoidance of G-CSF and the addition of prophylactic corticosteroids after autologous stem cell transplantation for multiple myeloma patients appeal for the at-home setting to reduce readmission for neutropenic fever
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) remains the standard of care for young multiple myeloma (MM) patients; indeed, at-home ASCT has been positioned as an appropriate therapeutic strategy. However, despite the use of prophylactic antibiotics, neutropenic fever (NF) and hospital readmissions continue to pose as the most important limitations in the outpatient setting. It is possible that the febrile episodes may have a non-infectious etiology, and engraftment syndrome could play a more significant role. The aim of this study was to analyze the impact of both G-CSF withdrawal and the addition of primary prophylaxis with corticosteroids after ASCT. METHODS: Between January 2002 and August 2018, 111 MM patients conditioned with melphalan were managed at-home beginning +1 day after ASCT. Three groups were established: Group A (n = 33) received standard G-CSF post-ASCT; group B (n = 32) avoided G-CSF post-ASCT; group C (n = 46) avoided G-CSF yet added corticosteroid prophylaxis post-ASCT. RESULTS: The incidence of NF among the groups was reduced (64%, 44%, and 24%; P<0.001), with a non-significant decrease in hospital readmissions as well (12%, 6%, and 2%; P = 0.07). The most important variables identified for NF were: HCT-CI >2 (OR 6.1; P = 0.002) and G-CSF avoidance plus corticosteroids (OR 0.1; P<0.001); and for hospital readmission: age ≥60 years (OR 14.6; P = 0.04) and G-CSF avoidance plus corticosteroids (OR 0.07; P = 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: G-CSF avoidance and corticosteroid prophylaxis post ASCT minimize the incidence of NF in MM patients undergoing at-home ASCT. This approach should be explored in a prospective randomized clinical trial.

title: Prospects of brassinosteroids in medicinal applications
abstract: Steroids are an imperative group of hormones which play a key role in the transmission of signals that mediate growth and physiological responses in most pluricellular organisms. Brassinosteroids (BRs), a class of plant-specific steroid hormones, control many of the developmental and physiological processes like their animal counterparts, including regulation of gene expression, cell division and expansion, differentiation, programmed cell death, and homeostasis. Recent studies have indicated that these hormones have antiviral, antifungal, antiproliferative, antibacterial, neuroprotective and immunomodulatory properties in animal system. BRs analogues have been reported to have antiviral activity against herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), arenaviruses as well as against replication of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) in Vero cells. Also, antiherpetic activities both in a human conjunctive cell line (IOBA-NHC) and murine herpetic stromal keratitis (HSK) experimental models have been reported. In human cells, anticancer structure-activity relationship of natural BRs revealed their high cytotoxic activity. Since, BRs and their analogues are reported to inhibit cell growth in cancer cell lines, they may be considered as promising phytohormones for potential anticancer drugs. The use of pollens in folk medicine also indicates scope of steroids of plant pollens in medicines. An attempt has been made in this paper to document the information available on the prospects of BRs in therapeutics.

title: A Human Monoclonal Antibody against Hepatitis B Surface Antigen with Potent Neutralizing Activity
abstract: This paper examines the discovery and characterization of a potent neutralizing human monoclonal antibody against Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg), thereby providing a molecular basis for therapeutic intervention. The antigen-specific antibody was isolated from a peripheral blood mononuclear cell collection from an exposed healthy individual who showed high antiviral activity in vitro but no symptoms of disease. Characterization studies revealed that this immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) mAb may be capable of binding to several conformational epitopes on HBsAg, and demonstrated its potential to potently neutralize infectivity without inducing complement activation or cytotoxicity. Our findings provide insight into the development of effective treatments against HBV infection and have implications for designing novel strategies for targeting potentially pathogenic antigens with humoral immune responses.

title: Role of Podocyte Injury in Glomerulosclerosis
abstract: Finding new therapeutic targets of glomerulosclerosis treatment is an ongoing quest. Due to a living environment of various stresses and pathological stimuli, podocytes are prone to injuries; moreover, as a cell without proliferative potential, loss of podocytes is vital in the pathogenesis of glomerulosclerosis. Thus, sufficient understanding of factors and underlying mechanisms of podocyte injury facilitates the advancement of treating and prevention of glomerulosclerosis. The clinical symptom of podocyte injury is proteinuria, sometimes with loss of kidney functions progressing to glomerulosclerosis. Injury-induced changes in podocyte physiology and function are actually not a simple passive process, but a complex interaction of proteins that comprise the anatomical structure of podocytes at molecular levels. This chapter lists several aspects of podocyte injuries along with potential mechanisms, including glucose and lipid metabolism disorder, hypertension, RAS activation, micro-inflammation, immune disorder, and other factors. These aspects are not technically separated items, but intertwined with each other in the pathogenesis of podocyte injuries.

title: Police harassment and psychosocial vulnerability, distress, and depressive symptoms among black men who have sex with men in the U.S.: Longitudinal analysis of HPTN 061
abstract: The mental health impact of exposure to police harassment is understudied, particularly among Black men who have sex with men (BMSM), a group at elevated risk of exposure to such discrimination. This study aimed to identify the associations among BMSM between recent police harassment and psychosocial vulnerability, psychological distress, and depression measured six months later. Data come from the HIV Prevention Trials Network (HPTN) 061 Study, a cohort study of BMSM recruited in 6 U.S. cities (Atlanta, GA, Boston, MA, Los Angeles, CA, New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, and Washington DC). Participants completed baseline, 6-month follow-up, and 12-month follow-up interviews. A convenience sample of 1553 BMSM was recruited between July 2009 and October 2010 of whom 1155 returned for a follow-up interview 12 months later. Accounting for previous police interaction, poverty, psychopathology, drug use, and alcohol use, we estimated associations between recent police harassment reported at the 6 month follow-up interview and 12 month outcomes including psychosocial vulnerability (elevated racial/sexual identity incongruence), psychological distress (being distressed by experiences of racism and/or homophobia), and depression. About 60% of men reported experiencing police harassment between the baseline and 6-month interview due to their race and/or sexuality. Adjusted analyses suggested police harassment was independently associated with a 10.81 (95% CI: 7.97, 13.66) point increase and 8.68 (95% CI: 6.06, 11.30) point increase in distress due to experienced racism and distress due to experienced homophobia scores, respectively. Police harassment perceived to be dually motivated predicted disproportionate levels of distress. Police harassment is prevalent and associated with negative influences on psychosocial vulnerability and psychological distress among BMSM. Reducing exposure to police harassment may improve the psychosocial health of BMSM.

title: The Impact of microRNAs in Renin–Angiotensin-System-Induced Cardiac Remodelling
abstract: This paper examines the impact of microRNAs on Renin–Angiotensin-System (RAS)-induced cardiac remodelling. Emerging evidence suggests that aberrant microRNA levels have a causal role in cardiovascular diseases such as hypertension and cardiac hypertrophy, however little is known about their effect on disease progression induced by RAS activation in the heart. To understand this relationship better, our research used animal models to identify specific changes in tissue phenotype upon administration of Angiotensin II (Ang II) and to determine whether these alterations were affected by modified expression of individual microRNAs. In contrast to previous studies, our results show that although many miRs are dysregulated during diseased states, their modulation has limited effects on hypertrophy induced specifically by an activated RAS pathway. This paper provides a foundation for future studies aiming to elucidate further how miRs modulate cardiac pathologies involving the renin angiotensin system.

title: Curcumin: Could This Compound Be Useful in Pregnancy and Pregnancy-Related Complications?
abstract:
The effective management of pregnancy-related complications, though crucial from a healthcare perspective, remains elusive. Despite extensive research efforts focused on identifying potential therapeutic solutions to smooth out pregnancies and their associated medical issues, many safe, reliable and affordable options continue to be absent in the market. In light of this dire situation, recent focus has shifted towards the investigation of naturally occurring compounds – such as curcumin - that could provide much sought after relief without escalating costs or posing health risks for pregnant women and their unborn children. This article presents an overview of existing scientific evidence concerning the intake of curcumin during pregnancy; discussing its antioxidant activity, antinociceptive effects on pain reduction as well as immunomodulatory properties which together may lend credence to its efficacy in preventing gestational ailments. Given these positive attributes along with perceived safety factors compared to other treatments under consideration makes curcumin a compound worthy further exploration within this clinical context.

title: Hypercapnia Alters Expression of Immune Response, Nucleosome Assembly and Lipid Metabolism Genes in Differentiated Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells
abstract: Hypercapnia, the elevation of CO(2) in blood and tissues, commonly occurs in severe acute and chronic respiratory diseases, and is associated with increased risk of mortality. Recent studies have shown that hypercapnia adversely affects innate immunity, host defense, lung edema clearance and cell proliferation. Airway epithelial dysfunction is a feature of advanced lung disease, but the effect of hypercapnia on airway epithelium is unknown. Thus, in the current study we examined the effect of normoxic hypercapnia (20% CO(2) for 24 h) vs normocapnia (5% CO(2)), on global gene expression in differentiated normal human airway epithelial cells. Gene expression was assessed on Affymetrix microarrays, and subjected to gene ontology analysis for biological process and cluster-network representation. We found that hypercapnia downregulated the expression of 183 genes and upregulated 126. Among these, major gene clusters linked to immune responses and nucleosome assembly were largely downregulated, while lipid metabolism genes were largely upregulated. The overwhelming majority of these genes were not previously known to be regulated by CO(2). These changes in gene expression indicate the potential for hypercapnia to impact bronchial epithelial cell function in ways that may contribute to poor clinical outcomes in patients with severe acute or advanced chronic lung diseases.

title: Continuing professional development module: An updated introduction to electroencephalogram-based brain monitoring during intended general anesthesia
abstract: This paper presents an updated introduction to electroencephalogram-based brain monitoring during intended general anesthesia (EGM) in order to evaluate the impact of continuing professional development module on the understanding of this particular technology. The purpose was to explore pertinent aspects of EGM, including its history, process guidance and latest developments related to advantages, limitations and efficacy compared with traditional monitoring systems applied in clinical settings. In addition, results from a study on medical professionals are discussed as further evidence for benefits linked with using an advanced educational course on EGM. Comparisons between previously held knowledge prior and following completion indicated that participants were able to improve their overall competencies and perform better when put into practice. Results obtained from this work support the potential usefulness of incorporating CPD modules into current academic training initiatives aiming at enhancing patient safety through improved usage practices when delivering general anesthesia care enhanced by use of EEG-based technologies.

title: Activation of toll-like receptor signaling pathways leading to nitric oxide-mediated antiviral responses
abstract: Adapting to a continually changing pathogenic landscape is essential for survival of immunocompetent organisms. Activation of defensive responses enables successful containment, permitting coexistence with cryptic pathogens or those which escape conventional prophylaxis mechanisms. In this context, Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling pathways can provide an efficient antiviral response against novel and evolving infectious agents. This review examines the pivotal role of TLRs in generated nitric oxide (NO)-mediated antiviral responses, elucidating underlying molecular activities facilitating both prevention and resolution from pathogenic infections.

title: Neurological Manifestations of Influenza A (H1N1): Clinical Features, Intensive Care Needs, and Outcome
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe neurological manifestations in children with Influenza A (H1N1). METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted in the Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) and Pediatric Neurology unit of a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India involving children with PCR confirmed Influenza A (H1N1) with neurological manifestations during 2019 outbreak. RESULTS: Six children (5 females, 1 male) were enrolled. All presented with neurological symptoms (seizures and altered sensorium) accompanied with fever and respiratory symptoms with duration of illness of 2–7 d. The admission Glasgow Coma Scale ranged from 4 to 12. Only 2 cases showed cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis. Neuroimaging was suggestive of diffuse cerebral edema, acute necrotizing encephalopathy of childhood, and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. All were treated with Oseltamivir. Four cases had clinical features of raised intracranial pressure (ICP) and were managed in PICU, 3 of them needed mechanical ventilation, 3 needed vasoactive drugs, 3 received 3% saline infusion, 1 underwent invasive ICP monitoring, and 3 (cases 4, 5 and 6) received intravenous methylprednisolone (30 mg/kg) for 5 d. Total duration of hospital stay was 10–30 d. Case 2 expired due to refractory raised ICP. Among survivors, 3 children had residual neurological deficits and the remaining 2 had achieved premorbid condition. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza A (H1N1) can present with isolated or predominant neurological manifestations which can contribute to poor outcome. The authors suggest to rule out H1N1 in any child who presents with unexplained neurological manifestations during seasonal outbreaks of H1N1.

title: Eckol Alleviates Intestinal Dysfunction during Suckling-to-Weaning Transition via Modulation of PDX1 and HBEGF
abstract: This study analyses the role of Eckol, an agar polysaccharide derivative isolated from seaweed Laver (Porphyra yezoensis), in ameliorating intestinal dysfunction during suckling-to-weaning transition. Nutritional imbalances that occur during this transitional period are associated with disruption of homeostatic regulation mechanisms and a dysregulated gut microbiota. In this experiment, we examined the effects of dietary supplementation with Eckol on small intestine morphology and expression levels of transcription factors critical for pancreatic development, beta cell maturation - paired box protein 1 (PDX1) and heparin binding EGF like growth factor (HBEGF). The results show that mice supplemented with Eckol showed improved intestinal integrity by modulating PDX1 and HBEGF gene expressions compared to control group. Our findings suggest potential use of Eckol as a dietary supplement to prevent nutritional imbalance induced small intestine damages during suckling- weaning transition.

title: Antibiotic resistance in patients with clinical features of healthcare-associated infections in an urban tertiary hospital in Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Available data on antibiotic resistance in sub-Saharan Africa is limited despite its increasing threat to global public health. As there is no previous study on antibiotic resistance in patients with clinical features of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in Sierra Leone, research is needed to inform public health policies. Our study aimed to assess antibiotic resistance rates from isolates in the urine and sputum samples of patients with clinical features of HAIs. METHODOLOGY: We conducted a cross-sectional study of adult inpatients aged ≥18 years at Connaught Hospital, an urban tertiary care hospital in Freetown between February and June 2018. RESULTS: Over the course of the study, we enrolled 164 patients. Risk factors for HAIs were previous antibiotic use (93.3%), comorbidities (58.5%) and age (≥65 years) (23.9%). Of the 164 samples, 89.6% were urine. Bacterial growth was recorded in 58.8% of cultured specimens; the type of specimen was an independent predictor of bacterial growth (p < 0.021). The most common isolates were Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae; 29.2% and 19.0% in urine samples and 18.8% and 31.3% in sputum samples, respectively. The overall resistance rates were 58% for all extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms, 13.4% for carbapenem-resistant non-lactose fermenting gram-negative bacilli, 8.7% for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and 1.3% for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE). There were no carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa (CRPA) isolates but all Staphylococcus aureus isolates were methicillin-resistant S. aureus. CONCLUSION: We demonstrated a high prevalence rate of ESBL-producing organisms which are a significant burden at the main tertiary hospital in Sierra Leone. Urgent action is needed to strengthen microbiological diagnostic infrastructure, initiate surveillance on antibiotic resistance and develop and implement policy framework on antibiotic stewardship.

title: Evaluation of Methods for the Concentration and Extraction of Viruses from Sewage in the Context of Metagenomic Sequencing
abstract: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of several methods for concentrating and isolating viruses from untreated sewage, in order to facilitate metagenomic sequencing. It is widely accepted that untreated wastewater contains a number of human-associated enteric viruses, as well as microorganisms with potentially pathogenic characteristics. Recent advances in metagenomics have highlighted the health risks associated with direct exposure to contaminated waters, making it essential for reliable techniques for virus extraction and concentration from sewage to be established. A comparison between two common single-step processing protocols is conducted: immunocapture viral nucleic acid pre-concentration (IVPC) and polyethylene glycol (PEG)-assisted ultrafiltration (PUUF). In addition, we also assess combined multi-step processes based on size exclusion filtration chromatography (SEFC), spiral membrane ultrafiltration running counter current to prior centrifugation rounds (CF+3MF+ST), or separation by sucrose gradients via differential centrifugation spin basket harvesting integrated sequential leaching/retrieval protocol (DC/SSLRP). Our results demonstrate that IVPC outperforms PUUF by 1.5 – 2 times depending upon catalogued RNA viral targets within inoculated samples, whilst SEFC removed approximately 30% more target than CF+3MF+ST method under certain conditions tested here. However further optimization is required due to significant differences among these methods in detection performance depending on particular type and amount of inputs used during processing.

title: Inclusion of Additional Unintended Consequences in Economic Evaluation: A Systematic Review of Immunization and Tuberculosis Cost-Effectiveness Analyses
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to review economic evaluations of immunization and tuberculosis to determine the extent to which additional unintended consequences were taken into account in the analysis and to describe the methodological approaches used to estimate these, where possible. METHODS: We sourced the vaccine economic evaluations from a previous systematic review by Nymark et al. (2009–2015) and searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase from 2015 to 2019 using the same search strategy. For tuberculosis economic evaluations, we extracted studies from 2009 to 2019 that were published in a previous review by Siapka et al. We followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidance. Studies were classified according to the categories and subcategories (e.g., herd immunity, non-specific effects, and labor productivity) defined in a framework identifying additional unintended consequences by Nymark and Vassall. Where possible, methods for estimating the additional unintended consequences categories and subcategories were described. title: CXCR6 regulates localization of tissue-resident memory CD8 T cells to the airways
abstract: The tissue-resident memory T cell population is a significant component of the adaptive immune system responsible for protecting against recurrent infections. We present an extensive investigation demonstrating that CXCR6 is critical in regulating the localization of this important cellular subset within the airway. To examine how CXCR6 affects tissue-resident memory CD8 T cell positioning, we combined physiological and functional analyses with comprehensive transcriptome profiling to comprehensively assess its role in vivo. Our results reveal that CXCR6 promotes the selection and retention of these cells at sites distant from the original source, identifying this receptor as a primary regulator of their migration to peripheral tissues such as bronchoalveolar lavages (BALs). This study provides new insights into how these cells are maintained and mobilized during infection or inflammation, potentially offering novel strategies for optimizing disease control or vaccine design.

title: In Vitro Viability and Cytotoxicity Testing and Same-Well Multi-Parametric Combinations for High Throughput Screening
abstract: In vitro cytotoxicity testing has become an integral aspect of drug discovery because it is a convenient, costeffective, and predictive means of characterizing the toxic potential of new chemical entities. The early and routine implementation of this testing is testament to its prognostic importance for humans. Although a plethora of assay chemistries and methods exist for 96-well formats, few are practical and sufficiently sensitive enough for application in high throughput screening (HTS). Here we briefly describe a handful of the currently most robust and validated HTS assays for accurate and efficient assessment of cytotoxic risk. We also provide guidance for successful HTS implementation and discuss unique merits and detractions inherent in each method. Lastly, we discuss the advantages of combining specific HTS compatible assays into multi-parametric, same-well formats.

title: Regulation of Male Fertility by the Renin-Angiotensin System
abstract: The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) is a peptidic system known mainly for its roles in the maintenance of blood pressure and electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. However, several tissues and cells have been described to possess an intrinsic RAS that acts locally through different paracrine and autocrine mechanisms. In the male reproductive system, several components of this system have been observed in various organs and tissues, such as the testes, spermatozoa and seminal fluid. Some functions attributed to this local RAS are maintenance of seminal plasma electrolytes, regulation of steroidogenesis and spermatogenesis, and sperm functions. However, their specific actions in these locations are not fully understood. Therefore, a deep knowledge of the functions of the RAS at both the testicular and seminal levels could clarify its roles in male infertility and sperm physiology, and the different RAS elements could be used to design tools enabling the diagnosis and/or treatment of male infertility.

title: Trafficking of activated cytotoxic T lymphocytes into the central nervous system: Use of a transgenic model
abstract: This study examines the trafficking of activated cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) into the central nervous system of a transgenic animal model. By linking immune responses in peripheral tissues with those within the CNS, this research will provide novel insights into protective and enduring immunity to infection or disease occurrence. The transgenic approach used enables an analysis of CTL trafficking under physiological conditions, which can potentially be explored further in investigations on neurodegenerative diseases caused by normally tissue-restricted agents. This work offers an innovative method for exploring real time dynamics associated with anatomical distribution changes that occur during infections caused by neurotropic pathogens and their countermeasures by host cells.

title: Characterization of Neutralizing Profiles in HIV-1 Infected Patients from whom the HJ16, HGN194 and HK20 mAbs were Obtained
abstract:
This article introduces the characterization of neutralizing profiles in HIV-1 infected patients from whom monoclonal antibodies such as HJ16, HGN194 and HK20 have been obtained. The purpose of this study is to explore the therapeutic activities of these mAbs against Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). Analyses performed on serum samples collected from three individuals included tests for sensitivity to agonists and antagonists, testing for epitope binding motifs using CD4+, CCR5+ receptor binding analysis. Through a combination of techniques including quantitative viruses production assays, antigenic cross reactivity measurements, correlation studies between ligand-receptor target sites and virus vulnerability profiles were established for all three types of mAbs. Results indicated that each antibody had different mechanisms for blocking HIV infection as well as varying levels of viral intracellular penetration capabilities. Furthermore, an in vitro model system combining yeast immunosequencing technology with bioluminescence signal transduction was used to directly observe real time changes in the strength and magnitude ratio between replication inhibition among various antigens after exposure to specific concentrations conditions allowing us to further establish individualized therapeutic strategies based on patient's serology characteristics by linking immune responses associated with susceptible or resistant cellular strain phenotypes across multiple cells lines within a single experiment format. Overall our findings suggest that host genetics may be playing an important role influencing efficacy rates observed when used in vivo treatments settings indicating caution towards potential off target effects when selecting treatment regimens personalized according population variability concerns which must be addressed through sustainable supportive monitoring post clinical interventions procedure setting systems..

title: Gene Silencing of SOCS3 by siRNA Intranasal Delivery Inhibits Asthma Phenotype in Mice
abstract: This study examines the potential of intranasal delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA) to silence the expression of suppressor-of-cytokines-signaling 3 (SOCS3), an inhibitor in JAK/STAT pathway, as a therapeutic strategy against asthma in mice. Recent studies suggest that targeting SOCS3 for gene silencing may provide an effective approach to limit allergic sensitization and airway inflammation associated with this respiratory condition. In addition, siRNA via intranasal delivery has emerged as a promising tool for treating allergic diseases due to its safety profile and ease of administration. Hence, this work aims to examine whether siRNA targeting SOCS3 delivered by intranasal route could lead to attenuation of airway inflammation from allergen challenge model in BALB/c mice. The results obtained support the protective effect gained from inhibiting airborne stimulation with siRNA intranasally administered targeted at SOCC3 gene which is acknowledged as contributing factor towards development or exacerbation of asthmatic conditions.

title: Characteristics of Patients Managed without Positive Pressure Ventilation While on Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
abstract:
This study explores the outcomes of patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) who were treated using only Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) with no augmentation from Positive Pressure Ventilation. This phenomenon, termed ECMO alone, is not as widely studied and discussed in literature concerning ARDS management. However, it is important to understand if there are any differences between this approach and conventional positive pressure ventilation therapy implementation or if difficulties arise without always having that additional option. Therefore, we conducted a retrospective analysis on 99 adult patients managed during the period 2019-2021 at Medical University Centre Zagreb in order to investigate characteristics associated with those subjects receiving ECMO alone for ARDS versus those under combined ECMO/positive pressure ventilation protocol. Variables compared included baseline characteristics such as age, sexe, cause of illness and primary location from which patients were admitted; clinical factors including Disease Severity Score (CTCAE v6), duration in Intensive Care Unit (ICU), vasoactive support need and median ventilator free days up until day 28 after hospitalization; laboratory markers like lactate levels on admission and length of mechanical circulatory support; complications etc., alongside patient related outcomes such as ICU mortality rate according to Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3–Revised criteria or Euroscore 2 scores during follow-up interval up to 100 days post discharge from hospital after successful extubation. Our aim was to gain better insight into profile of these particular population supported by alternatively developing regime basing solely on advanced supportive respiratory technique without initiating added positive pressure via conventional artificial breathing machines prerequisites instead thus highlighting potential considerations during diagnostic process or prior treatment strategy design when aiming best match care plan adhering individual features while achieving maximum benefit when tackling severe forms of disease manifestation so often observed within this field regardless available technological advances currently used .

title: Identification of New Rofecoxib-Based Cyclooxygenase-2 Inhibitors: A Bioinformatics Approach
abstract: This study presents the application of bioinformatics techniques to search for new Rofecoxib-based cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitors with potential clinical applications. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is a proinflammatory enzyme involved in many different human diseases, and its inhibition using nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can be beneficial for treating such disorders. Rofecoxib, a prototypical COX-2 inhibitor which has been removed from the market due to safety issues regarding cardiovascular events, still provides an important scaffold template for further structural modifications leading towards more promising functional molecules. A complete workflow including conformational analysis and pharmacophore feature extraction was followed by enrichment hybrid virtual screening against nonholonomic databases consisting of existing compounds with high binding affinities to ROFECOXIB. Results showed satisfactory precision values and possibility of identifying hits displaying similar biological activities as those exhibited by original ROFECOXIB structure itself. With this approach we provide novel insights about designing safer drug candidates with improved COX 2 inhibitory profiles upon chemical modification compared to rofecoxib analogue group once synthesized in laboratory settings.

title: Infectious Mechanisms Regulating Susceptibility to Acute Exacerbations of COPD
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive insight into the understanding of how infectious agents play an integral role in acute exacerbations of COPD. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory disease which is characterised by progressive deterioration of airflow caused by inflammation and obstruction, usually due to cigarette use. As it becomes increasingly common among populations worldwide, managing this potentially fatal condition has become an important aspect of contemporary healthcare practice. Acute exacerbations severely impair lung function and can even lead to death within days if not appropriately managed in time; however, the underlying mechanisms regulating susceptibility remain poorly understood. Through observational studies as well as laboratory techniques such as gene sequencing and immunofluorescence microscopy, this research aims to unravel these mysteries surrounding infectious processes that may increase or decrease risk for developing acute exacerbations of COPD for individuals suffering from this incapacitating disease.

title: Glial proteins in canine distemper virus-induced demyelination: A sequential immunocytochemical study
abstract: This paper presents a sequential immunocytochemical study aimed at determining the level of glial proteins in canine distemper virus-induced demyelination. A detailed investigation was conducted on tissue samples from dogs infected with Canine Distemper Virus (CDV) to evaluate the expression of glial proteins, such as Glutamate Aspartate Transporter (GLAST), Gliosis-associated protein 1 (GFAP) and Myelin Proteolipid Protein (PLP). The results obtained will help scientists deduce pathogenic mechanisms associated with CDV infection and its consequent neurological dysfunctions. In conclusion, upon completion, this sequential immunocytochemical approach will provide better understanding regarding the impact of CDV infection on neurochemistry and can also lead to further refinements in preventive measures against viral encephalitis.

title: Widespread Prevalence of Antibodies Against Swine Influenza A (pdm H1N1 09) Virus in Pigs of Eastern Uttar Pradesh, India
abstract: Swine influenza virus (SIV) belongs to family Orthomyxoviridae and can cause acute respiratory infection in pigs. Several pandemic H1N1 human fatal influenza cases were reported in India. Though pigs are predisposed to both avian and human influenza virus infections with the potential to generate novel reassortants, there are only a few reports of SIV in Indian pigs. We conducted a serological survey to assess the status of H1N1 infection in pigs of various states in India, between 2009 and 2016. Based on Haemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay, seroprevalence rate of H1N1 virus ranged between 5.2% (2009) and 36.3% (2011). Widespread prevalence of antibody was observed in eastern Uttar Pradesh from 6.2 to 37.5% during the study period. Co-circulation of seasonal H1N1 virus along with pandemic H1N1 virus was indicated by the presence of specific antibodies against seasonal H1N1 virus in eastern part of Uttar Pradesh. Seroprevalence rate in pigs and influenza infection trend in human shows the possible spill over transmission of influenza to pigs from human. Hence, besides serological surveillance, continuous and systematic molecular surveillance should be implemented in pig population to reduce/quantify the risk and emergence of pandemic influenza.

title: DNA Vaccines Against Mycoplasma Elicit Humoral Immune Responses in Ostriches
abstract: In ostriches, the population densities resulting from intensive rearing increases susceptibility to pathogens such as mycoplasmas. In addition to good management practices, vaccination offers an attractive alternative for controlling mycoplasma infections in food animals, instead of using antibiotics, which often leave unacceptable residues. The use of live attenuated vaccines, however, carry the concern of reversion to virulence or genetic recombination with field strains. Currently there are no commercially available vaccines against ostrich-infecting mycoplasmas and this study therefore set out to develop and evaluate the use of a DNA vaccine against mycoplasma infections in ostriches using an OppA protein as antigen. To this end, the oppA gene of “Mycoplasma nasistruthionis sp. nov.” str. Ms03 was cloned into two DNA vaccine expression vectors after codon correction by site-directed mutagenesis. Three-months-old ostriches were then vaccinated intramuscularly at different doses followed by a booster vaccination after 6 weeks. The ability of the DNA vaccines to elicit an anti-OppA antibody response was evaluated by ELISA using the recombinant OppA protein of Ms03 as coating antigen. A statistically significant anti-OppA antibody response could be detected after administration of a booster vaccination indicating that the OppA protein was successfully immunogenic. The responses were also both dose and vector dependent. In conclusion, the DNA vaccines were able to elicit an immune response in ostriches and can therefore be viewed as an option for the development of vaccines against mycoplasma infections.

title: Trialstreamer: A living, automatically updated database of clinical trial reports
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard method for evaluating whether a treatment works in health care but can be difficult to find and make use of. We describe the development and evaluation of a system to automatically find and categorize all new RCT reports. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Trialstreamer continuously monitors PubMed and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, looking for new RCTs in humans using a validated classifier. We combine machine learning and rule-based methods to extract information from the RCT abstracts, including free-text descriptions of trial PICO (populations, interventions/comparators, and outcomes) elements and map these snippets to normalized MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) vocabulary terms. We additionally identify sample sizes, predict the risk of bias, and extract text conveying key findings. We store all extracted data in a database, which we make freely available for download, and via a search portal, which allows users to enter structured clinical queries. Results are ranked automatically to prioritize larger and higher-quality studies. RESULTS: As of early June 2020, we have indexed 673 191 publications of RCTs, of which 22 363 were published in the first 5 months of 2020 (142 per day). We additionally include 304 111 trial registrations from the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. The median trial sample size was 66. CONCLUSIONS: We present an automated system for finding and categorizing RCTs. This yields a novel resource: a database of structured information automatically extracted for all published RCTs in humans. We make daily updates of this database available on our website (https://trialstreamer.robotreviewer.net).

title: Tuberculosis Susceptibility and Vaccine Protection Are Independently Controlled by Host Genotype
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a highly contagious and potentially fatal disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which has been part of human history for centuries. Despite significant medical advancements in diagnosis and treatment options, the global incidence of TB continues to rise due to the emergence of multi-drug resistant strains. It is therefore essential to determine how its transmission can be mitigated. In this study, we explored how host genotype directly affects the risk of infection with TB through susceptibility factors and vaccine protection efficacy against post-exposure diseases using an animal model system comprised of C3H/HeJ mice strain. Our results indicate that susceptibility and vaccine protection are independently controlled by hostgenotype rather than linked together under one mechanism; thus providing insight into processes underlying mycobacterial immunity/resistance across different susceptible/resistant mouse backgrounds. title: Performance of Zoster Vaccine Live (Zostavax): A Systematic Review of 12 years of Experimental and Observational Evidence
abstract: BACKGROUND: One in three people in the U.S. will develop herpes zoster during their life. Zoster Vaccine Live (ZVL or Zostavax™), has been licensed in the U.S. since 2006 to prevent herpes zoster. ZVL protection has been shown to wane with time and estimates of effect can be imprecise. We performed a systematic review of the duration of efficacy and effectiveness of ZVL against herpes zoster (HZ). METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and clinicaltrials.gov for vaccine efficacy or effectiveness (VE) studies of ZVL. Two authors independently screened each title and abstract, and potential VE studies were reviewed in-depth. Eligibility criteria included original data on ZVL prevention of HZ in a general population of immunocompetent recipients ≤ 60 years old. Selected articles were abstracted, independently reviewed, and discrepancies adjudicated. We attempted to locate relevant unpublished work and contacted authors for additional data, where necessary. Measures of association were illustrated on a forest plot and converted to VE (1-hazard ratio or risk ratio or odds ratio). RESULTS: We screened 1302 articles; 17 underwent full text review and 8 met inclusion criteria and were abstracted for this review. Selected studies included 1 phase III randomized controlled trial, 2 quasi experimental and 5 observational studies. One experimental and 5 observational studies estimated VE during the period from vaccination up to 4 years following vaccination; estimates across studies ranged from 33%-55%. Two quasi experimental and 3 observational studies estimated VE for ≥ 4 years following vaccination; estimates ranged from 19%-40%; the median estimate was 24% (Figure). Pooled VE was not calculated due to heterogeneity in length of follow up, age distribution of study subjects, as well as adjustment for factors such as underlying medical conditions. CONCLUSION: Most experimental and observational studies estimate VE just above 50% during the 3 years following receipt of ZVL. Beyond 3 years, ZVL protection wanes, with most studies estimating a VE of ≤24% after 4 years. Information on overall efficacy and duration of protection from ZVL will guide policy decisions regarding its use. DISCLOSURES: E. Belongia, Novavax: Investigator, Research support

title: Integrating food security into public health and provincial government departments in British Columbia, Canada
abstract: Food security policy, programs, and infrastructure have been incorporated into Public Health and other areas of the Provincial Government in British Columbia, including the adoption of food security as a Public Health Core Program. A policy analysis of the integration into Public Health is completed by merging findings from 48 key informant interviews conducted with government, civil society, and food supply chain representatives involved in the initiatives along with relevant documents and participant/direct observations. The paper then examines the results within the context of historic and international trends and theoretical models of food policy, community food security, and applied policy research. Public Health re-emerged as a driver of food security in BC—both as a key player and in positing the public’s health as a driver in food security and food systems. While Public Health’s lead role supported an increase in legitimacy for food security in BC, interviewees described a clash of cultures between Public Health and civil society. The clash of cultures occurred partly as a result of Public Health’s limited food security mandate and top down approach. Consequently civil society voice at the provincial level was marginalized. A social policy movement toward a new political paradigm—regulatory pluralism—calls for greater engagement of civil society, and for all sectors to work together toward common goals. A new, emerging policy map is proposed for analyzing the dynamics of food security and health promotion initiatives in BC.

title: Reducing Spreading Processes on Networks to Markov Population Models
abstract: This paper presents an approach for deriving Markov population models from spreading processes on networks. In recent decades, the application of Markov models to analyse the spread of phenomena on complex connected networks has become essential for various domains such as epidemiology, sociology and engineering disciplines. Yet despite their utility and successful applications, current techniques lack flexibility in terms of modelling these processes from scratch. We propose a framework which starts by introducing a minimum description needed to describe a larger system involving agents that can influence each other based on their relations. We then use this framework to develop an automatic identification procedure that transforms original edge-based interactions into nodes with appropriate dynamics so they fit within the sphere of existing theoretical results enabling effective modelling through reduced sets with clear interpretations using commonly accepted standard tools allowing end users complete control over network parameters. Finally, we show how multiple access points can be observed leading not only toward improved accuracy but faster methods using considerably small amounts data processing requests compared to previous works thereby opening new possibilities in real time or applied settings as well as encouraging further research in large scale simulations while also providing evidence towards future trends related to recently proposed mathematical treatments towards complexity theory problems

abstract: This study provides the first report of a whole-genome sequence of a Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea Virus (PEDV) isolate collected in Belgium during an outbreak that occurred in January 2015. title: Impact of Outpatient Neuraminidase Inhibitor Treatment in Patients Infected With Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 at High Risk of Hospitalization: An Individual Participant Data Metaanalysis
abstract: This study presents a metaanalysis of individual participant data assessing the impact of outpatient neuraminidase inhibitor treatment on hospitalization rates among patients infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. The primary aim was to perform an updated publicly available review and quantify the benefit associated with early outpatient management in high-risk patients. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, laboratory confirmed secondary infection, risk factors for hospitalization, adverse events, and use of additional antiviral medications. We identified twenty studies published after 2009 containing information pertaining to our outcome measures that met inclusion criteria. Risk ratios were calculated using random effects analyses for both odds ratio (OR) and hazard ratio (HR). We found that compared to no treatment or comparison therapies such as amantadine/rimantadine or watchful waiting without neuraminidase inhibitors, oseltamivir showed statistically significant reduced hazards of hospitalization [Adjusted OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.37–079], while zanamivir showed trends towards benefit [Adjusted HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.52–1]. This is one of few IPD meta-analyses conducted exploring the benefits and harms associated with neuraminidase inhibitor treatments at reducing morbidity caused by influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infections among at risk patient populations worldwide making it a valuable contribution to current literature knowledge base and policy decisions regarding clinical preventive measures against this increasingly prevalent health problem Infectious Disease Control & Prevention Measures: Impact Of Outpatient Neuraminidase Inhibitor Treatment In Patients Infected With Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 At High Risk Of Hospitalization – An Individual Participant Data Metaanalysis

title: Public Perception on Healthcare Services: Evidence from Social Media Platforms in China
abstract: The modern healthcare system is undergoing rapid transformation, with social media playing a significant role in targeting and serving the needs of patients. As one of the most developed countries worldwide, China serves as an interesting case to investigate how public opinion on health services is affected by digital channels. This study explores the use of online platforms among consumers in China to gauge consumer sentiment toward medical services based on data collected from three major social media platforms. It draws attention to current trends in consumer behaviour and addresses concerns about trustworthiness of service providers that have been enhanced as a result of increased usage and visibility. Furthermore, it demonstrates implications for policy makers concerning public perception that may influence health care decisions. Finally, tactical recommendations are suggested for stakeholders such as healthcare marketers who leverage these types of networks in order to better serve their targets customers effectively. Given its relevance for understanding the nation-wide insight into patient feedback about health services provider, this paper provides valuable insights into "Public Perception on Healthcare Services: Evidence from Social Media Platforms in China".

title: Interleukin-1β decreases HLA class II expression on a glioblastoma multiforme cell line
abstract: Antigens encoded within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) are not normally expressed in the central nervous system (CNS), but can be induced by treatment with interferon-γ (IFN-γ). Other cytokines released during an inflammatory process can potentially influence MHC expression as well. One cytokine of interest is interleukin-1 (IL-1), an immunoregulatory polypeptide that is produced by macrophages and also by cells in the CNS. In this study, the effedt of IL-1β on MHC expression in a human glioblastoma multiforme cell line, U-105 MG, has been examined. Treatment of U-105 MG with 10 U IL-1β/ml for a period of 5 days resulted in a decrease in constitutive cell surface HLA class II expression and limited the induction of class II by IFN-γ. This effect was also observed on steady-state levels of class II RNA and could be neutralized with antibodies to IL-1β. All class II transcripts examined (HLA-DR, -DQ, and -DP α and β) were affected. Class I expression was only marginally changed by IL-1β treatment. A minimal concentration of 1 U IL-1β/ml was required to reduce class II expression and a kinetics experiment indicated that U-105MG must be treated for at least 4 days with IL-1β for a decrease in class II expression to be observed. This study suggests that IL-1 may play a role in limiting immunoreactivity in the CNS by limiting class II induction.

title: Rotavirus excretion by kids in a naturally infected goat herd
abstract: A cross-sectional study was carried out in a dairy goat herd, investigating the presence of rotavirus by means of ELISA, polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) and two latex agglutination tests in feces of 63 goat kids younger than 1 month, with and without diarrhea, and in feces of 19 adult goats during the first few days after parturition. All animals belonged to a herd located in the mountains of the León province (NW Spain). Rotaviruses were found in 18 out of 63 goat kid fecal samples but no significant association between shedding of rotavirus and presence of diarrhea could be established. Rotaviruses were found in kids aged 6 to 21 days, and more frequently between 6 and 10 days. No shedding of virus was detected in any of the adults. Considering ELISA as the reference test, PAGE and both latex agglutination tests were less sensitive. One of the latex tests was also highly non-specific. All PAGE-positive samples showed the typical electropherotype of group A rotavirus. Feces were also screened for other pathogens including Escherichia coli, Clostridium perfringens and Cryptosporidium parvum. C. parvum oocysts were detected in the feces of six out of 45 goat kids tested, all six suffering from diarrhea. This paper represents the first description of rotavirus infections in goats in Spain. The possible mechanisms of viral diffusion within the herd and its role as pathogen in goats are discussed.

title: From Medical Geography to Computational Epidemiology – Dynamics of Tuberculosis Transmission in Enclosed Spaces
abstract: Medical geographers study the geographic distribution of health and health-related phenomena such as diseases, and health care facilities. Seeking to understand who is getting what diseases or health services where and why, they examine spatial disparities in access to health care services, and the geographic distribution of health risks. Medical geographers apply tools of geographic enquiry such as disease mapping and geographical correlation studies to health-related issues (Elliot et al., 2000; Pickle, 2002). Some have called this research endeavor spatial epidemiology (Cromley, 2003; Rushton, 2003a).

title: Metoprolol prevents neuronal dendrite remodeling in a canine model of chronic obstructive sleep apnea
abstract: This abstract provides an overview of a study investigating the effects of metoprolol on neuronal remodeling in a canine model of chronic obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Our results indicate that treatment with low-dose metoprolol can reverse OSA-induced dendrite alteration in dogs. Metoprolol was administered, starting from seven days after induction and for no more than thirty days following the onsetting symptoms, resulting in significant reduction of reactive oxygen species production linked to soma remodeling. Analysis revealed preservation or restoration to normal levels for most dendrites affected by pathological changes due to OSA. The present data suggest that metoprolol is able to reduce oxidative stress related damage by blocking β1 adrenoceptor activation and inducing mitochondrial biogenesis associated with enhanced antioxidant activity; thus helping protect against decrease memory capacity in animals suffering from OSA.

title: Optimizing classical risk scores to predict complications in head and neck surgery: a new approach
abstract: PURPOSE: To validate tools to identify patients at risk for perioperative complications to implement prehabilitation programmes in head and neck surgery (H&N). METHODS: Retrospective cohort including 128 patients submitted to H&N, with postoperative Intermediate Care Unit admittance. The accuracy of the risk calculators ASA, P-POSSUM, ACS-NSQIP and ARISCAT to predict postoperative complications and mortality was assessed. A multivariable analysis was subsequently performed to create a new risk prediction model for serious postoperative complications in our institution. RESULTS: Our 30-day morbidity and mortality were 45.3% and 0.8%, respectively. The ACS-NSQIP failed to predict complications and had an acceptable discrimination ability for predicting death. The discrimination ability of ARISCAT for predicting respiratory complications was acceptable. ASA and P-POSSUM were poor predictors for mortality and morbidity. Our new prediction model included ACS-NSQIP and ARISCAT (area under the curve 0.750, 95% confidence intervals: 0.63–0.87). CONCLUSION: Despite the insufficient value of these risk calculators when analysed individually, we designed a risk tool combining them which better predicts the risk of serious complications. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (10.1007/s00405-020-06133-1) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

title: The Effect of E-Learning on the Attitude Toward Dengue Prevention and the Acceptance of Dengue Vaccination
abstract: BACKGROUND: A community’s attitude toward dengue prevention and its acceptance of dengue vaccine and vaccination play an essential role in the success of the dengue infection prevention program. To develop their attitude and acceptance, the implementation of learning media is required. OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study was to examine the effectiveness of e-learning for developing the community’s attitude toward dengue prevention and its acceptance of dengue vaccine and vaccination. METHODS: This study employed a quasi-experimental method with pre- and post-test design by involving 85 subjects that were purposively selected from the low-prevalence area of dengue infection in the City of Bandung, West Java Province, Indonesia. A valid and reliable questionnaire was delivered during pre- (day 1) and post-test (day 7). For the e-learning, it was given on day 1 after completing the pre-test. A descriptive statistical method was applied to describe the research variables, to analyze the correlation between the subjects’ attitude and acceptance, and to examine the significant differences (pre- and post-test) between the subjects’ attitude toward dengue prevention and their acceptance of dengue vaccine and vaccination. RESULTS: Approximately 88.24% and 11.76% of subjects have good and fair knowledge about dengue disease, respectively. Concerning knowledge about dengue vaccine, 44.71% and 55.29% of them them have good and fair knowledge, respectively. In particular, there is an increase in their attitude toward dengue prevention (p-value <0.05), their acceptance of dengue vaccine (p-value <0.05) and their acceptance of dengue vaccination program (p-value <0.05) after they got information from e-learning. CONCLUSION: E-learning could have significant effects to increase the community’s attitude toward dengue prevention and their acceptance of dengue vaccine and vaccination.

title: Respiratory Viral Infections in Multiple Myeloma Patients
abstract: The abstract of the journal titled 'Respiratory Viral Infections in Multiple Myeloma Patients' explores the potential impact and nature of virus-caused respiratory infections on multiple myeloma (MM) patients. Recent studies highlight an increased risk to MM patients due to immunosuppressed state that characterizes the disease, along with higher prevalence of viral infections compared to healthy individuals. In this study, we provide a comprehensive overview related to viral pulmonary infections experienced by individuals diagnosed with MM, as well as efforts towards prevention and treatment. We investigate how various viruses such as adenovirus 16 may complications associated with progression of MM, including therapeutic induction failure or even poor prognosis. To understand molecular mechanisms underlying these processes, applicable data from both animal models and human clinical trials were examined for qualitative evaluation of the associations between respiratory infection events and outcome measures for those affected by this hematological disorder. Our results suggest that active surveillance is essential for prompt management strategies among MMR patients when potentially infected with any type of virus identified through diagnosis techniques commonly used in a clinical setting like positive throat cultures or PCR evaluations which could improve outcomes seen in these complex cases..

title: Investigation on Combined Inhalation Exposure Scenarios to Biocidal Mixtures: Biocidal and Household Chemical Products in South Korea
abstract: Global regulations of biocides have been continuously enhanced for protecting human health and the environment from potentially harmful biocidal products. Such regulations consider the combined toxicity caused by mixture components in a biocidal product of which approval and authorization are to be enhanced. Although the combined exposure scenarios of components in mixtures are firstly needed to conduct the mixture risk assessment, systematic combined exposure scenarios are still lacking. In this study, combined inhalation exposure scenarios of biocides in household chemical and biocidal products marketed in South Korea were investigated based on the European Union (EU) and Korean chemical product databases and various data sources integration. The information of 1058 biocidal products and 675 household chemical products that are likely to cause inhalation exposure with two or more biocides was collected, and mixture combination patterns were investigated. Binary mixtures occupied 72% in biocidal products. The most frequently appearing binary mixture was phthalthrin and d-phenothrin. Based on the frequency of use, we suggested a priority list of biocide mixture combinations which need to be firstly evaluated for identifying their combined toxicity for the mixture risk assessment. This study highlights that the derived combined inhalation exposure scenarios can support and facilitate further studies on priority settings for mixture risk assessment and management of potentially inhalable biocides.

title: eDNAir: proof of concept that animal DNA can be collected from air sampling
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is one of the fastest developing tools for species biomonitoring and ecological research. However, despite substantial interest from research, commercial and regulatory sectors, it has remained primarily a tool for aquatic systems with a small amount of work in substances such as soil, snow and rain. Here we demonstrate that eDNA can be collected from air and used to identify mammals. Our proof of concept successfully demonstrated that eDNA sampled from air contained mixed templates which reflect the species known to be present within a confined space and that this material can be accessed using existing sampling methods. We anticipate this demonstration will initiate a much larger research programme in terrestrial airDNA sampling and that this may rapidly advance biomonitoring approaches. Lastly, we outline these and potential related applications we expect to benefit from this development.

title: Prolonging herd immunity to cholera via vaccination: Accounting for human mobility and waning vaccine effects
abstract: The hallmark of cholera control has traditionally relied on providing safe water and sanitation services to limit spread of the bacterium in a population. Vaccination have also been used as an additional tool to prevent infection; however, this approach faces unique challenges due to human mobility patterns and waning effects of the vaccine over time. In order to maintain herd immunity, it is imperative for public health planners to accurately predict epidemiological trends associated with these two confounding factors. This paper investigates how changes in spatial movement interventions and vaccine protection duration can influence total disease burden in endemic areas by considering network-based models that represent both direct contact transmission within households and indirect transmission via short-distance travel between communities. The results suggest implementation strategies for extending preventive coverage further beyond traditional targets, thereby reducing overall suffering from cholera cases despite imperfectly modeled underlying processes such as disease dynamics and vaccination uptake data. title: Relevance of Autophagy Induction by Gastrointestinal Hormones: Focus on the Incretin-Based Drug Target and Glucagon
abstract: This paper will evaluate the relevance of autophagy induction by gastrointestinal hormones such as incretin-based drugs and glucagon. A detailed background on how these hormones influence autophagic flux together with their associated mechanisms is explored. The current therapeutic strategies involving modulating hormone levels as a potential treatment for major diseases, along with its drawbacks and effectiveness, are put forth in this review. Furthermore, various experimental findings on the pharmacological activation of intracellular components linked to autophagy induction by hormones, evaluated against established principles of target validation is discussed. This research provides insight into optimizing drug targeting techniques towards improving sensitivity and effectiveness of therapeutics involved in modulating cellular signaling pathways related to autophagy modulation in human health applications.

title: Analysis of Chemokines and Receptors Expression Profile in the Myelin Mutant Taiep Rat
abstract: This paper seeks to comprehend the modulation of chemokine expression and their cognate receptors in myelin mutant Taiep rats. Converging evidence indicates that alterations in immune system homeostasis due to neurological dysfunction are, at least partially, regulated by a complex network of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines associated with autoimmune pathology. Herein, we present an extensive analysis focusing on the quantitative assessment and comparison of mRNA expression for several chemokine receptors as well as selected members of the CXC-, CC-, C- and X-chemokine families across two distinct rodent brain regions: cortex (CTX) and hippocampus (HIP). Furthermore, this work aims at elucidating whether there is a differential regulation pattern between both myelin mutants where one strain lacks normal central nervous system development while the other shows less extreme phenotype. Our results show changes in gene transcript levels related to specific functional pathways affecting innate immunity among Taiep rat strains thus indicating possible new therapeutic strategies offering innovative ways towards alleviating pathological processes related to inflammatory or neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Influenza A Virus Polymerase Recruits the RNA Helicase DDX19 to Promote the Nuclear Export of Viral mRNAs
abstract: This research study titled 'Influenza A Virus Polymerase Recruits the RNA Helicase DDX19 to Promote the Nuclear Export of Viral mRNAs', provides new insights into how influenza A virus (IAV) has evolved to exploit cellular machineries as part of a highly orchestrated life cycle. By analyzing IAV-infected cells, we discovered that its viral polymerase recruits DDX19 helicases to promote its nuclear export, thereby providing evidence for the role played by exported mRNAs in viral replication and expression. This is likely an evolutionary adaptation enabling the efficient shuttling of large segments of viral genome across cell nuclei and cytoplasmic compartments. As such, this work uncovers novel molecular details regarding even infection by viruses belonging within the same family, exposing individualized protein/RNA interactions necessary for successful replication and virulence through various stages of infection. Such explanations help elucidate why certain members are more pathogenic than others in spite of sharing similar genetic barcodes. On another level, our data suggests potential therapeutic avenues against not just IAVs but other negative-sense single stranded RNA viruses related to it too.

title: Evaluation of the human adaptation of influenza A/H7N9 virus in PB2 protein using human and swine respiratory tract explant cultures
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the human adaptation of influenza A/H7N9 virus in the PB2 protein using explant cultures collected from both human and swine respiratory tracts. It has been observed that different mechanisms are involved in adaptation occurring at the level of amino acid residues located within this particular protein indicated by a number of studies. To gain further insight into these differences, we conducted experiments to examine the efficiency and capacity for adaptation which occurs when transforming H7N9 viruses between species. Our results will be helpful for better understanding how A/H7N9 virus can spread among humans, especially as it relates to their ability to adapt key proteins such as PB2, thus suggesting more effective pathogen control interventions.

title: The essential role of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 2 enzyme in thermal homeostasis upon cold stress
abstract: The essential role of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 2 enzyme in thermal homeostasis upon cold stress is an exploration on the evolutionary adaptation of temperature regulation in poikilothermic organisms. The research aimed to understand the effect of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 2 enzyme (FBP2) on metabolic activities that are involved in thermoregulatory processes and its involvement as an integral pathway for maintaining thermal equilibrium. Utilizing molecular biology techniques, we studied gene expression levels and enzymatic activity under experimental conditions simulating low ambient temperatures. Consequently, our results demonstrate that a decrease in FBP2 leads to decreased concentrations of glucose metabolites which correlate with impaired brown adipose tissue thermogenesis thus highlighting the importance of FBP2 for adequate cold tolerance ability. Our findings shed further light onto our understanding about physiological mechanisms regulating energy dissipation during cold exposures, providing important implications for both clinical settings and species survival strategies associated with climate change alterations
