title: Occurrence of pendelluft under pressure support ventilation in patients who failed a spontaneous breathing trial: an observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pendelluft, the movement of gas within different lung regions, is present in animal models of assisted mechanical ventilation and associated with lung overstretching. Due to rebreathing of CO(2) as compared to fresh gas, pendelluft might reduce ventilatory efficiency possibly exacerbating patient’s respiratory workload during weaning. Our aim was to measure pendelluft by electrical impedance tomography (EIT) in patients who failed a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT). METHODS: This is an observational study conducted in a general intensive care unit of a tertiary-level teaching hospital. EIT signal was recorded in 20 patients while pressure support (PS) ventilation was progressively reduced from clinical level (baseline) to 2 cmH(2)O, as in an SBT; four ventral-to-dorsal lung regions of interest were identified for pendelluft measurement. A regional gas movement (> 6 mL) occurring in a direction opposite to the global EIT signal was considered diagnostic for high pendelluft. RESULTS: Eight patients out of 20 (40%) were classified as high-pendelluft; baseline clinical characteristics did not differ between high- and low-pendelluft patients. At PS reduction, pendelluft and EtCO(2) increased more in the high-pendelluft group (p < .001 and .011, respectively). The volume of gas subject to pendelluft moved almost completely from the ventral towards the dorsal lung regions, while the opposite movement was minimal (16.3 [10:32.8] vs. 0 [0:1.8] mL, p = .001). In a subgroup of patients, increased pendelluft volumes positively correlated with markers of respiratory distress such as increased respiratory rate, p0.1, and EtCO(2). CONCLUSIONS: Occult pendelluft can be measured by EIT, and is frequently present in patients failing an SBT. When present, pendelluft increases with the reduction of ventilator support and is associated with increased EtCO(2), suggesting a reduction of the ability to eliminate CO(2).

title: Ebola Virus Maintenance: If Not (Only) Bats, What Else?
abstract: Ebola virus, a pathogen responsible for several outbreaks of viral haemorrhagic fever in humans and non-human primates, is currently thought to be maintained asymptomatically in bats. Despite an overwhelming number of evidence pointing to these hosts, the natural reservoirs remain largely unresolved due to inconsistencies between different surveys. This transversal study aimed to reanalyse existing datasets of animal species collected from central African countries affected by human Ebola outbreaks in order to identify other potential maintenance hosts beyond the traditional reservoir candidates. Molecular methods were used on samples taken from 1268 animals across 20 families including bat (Chiroptera), rodents (Rodentia) and others; analyses revealed that viruses similar to those involved in known outbreaks occurred primarily amongst sampled paenodontids family members but also occurred within other selected species. These proposed host-specific compounds have crucial implications towards Liberia’s effective disease management policy while highlighting some alternative/reservoir hosts likely contributing significantly towards this unique emerging phenomenon's maintenance cycle dynamics equilibrium.; suggesting requirement for much deeper investigation into the epidemiology and ecology associated with this debilitating zoonotic infection.

title: How Does Urban Farming Benefit Participants’ Health? A Case Study of Allotments and Experience Farms in Tokyo
abstract: This paper examines how urban farming initiatives in Tokyo can benefit the health of participants involved. Applying a qualitative research methodology, the study employs a case study analysis of two distinct types of urban farms: allotment and experience farms. Semi-structured interviews are used to ask about physical, social, and emotional aspects that may influence or be influenced by engaging in such activities. To consider generalizability limitations associated with this approach, information was supplemented by literature reviews on relevant topics related to public health outcomes associated with urban agriculture initiatives elsewhere in Japan and internationally. The proposed outcome measures focus on key domains identified through stakeholder engagement as important considerations when assessing public health involvement before, during and after taking part in any form of urban farming project; including environmental factors, community building experiences and food security motivations revealed during our fieldwork data collection phase.. Results will provide evidence regarding ways in which participation leads to improved physical activity levels among individuals living within large city environments who have limited access to green spaces (e.g., elderly people) as well as those seeking healthier lifestyles (e.g., young people).

title: Ubiquitin-Specific Proteases 25 Negatively Regulates Virus-Induced Type I Interferon Signaling
abstract: Ubiquitination and deubiquitination have emerged as critical regulatory processes in the virus-triggered type I interferon (IFN) induction pathway. In this study, we carried out a targeted siRNA screen of 54 ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs) and identified USP25 as a negative regulator of the virus-triggered type I IFN signaling pathway. Overexpression of USP25 inhibited virus-induced activation of IFN-β, interferon regulation factor 3 (IRF3) and nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), as well as the phosphorylation of IRF3 and NF-κB subunit p65. Furthermore, Knockdown of USP25 potentiated virus-induced induction of the IFN-β. In addition, detailed analysis demonstrated that USP25 cleaved lysine 48- and lysine 63-linked polyubiquitin chains in vitro and in vivo, and its deubiquitinating enzyme (DUB) activity, were dependent on a cysteine residue (Cys178) and a histidine residue (His607). USP25 mutants lacking DUB activity lost the ability to block virus-induced type I IFN to some degree. Mechanistically, USP25 deubiquitinated retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), tumornecrosis factor (TNF) receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), and TRAF6 to inhibit RIG-I-like receptor-mediated IFN signaling. Our findings suggest that USP25 is a novel DUB negatively regulating virus-induced type I IFN production.

title: Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae: Ecology, Infection Dynamics and Disease Epidemiology
abstract: Since 2008, the kiwifruit industry has been devastated by a pandemic outbreak of Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa), the causal agent of bacterial canker. This disease has become the most significant limiting factor in kiwifruit production. Psa colonizes different organs of the host plant, causing a specific symptomatology on each of them. In addition, the systemic invasion of the plant may quickly lead to plant death. Despite the massive risk that this disease poses to the kiwifruit industry, studies focusing on Psa ecology have been sporadic, and a comprehensive description of the disease epidemiology is still missing. Optimal environmental conditions for infection, dispersal and survival in the environment, or the mechanisms of penetration and colonization of host tissues have not been fully elucidated yet. The present work aims to provide a synthesis of the current knowledge, and a deeper understanding of the epidemiology of kiwifruit bacterial canker based on new experimental data. The pathogen may survive in the environment or overwinter in dormant tissues and be dispersed by wind or rain. Psa was observed in association with several plant structures (stomata, trichomes, lenticels) and wounds, which could represent entry points for apoplast infection. Environmental conditions also affect the bacterial colonization, with lower optimum values of temperature and humidity for epiphytic than for endophytic growth, and disease incidence requiring a combination of mild temperature and leaf wetness. By providing information on Psa ecology, these data sets may contribute to plan efficient control strategies for kiwifruit bacterial canker. title: The design of tourism product CAD three-dimensional modeling system using VR technology
abstract: In view of the high homogeneity of tourism products all over the country, an attempt is made to design virtual visit tourism products with cultural experience background, which can reflect the characteristics of culture + tourism in different scenic spots, so that tourists can deeply experience the local culture. Combined with computer aided design (CAD), the virtual three-dimensional (3D) modeling system of scenic spots is designed, and VR real scene visit interactive tourism products suitable for different scenic spots are designed. 360° VR panoramic display technology is used for 360° VR panoramic video shooting and visiting system display production of Elephant Trunk Hill park scenery. A total of 157 images are collected and 720 cloud panoramic interactive H5 tool is selected to produce a display system suitable for 360° VR panoramic display of scenic spots. Meanwhile, based on single view RGB-D image, the latest convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm and point cloud processing algorithm are used to design the indoor 3D scene reconstruction algorithm based on semantic understanding. Experiments show that the pixel accuracy and mean intersection over union of the indoor scene layout segmentation network segmentation results are 89.5% and 60.9%, respectively, that is, it has high accuracy. The VR real scene visit interactive tourism product can make tourists have a more immersive sense of interaction and experience before, during and after the tour.

title: The Impact of Diet, Nutrition and Nutraceuticals on Oral and Periodontal Health
abstract: Oral and periodontal diseases can determine severe functional, phonatory and aesthetic impairments and are the main cause of adult tooth loss. They are caused by some specific bacteria that provoke an intense local inflammatory response and affect—with particular gravity—susceptible subjects, because of reasons related to genetics and lifestyles (e.g., smoking and home oral hygiene habits). They are more frequent in the disadvantaged segments of society and, in particular, in subjects who have difficulty accessing preventive services and dental care. Some systemic diseases, such as uncontrolled diabetes, can increase their risk of development and progression. Recently, in addition to the obvious considerations of severe alterations and impairments for oral health and well-being, it has been noted that periodontitis can cause changes in the whole organism. Numerous clinical and experimental studies have highlighted the presence of a strong association between periodontitis and some systemic diseases, in particular, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, lung diseases and complications of pregnancy. The purpose of this editorial is to provide a current and thoughtful perspective on the relationship of diet and natural agents on oral, periodontal diseases, and chewing disorder preventions which may reflect good systemic conditions and related quality of life or to analyze indirect effects through the contribution of diet and nutrition to systemic health in order to obtain a modern diagnostic–therapeutic approach.

Some systemic diseases, such as uncontrolled diabetes, can increase their risk of development and progression. Recently, in addition to the obvious considerations of severe alterations and impairments for oral health and well-being, it has been noted that periodontitis can cause changes in the whole organism. Numerous clinical and experimental studies have highlighted the presence of a strong association between periodontitis and some systemic diseases, in particular, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, lung diseases and complications of pregnancy. The purpose of this editorial is to provide a current and thoughtful perspective on the relationship of diet and natural agents on oral, periodontal diseases, and chewing disorder preventions which may reflect good systemic conditions and related quality of life or to analyze indirect effects through the contribution of diet and nutrition to systemic health in order to obtain a modern diagnostic–therapeutic approach.

title: An Angelman syndrome substitution in the HECT E3 ubiquitin ligase C-terminal Lobe of E6AP affects protein stability and activity
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of an Angelman syndrome substitution in the HECT E3 ubiquitin ligase C-terminal Lobe of E6AP on protein stability and activity. Angelman syndrome (AS) is a genetic disorder characterized by developmental delays, reduced intellectual abilities and motor difficulties; caused by a deficiency of UBE3A levels or localization. Recently, it was shown that substitutions at certain conserved residues within this domain can occur, leading to varying phenotypes in individuals with AS. This research aimed to elucidate how these substitutions could lead to modifications in protein stability and activity based on two selected single nucleotide polymorphisms detected from 160 families affected by AS. By using X-ray crystallography combined with biochemical experiments we studied the structural conformation and thermodynamic properties for both wildtype (WT) and mutated forms of E6AP proteins; results indicating that substitution at specific amino acids have a drastic impact on protein stability as well as kinetics associated activities such as substrate binding affinities. Overall our findings provide evidence that this Angelman Syndrome substitution in HECT E3 ubiquitin ligase C-terminal lobe affects protein stability and activity significantly, thus potentially providing new insights into molecular mechanisms underlying this neuronal deficit disorder.

title: High-vs low-dose cytarabine combined with interferon alfa in patients with first chronic phase chronic myeloid leukemia. A prospective randomized phase III study
abstract: The purpose of this prospective randomized phase III study is to compare the efficacy and safety of high-dose versus low-dose cytarabine combined with interferon alfa in patients diagnosed with first chronic phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). Conducted by specializing clinicians at a renowned oncology center, 237 newly diagnosed CML cases were included. Subjects were randomized into two groups consisting of 119 participants receiving high-dose cytarabine alongside interferon alfa and 118 individuals treated via low-dose cytarabine plus interferon alfa for six months post treatment. Both comparison arms include three phases: induction, consolidation and maintenance followings remission achievement. The primary endpoint was overall survival rate plus the secondary endpoint being cumulative incidence rates of complete morphological response during the 6 month duration following completion of therapy. Results from this study suggest that despite both arms similarly achieving excellent outcomes, application of lower doses seems to provide an increased safety profile while maintaining significant long-term anti leukemic effects as compared to higher dose regimens in previously untreated CML patients receiving advanced therapies such as TKI's or stem cell transplantation/immunotherapy are concerned . Therefore it can be concluded that low doses may be an alternative choice when considering initial polychemotherapy protocols for adult — newly diagnosed CP -CML patients seeking curative intent management strategies under current clinical practice settings

title: Insights Into the Role of Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress in Infectious Diseases
abstract: This research paper seeks to explore the intricate and dynamic relationship between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and infectious diseases. Overconfident innate immunity pathways, misfolded proteins accumulation, disruption of eukaryotic cellular homeostasis all contribute to the development and progression of various microbial infections. With ever-growing evidence emphasizing a cross-talk between ER stress response and infection susceptibility, there is an urgent need for comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms connecting these two interrelated processes. To this aim, we conducted an in-depth exploration using both computational approaches as well as animal models, with an overriding focus on uncovering which pathways are involved in exacerbating or mitigating associations between ER stress response deregulation and microbial pathogenesis. By synthesizing our findings integrative bioinformatic results together with individual studies from cell culture experiments through mammalian infection models into a cohesive narrative we hope to critically advance current knowledge about the role endoplasmic reticulum stress plays within infectious disease nature network dynamics.

title: Management of Musculoskeletal Pain: An Update with Emphasis on Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain
abstract: This article reviews the recent evidence base on management of musculoskeletal pain, with particular emphasis placed on people living with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Musculoskeletal conditions are highly prevalent and account for a significant amount of time lost to work-related sickness absence; therefore, effective strategies to manage this condition are important. Medical practitioners play an essential role in correctly classifying the type of pain experienced by their patients, selecting appropriate pharmacological and nonpharmacological treatments responsible for successful symptom control, and implementing preventative measures aiming at reducing health burden in individuals without underlying organic disease. The current paper provides an updated review about epidemiology data on common chronic musculoskeletal pains (i.e., back/neck pain); underlines how medical professionals should address both primary care such as drug therapy(s) or physical activity programs along with secondary interventions (e.g., psychological support); explores the effectiveness of various types of medication including opioids; describes relevant nursing approaches regarding assessment and comorbidities; and finally appraises wider economic costs associated to these general disorders from society perspective. This manuscript offers valuable insights into current trends concerning management of muscuolteketal diseases that will be beneficial to medical doctors specializing in this field when formulating best practice guidelines for clinical setting involving individualized patient care plans as well as policy makers seeking cost-effective solutions offered by healthcare systems worldwide

title: Population Density Affects the Outcome of Competition in Co-cultures of Gardnerella Species Isolated from the Human Vaginal Microbiome
abstract: Negative frequency-dependent selection is one possible mechanism for maintenance of rare species in communities, but the selective advantage of rare species may be checked at lower overall population densities where resources are abundant. Gardnerella spp. belonging to cpn60 subgroup D, are detected at low levels in vaginal microbiomes and are nutritional generalists relative to other more abundant Gardnerella spp., making them good candidates for negative frequency-dependent selection. The vaginal microbiome is a dynamic environment, and the resulting changes in density of the microbiota may explain why subgroup D never gains dominance. To test this, we co-cultured subgroup D isolates with isolates from the more common and abundant subgroup C. Deep amplicon sequencing of rpoB was used to determine proportional abundance of each isolate at 0 h and 72 h in 152 co-cultures and to calculate change in proportion. D isolates had a positive change in proportional abundance in most co-cultures regardless of initial proportion. Initial density affected the change in proportion of subgroup D isolates either positively or negatively depending on the particular isolates combined, suggesting that growth rate, population density and other intrinsic features of the isolates influenced the outcome. Our results demonstrate that population density is an important factor influencing the outcome of competition between Gardnerella spp. isolated from the human vaginal microbiome. title: The Historical, Present, and Future Role of Veterinarians in One Health
abstract: This article focuses on the pivotal and continuously adapting role of veterinarians in One Health throughout history, present, and projected into the future. title: Psychiatry peer review groups in Australia: a mixed-methods exploration of structure and function
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to examine Australian psychiatrists’ experience of participation in a small group learning format of continuing professional development, known as peer review groups (PRGs), with a particular emphasis on group structure and functions. METHOD: An exploratory mixed-methods study comprising a survey (n=77) and semistructured interviews (n=6) with Australian psychiatrists participating in a PRG in the previous 12 months. RESULTS: Qualitative findings indicate that PRGs address experiential learning through a focus on both breadth and specificity of work, as well as participants’ experiences. Participants described using PRGs as a forum to manage difficult and complex work (through critiquing work, learning from one another, considering theory and guidelines, benchmarking, validating, reflecting and generalising learning) and to manage stress and well-being associated with crises, everyday stress and professional isolation. Particular structural aspects of PRGs considered essential to achieve these functions were self-selection of members, self-direction of meeting content and provision of a safe environment. These findings were convergent with the quantitative findings from scale survey data. Difficulties experienced during PRG participation are also described. CONCLUSION: Qualitative and quantitative findings from psychiatry PRGs demonstrate how practice-based professional experience functions as both a source of learning and of collegial connection that contributes to well-being and reduction in professional stress. Study limitations and future research directions are discussed.

title: Xanthohumol ameliorates Diet-Induced Liver Dysfunction via Farnesoid X Receptor-Dependent and Independent Signaling
abstract: The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) plays a critical role in the regulation of lipid and bile acid (BA) homeostasis. Hepatic FXR loss results in lipid and BA accumulation, and progression from hepatic steatosis to nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). This study aimed to evaluate the effects of xanthohumol (XN), a hop-derived compound mitigating metabolic syndrome, on liver damage induced by diet and FXR deficiency in mice. Wild-type (WT) and liver-specific FXR-null mice (FXR(Liver−/−)) were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) containing XN or the vehicle formation followed by histological characterization, lipid, BA and gene profiling. HFD supplemented with XN resulted in amelioration of hepatic steatosis and decreased BA concentrations in FXR(Liver−/−) mice, the effect being stronger in male mice. XN induced the constitutive androstane receptor (CAR), pregnane X receptor (PXR) and glucocorticoid receptor (GR) gene expression in the liver of FXR(Liver−/−) mice. These findings suggest that activation of BA detoxification pathways represents the predominant mechanism for controlling hydrophobic BA concentrations in FXR(Liver−/−) mice. Collectively, these data indicated sex-dependent relationship between FXR, lipids and BAs, and suggest that XN ameliorates HFD-induced liver dysfunction via FXR-dependent and independent signaling.

title: Mycotoxicosis produced in rats by cultural products of an isolate of aspergillus ochraceus
abstract: The toxicity of an isolate of Aspergillus ochraceus was examined in weanling male Sprague-Dawley rats fed diets containing a rice culture or fungal mat of the organism for 5 wk. The ground rice culture was mixed with a commercial purified diet at concentrations of 5, 7·5 and 10% and the fungal mat at concentrations of 1, 2 and 3%. In groups fed the rice-culture diets, weight gains were reduced and all the rats in the group fed the 10% diet died. Rats fed fungal-mat diets showed a marked reduction in weight gain, and the death rate was high (about 83%) in groups fed the 2 or 3% diet. Gross lesions found in groups fed either type of diet included focal necrosis in the liver, greenish discoloration of the kidneys, gastric ulceration, ulceration of the scrotal epidermis and corneal opacity. Histological changes in the liver included necrosis of the epithelium of biliary ducts, periductal oedema, pericholangitis, periductal fibrosis and disseminated focal hepatocellular necrosis. Necrosis of epithelium occurred also in the extraheptic ducts and was accompanied by an interstitial pancreatitis in certain rats. Foci of leucocytes and macrophages were found in the dermis of the scrotum and in the epididymal adipose connective tissue. Ulceration of the epidermis occurred late in the sequence of scrotal changes. Ocular lesions comprised corneal oedema, interstitital keratitis, iridocyclitis and hypopyon. Renal lesions consisted of tubular necrosis and hyaline and biliary casts within convoluted tubules.

title: Mo-Buzz: Socially-Mediated Collaborative Platform for Ubiquitous Location Based Service
abstract: This paper describes a middleware platform for user-generated multimedia contents which facilitates visualization and communication of vector-borne diseases (dengue, malaria, etc.). It acts as a community platform, where diverse users from geographically distributed locations can collaborate to seek and contribute multimedia contents of such diseases and related issues (breeding sites, etc.). Some of the essential services supported by the system are display of live hotspots, timeline, multimedia and Twitter-feed visualization, and location based services for both users and authorities. As a proof-of-concept, dengue disease was selected to build services using this platform to observe its capabilities.

title: A ribosomal frameshifting error during translation of the argl mRNA of Escherichla coli
abstract: This study investigates the effect of ribosomal frameshifting occurring during translation of the argl mRNA in Escherichia coli. Using computational analysis and enzymatic assays to measure translational fidelity, we analyzed whether trans-translation may lead to changes in protein expression levels. Our results showed that a significant amount of error was introduced during ribosomal frameshift events as compared with codon misreadings, suggesting that improper base pairing interactions at the stoppage site could be an important contributing factor for this type of errors. Additionally, we observed that some proteins were upregulated due to abnormal shifting, possibly revealing novel metabolic capabilities generated by this phenomenon. The implications for gene regulation are discussed within our paper.

title: Early Clinical Features of Dengue Virus Infection in Nicaraguan Children: A Longitudinal Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tens of millions of dengue cases and approximately 500,000 life-threatening complications occur annually. New tools are needed to distinguish dengue from other febrile illnesses. In addition, the natural history of pediatric dengue early in illness in a community-based setting has not been well-defined. METHODS: Data from the multi-year, ongoing Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study of approximately 3,800 children aged 2–14 years in Managua, Nicaragua, were used to examine the frequency of clinical signs and symptoms by day of illness and to generate models for the association of signs and symptoms during the early phase of illness and over the entire course of illness with testing dengue-positive. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using generalized estimating equations (GEE) for repeated measures, adjusting for age and gender. RESULTS: One-fourth of children who tested dengue-positive did not meet the WHO case definition for suspected dengue. The frequency of signs and symptoms varied by day of illness, dengue status, and disease severity. Multivariable GEE models showed increased odds of testing dengue-positive associated with fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, petechiae, positive tourniquet test, vomiting, leukopenia, platelets ≤150,000 cells/mL, poor capillary refill, cold extremities and hypotension. Estimated ORs tended to be higher for signs and symptoms over the course of illness compared to the early phase of illness. CONCLUSIONS: Day-by-day analysis of clinical signs and symptoms together with longitudinal statistical analysis showed significant associations with testing dengue-positive and important differences during the early phase of illness compared to the entire course of illness. These findings stress the importance of considering day of illness when developing prediction algorithms for real-time clinical management.

title: Improving the Hospital Quality of Care during Winter Periods by Optimizing Budget Allocation Between Rotavirus Vaccination and Bed Expansion
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the possible optimization of budget allocations for hospital care during winter periods to improve quality of care. The authors explore both rotavirus vaccination and bed expansion as two cost-effective segments in improving patient health outcomes and overall hospital performance throughout flu season. Exploring epidemiological data, healthcare policy, and traditional economic principles, they create an evidence-based evaluation system that would help administrators on all levels use their budgets more efficiently to achieve better results. This research aims to shed light upon the vital importance of carefully examining resource distribution in hospitals to ensure balance between key resources within a limited timeframe and constrained budget allocation needs. By leveraging advanced macroeconomic models and forecasting analytics, the authors generate valuable practical advice for healthcare facility managers that improves outcome predictability, which maximizes return on investment.

title: Investigation of the Phytochemical Composition, Antioxidant Activity, and Methylglyoxal Trapping Effect of Galega officinalis L. Herb In Vitro
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the composition of phytochemicals, antioxidant activity and methylglyoxal (MG) trapping effect of Galega officinalis L. herb in vitro. It is an herbal medicine traditionally used for diabetes management as well as antidiabetic, anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties. Although its use in traditional medicine has been extensively documented, studies on the chemical components in G. officinalis are lacking. title: Inhibitory Effect and Possible Mechanism of Action of Patchouli Alcohol against Influenza A (H2N2) Virus
abstract: This paper examines the inhibitory effects of patchouli alcohol against Influenza A (H2N2) virus and investigates its potential mechanism of action. Patchouli alcohol, derived from Pogostemon cablin, is a major component of essential oils and has been reported as having antiviral activity against various types of bacteria. In this study, MTT assays were performed to determine the cytotoxicity of patchouli alcohol at different concentrations followed by in vitro infection with H2N2 influenza virus on Vero cells in the presence or absence of patchouli alcohol. The results indicate that patchouli alcohol inhibited H2N2 replication without causing any adverse effects on cell morphology or viability suggesting it can potentially be used for treatment purposes. Further evaluations were carried out to analyze whether apoptosis mediates the antiviral effect through caspase 3/7 activation experiments; these results showed no significant expression variation when compared with control cells indicating an alternative mechanism is involved at play hereinr. In conclusion, this research provides evidence that patchouli alcohol may be beneficial in treating Influenza A (H2N2).

title: The Role of Microglia in Bacterial Meningitis: Inflammatory Response, Experimental Models and New Neuroprotective Therapeutic Strategies
abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of microglial cells in bacterial meningitis, the most severe form of infection afflicting the central nervous system. Bacterial meningitis is a major cause of death and disability globally, particularly among infants and young children. In this context, recent evidence implicates microglia as a key contributor to inflammation induced neuronal damage and mental health deficits associated with this condition. In particular, this works seek to review emerging theories on inflammatory response modulation by microglia during bacterial meningitis; identify suitable experimental models to study these processes; discuss novel therapeutic strategies for targeting protective responses mediated by microglia for improving prognosis and quality of life. Ultimately, increasing knowledge about how neurologic immunity works may lead to new avenues for advancing treatment protocols against bacterial meningitis and other neuropathologies triggered by infections.

title: N-substituted phenylbenzamides of the niclosamide chemotype attenuate obesity related changes in high fat diet fed mice
abstract: This study evaluates the ability of novel N-substituted phenylbenzamides to modulate obesity related changes in mice fed a high fat diet. Overweight and obesity are major public health issues, caused by several factors including dietary habits. Niclosamide is an established anthelmintic agent with promising anti-obesity activity; however its pharmacokinetic properties limit its application as an obesity treatment. In this study, we attempt to overcome these limitations through design and synthesis of N-substituted derivatives of the niclosamide chemotype which share similar biologic effects but improved systemic pharmacokinetics. Results demonstrate that some synthesized compounds were able to significantly attenuate weight gain, fatty acid accumulation, lipogenesis markers and inflammatory pathways activation in high obese diet fed mice compared with control group; thus offering potential therapeutic agents for the treatment of overweight/obesity associated pathologies.

title: The infection of primary avian tracheal epithelial cells with infectious bronchitis virus
abstract: This study examined the infection of primary avian tracheal epithelial cells with infectious bronchitis virus (IBV). To determine cellular and molecular effects, cultures of primary tracheal cells were exposed to viral challenge in vitro. After a brief period of post-vaccinal immunity, the unusual tropism and pathogenicity of IBV was assessed within 3 days post-exposure. The results suggest that, upon successful infection, IBV caused significant dysregulation in cell surface proteins as well as gene expression profiles representative of distinct viral response pathways associated with host defence mechanisms. Additionally, this study revealed profound morphological changes consistent with classical cytopathic effects. Collectively, the findings provide an invaluable insight into the virulence mechanism—and pathology—of IBV from avian hosts and serve to advance our current understanding on how this highly contagious virus can ultimately affect poultry health.

title: A Novel Behavioral Intervention for Rural Appalachian Cancer Survivors (weSurvive): Participatory Development and Proof-of-Concept Testing
abstract: Facing a greater cancer burden and fewer support services, rural Appalachian communities are particularly challenged in meeting the needs of cancer survivors. Despite their higher risk, there is a paucity of research to address maladjustment among rural Appalachian cancer survivors (RACS). This paper presents findings from participatory development and proof-of-concept testing of weSurvive – a novel hybrid behavioural intervention designed to improve mental health outcomes following cancer treatment within RACS. The qualitative process revealed distinct psychological experiences which shaped intervention components targeting self-management skills that work synergistically with lifestyle supports. We then conducted two trials to examine feasibility responses for the entire program (n = 42) and its individualized sessions (n = 200), respectively. Participants reported improved coping self-efficacy and life satisfaction after both studies, regardless session plans. To conclude, our empirical evidence suggests that weSurvive may be an effective method for aiding RACS in postcancer recovery; further prospective long-term evaluations should inform complete efficacy claims as well as modifiable dynamics related to adapting this type of programme for diverse cultural settings in Appalachia regionally and beyond.

title: H5N1 Virus Hemagglutinin Inhibition of cAMP-Dependent CFTR via TLR4-Mediated Janus Tyrosine Kinase 3 Activation Exacerbates Lung Inflammation
abstract: The host tolerance mechanisms to avian influenza virus (H5N1) infection that limit tissue injury remain unknown. Emerging evidence indicates that cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), a cAMP-dependent Cl(−) channel, modulates airway inflammation. Janus tyrosine kinase (JAK) 3, a JAK family member that plays a central role in inflammatory responses, prominently contributes to the dysregulated innate immune response upon H5N1 attachment; therefore, this study aims to elucidate whether JAK3 activation induced by H5N1 hemagglutinin (HA) inhibits cAMP-dependent CFTR channels. We performed short-circuit current, immunohistochemistry and molecular analyses of the airway epithelium in Jak3(+/+) and Jak3(+/−) mice. We demonstrate that H5N1 HA attachment inhibits cAMP-dependent CFTR Cl(−) channels via JAK3-mediated adenylyl cyclase (AC) suppression, which reduces cAMP production. This inhibition leads to increased nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling and inflammatory responses. H5N1 HA is detected by TLR4 expressed on respiratory epithelial cells, facilitating JAK3 activation. This activation induces the interaction between TLR4 and Gαi protein, which blocks ACs. Our findings provide novel insight into the pathogenesis of acute lung injury via the inhibition of cAMP-dependent CFTR channels, indicating that the administration of cAMP-elevating agents and targeting JAK3 may activate host tolerance to infection for the management of influenza virus–induced fatal pneumonia.

title: Chai Jing: The Power of Vulnerability
abstract: In the past seventeen years Chai Jing has risen from China’s official media to become a recognized investigative journalist, public intellectual, author, and more recently, an independent filmmaker and environmental activist. Her experience and work reflect how China’s news apparatus has reformed to adapt to the drastic societal changes with emotion being used to open up new ways of news communication. Her documentary Under the Dome further shows how the internet has transformed the ecology of media and provided innovative platforms for social engagement. Chai’s embracing her own feelings of vulnerability, which dominated the beginning of her career, and using it to channel public feelings and drive news reporting has made her a distinctively controversial media personality. Her leaving the CCTV can be viewed as a self-marginalization that helps her sustain that vulnerability, through which she gains resilience and critical power. The use of maternal voice in Under the Dome exemplifies her use of the power of vulnerability in its most mature form. The controversiality about that voice signals that post-socialist China remains a space where environmental and gender discourses are contested and negotiated.

title: Effects of higher PEEP and recruitment manoeuvres on mortality in patients with ARDS: a systematic review, meta-analysis, meta-regression and trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Mortality in patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) remains a major public health issue, and therefore the optimal approach for mechanical ventilation is of significant interest. The aim of this systematic review, meta-analysis, meta-regression and trial sequential analysis is to investigate whether recruitment manoeuvres or higher Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP) levels has any association with mortality rates among these patients receiving mechanical ventilation. A comprehensive search strategy was implemented to identify all relevant randomized controlled trials from inception until December 2020 concerning the effects of PEEP strategies involving different levels and recruitment manoeuvres on ventilator outcomes related to ICU mortality in ARDS population. After evaluating the methodological quality, data synthesis was performed using Risk Ratio as effect size measure. Our research allowed us to have a better understanding regarding potential candidates for recruitment manoeuvres that could be beneficial in reducing ICU mortality among adult subjects affected by ARDS who receive positive pressure ventilation.

title: Inhibition of hepatitis C virus replication by Monascus pigment derivatives that interfere with viral RNA polymerase activity and the mevalonate biosynthesis pathway
abstract: The hepatitis C virus (HCV) has become an important human pathogen due to the emergence of antiviral resistance, a situation that calls for finding alternative therapies. In this study, we investigated the inhibitory efficacy of Monascus pigment derivatives on HCV replication and identified their mechanism of action. We found that Monascus pigments interfered with viral RNA polymerase activity as well as mevalonate biosynthesis pathways involved in lipid metabolism and host-virus interactions. Our results suggest that these compounds have potential as viral inhibitors through multiple targets leading to decreased HCV replication levels. These findings could lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies against hepatitis C infection in humans providing new treatments with increased safety profiles compared with existing medications and allowing better clinical management

title: Ultrastructural study of myelinating cells and sub-pial astrocytes in developing rat spinal cord()
abstract: The anterior funiculus of the spinal cervical cord of post-natal rats was examined ultrastructurally. The myelinating cells found one day after birth contained a large amount of evenly distributed ribosomes up to the outer tongue of mesaxons, representing the cytoplasmic density. These cells were separated by astrocytic processes from the pial basement membrane, even when they were located on the pial surface. Astrocytes contained glial fibrils from one day onwards and often attached their processes to the pial basement membrane. Although the cytoplasmic processes of astrocytes occasionally wrapped axons, they were never shown to form the initial layer of myelin sheaths. However, the tenuous processes of the sub-pial astrocytes were occasionally rolled in myelin lamellae, as if a part of the myelin sheaths was constructed by astrocytic processes. The interpretation for this finding is discussed in relation to function and potency of the astrocytes, and variations and anomalies of nervous ontogeny.

title: A nationwide assessment of the burden of healthcare-associated infections and antimicrobial use among surgical patients: results from Serbian point prevalence survey, 2017
abstract: BACKGROUND: As the only non-European Union (EU) country, Serbia participated in a second point prevalence survey of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and antimicrobial use (AMU) organized by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) in the EU countries. Here, we aimed to estimate the prevalence of HAI and AMU in patients who had recently undergone a surgery and to compare risk profile, HAI rates, and AMU among surgical patients and non-surgical patients. METHODS: A national PPS was performed in 65 Serbian acute-care hospitals, in November 2017. In this paper, the data of 61 hospitals for adult acute-care were analyzed. To ensure the comparability of study design we used the Serbian translation of ECDC case definitions and ECDC PPS protocol. The trained infection control staff, led by a hospital coordinator, reviewed medical records to identify HAI active at the time of the survey and AMU. Only inpatients admitted to the ward before 8 a.m. on the day if the survey were included. RESULTS: A total of 12,478 patients from 61 hospitals for adult acute-care were eligible for inclusion in this study. Significantly higher proportions of surgical patients were female, belonged to the 60-to-79 age group, and were less severely ill. Also, extrinsic factors (invasive devices, hospitalization at the ICU, and prior antibiotics therapy) were more frequent in surgical patients. Prevalence of HAIs was higher among surgical patients (261/3626; 7.2%) than among non-surgical patients (258/8852; 2.9%) (p < 0.0001). The highest prevalence of all HAIs was noted in patients who had kidney transplantation (4/11; 36.4%), while SSIs were the most prevalent among patients who had peripheral vascular bypass surgery (3/15; 20.0%). Non-surgical patients received treatment for community-acquired infections in significantly higher proportion (2664/8852; 64.3) (p < 0.001). Surgical prophylaxis for more than 1 day was applied in 71.4% of surgical patients. CONCLUSION: We have provided an insight into the burden of HAIs and AMU among Serbia acute-care hospitals, and highlighted several priority areas and targets for quality improvement.

title: Testing, tracing and isolation in compartmental models
abstract: Existing compartmental mathematical modelling methods for epidemics, such as SEIR models, cannot accurately represent effects of contact tracing. This makes them inappropriate for evaluating testing and contact tracing strategies to contain an outbreak. An alternative used in practice is the application of agent- or individual-based models (ABM). However ABMs are complex, less well-understood and much more computationally expensive. This paper presents a new method for accurately including the effects of Testing, contact-Tracing and Isolation (TTI) strategies in standard compartmental models. We derive our method using a careful probabilistic argument to show how contact tracing at the individual level is reflected in aggregate on the population level. We show that the resultant SEIR-TTI model accurately approximates the behaviour of a mechanistic agent-based model at far less computational cost. The computational efficiency is such that it can be easily and cheaply used for exploratory modelling to quantify the required levels of testing and tracing, alone and with other interventions, to assist adaptive planning for managing disease outbreaks.

title: Clinical relevance and impact of Corynebacterium isolation in lower respiratory tract of critically ill patients requiring mechanical ventilation
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive overview of the clinical relevance and impact of Corynebacterium isolation in lower respiratory tract samples from mechanically ventilated critically ill patients. There has been an emergence of these bacteria as potential pathogens relevant to healthcare-associated infections, yet their true role remains largely unclear due to limited research. We have conducted an extensive review of literature related to Corynebacterium species identified by conventional methods or specialized techniques such as microarrays or sequencing, with additional focus on the antimicrobial susceptibility pattern, drug resistance mechanisms and consequences for patient outcomes. The findings suggest that although there appears to be associations between particular genotypes and phenotypic properties affecting treatment decisions among critical care patients possessing shared risk factors such as those unresponsive to antibiotic therapy or long ventilation duration, so far only very few studies are available covering this specific topic in ventilation-dependent population groups and further investigations into laboratory attests associated with disease progression would be beneficial. Our ultimate aim is provide concise recommendations based upon evidence which should lead towards better identification, control and management strategies for corynebacterial isolates within severely ill hospitalized individuals exhibiting prolonged mechanical ventilation status.

title: Risk factors associated with lower extremity amputation in Sudanese individuals with diabetes: The need for improvement in primary health care system
abstract: The situation of lower extremity amputations due to diabetes in Sudanese individuals is increasingly concerning as one of the most prevalent and devastating complications of diabetes. This paper aims to identify, analyze and describe risk factors associated with these types of amputations, so that preventive strategies targeted at improving primary healthcare can be devised. The study consisted of a retrospective analysis, involving clinical information from medical files in Khartoum state during 2017-2018, containing demographic data and emergency scenarios which led to the need for an amputation procedure. An assessment was done regarding preoperative evaluation by doctors with particular emphasis on patient's history and preventative measures taken before it became necessary for this type of intervention. In addition implications for self-care programs towards future patients will also discussed. It is hoped that such research can provide relevant insights into risk factors and indicate areas requiring improvement in the health care system in general leading up to potentially diminished frequency of those tragic outcomes among Sudanese diabetic patients due to greater awareness among diagnosis personnel as well as public education campaigns regarding early detection methods accurate management approaches .

title: Differential tropism of human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) variants and induction of latency by HHV-6A in oligodendrocytes
abstract: Abstract: Differential tropism of human herpesvirus variants, particularly Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), is an important determinant for latency and transmission. Recent studies have suggested that the two distinct HHV-6 variants; A and B can show varied tropisms with host cells as well as diverse immune responses in different individuals. The key finding from the results was an observed induction of latent infection by HHV-6A variant in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells suggesting a potential association between viral environment, genotype, and immunogenic response to certain cellular components. This study aimed to define differential replication capacities of the two primary variants namely HHV-6A and HHV-6B as well as its associated impact on ligand binding capability while spreading through neural tissues. title: The Impact of Infectious Diseases on the Development of Africa
abstract: Despite the success of vaccination programs for polio and some childhood diseases, other diseases like HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, acute respiratory infections and diarrheal disease are causing high mortality rates in Africa. However, mortality figures give only a partial measure of the toll asked by infectious diseases, and the global burden includes also health impact measured by disabilities, deformities, loss of productivity, care and treatment caused by a multitude of diseases like lymphatic filariasis, leishmaniasis, schistosomiasis, sleeping sickness and others. The impact of infectious diseases can be traced according to economic performance of African countries, showing that 34 out of 53 countries are classified as low-income economies. The disease burden is, however, more devastating since it affects all components of human development, including income, health and education. The impact of infectious diseases on African countries is no longer a crisis only for the healthcare sector, but presents a challenge to all sectors. It has the potential to reverse those gains made in human development in the last few years. Consequently, beyond health issues, these diseases should and must globally be seen as a development concern, affecting education and knowledge acquisition, income and social status, productivity and economic growth and other direct and indirect components of human development such as gender equality and human rights. For health strategies to be successful, international solidarity and public-private partnerships are needed to tackle the problems of shortage and lack of treatments, resistance and the need for new drugs, vaccines and diagnostic procedures. However, the output of international initiatives will remain limited without the national and local implication.

title: Reverse Genetics Approaches for the Development of Influenza Vaccines
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the application of reverse genetics approaches to the development of viable influenza vaccines. Vaccines based on whole genome sequencing allow for an improved antigenic response and minimal production cost, while also allowing adjustment to changing pandemic conditions. The reverse genetics approach relies on recombinant technologies to create virus-like particles (VLPs) that mimic wild type structures and elicit effective immunological responses. Reverse genetics is becoming increasingly recognized as the gold standard in vaccine development due its flexibility, specificity, and efficacy potential; it has already been successfully used in other viral vaccine systems including rabies, foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV), Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV), VSIV and SIV among others. This paper aims to explore existing knowledge surrounding these approaches whilst also highlighting further research avenues for advancing our understanding of how VLP synthesis through this technique can be applied effectively within influenza vaccine design strategies.

title: Molecular and electrophysiological features of spinocerebellar ataxia type seven in induced pluripotent stem cells
abstract:
This paper describes a study into the molecular and electrophysiological features of spinocerebellar ataxia type seven (SCA7) using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Spinocerebellar ataxias are a family of neurodegenerative disorders, typically characterized by cerebellum-related motor deficits such as impaired coordination and balance. SCA7 is one of nine known subtypes of these conditions and is caused by incremental expansion in trinucleotide repeat sequences in the gene CAG. A better understanding of this disorder will contribute to improved treatments for those suffering from its symptoms. The aim was to examine potential differences between patient iPSCs exhibiting normal levels of repeats against those with an expanded number, in terms of both genetic expression profiles as well as cell morphology and function including voltage clamp experiments on neurons differentiated from the iPSCs. The results suggest that distinct molecular phenotypes can already be observed under controlled laboratory settings while long-term effects upon morphology remain unclear. This study provides insight into disease pathogenesis which has implications for developing novel therapeutic approaches for patients affected by SCA7 or similar diagnoses.

title: Nonhuman primate species as models of human bacterial sepsis
abstract: This article presents an in-depth exploration of the potential for nonhuman primate species to serve as models of human bacterial sepsis. Sepsis is a scourging disease that has exacted a heavy toll on human populations throughout history and continues to present immense clinical challenges. Recent advances in technologies such as gene editing, computational genomics, toxicology testing, and microbiome analyses have made it possible to make meaningful comparisons between humans using primates due to their phylogenetic proximity. We discuss the utility of primates as research models by examining comparative immunity systems and reinforcing factors that challenge current approaches towards treatment or vaccine development paradigms. We hope our findings will assist researchers in uncovering better diagnostic strategies or identification of targets against this disease complex with great life-threatening consequences both locally and globally.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics and driving forces of terrorist attacks in Belt and Road regions
abstract: This study examines the spatiotemporal characteristics and driving forces of terrorist attacks in Belt and Road regions, with a focus on how these characteristics interact with regional security situations. By providing an analysis of various high-risk areas along the Belt and Road route, this research seeks to identify opportunities for mitigating threats by examining the underlying factors contributing to the initiation or expansion of terrorism. Using data from open source media reports, combined with other relevant geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial datasets, we will provide insights into spatiotemporal variations as well as trends within terrorism incidents across much of Asia. Furthermore, this research explores how changes in terrorist behaviour patterns correspond to political alignments among various countries that are affected by or associated with terrorist networks operating in these regions. The findings presented here are expected to inform both governments' decisions about their own security measures as well as bilateral relations between nations involved in these initiatives.

title: The American Organization of Nurse Executives and Global Citizenship
abstract: This paper examines the growing necessity of global citizenship among American nurse executives. With the aim of identifying important challenges for nurse leaders in developing this necessary practice, the paper explores how choices made by these professionals can have far-reaching consequences and impact a wide array of healthcare systems around the world. Through both qualitative research methods such as interviews and quantitative data analysis, insights will be provided into why it is essential for them to possess a mindset that embraces cultural sensitivity, human rights advocacy, social justice considerations and sustainability principles when leading change initiatives with stakeholders from different countries or regions. Furthermore, implications for further inquiry related to patient care outcomes across numerous setting contexts worldwide will also be discussed.

title: Pulmonary sequelae in a patient recovered from swine flu
abstract: This paper examines the long-term pulmonary sequelae of severe swine flu in a patient who has recovered. Although it is well established that swine flu infection can cause significant acute respiratory illness, little is known about the chronic consequences in individuals affected. Our findings suggest that even if a full recovery from an episode of severe swine flu may be achieved over time, ongoing physiological changes to the lungs resulting from prior episodes remain with associated physiological and psychological impacts on general health and quality of life. The implications for clinical management are discussed.

title: Inflammatory Diseases of the Meninges
abstract:
This paper explores the inflammatory diseases that affect the meninges, which are a group of membranes that form a protective layer around the brain and spinal cord. It describes their causes, symptoms, diagnosis and treatments in order to increase awareness about these health issues. Furthermore, it reviews the potential implications for long-term cognitive impairment and physical disabilities in individuals who suffer from this condition. The research contributes to our current understanding of these potentially serious yet manageable conditions by providing insight into their possible age-related impacts. By investigating how doctors provide care and manage symptomatic relief efforts as well as tracking patient progress over time with comprehensive assessments, we can better equip medical providers to provide accurate diagnoses while simultaneously tailoring treatment plans to meet individual needs. Ultimately, such research is necessary to enhance detection rates and reinforce effective treatment strategies for affected patients throughout different stages of disease progression in order to mitigate its impact on quality-of-life while preserving overall wellbeing during flares.

title: Predictive and Reactive Distribution of Vaccines and Antivirals during Cross-Regional Pandemic Outbreaks
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the efficacy of predictive and reactive distribution models in the context of cross-regional pandemic outbreaks. Drawing upon data from a series of outbreak simulations, the authors examine how well geographic considerations are taken into account when applying both preventive strategies, while further exploring which factors have to be considered for obtaining optimal results. Analysis is conducted as to whether vaccination or antiviral therapy provide superior effectiveness in controlling a pandemic spread. Such findings may lead to improved management strategies being available in future pandemics by enabling public health policy makers with more effective distribution tools at their disposal.

title: Expansion of RiPP biosynthetic space through integration of pan-genomics and machine learning uncovers a novel class of lanthipeptides
abstract: This paper reports on the discovery of a novel lanthipeptide biosynthetic space through the integration of pan-genomic and machine learning approaches. The expansion of ribosomally synthesized peptides (RiPPs) has been hampered by limited computational resources for identifying catalytic domains within microbial genomes and for predicting pathways based on domain composition. To address this limitation, an analysis was conducted using brute-force scanning through large genomic databases along with advanced deep learning algorithms to identify RiPP synthetase components characters up until now unseen in RiPP structures. As a direct result, our study presented here is the first example describing lanthipeptides explained in terms of pan-genomics with machine learning as well as details on their characteristics and potential applications. Our findings are expected to facilitate further research into bioactive metabolites with both therapeutic relevance and industrial application in bioscavaging processes due to their chemical stability under extreme environmental conditions and potential development towards small molecule therapeutics

title: Human temperatures for syndromic surveillance in the emergency department: data from the autumn wave of the 2009 swine flu (H1N1) pandemic and a seasonal influenza outbreak
abstract:
Due to the emergence of unforeseen global pandemics, understanding and responding effectively to infectious diseases has become increasingly important. In this research, the aim is to evaluate human temperatures as a source for syndromic surveillance in the emergency department during both an autumn wave of 2009 swine flu (H1N1) pandemic outbreak and a separate seasonal influenza outbreak over two continuous years. The authors studied temperature spreads defined by 0-4th quartiles in frequent visits coming from general practitioners for viral diagnosis in order to determine whether there was any noteworthy difference between normal temperatures and those feverish patients who went through further diagnostic procedures or were directly hospitalized. 
The results were analyzed with descriptive statistics such as mean, median, maximum and minimum values with consideration towards patient characteristics like gender and age group which helped conclude that especially individuals aged 16-50 had higher median body temperatures compared to other age classes while no significant differences have been recorded upon distinguishing genders. Initial observations suggested that using temperature measurements can provide an effective mechanism for quick communication network concerning emerging epidemics of such magnitude without overwhelming screening capacity or hospital resources yet further studies should definitely take into consideration data sources unrelated solely to human physiology like geographical mapping or secondary ambulatory services analysis so it could prove more illustrative on population displacement & mobility patterns of infectious outbreaks along with development index measurements looking towards socio-economic findings which lead towards better implementation timing not only at regional level but throughout different countries worldwide.

abstract: This study investigates the outcome of eliminating Staphylococcus aureus nasal carriage in intensive care patients and its effect on infection rates. title: Dichloroacetate-induced metabolic reprogramming improves lifespan in a Drosophila model of surviving sepsis
abstract: This study examines how metabolic reprogramming with dichloroacetate (DCA), a pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase-4 inhibitor, may affect lifespan in models of sepsis induced by infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Sepsis is characterized by an aberrant systemic inflammatory response to infections and affects millions globally, often leading to death within hours or days of diagnosis regardless of treatment. Thus far, reliable intervention strategies are limited and understanding the complex interplay between inflammation and metabolism during sepsis has been difficult to assess directly in humans. Using Drosophila melanogaster as a model organism for studying these connections, this work provides evidence that DCA can improve survival rates in fly models experiencing an acute challenge from P. aeruginosa infection and suggests a mechanism through which it does so — modifying host metabolism via activation signals at the epigenetic level. Additionally, our findings demonstrate potential efficacy for therapeutic applications involving DCA as a way of improving outcomes in individuals impacted by this challenging infectious disease process.

title: Fragmented Politics in Hong Kong—Analyzing the Pro-democracy Cohesion in the Legislative Council Before 2019
abstract: This study is to analyze how the fragmentation of the pro-democracy camp affected their council voting and policy stances before 2019. The quantitative measurements including the rice and unity indices are adopted to evaluate the cohesions of the pro-Beijing and pro-democracy camps in bill voting, in which the strategies employed by the pro-democracy camp are further analyzed. Before the 2010s, the moderate democrats deliberately separated from the administration and some of them also kept distance from the radical groups. However, since the radical ideologies gained supports from time to time, the moderate democrats had been forced to follow more pro-active lines against the administration. Although the political sphere of Hong Kong has drastically changed after the 2019 Anti-extradition Protests, the cohesion of the pro-democracy parties in the previous terms of the Legislative Council still facilitates to understand the legislative process in the city. In this article, 18 then members of the Legislative Council from different parties were interviewed in 2018, providing various insights on the analysis of pro-democracy cohesion and fragmented politics in Hong Kong.

title: Mode and tempo of human hepatitis virus evolution
abstract: This paper seeks to understand the mode and tempo of human hepatitis virus evolution across populations. By understanding why, when and how bacterial strains evolve, we can identify factors that drive diversification processes in humanity, providing means for detection and prevention of emerging and existing pathogenic strands. Using a combination of population genetics approaches and clinical case studies from around the world will give us insight into what evolutionary strategies allow infection to remain widespread within various populations over time. This knowledge is vital if we are to gain an accurate vision of evolutionary applications in our species as it relates to health outcomes..

title: A model for HIV/AIDS pandemic with optimal control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to model the spread of HIV/AIDS and proposes optimal control strategies for achieving disease elimination. We show that an optimal control strategy based on drug intervention, vaccination and strategic behavior modification can be utilized to suppress virus transmission while taking into account patient-level preferences, which offers superior public health outcomes compared with traditional approaches. To this end, we develop a mathematical model that incorporates heterogeneous preferences among patients in order to explain decision making at the individual level and generate efficient management methods. The study provides insights regarding the application of genetic algorithms to solve complex optimization problems in telemedicine and epidemiology disciplines, along with findings on how social networks impact behavioral change related interventions.

title: Effect of plasma vitamin C levels on Parkinson’s disease and age at onset: a Mendelian randomization study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Until now, epidemiological evidence regarding the association between vitamin C intake (both diet and supplements) and Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains inconsistent. Hence, it is necessary to establish the causal link between vitamin C levels and PD, and further develop effective therapies or prevention. METHODS: We selected 11 newly identified plasma vitamin C genetic variants from a large-scale plasma vitamin C GWAS dataset (n = 52,018) as the effective instrumental variables, and extracted their corresponding GWAS summary statistics from PD (33,674 PD cases and 449,056 controls) and PD age at onset (AAO) (n = 28,568). We then performed a Mendelian randomization (MR) study to evaluate the causal association of plasma vitamin C levels with PD and PD AAO using inverse-variance weighted (IVW), the weighted median, MR-Egger, and MR-PRESSO test. RESULTS: We did not observe any significant association between genetically increased vitamin C levels and PD. Interestingly, we found a reduced trend of PD AAO (1.134 years) with 1 SD genetically increased vitamin C levels using IVW (beta = − 1.134, 95% CI: [− 2.515, 0.248], P = 0.108). Importantly, this trend was further successfully verified using both weighted median and MR-Egger. Each 1 SD genetically increased vitamin C levels could reduce PD AAO 1.75 and 2.592 years using weighted median (beta = − 1.750, 95% CI: [− 3.396, − 0.105], P = 0.037) and MR-Egger (beta = − 2.592, 95% CI: [− 4.623, − 0.560], P = 0.012). CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrated the causal association between genetically increased plasma vitamin C levels and reduced PD AAO in people of European descent. title: An increasing trend in geriatric trauma patients undergoing surgical stabilization of rib fractures
abstract: PURPOSE: The proportion of geriatric trauma patients (GTPs) (age ≥ 65 years old) with chest wall injury undergoing surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) nationally is unknown. We hypothesize a growing trend of GTPs undergoing SSRF, and sought to evaluate risk of respiratory complications and mortality for GTPs compared to younger adults (18–64 years old) undergoing SSRF. METHODS: The Trauma Quality Improvement Program (2010–2016) was queried for patients with rib fracture(s) who underwent SSRF. GTPs were compared to younger adults. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed. RESULTS: From 21,517 patients undergoing SSRF, 3,001 (16.2%) were GTPs. Of all patients undergoing SSRF in 2010, 10.6% occurred on GTPs increasing to 17.9% in 2016 (p < 0.001) with a geometric-mean-annual increase of 11.5%. GTPs had a lower median injury severity score (18 vs. 22, p < 0.001), but had a higher rate of mortality (4.7% vs. 1.2%, p < 0.001). After controlling for covariates, GTPs had an increased associated risk of mortality (OR 4.80, CI 3.62–6.36, p < 0.001). On a separate multivariate analysis for all trauma patients with isolated chest Abbreviated Injury Scale 3, GTPs were associated with a similar four-fold risk of mortality (OR 4.21, CI 1.98–6.32, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Spanning 7 years of data, the proportion of GTPs undergoing SSRF increased by over 7%. Although GTPs undergoing SSRF had lesser injuries, their risk of mortality was four times higher than other adult trauma patients undergoing SSRF, which was similar to their increased background risk of mortality. Ultimately, SSRF in GTPs should be considered on an individualized basis with careful attention to risk–benefit ratio. title: Inflammatory Cytokine Expression Is Associated with Chikungunya Virus Resolution and Symptom Severity
abstract: This article presents new research on the role of inflammatory cytokine expression inpatients afflicted with chikungunya virus. The aim of this study was to evaluate how elevated levels ofseveral proinflammatory cytokines were associated with chikungunya clinical resolution, aswell as symptom severity during acute infection. An observational, prospective clinical trialwas conducted at a single medical center across four European countries. Analysis of outcomemeasures (inflammation and disease-specific symptoms) suggested that patients who developedhigh levels of certain cytokines shortly after initial diagnosis experienced more severeacute symptoms compared to lower-cytokine expression patients. Findings from this interimanalysis revealed that greater initial and peak level production for specific cytokines playeda significant role in determining disease progression in both groups even after adjusting formultiple confounders like age, gender or ethnicity; suggesting enhanced inflammation maybe linked to less effective viral clearance mechanisms requiring intervention efforts toprevent long-term comorbidity due to neglected arthritic sequelae..

title: The effect of network mixing patterns on epidemic dynamics and the efficacy of disease contact tracing
abstract: In networks, nodes may preferentially contact other nodes with similar (assortatively mixed) or dissimilar (disassortatively mixed) numbers of contacts. Different patterns of contact support different epidemic dynamics, potentially affecting the efficacy of control measures such as contact tracing, which aims to identify and isolate nodes with infectious contacts. We used stochastic simulations to investigate the effects of mixing patterns on epidemic dynamics and contact-tracing efficacy. For uncontrolled epidemics, outbreaks occur at lower infection rates for more assortatively mixed networks, with faster initial epidemic growth rate and shorter epidemic duration than for disassortatively mixed networks. Contact tracing performs better for assortative mixing where epidemic size is large and tracing rate low, but it performs better for disassortative mixing at higher contact rates. For assortatively mixed networks, disease spreads first to highly connected nodes, but this is balanced by contact tracing quickly identifying these same nodes. The converse is true for disassortative mixing, where both disease and tracing are less likely to target highly connected nodes. For small epidemics, contact tracing is more effective on disassortative networks due to the greater resilience of assortative networks to link removal. Multi-step contact tracing is more effective than single-step tracing for assortative mixing, but this effect is smaller for disassortatively mixed networks.

title: Management of Fulminant Hepatitis B
abstract: This article examines the Management of Fulminant Hepatitis B and its effects on patient outcomes. Fulminant hepatitis is a severe and potentially life-threatening form of acute liver failure that requires close monitoring, intensive care and timely therapeutic interventions in order to stabilize hemodynamic parameters, improve hepatic synthetic function, reduce pro-inflammatory responses and provide hepatoprotection. Although it is caused by various viruses, including hepatitis A, B or C virus infection as well as many other pathogenic agents such as alcoholic beverages and drugs, this paper focuses exclusively on cases where it emerges due to an imbalance between inflammatory responses toward HBV infection and impaired antiviral immunity. The aim here is to review current evidence regarding effective management strategies for fulminant hepatitis B based on immunomodulation with interferon therapy combined with appropriate supportive measures or sorafenib treatment at high doses depending upon stage of disease manifestationulmonary implications arising from cortisol use. Ultimately, this study offers guidance into characterizing individualized approaches needed to counteract fatal outcomes associated with precisely timed combined therapies designed to target the moderators imposed solidity of fulminant hepatitis B.

title: Effects of illness perceptions on health-related quality of life in patients with rheumatoid arthritis in China
abstract: OBJECTIVES: For patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in China, little is known of how their illness perceptions affect their health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The present study investigated associations between specific illness perceptions due to RA and HRQoL features. METHODS: For 191 patients with RA, illness perceptions were measured using the Brief Illness Perceptions Questionnaire (BIPQ) comprising 8 domains. HRQoL was determined with the Medical Outcomes Study 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36). Multivariate linear regression analyses were performed. RESULTS: The overall BIPQ of patients with RA was 49.09 ± 11.06. The highest and lowest scores were for concern (9.15 ± 1.81) and personal control (4.30 ± 2.52), respectively. Multivariate stepwise regression analyses showed that the overall BIPQ was significantly negatively associated with each HRQoL feature, and HRQoL total score (β = − 0.343, P < 0.001, 95% CI − 7.080 to − 4.077). Positive associations between BIPQ features and HRQoL included personal control (β = 0.119, P = 0.004, 95% CI 2.857–14.194) and treatment control (β = 0.084, P = 0.029, 95% CI 0.640–12.391). Negative associations with HRQoL were identity (β = − 0.105, P = 0.034, 95% CI − 13.159 to − 0.430) and emotional response (β = − 0.207, P < 0.001, 95% CI − 18.334 to − 6.811). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with RA in China perceive their illness in ways that affect their HRQoL. These results suggest that strategies that target these perceptions may improve the quality of life of these patients.
