title: First Discovery and Stucture-Activity Relationship Study of Phenanthroquinolizidines as Novel Antiviral Agents against Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV)
abstract: This study reports the successful identification and structure-activity relationship (SAR) investigation of phenanthroquinolizidines as a novel antiviral agent against Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV). Using computational methods, 18 phenanthroquinolizidine derivatives were synthesized and evaluated for their activity against TMV. Of these compounds, two exhibited promising inhibitory activities with abilities to block viral assembly in Agrobacterium tumefaciens and reduce disease symptoms on Nicotiana benthamiana. Structural modification studies together with molecular modeling greatly provided insight into the interactions between the molecules and active sites of TMV resulting in recommendations for further optimization efforts. This is groundbreaking work with potential implications for natural product drug discovery concerning methods aimed at controlling plant virus diseases.

title: Ultrastructure and immuno-cytochemistry of BHK-21 cells infected with a modified Bucyrus strain of equine arteritis virus
abstract: This paper examines the ultrastructure and immuno-cytochemistry of BHK-21 cells infected with a modified Bucyrus strain of equine arteritis virus. By deploying transmission electron microscopy, indirect immunofluorescence techniques, as well as RT-PCR for viral load determination, we observed virus particles inside biochemical compartments along with cytoskeleton structures in wild type and mutant cell lines. Traditional virological methods were applied to evaluate antiviral activity against different viruses from various hosts. We herein report that these modifications in the structure of important virion components allowed significant changes in infectivity when using either vector or permanent transfected cells. The findings presented could provide valuable insights on some of the molecular mechanisms underlying efficient viral replication during infections with modified strains and help devise preventive strategies against this potentially devastating disease of horses.

title: A Multiple Antigenic Peptide Mimicking Peptidoglycan Induced T Cell Responses to Protect Mice from Systemic Infection with Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: This study investigates a novel therapeutic approach which could effectively protect mice from systemic infection with Staphylococcus aureus. In the article, ‘A Multiple Antigenic Peptide Mimicking Peptidoglycan Induced T Cell Responses to Protect Mice from Systemic Infection with Staphylococcus aureus’, we evaluate an immunoprotective peptide – multiple antigenic peptides (MAPs) – and its ability to induce T cell responses against pathogenic S. aureus in vivo after injection into mouse models of respiratory tract infection. Through detailed antibody-mediated humoral responses and direct cytotoxic mechanisms, MAPs showed promising results by inhibiting bacterial replication and raising the serum concentration of desired antibacterial pathways in infected mice compared to ones treated only with PBS or naïve sera control groups. Our findings emphasize the importance of further research on developing strategies for using synthetic vaccines as viable alternatives for treating infectious diseases that could potentially enhance host resistance against persistent pathogens such as S. aureus without inducing life-threatening reactions upon treatment administration.

title: Neutrophil heterogeneity and its role in infectious complications after severe trauma
abstract: BACKGROUND: Trauma leads to a complex inflammatory cascade that induces both immune activation and a refractory immune state in parallel. Although both components are deemed necessary for recovery, the balance is tight and easily lost. Losing the balance can lead to life-threatening infectious complications as well as long-term immunosuppression with recurrent infections. Neutrophils are known to play a key role in these processes. Therefore, this review focuses on neutrophil characteristics and function after trauma and how these features can be used to identify trauma patients at risk for infectious complications. RESULTS: Distinct neutrophil subtypes exist that play their own role in the recovery and/or development of infectious complications after trauma. Furthermore, the refractory immune state is related to the risk of infectious complications. These findings change the initial concepts of the immune response after trauma and give rise to new biomarkers for monitoring and predicting inflammatory complications in severely injured patients. CONCLUSION: For early recognition of patients at risk, the immune system should be monitored. Several neutrophil biomarkers show promising results and analysis of these markers has become accessible to such extent that they can be used for point-of-care decision making after trauma.

title: Nanoparticle delivery of microRNA-146a regulates mechanotransduction in lung macrophages and mitigates injury during mechanical ventilation
abstract:
Nanoparticle Delivery of microRNA-146a Regulates Mechanotransduction in Lung Macrophages and Mitigates Injury during Mechanical Ventilation
The use of mechanical ventilation (MV) has been essential for the survival of many individuals, particularly those with severe lung injury. Recent advances have elucidated processes involved in lung inflammation following MV, including mechanoreceptor function and activation of reactive oxygen species production. However, little is known about how to modulate these processes to minimize adverse outcomes from MV-induced damage. This study aims to explore nanotechnology as a therapeutic method by which microRNA-146a delivery can regulate mechanotransduction signals influencing oxidative stress mediators and attenuate lung injury during MV. We hypothesized that nanoparticle-incorporated miR-146 will interact with target genes within the alveolar macrophage critical pathway regulating aggressive proinflammatory activities caused by MV exposure leading to improved long term outcome post injury. To investigate this hypothesis we used an immune competent murine model with controlled experimental conditions wherein treatment was shown to mitigate clinically relevant histopathology biomarkers associated with pulmonary dysfunction induced by mechanical stressors. Our results demonstrate that nanosecond incorporated microRNA regulates inflammatory pathways resulting in reduced morbidity and mortality underscoring its potential as promising therapy for reducing airway inflammation associated conditions exacerbated due to repeated VMs requiring clinical intervention strategies collectively suggesting enhanced safety profiles for mechanically ventilated patients receiving nanoformulated miR-146a treatments compared to traditional therapies.

title: Immunofocusing and enhancing autologous Tier-2 HIV-1 neutralization by displaying Env trimers on two-component protein nanoparticles
abstract: The HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein trimer is poorly immunogenic because it is covered by a dense glycan shield. As a result, recombinant Env glycoproteins generally elicit inadequate antibody levels that neutralize clinically relevant, neutralization-resistant (Tier-2) HIV-1 strains. Multivalent antigen presentation on nanoparticles is an established strategy to increase vaccine-driven immune responses. However, due to nanoparticle instability in vivo, the display of non-native Env structures, and the inaccessibility of many neutralizing antibody (NAb) epitopes, the effects of nanoparticle display are generally modest for Env trimers. Here, we generate two-component self-assembling protein nanoparticles presenting twenty SOSIP trimers of the clade C Tier-2 genotype 16055. We show in a rabbit immunization study that these nanoparticles induce 60-fold higher autologous Tier-2 NAb titers than the corresponding SOSIP trimers. Epitope mapping studies reveal that the presentation of 16055 SOSIP trimers on these nanoparticle focuses antibody responses to an immunodominant apical epitope. Thus, these nanoparticles are a promising platform to improve the immunogenicity of Env trimers with apex-proximate NAb epitopes.

Thus, these nanoparticles are a promising platform to improve the immunogenicity of Env trimers with apex-proximate NAb epitopes.

title: On the challenges associated with the study of police use of deadly force in the United States: A response to Schwartz & Jahn
abstract: In response to Gabriel Schwartz and Jaquelyn Jahn’s descriptive study, “Mapping fatal police violence across U.S. metropolitan areas: Overall rates and racial/ethnic inequalities, 2013–2017,” I provide three reflections. First, the framing of this issue is vitally important. Second, police-involved fatalities represent a nonrandom sample of all incidents involving police use of deadly force (i.e., physical force that causes or is likely to cause death), and unfortunately, we lack comprehensive data on use of deadly force that does not result in fatalities. Finally, to make sense of who is killed by the police, researchers must also identify who was exposed to the risk of being killed by the police.

title: 2HybridTools, a handy software to facilitate clone identification and mutation mapping from yeast two-hybrid screening
abstract: Yeast Two-Hybrid (Y2H) and reverse Two-Hybrid (RY2H) are powerful protein–protein interaction screening methods that rely on the interaction of bait and prey proteins fused to DNA binding (DB) and activation domains (AD), respectively. Y2H allows identification of protein interaction partners using screening libraries, while RY2H is used to determine residues critical to a given protein–protein interaction by exploiting site-directed mutagenesis. Currently, both these techniques still rely on sequencing of positive clones using conventional Sanger sequencing. For Y2H, a screen can yield several positives; the identification of such clones is further complicated by the fact that sequencing products usually contain vector sequence. For RY2H, obtaining a complete sequence is required to identify the full range of residues involved in protein–protein interactions. However, with Sanger sequencing limited to 500–800 nucleotides, sequencing is usually carried from both ends for clones greater than this length. Analysis of such RY2H data thus requires assembly of sequencing products combined with trimming of vector sequences and of low-quality bases at the beginning and ends of sequencing products. Further, RY2H analysis requires collation of mutations that abrogate a DB/AD interaction. Here, we present 2HybridTools, a Java program with a user-friendly interface that allows addressing all these issues inherent to both Y2H and RY2H. Specifically, for Y2H, 2HybridTools enables automated identification of positive clones, while for RY2H, 2HybridTools provides detailed mutation reports as a basis for further investigation of given protein–protein interactions.

title: An Integrated Pharmacophore/Docking/3D-QSAR Approach to Screening a Large Library of Products in Search of Future Botulinum Neurotoxin A Inhibitors
abstract: Botulinum toxins are neurotoxins produced by Clostridium botulinum. This toxin can be lethal for humans as a cause of botulism; however, in small doses, the same toxin is used to treat different conditions. Even if the therapeutic doses are effective and safe, the adverse reactions could be local and could unmask a subclinical impairment of neuromuscular transmissions. There are not many cases of adverse events in the literature; however, it is possible that sometimes they do not occur as they are transient and, if they do occur, there is no possibility of a cure other than to wait for the pharmacological effect to end. Inhibition of botulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) effects is a strategy for treating botulism as it can provide an effective post-exposure remedy. In this paper, 13,592,287 compounds were screened through a pharmacophore filter, a 3D-QSAR model, and a virtual screening; then, the compounds with the best affinity were selected. Molecular dynamics simulation studies on the first four compounds predicted to be the most active were conducted to verify that the poses foreseen by the docking were stable. This approach allowed us to identify compounds with a calculated inhibitory activity in the range of 316–500 nM.

title: Modulation of resistance to Salmonella typhimurium infection in mice by mouse hepatitis virus (MHV)()
abstract: This article presents the findings of a study that evaluated the effects of Mouse Hepatitis Virus (MHV) inoculation on resistance to Salmonella typhimurium infection in mice. MHV is an important mouse pathogen and its ability to modulate host immune response has been well-documented; however, how it affects susceptibility or resistance against foodborne pathogens like Salmonella typhimurium remains poorly understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of prior MHV exposure through either intraperitoneal injection or aerosol route on subsequent robustness against S. typhiurium challenge in BALB/c and C57BL6 mice models for both acquired and innate immunity related outcomes. Results showed that pre-exposure to MHV resulted in differentially attenuated responses when compared with control groups for certain parameters such as typical signs indicative of S. typhimurium infections, body weight gain, folate uptake into serum from diet consumed by animals as well as concentrations of lipopolysaccharides derived from intestinal microbiota which serve as endotoxin induction factor during infection with S. typhirum .  Collectively, these results indicate that application routes used seemed to influence significantly variables measured including two different markers associated with disease outcome upon subsequent Salmonella Typhi muruim challenge suggesting promising roles for intervention strategies targeting immunomodulation via virally encoded elements under consideration in future research efforts towards mitigation undesired enteric foodborne illness events.

title: Hematopoietic Cancer Cell Lines Can Support Replication of Sabin Poliovirus Type 1
abstract: This article examines a novel research study conducted by our team to answer the critical question of whether hematopoietic cancer cell lines can support the replication of Sabin poliovirus type 1. Our experiment involved culturing early generation and later passage (LP) derived cancerous cells in advanced-serum-free media supplemented with substances that can facilitate viral transduction. We also analysed measurements such as viral titers, cytopathic effects as well as in vitro assays to determine cell viability and infection rates. The results showed that both LP1 and LP2 cells supported successful replication of the virus conclusively demonstrating for the first time their role as potential hosts for poliovirus growth. Taken together, this report highlights an important breakthrough in understanding how malignant cellular functions interact with environmental components to potentially drive mutations from which dangerous infectious diseases emerge into pandemic proportions within certain populations worldwide.

title: In vivo protection against ZIKV infection and pathogenesis through passive antibody transfer and active immunisation with a prMEnv DNA vaccine
abstract: This study examines the efficacy of a novel prMEnv DNA vaccine as an active immunisation, alongside passive antibody transfer, to protect against Zika Virus (ZIKV) infection and pathogenesis. While civilian populations risk exposure to ZIKV due to increasing urbanisation in endemic regions, it is especially important for susceptible travellers due to potential neurological involvement from the virus. In order to identify if any protection was achieved and investigate associated immunological properties through the defence of induced immunity, experimental models were used in vivo. Results showed that both strategies improved functionality relative with unvaccinated control animals and offered significant synergistic benefits when administered together in terms of viral inhibition stages at different post-infection intervals. Consequently, this research can provide valuable insight into how regular administration may be employed through vaccination campaigns or clinics offering mosquito bite prevention services..

title: The Relationship Exploration between Public Migration Attention and Population Migration from a Perspective of Search Query
abstract: Rapid population migration has been viewed as a critical factor impacting urban network construction and regional sustainable development. The supervision and analysis of population migration are necessary for guiding the optimal allocation of urban resources and for attaining the high efficiency development of region. Currently, the explorations of population migration are often restricted by the limitation of data. In the information era, search engines widely collect public attention, implying potential individual actions, and freely provide open, timelier, and large-scope search query data for helping explore regional phenomena and problems. In this paper, we endeavor to explore the possibility of adopting such data to depict population migration. Based on the search query from Baidu search engine, three migration attention indexes (MAIs) are constructed to capture public migration attention in cyber space. Taking three major urban agglomerations in China as case study, we conduct the correlation analysis among the cyber MAIs and population migration in geographical space. Results have shown that external-MAI and local-MAI can positively reflect the population migration inner regions and across regions from a holistic lens and that intercity-MAI can be a helpful supplement for the delineation of specific population flow. Along with the accumulation of cyber search query data, its potential in exploring population migration can be further reinforced.

title: Probing the impact of nairovirus genomic diversity on viral ovarian tumor domain protease (vOTU) structure and deubiquitinase activity
abstract: This study explores the consequences of nairovirus genomic diversity on viral ovarian tumor domain protease (vOTU) structure and deubiquitinase activity. Nairoviruses are well-known for their involvement in various ovarian tumors, yet there has been limited research on how unique microbial genetic variants can potentially modulate proteins critical to the transformation process. This paper examines whether distinct nairoviral sequence variation influences vOTU configuration and its ubiquitin deconjugation catalytic efficiency. To assess this functional relationship, artificial genomes bearing mutational signatures associated with specific gene expression levels were generated using a molecular engineering platform. Subsequent infiltration into ovarian cells was conducted to ascertain if alterations occurred in vOTU shape or deubiquitination capability due to infection with diverse varieties of nominal viruses from different habitats spanning multiple continents around the globe. Statistical analyses quantified any potential biological divergence engendered by elemental changes at the genomic level and identified possible links between proteolysis efficacy fluctuation and broader collective biodiversity within the inflammatory environments containing both host and pathogen populations trapped together in a perpetual death spiral of evolutionary selection pressure throughout varying periods of time intervals. The end result should enable researchers to gain further insight into how evolutionary mechanisms form unity out of disorder through differential survival success as species attempt adaptation strategies against hostile elements encountered in external surroundings that could profoundly affect cellular biochemistry topology forevermore

title: Mysterious disease spreads in China
abstract:
The Mysterious Disease Outbreak in China: Implications and Strategies for Containing Transmission. 
An unprecedented epidemic of unknown origin has recently engulfed the Chinese province of Wuhan, spreading to as many as sixteen cities with confirmed cases now reported across six provinces and two municipalities. Despite urgent quarantine measures taken by the Chinese government, understanding the virus causing this outbreak is still unclear. In lieu of this uncertainty, we seek to examine associated factors promoting transmission through a comprehensive review comparing population data from infected areas and potential impact on healthcare infrastructure resulting from such an infectious disease pandemic. We discuss plausible strategies toward controlling further spread, aiming to ensure sustainable containment for individuals and communities at risk throughout mainland China.

title: A case of primary disseminated rhinosporidiosis and dapsone-induced autoimmune hemolytic anemia: A therapeutic misadventure
abstract: Rhinosporidiosis, a chronic inflammatory disease, which is caused by the aquatic microorganism Rhinosporidium seeberi, is endemic in India and in many other regions of the tropics. It primarily infects mucocutaneous surfaces of nose, nasopharynx, and conjunctiva through transepithelial invasion. However, over the centuries, atypical involvement of other body parts, especially viscera, bone, subcutaneous layers, genitals, the tracheobronchial tree, and even the skull has been, though rarely, reported. This chronic granulomatous infection is notorious for its propensity for recurrence following autoinoculation and poor response to most of the anti-microbials except dapsone. Surgical excision followed by cauterization remains the treatment of choice when an operation is feasible. We herein report a case of an immunocompetent person with primary disseminated dermato-pulmonary rhinosporidiosis, which created significant diagnostic dilemma at the beginning, got complicated due to dapsone-induced direct anti-globulin test-positive autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and finally responded to prolonged multidrug therapy with liposomal amphotericin B, ketoconazole and cycloserine. This report establishes the importance of tissue diagnosis in rhinosporidiosis and even, in resource-poor set-ups, a simple histopathological diagnosis can promote an early and affordable accurate diagnosis, and subsequently, a proper therapeutic intervention.

title: Necrotizing Enterocolitis and Infection
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the association between necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and infection. Studies published within the past twenty years are appraised for their role in elucidating this complex relationship, exploring potential risk factors, underlying etiological agents and preventive treatments. Together, these findings provide important information with regard to NEC diagnosis measures and clinical management protocols to improve patient outcomes.

title: Strand-Specific Quantitative Reverse Transcription-Polymerase Chain Reaction Assay for Measurement of Arenavirus Genomic and Antigenomic RNAs
abstract: Arenaviruses are an important family of viruses that infect a wide range of rodents and cause diseases in both humans and animals. Recent studies have shown that strand-specific reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay can be used to detect the presence of arenavirus specific RNA molecules from infected cells. The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a strand-specific quantitative RT-PCR (qRT-PCR) assay for accurate quantification of arenavirus genomic and antigenomic RNAs. Primers were designed to target conserved regions on the 3’ UTRs region of all known Old World Arenavirus (OWA), New World Arenavirus (NWA) species, based on their sequence heterogeneity analysis. This qRT-PCR method was then tested with different concentrations of OWA, NWA virus cell lysates using standard curves created with reference RNAs synthesized in vitro; results showed a linear correlation between Ct values obtained by normal qRT PCR method and the developed strand specific Q RT PCR assay. The detection limit determined by the assay could accurately measure low abundance transcript levels as low 0.12 copies/μl. title: A comparison of facemask and respirator filtration test methods
abstract: The increasing demand for the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) has made the quality of filtration materials an important factor to consider. This study compared two common test methods used to assess filter efficiency in facemasks and respirators, namely particle penetration and gas-phase tests. The goal was to determine which method produced more accurate results by studying both particulate concentration limit (PCL) testing, as well as N95 tests for small particles such as viruses or bacteria. Results indicate that the PCL procedure provides a general measure of total aerosol penetration whereas N95 reports aerosol leakage at different size ranges. Ultimately, it can be concluded that gas-based testing is used best when filtering capacity of a specific material is required while PCL offers utmost accuracy when evaluating overall airflow structure—an important matter when deciding on suitable PPE products for personal or workplace safety needs. title: Immunogenicity of the inactivated influenza vaccine in children who have undergone allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant
abstract: Influenza vaccination is recommended for children following allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT), however there is limited evidence regarding its benefit. A prospective multicentre study was conducted to evaluate the immunogenicity of the inactivated influenza vaccine in children who have undergone HSCT compared with healthy age-matched controls. Participants were vaccinated between 2013 and 2016 according to Australian guidelines. Influenza-specific hemagglutinin inhibition antibody titres were performed prior to each vaccination and 4 weeks following the final vaccination. title: Assessment of transport stress on cattle travelling a long distance (≈648 km), from Jessore (Indian border) to Chittagong, Bangladesh
abstract: The effect of long-distance transport on cattle health has not frequently been studied in Bangladesh. The current study investigated the health conditions, and the extent and pattern of cattle injuries, along with haemato-biochemical and hormonal changes, before and after long-distance transportation (≈648 km) from the market of origin to the market of destination. A total of 100 adult cattle were selected at the Benapole live cattle market, Bangladesh, for physical examination before and after transportation. Fifty of these cattle were randomly selected for additional haemato-biochemical evaluation just before the start of transportation (0 hour), immediately after arrival at the destination market (13.8±0.9 hours after the start of transportation) and 24 hours after arrival at the destination market. The external health conditions and injuries were assessed. Animals were fasting in the vehicle during transportation and provided only with paddy straw and water before sale at the destination market. Before and after transportation, the overall frequency of cattle injuries varied significantly (26 per cent before v 47 per cent after transportation; P<0.001). Cattle health conditions diverged significantly (such as nasal discharge: 15 per cent v 28 per cent; P=0.03). The values of haemoglobin (P=0.01), total erythrocyte count (P=0.001), total leucocyte count (P<0.001), lymphocyte (P=0.005), neutrophil (P=0.01) and eosinophil (P=0.01) varied significantly. The values of serum total protein (P=0.006), creatine kinase (P<0.001), triglyceride (P=0.04), calcium (P=0.003), phosphorus (P<0.001) and alkaline phosphatase (P=0.04) significantly differed. The overall findings indicate a high degree of transport stress and poor animal welfare.

title: Evaluation of Coseasonality of Influenza and Invasive Pneumococcal Disease: Results from Prospective Surveillance
abstract: The study of the temporal relationship between influenza and other infectious diseases has been an ongoing discussion in recent years. The research conducted by this paper, ‘Evaluation of Coseasonality of Influenza and Invasive Pneumococcal Disease: Results from Prospective Surveillance’ offers a comprehensive investigation into the link between seasonal trends in influenza incidence and concurrent invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD). Using prospective surveillance data collected over three flu seasons in Shanghai, China, this study evaluated any spatio-temporal association of these infections through space-time scan statistics results to demonstrate evidence for coseasonality between them. Results were compared against two different control datasets across multiple age groups to further investigate their interdependence. This paper can provide insight into effective vaccine strategies if a coseasonal relationship is rationalized as well as informing clinical diagnosis especially in areas with high prevalence rates. Ultimately, our findings offer support that may help clinicians better predict co-occurring epidemics and therefore improve infection prevention activities throughout the year.

title: The role of vegetative cell fusions in the development and asexual reproduction of the wheat fungal pathogen Zymoseptoria tritici
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ability of fungal cells to undergo cell-to-cell communication and anastomosis, the process of vegetative hyphal fusion, allows them to maximize their overall fitness. Previous studies in a number of fungal species have identified the requirement of several signaling pathways for anastomosis, including the so far best characterized soft (So) gene, and the MAPK pathway components MAK-1 and MAK-2 of Neurospora crassa. Despite the observations of hyphal fusions’ involvement in pathogenicity and host adhesion, the connection between cell fusion and fungal lifestyles is still unclear. Here, we address the role of anastomosis in fungal development and asexual reproduction in Zymoseptoria tritici, the most important fungal pathogen of wheat in Europe. RESULTS: We show that Z. tritici undergoes self-fusion between distinct cellular structures, and its mechanism is dependent on the initial cell density. Contrary to other fungi, cell fusion in Z. tritici only resulted in cytoplasmic mixing but not in multinucleated cell formation. The deletion of the So orthologous ZtSof1 disrupted cell-to-cell communication affecting both hyphal and germling fusion. We show that Z. tritici mutants for MAPK-encoding ZtSlt2 (orthologous to MAK-1) and ZtFus3 (orthologous to MAK-2) genes also failed to undergo anastomosis, demonstrating the functional conservation of this signaling mechanism across species. Additionally, the ΔZtSof1 mutant was severely impaired in melanization, suggesting that the So gene function is related to melanization. Finally, we demonstrated that anastomosis is dispensable for pathogenicity, but essential for the pycnidium development, and its absence abolishes the asexual reproduction of Z. tritici. CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrate the role for ZtSof1, ZtSlt2, and ZtFus3 in cell fusions of Z. tritici. Cell fusions are essential for different aspects of the Z. tritici biology, and the ZtSof1 gene is a potential target to control septoria tritici blotch (STB) disease.

title: Blood SIRT1 Shows a Coherent Association with Leptin and Adiponectin in Relation to the Degree and Distribution of Adiposity: A Study in Obesity, Normal Weight and Anorexia Nervosa
abstract: Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) is a sensor of cell energy availability, and with leptin and adiponectin, it regulates metabolic homeostasis. Widely studied in tissues, SIRT1 is under evaluation as a plasmatic marker. We aimed at assessing whether circulating SIRT1 behaves consistently with leptin and adiponectin in conditions of deficiency, excess or normal fat content. Eighty subjects were evaluated: 27 with anorexia nervosa (AN), 26 normal-weight and 27 with obesity. Bloodstream SIRT1, leptin and adiponectin (ELISA), total and trunk fat mass (FM) %, abdominal visceral adipose tissue, liver steatosis and epicardial fat thickness (EFT) were assessed. For each fat store, the coefficient of determination (R(2)) was used to evaluate the prediction capability of SIRT1, leptin and adiponectin. Plasma SIRT1 and adiponectin coherently decreased with the increase of FM, while the opposite occurred with leptin. Mean levels of each analyte were different between groups (p < 0.005). A significant association between plasma variables and FM depots was observed. SIRT1 showed a good predictive strength for FM, particularly in the obesity group, where the best R(2) was recorded for EFT (R(2) = 0.7). Blood SIRT1, adiponectin and leptin behave coherently with FM and there is synchrony between them. The association of SIRT1 with FM is substantially superimposable to that of adiponectin and leptin. Given its homeostatic roles, SIRT1 may deserve to be considered as a plasma clinical/biochemical parameter of adiposity and metabolic health.

title: Association Between Angiopoietin-2 and Enterovirus 71 Induced Pulmonary Edema
abstract: This paper provides an evidence-based understanding of the association between Angiopoietin-2 (ANGPT2) and Enterovirus 71 (EV71) induced pulmonary edema. Both ANGPT2 and EV71 are viruses that have been incriminated in various respiratory disorders, but also possess potentially beneficial effects when judiciously managed. This article extensively reviews existing studies in humans, animal models, and clinical experiments to determine if there is a connection between these two pathogens that could lead to pulmonary edema. The results implicate factors such as extracellular alkalinization, infection dose, viral load and migration patterns which suggest how excess production of ANGJP2 or overloading of virus particles can contribute towards increased fluid pressure within the alveolar walls causing pulmonary edema. Furthermore, detailed evaluations were conducted on immunopathogenesis manifestations since both viruses induce their own specific consequences on mediator strength as well as features related to cell death/inflammation resulting from immune responses against them separately or in combination with each other's presence. The discussions provide further insight into these aspects while providing a platform for future prospective studies to understand more precisely mechanisms behind dual infections by both viruses that leads up to the pathological progression of influenza complications culminating into pulmonology overloads due to severe cases of overlapping Pulmonary Edema associated with ANGPT2 & EV71 patterns together at higher rates than previously observed levels alone either one pathogen alone based upon current literature available now .

title: Additional evidence on the efficacy of different Akirin vaccines assessed on Anopheles arabiensis (Diptera: Culicidae)
abstract: This study investigated the efficacy of different Akirin vaccines in reducing populations of Anopheles arabiensis, a vector that transmits malaria. In order to accomplish this, a series of trials were conducted across multiple regions which varied in terms of their climactic conditions and abundance of parasites capable of causing the disease. The results showed that one particular vaccine was significantly more effective than other forms when compared with both naturally infected and simulated infection control groups during periods ranging from 3-7 months. Additionally, changes in mortality rates over time showed no significant differences between treatment results at various maturity stages of A.arabiensis life cycle. Moreover, analysis indicated vaccinated groups had lower levels immunity against natural infestations which implies improved protection against malaria spread by this species even after exposure to possible future outbreaks. Thus it can be concluded that vaccination with the tested Akirin vaccine induces efficient reduction on A.arabiensis population size as well as increases its susceptibility towards parasite infections inducing deference among treated populations and control ones disinfected against infectious vectors or exposed simultaneously to them for longer periods or subsequently after several generations

title: Family veto in organ donation: the experiences of Organ and Tissue Donation Coordinators in Ontario
abstract: This article explores the experiences of Organ and Tissue Donation Coordinators in Ontario as they navigate family vetoes during organ donation. Through a qualitative research design, this study examines how coordinators work with families towards successful donations or to preserve patient autonomy when appeals for an override are not possible. The results shed light on gaps in the current legal framework that prevent effective rights balancing between preserving patient authorization and respecting familial wishes. The findings demonstrate ways to improve efforts to maximize the impact of organ donation while mitigating potential risks caused by family vetoing decisions. By focusing on understanding decision-making processes, this paper provides valuable insight into best practices to optimize coordination processes and ultimately increase rates of successful donations in Canada.

title: Reporting errors in infectious disease outbreaks, with an application to Pandemic Influenza A/H1N1
abstract: This paper presents a systematic review of the errors that occur in reporting infectious disease outbreaks and highlights their presence with an example case study on Pandemic Influenza A/H1N1. We investigate the various sources and impacts of errors associated with this important topic, in order to identify weak points in current surveillance systems and suggest measures for improvement. Our findings suggest that discrepancies exist between reported cases versus true rates, due to factors such as inconsistencies among variable definitions, measurement biases resulting from flawed assumptions about population composition, selective sample sizes leading to biased trends estimation and incomplete risk factor data on which forecasting models are based. This paper provides insight into how distinct stakeholders use or interpret information differently over time - as it applies to Pandemic Influenza A/H1N1 - emphasizing both potential pitfalls and positive outcomes stemming from accurate reporting of disease events.

title: Type III Interferon-Mediated Signaling Is Critical for Controlling Live Attenuated Yellow Fever Virus Infection In Vivo
abstract: This paper examines how Type III Interferon-Mediated Signaling (IFNλ-signaling) contributes to immune control of in vivo Live Attenuated Yellow Fever Virus (YFV) infection. IFNλ signaling plays a protection role in chronic viral infection and enhancing antiviral defense pathways, but its significance in controlling acute infections such as YFV is unclear. To investigate this phenomenon further, mice were infected with wild type or mutant versions of YFV that lack the activation of IFNλ signaling pathways and its potential effects on controlling virus spread were studied by measuring survival rates and viremia titers. Our results demonstrate an essential contribution from IFNλ signaling for host resistance against challenge with live attenuated virus; deficiency groups exhibited significantly lower overall survival rate than normal controls supporting our hypothesis showing that timely yfv clearance depends not just the presence of adaptive immunity but also on intrinsic mechanisms mediated through Interferon-Lambda signal pathway. These findings have important implications for understanding how appropriately activated innate responses, cause better resolution against various forms of viral infections

title: Models for Heart Failure Admissions and Admission Rates, 2016 through 2018
abstract: This paper presents research on Models for Heart Failure Admissions and Admission Rates from 2016 to 2018. Through rigorous analysis, we seek to identify key factors associated with hospital admission rates in identifying different patterns between hospitals. By applying our findings of logistic regression models based on predictors such as patient demographic information, gender, primary diagnosis of heart failure, age at the time of diagnosis, physicians-specific visits and hospitalized days etc., we will be able to determine whether these factors differentiate hospital admission rates among various healthcare providers. Additionally, we aim to use our results in analyzing regional variations across hospitals during this period and thereby offer valuable insights into measures that may help reduce future admissions due to heart failure. Ultimately this research can assist healthcare providers by improving their overall performance towards improved prevention practices related to cardiac health within the community.

title: Toward minimal bacterial cells: evolution vs. design
abstract: Recent technical and conceptual advances in the biological sciences opened the possibility of the construction of newly designed cells. In this paper we review the state of the art of cell engineering in the context of genome research, paying particular attention to what we can learn on naturally reduced genomes from either symbiotic or free living bacteria. Different minimal hypothetically viable cells can be defined on the basis of several computational and experimental approaches. Projects aiming at simplifying living cells converge with efforts to make synthetic genomes for minimal cells. The panorama of this particular view of synthetic biology lead us to consider the use of defined minimal cells to be applied in biomedical, bioremediation, or bioenergy application by taking advantage of existing naturally minimized cells.

title: Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality among Patients with Pulmonary Tuberculosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: This meta-analysis aims to identify relevant predictors of in-hospital mortality among patients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB). A systematic search was carried out through multiple databases and bibliographical references. The included studies assessing in-hospital mortality due to PTB had a cohort design, with at least five participants per study. Eligibility criteria also required studies to have primary data regarding predictors related to outcomes. Through the pooling of data from forty-six observational studies involving 71,081 individuals, this review will establish which variables play an independent role in uncovering potentially fatal complications associated with TB infection. By determining whether key process markers present during hospital care could be useful instruments for managing patient prognosis, it should contribute significantly towards improving patient outcome by strengthening clinical decision making processes and health policies.

title: Preliminary investigation demonstrating the GHITM gene probably involved in apoptosis and growth of the golden apple snail (Pomacea canaliculata)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary investigation into the possible involvement of GHITM (Glycyl-Histidyl-Isoluecine Trypsin inhibitor) in apoptosis and growth of the golden apple snail (Pomacea canaliculata). It has been recently proposed that interferences with Glyma proteins expression, such as those related to glycosylated proteins and enzymes in the digestive system are genetically regulated. As a result of this proposal, it was hypothesized that genetic elements affecting levels of these molecules would modify growth trajectories and developing processes throughout ontogeny. The effects observed were further explored through an experiment involving tracking changes at transcriptional level in selected genes across multiple Pomacea Canaliculata individuals throughout their entire life cycle. Results indicated possible significant control by GHITM gene over patterns associated to apoptotic activities and general growth in golden apple snails.

title: Epiglottitis, Acute Laryngitis, and Croup
abstract: Epiglottitis, acute laryngitis, and croup (acute laryngotracheobronchitis) are infections of the upper airway, affecting the epiglottis, larynx, and larynx and trachea, respectively. Epiglottitis is a bacterial infection, while viruses cause nearly all cases of acute laryngitis and croup. Acute laryngitis in adults is usually self-limited. Epiglottitis, which used to be prevalent in children under age 5, is now seen more often in adults than in children. This decline in childhood epiglottitis is due to the Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine. Streptococci, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, are now important causes of epiglottitis. Croup is a viral infection, usually due to parainfluenza virus, that primarily affects children ages 6 months to 3 years old. Epiglottitis and croup can cause life-threatening loss of the airway, and misdiagnosis or mismanagement can result in fatalities. This chapter reviews the clinical features and treatment of these three upper respiratory tract infections.

This decline in childhood epiglottitis is due to the Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine. Streptococci, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, are now important causes of epiglottitis. Croup is a viral infection, usually due to parainfluenza virus, that primarily affects children ages 6 months to 3 years old. Epiglottitis and croup can cause life-threatening loss of the airway, and misdiagnosis or mismanagement can result in fatalities. This chapter reviews the clinical features and treatment of these three upper respiratory tract infections.

title: Development and evaluation of an interactive web-based decision-making programme on relapse management for people with multiple sclerosis (POWER@MS2)—study protocol for a randomised controlled trial
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory, degenerative disease of the central nervous system manifesting at first with relapses in about 85% of cases. In Germany, intravenous therapy with high-dose corticosteroids is the treatment standard of acute relapses. The treatment leads to a faster reduction of symptoms in about 25 of 100 treated patients but has no proven long-term benefits over placebo treatment. Intravenous treatment is not superior to oral treatment. Therefore, informed decisions on relapse management are required. An earlier randomised controlled trial showed that evidence-based patient information and education on relapse management leads to more informed decisions and more relapses not treated or treated with oral corticosteroids. This study aims to evaluate whether a web-based relapse management programme will positively change relapse management and strengthen autonomy in people with multiple sclerosis. METHODS: The pragmatic double-blind randomised controlled trial is accompanied by a mixed-methods process evaluation and a health economic evaluation and follows the UK Medical Research Council guidance on developing and evaluating complex interventions. A total of 188 people with possible or relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with ≥ 1 relapse within the last year and/or ≥ 2 relapses within the last 2 years will be recruited and randomised using blocks. The intervention group receives a web- and dialogue-based decision aid on relapse management, a nurse-led webinar and access to a monitored chat forum. The control group receives standard information, which will be made available via the same online platform as the intervention. The primary endpoint is the proportion of relapses not treated or treated with oral corticosteroids. Key secondary endpoints are the annualised relapse rate, decision-making, empowerment, quality of life and cost-effectiveness. Facilitators and barriers will be assessed by mixed-methods process evaluation measures. The study ends when 81 relapses have been documented or after 24 months of observation per individual patient. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. DISCUSSION: We hypothesise that the intervention will enhance patient empowerment and have a positive impact on patients’ relapse management. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.govNCT04233970. Registered on 18 January 2020

title: Immunization Coverage in Migrant School Children Along the Thailand-Myanmar Border
abstract: The objective of this project was to document and increase vaccine coverage in migrant school children on the Thailand-Myanmar border. Migrant school children (n = 12,277) were enrolled in a school-based immunization program in four Thai border districts. The children were evaluated for vaccination completion and timing, for six different vaccines: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG); Oral Polio vaccine (OPV); Hepatitis B vaccine (HepB); Diphtheria, Pertussis and Tetanus vaccine (DTP); Measles Containing Vaccine or Measles, Mumps and Rubella vaccine (MMR); Tetanus and Diphtheria containing vaccine (Td). Vaccine coverage proportions for BCG, OPV3, DTP3, HepB3 and measles containing vaccine were 92.3, 85.3, 63.8, 72.2, and 90.9 % respectively. Most children were able to receive vaccines in a time appropriate manner. School-based immunization programs offer a suitable vaccine delivery mechanism for hard-to-reach populations. However, these data suggest overall low vaccine coverage in migrant populations. Further efforts toward improving appropriate vaccine coverage and methods of retaining documentation of vaccination in mobile migrant populations are necessary for improved health.

title: An overview of management of intracranial hypertension in the intensive care unit
abstract: The management of intracranial hypertension is an important issue within the healthcare sector today. Intracranial hypertension (ICH) can result in a range of complications, including vision loss and stroke, among others which further complicate a patient’s overall care plan. As such, effective treatments must be implemented correctly to manage certain components of ICH that present in the intensive care unit (ICU). This article presents an overview of management strategies for ICH prior to ICU admission, along with strategies found to be most successful once a patient enters into the ICU setting. The discussion also continues on to include discussions on current trends related to treatment protocols involved in managing intractable ICH cases along with methods necessary for efficient communication between interdisciplinary members essential for deciding appropriate interventions from admission up until discharge from ICU care utilization. We conclude this article by providing some closing remarks regarding potential steps forward when focusing on high-risk patients displaying signs consistent with intracranial hypertension in order for health specialists responsible for their ongoing treatment and clinical outcomes are equipped with the best resources possible.

title: Global health diplomacy for obesity prevention: Lessons from tobacco control
abstract: This study examines global health diplomacy for obesity prevention based on lessons learned from the tobacco control movement. It combines international relations principles and experiences from a range of policy makers, nongovernment organizations and public health experts to assess how global influences can be used to positively shape countries in terms of their policies concerning obesity. It also considers important ethical considerations such as balancing public accountability with government interests and understanding the impact of trans-boundary influencers. The aim is to provide an intimate evaluation of effective negotiating strategies that may assist governments in tackling one of the most pressing issues facing today's world: excess weight gain and related disease burden.

title: Effect of water deficit on biomass production and accumulation of secondary metabolites in roots of Glycyrrhiza uralensis
abstract: This paper examines the effect of water stress on biomass production and accumulation of secondary metabolites in Glycyrrhiza uralensis roots. We hypothesize that water stress could affect the growth and development process as well as increase production and accumulation of secondary metabolites in G. uralensis roots, showing its adaptive advantage to drought-like conditions. The experiment was conducted under sand culture or field condition by irrigating with half or full amount of irrigation amounts. Results showed a significant reduction in biomass production when exposed to water deficit, while increases up to 2 fold is observed for flavonoids, saponins and phenolics compared with control plants receiving regular irrigations. This study will provide insights into better utilization of wild species such as G. uralensis under difficult environmental conditions like arid climates with the aim improving productivity through sustainable utilization practices.

title: Differential Effects of IL-12 on Tregs and Non-Treg T Cells: Roles of IFN-γ, IL-2 and IL-2R
abstract: This study seeks to investigate the differential effects of interleukin-12 (IL-12) on regulatory T cells (Tregs) and non-Treg T cells, focusing particularly on the roles of interferon gamma (IFNγ), interleukin 2 (IL-2), and IL-2R. Emerging evidence suggests that these three molecules are key mediators in controlling immune responses through their actions on CD4+ effector T cell subsets; however, it remains unknown how these cytokines regulate inflammatory responses for different types of activated T cells, such as regulatory versus non‑Tregs. Utilizing in vitro cultures and mouse models with impaired IFNγ, IL‑2 and/or IL‑2 receptors provides insight into this important yet understudied area related to immunoregulation. The results gathered from our investigations can ultimately contribute towards a greater understand between biological processes on a mechanistic level while informing therapeutic considerations aiming at modulating particular aspects of inflammation or chemokine production through inhibition, enhancement or neutralization strategies.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus whole-genome sequencing identifies convergent evolution of sequence duplication in the C-terminus of the G gene
abstract: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is responsible for considerable morbidity and mortality worldwide and is the most important respiratory viral pathogen in infants. Extensive sequence variability within and between RSV group A and B viruses and the ability of multiple clades and sub-clades of RSV to co-circulate are likely mechanisms contributing to the evasion of herd immunity. Surveillance and large-scale whole-genome sequencing of RSV is currently limited but would help identify its evolutionary dynamics and sites of selective immune evasion. In this study, we performed complete-genome next-generation sequencing of 92 RSV isolates from infants in central Tennessee during the 2012–2014 RSV seasons. We identified multiple co-circulating clades of RSV from both the A and B groups. Each clade is defined by signature N- and O-linked glycosylation patterns. Analyses of specific RSV genes revealed high rates of positive selection in the attachment (G) gene. We identified RSV-A viruses in circulation with and without a recently reported 72-nucleotide G gene sequence duplication. Furthermore, we show evidence of convergent evolution of G gene sequence duplication and fixation over time, which suggests a potential fitness advantage of RSV with the G sequence duplication.

title: Design, synthesis, heme binding and density functional theory studies of isoindoline-dione-4-aminoquinolines as potential antiplasmodials
abstract: AIM: WHO Malaria report 2017 estimated 216 million cases of malaria and 445,000 deaths worldwide, with 91% of deaths affecting the African region. RESULTS/METHODOLOGY: Microwave promoted the synthesis of cycloalkyl amine substituted isoindoline-1,3-dione-4-aminoquinolines was urbanized for evaluating their antiplasmodial activities. Compound with the optimum combination of propyl chain length and hydroxyethyl piperazine proved to be the most potent among the synthesized scaffolds against chloroquine-resistant W2 strain of Plasmodium falciparum with an IC(50) value of 0.006 μM. Heme-binding along with density functional theory studies were further carried out in order to delineate the mechanism of action of the most active compound. CONCLUSION: The synthesized scaffold can act as a therapeutic template for further synthetic modifications toward the search for a new antimalarial agent.

title: Immunogenetic Mechanisms Driving Norovirus GII.4 Antigenic Variation
abstract: The emergence of norovirus GII.4 as one of the predominant causative agents of gastroenteritis has compelled researchers to gain insights into its immunogenetic mechanisms. This article presents a comprehensive overview and evaluation of current research outlining how antigenic variation contributes to the viral evolution and spread globally. Through employing advanced molecular immunological techniques, it is proposed that norovirus GII.4 utilises a combination of genetic rearrangement and mutability strategies, allowing antigenic diversity which results in recurrent pandemics despite herd immunity among human populations. Further analysis explores potential implications for treatment approaches, highlighting promising new avenues such as antibody-based interventions to target multiple mutations while taking into account varying local outbreaks. The need for constant vigilance amongst healthcare practitioners is also addressed, by discussing ways in which monitoring of both regional patterns and antigenic characterization can lead to improved identification practices when managing associated clinical cases tied with this virus type

title: Evasion of autophagy mediated by Rickettsia surface protein OmpB is critical for virulence
abstract: Rickettsia are obligate intracellular bacteria that evade antimicrobial autophagy in the host cell cytosol by unknown mechanisms. Other cytosolic pathogens block different steps of autophagy targeting, including the initial step of polyubiquitin coat formation. One mechanism of evasion is to mobilize actin to the bacterial surface. Here, we show that actin mobilization is insufficient to block autophagy recognition of the pathogen Rickettsia parkeri. Instead, R. parkeri employs outer membrane protein B (OmpB) to block ubiquitylation of bacterial surface proteins, including OmpA, and subsequent recognition by autophagy receptors. OmpB is also required for the formation of a capsule-like layer. Although OmpB is dispensable for bacterial growth in endothelial cells, it is essential for R. parkeri to block autophagy in macrophages and to colonize mice because of its ability to promote autophagy evasion in immune cells. Our results indicate that OmpB acts as a protective shield to obstruct autophagy recognition, revealing a distinctive bacterial mechanism to evade antimicrobial autophagy.

title: Systems Analysis of a RIG-I Agonist Inducing Broad Spectrum Inhibition of Virus Infectivity
abstract: This paper presents a systems analysis of the effects of RIG-I agonism on broad spectrum virus infectivity. The utilization of a novel experimental system for high throughput amplification and quantification by real time PCR (RT-PCR) allows identification and assessment of potential therapeutic agents at an unprecedented level of resolution. A comprehensive cell culture dataset is employed to determine success metrics such as viral inhibition, host response transcriptional profiles, cellular health scores, cytokine levels and more. It is shown that treating cells with C14D6GARIG1 agonist triggers a robust antiviral response across multiple families of RNA viruses in a dose dependent fashion while maintaining healthy host cell growth kinetics in infected cultures under potentially lethal conditions due to viral infection. Our results indicate that inducer compounds like C14D6GARIG1 may have major implications for controlling future outbreaks through functioning as broad spectrum inhibitors capable targeting several types of enveloped RNA viruses at once.

title: Smoking Cessation Using Wearable Sensors: Protocol for a Microrandomized Trial
abstract: This paper describes the protocol for a microrandomized trial, investigating the efficacy of Wearable Sensors in assisting individuals to quit smoking. As a growing cause of preventable morbidity and mortality, smoking cessation is an area of critical importance for public health. Studies have found that incorporating digital technology into smoking cessation programs may be effective at helping people kick nicotine addiction; however, the optimal intervention strategies are yet to be determined. Here we propose utilizing sensor-based technology alongside standard counseling methods to explore not only if quitting is possible but also how it occurs over time. The goal is to outline a methodical process aimed at encouraging persistent use as well as long-term compliance with intended goals supporting an improved quality of life and overall reduction in smoker numbers around the world.

title: MDMA-facilitated cognitive-behavioural conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder: an uncontrolled trial
abstract: Cognitive-behavioural conjoint therapy (CBCT) for PTSD has been shown to improve PTSD, relationship adjustment, and the health and well-being of partners. MDMA (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine) has been used to facilitate an individual therapy for PTSD. This study was an initial test of the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of MDMA-facilitated CBCT. Six couples with varying levels of baseline relationship satisfaction in which one partner was diagnosed with PTSD participated in a condensed version of the 15-session CBCT protocol delivered over 7 weeks. There were two sessions in which both members of the couple were administered MDMA. All couples completed the treatment protocol, and there were no serious adverse events in either partner. There were significant improvements in clinician-assessed, patient-rated, and partner-rated PTSD symptoms (pre- to post-treatment/follow-up effect sizes ranged from d = 1.85–3.59), as well as patient depression, sleep, emotion regulation, and trauma-related beliefs. In addition, there were significant improvements in patient and partner-rated relationship adjustment and happiness (d =.64–2.79). These results are contextualized in relation to prior results from individual MDMA-facilitated psychotherapy and CBCT for PTSD alone. MDMA holds promise as a facilitator of CBCT to achieve more robust and broad effects on individual and relational functioning in those with PTSD and their partners.

title: Prediction of RNA Pseudoknots Using Heuristic Modeling with Mapping and Sequential Folding
abstract: This article seeks to present a new heuristic model for the prediction of RNA pseudoknots through the use of mapping and sequential folding. Pseudoknotting is a common phenomenon in RNAs which can lead to important impacts on the course of expression and helps modulate regulatory pathways. The current state-of-the-art methods demonstrate strengths but also shortfalls, such as false positives and ambiguous results; these issues will be explored with a focus on developing an effective methodology that allows for stable pseudo predictions. Several sequence algorithms will be deployed within this study, including secondary structure prediction as these are vital components when attempting accurate high coverage mapping between sequences in understanding complex structures. This research offers insights into how far we have gone towards unraveling mechanisms behind RNA function regulation thanks to advancements in precision computing techniques, applications with neural networks systems, 3D modelling proposals and genomic editing tools capabilities evolution over time.

title: DGENERATIVE CHANGES IN NEUTROPHILS-AN INDICATOR OF BACTERIAL INFECTION
abstract: This study aims to elucidate the relationship between neutrophils, a major component of innate immunity, and bacterial infection. Exploring early stages could provide insight into how neutrophil-mediated defense is affected by these microbial pathogens. title: Gene therapy for cystic fibrosis: an example for lung gene therapy
abstract: Gene therapy is currently being evaluated for a wide range of acute and chronic lung diseases. The requirement of gene transfer into the individual cell types of the complex lung structure will very much depend on the target disease. Over the last decade, the gene therapy community has recognized that there is not even one vector that is good for all applications, but that the gene transfer agent has to be carefully chosen. Gene therapy is particularly attractive for diseases that currently do not have satisfactory treatment options and probably easier for monogenic disorders than for complex diseases. Cystic fibrosis (CF) fulfills these criteria and is therefore a good candidate for gene therapy-based treatment. This review will focus on CF as an example for lung gene therapy and discuss the progress made in this field over the last couple of years.

title: Effect of overground locomotor training on ventilatory kinetics and rate of perceived exertion in persons with cervical motor-incomplete spinal cord injury
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Pre-post, pilot study. OBJECTIVES: To characterize ventilatory (V(E)) responses to exercise following warm-up walking in individuals with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury (iSCI) during constant work rate (CWR) exercise. Secondarily, to investigate V(E) and tidal volume (V(T)) variability, and ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) before and after overground locomotor training (OLT). SETTING: Research laboratory. METHODS: A 6-min CWR walking bout at preferred pace was used as a warm-up followed by 6 min of rest and a second 6-min CWR bout at above preferred walking pace. The second CWR bout was analyzed. Breath-by-breath ventilatory data were examined using a curvilinear least squares fitting procedure with a mono-exponential model. V(E) and V(T) variability was calculated as the difference between the observed and predicted values and RPE was taken every 2 min. RESULTS: Participants (n = 3, C4–C5) achieved a hyperpneic response to exercise in V(E) and V(T). OLT resulted in faster ventilatory kinetics and reductions of 24 and 29% for V(E) and V(T) variability, respectively. A 30% reduction in RPE was concurrent with the reductions in ventilatory variability. CONCLUSIONS: OLT may improve ventilatory control during CWR in patients with cervical motor-iSCI. These data suggest that in some participants with iSCI, ventilation may influence RPE during walking. Future research should investigate mechanisms of ventilatory variability and its implications in walking performance in patients with iSCI.

title: Kynurenic acid, an IDO metabolite, controls TSG-6-mediated immunosuppression of human mesenchymal stem cells
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been demonstrated to be anti-inflammatory against various immune disorders through several factors, including indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) and TNF-stimulated gene 6 (TSG-6). However, little is known about the necessity for both of these key immunosuppressive factors. Here we employed the mouse lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute lung injury (ALI) model, and found that IDO is necessary to achieve the effect of human umbilical cord-derived MSC (hUC-MSC)-based treatment on ALI. Notably, when IDO was deleted or inhibited, the expression of TSG-6 was decreased. This specific IDO-mediated regulation of TSG-6 expression was found to be exerted through its metabolite, kynurenic acid (KYNA), as inhibition of KYNA production led to decreased TSG-6 expression. Importantly, KYNA pretreatment of human MSCs enhanced their therapeutic effect on ALI. Mechanistically, KYNA activates aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), which directly binds to the TSG-6 promoter to enhance TSG-6 expression. Therefore, our study has uncovered a novel link between IDO and TSG-6, and demonstrates that a metabolite of IDO controls the TSG-6-mediated anti-inflammatory therapeutic effects of human MSCs.

title: Role of Macrophages and RhoA Pathway in Atherosclerosis
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the contributions of macrophages and the RhoA pathway in atherosclerosis progression. Atherogenesis is a complex process, accompanied by endothelial dysfunction and accelerated vessel wall inflammation. Despite extensive research, details about how macrophage-mediated inflammatory pathways interact with RhoA pathway activities in atherosclerosis remain largely unknown. Hence, this paper seeks to explore these connections by performing comparative analyses on mouse models with different genotypes at risk for developing early lesions of vascular inflammation. Our results may help guide clinical interventions or treatments that have the potential to counter or reduce hyperresponsiveness of vascular cells associated with this disease.

title: Hospital Triage System for Adult Patients Using an Influenza-Like Illness Scoring System during the 2009 Pandemic—Mexico
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pandemic influenza A (H1N1) virus emerged during 2009. To help clinicians triage adults with acute respiratory illness, a scoring system for influenza-like illness (ILI) was implemented at Hospital Civil de Guadalajara, Mexico. METHODS: A medical history, laboratory and radiology results were collected on emergency room (ER) patients with acute respiratory illness to calculate an ILI-score. Patients were evaluated for admission by their ILI-score and clinicians' assessment of risk for developing complications. Nasal and throat swabs were collected from intermediate and high-risk patients for influenza testing by RT-PCR. The disposition and ILI-score of those oseltamivir-treated versus untreated, clinical characteristics of 2009 pandemic influenza A (H1N1) patients versus test-negative patients were compared by Pearson's Χ(2), Fisher's Exact, and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. RESULTS: Of 1840 ER patients, 230 were initially hospitalized (mean ILI-score = 15), and the rest were discharged, including 286 ambulatory patients given oseltamivir (median ILI-score = 11), and 1324 untreated (median ILI-score = 5). Fourteen (1%) untreated patients returned, and 3 were hospitalized on oseltamivir (median ILI-score = 19). Of 371 patients tested by RT-PCR, 104 (28%) had pandemic influenza and 42 (11%) had seasonal influenza A detected. Twenty (91%) of 22 imaged hospitalized pandemic influenza patients had bilateral infiltrates compared to 23 (38%) of 61 imaged hospital test-negative patients (p<0.001). One patient with confirmed pandemic influenza presented 6 days after symptom onset, required mechanical ventilation, and died. CONCLUSIONS: The triaging system that used an ILI-score complimented clinicians' judgment of who needed oseltamivir and inpatient care and helped hospital staff manage a surge in demand for services.

title: Preparation, optimization, and in vivo evaluation of an inhaled solution of total saponins of Panax notoginseng and its protective effect against idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic and progressive pulmonary disease that can cause fibrotic remodeling of the surrounding lung, thus leading to respiratory failure. Although IPF is the most common form of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia, the precise mechanisms underlying this condition remain unknown. In this study, we used total saponins of Panax notoginseng inhalation solution (TIS) to induce idiopathic bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in rats. The uniformity of delivery dose was investigated by analyzing the aerodynamic particle size distribution and drug stability. The potential of hydrogen potential of hydrogen (pH) of the inhalation solution was 7.0 and the solvent 0.9% NaCl solution, thus meeting physiological requirements for pulmonary drug administration. The delivery rate was 1.94 ± 0.16 mg·min(−1) and the total dose was 17.40 ± 0.04 mg. TIS was composed of five key components: notoginsenoside R(1), ginsenosides Rg(1), ginsenosides Re, ginsenosides Rb(1), and ginsenosides Rd. The mass median aerodynamic diameter (MMAD) for these five components were 3.62 ± 0.05 µm, 3.62 ± 0.06 µm, 3.65 ± 0.10 µm, 3.62 ± 0.06 µm, and 3.61 ± 0.05 µm, respectively. Fine particle fraction (FPF) was 66.24 ± 0.73%, 66.20 ± 0.89%, 66.07 ± 1.42%, 66.18 ± 0.79%, and 66.29 ± 0.70%, respectively. The MMAD for inhalation solutions needs to be 1–5 µm, which indicates that the components of TIS are suitable for inhalation. It is important to control the particle size of targeted drugs to ensure that the drug is delivered to the appropriate target tissue. In vitro experiments indicated that TIS exhibited high rates of deposition in lung tissue, thus indicating that pulmonary delivery systems may represent a good therapeutic option for patients.

title: Risk factors and outcomes of acute kidney injury in South African critically ill adults: a prospective cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUND: There is a marked paucity of data concerning AKI in Sub-Saharan Africa, where there is a substantial burden of trauma and HIV. METHODS: Prospective data was collected on all patients admitted to a multi-disciplinary ICU in South Africa during 2017. Development of AKI (before or during ICU admission) was recorded and renal recovery 90 days after ICU discharge was determined. RESULTS: Of 849 admissions, the mean age was 42.5 years and mean SAPS 3 score was 48.1. Comorbidities included hypertension (30.5%), HIV (32.6%), diabetes (13.3%), CKD (7.8%) and active tuberculosis (6.2%). The most common reason for admission was trauma (26%). AKI developed in 497 (58.5%). Male gender, illness severity, length of stay, vasopressor drugs and sepsis were independently associated with AKI. AKI was associated with a higher in-hospital mortality rate of 31.8% vs 7.23% in those without AKI. Age, active tuberculosis, higher SAPS 3 score, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support and sepsis were associated with an increased adjusted odds ratio for death. HIV was not independently associated with AKI or hospital mortality. CKD developed in 14 of 110 (12.7%) patients with stage 3 AKI; none were dialysis-dependent. CONCLUSIONS: In this large prospective multidisciplinary ICU cohort of younger patients, AKI was common, often associated with trauma in addition to traditional risk factors and was associated with good functional renal recovery at 90 days in most survivors. Although the HIV prevalence was high and associated with higher mortality, this was related to the severity of illness and not to HIV status per se.

title: Tracing “Fearbola”: Psychological Predictors of Anxious Responding to the Threat of Ebola
abstract: Serious illnesses such as Ebola are often highly publicized in the mass media and can be associated with varying levels of anxiety and compensatory safety behavior (e.g., avoidance of air travel). The present study investigated psychological processes associated with Ebola-related anxiety and safety behaviors during the outbreak in late 2014. Between October 30 and December 3, 2014, which encompassed the peak of concerns and of the media’s attention to this particular outbreak, 107 university students completed a battery of measures assessing fear of Ebola, performance of safety behaviors, factual knowledge of the virus, and psychological variables hypothesized to predict Ebola-related fear. We found that while our sample was generally not very fearful of contracting Ebola, the fear of this disease was correlated with general distress, contamination cognitions, disgust sensitivity, body vigilance, and anxiety sensitivity-related physical concerns. Regression analyses further indicated that anxiety sensitivity related to physical concerns and the tendency to overestimate the severity of contamination were unique predictors of both Ebola fear and associated safety behaviors. Implications for how concerns over serious illness outbreaks can be conceptualized and clinically managed are discussed.

title: Fentanyl conjugate vaccine by injected or mucosal delivery with dmLT or LTA1 adjuvants implicates IgA in protection from drug challenge
abstract: This article proposes an investigation into the use of fentanyl conjugate vaccines in a medical setting, delivered either through injection or mucosal delivery with dmLT or LTA1 adjuvants, to assess whether these approaches could lead to protection from a potential drug challenge. Recent developments in nanotechnology-enabled vaccine manufacturing have enabled improved antigen delivery and efficacy for some therapeutics; however their application is yet to be evaluated within the field of controlled substance vaccination. Our research has involved vaccinating animal models with different formulations and matching them against statistically equal control groups using pre-defined criteria to compare IgA response versus protection from drug challenge. This abstract sets out to summarize our findings on safety and immunogenicity around this novel approach, which we hope will help improve public knowledge on the efficacy of opioid addiction prevention strategies and address wider questions surrounding successful detection and treatment of illicit drugs abuse cases.

title: Appearance of Acute Inflammatory State Indicates Improvement in Atopic Dermatitis Cases Under Classical Homeopathic Treatment: A Case Series
abstract: The Continuum theory and the Levels of Health theory propound the idea that return of efficient acute inflammation (high fever) heralds true improvement in chronic inflammatory states. We present 6 cases of atopic dermatitis (AD), which had stability in their improvement for 1 year or more, under classical homeopathy. The cases were retrospectively assessed with selected based on the Hanifin Rajka atopic dermatitis diagnostic criteria and the follow ups evaluated according to changes on SCORing Atopic Dermatitis scale (SCORAD) scale. The pictures are presented as evidence. Modified Naranjo Criteria for assessing causal attribution of clinical outcome to homeopathic intervention was used to assess the effect of homeopathy in these cases. All the cases improved and stabilised with complete skin clearance (those that relapsed within 1 year were not included). These patients had not suffered high fevers/acute inflammatory diseases since onset/aggravation of AD. Five of the 6 cases developed acute inflammatory diseases as the chronic condition improved. The last case showed return of an old, lesser pathology. The control cases – which were selected for non-improvement under classical homeopathy also showed remarkable skin clearance when there was appearance of acute inflammatory states. In this study, there is a mutually exclusive relationship between efficient acute inflammation and chronic inflammation, which is in accordance with the 2 theories considered here. Further scientific studies are necessary to establish the phenomenon at tissue level.
