title: Measuring Software Maintainability with Naïve Bayes Classifier
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for software maintainability measurement using Naïve Bayes Classifier (NBC). Maintainability is a critical quality attribute of software and recurrently posed as one of the most important criteria within development processes. Existing approaches to measure maintainability often rely on traces which require complex models with manual extraction, and thus yield ambiguous results. Our approach obtains minor improvements over existing alternatives while avoiding an exhaustive taskset evaluation process, by building metrics in combination with NBC capabilities performing classification operations—hence proposing a more efficient way of computing accurate predictions. We propose that such model is appropriate to asses the nine aspects stipulated in IEEE Standard 982.1-1988 standard rule set, thus providing effective feedback regarding maintenance endeavors outcomes prior project finalization stage while accounting shorter development cycles leadtimes constrains. Results suggest over 90% accuracy can be achieved to predict consistency across achieving major factors related staff availability depending on code quality levels given metric reliable assessments are produced at any build validation step; leading towards greater increase scalability when 2 or more applications must coexist sharing similar or cohesive resources along development life-cycle lifespans.

title: Introduction to artificial intelligence in ultrasound imaging in obstetrics and gynecology
abstract:
This article provides an introduction to artificial intelligence (AI) in ultrasound imaging in obstetrics and gynecology. In recent years, AI has gained increased prominence due to its potential to revolutionize healthcare diagnostics and monitor outcomes, mostly through automated image/data analysis. Its application in ultrasound imaging is increasingly being implemented as a form of advanced medical technology that has the potential to significantly improve patient care by providing advance monitoring and guidance during pregnancy, delivery or management of infertility or gynecological disorders. 

Ultrasound imaging plays an integral role in the practice of Obstetrics and Gynecology with applications ranging from diagnosis of fetal anomalies, prenatal surveillance and preconception counseling, among other cases. Although manual interpretation remains as the gold standard for imaging assessment within this specialty, AI-assisted scanning can be more reliable since it allows faster examination times accompanied by improved accuracy rates compared with conventional ultrasonography. It also helps radiologists reduce errors related to fatigue which may arise due maintenance of concentration throughout a long scanning session under pressure when assessing large number of patients on a daily basis. Furthermore, AI integrated into ultrasounds offers digital data management systems where images are immediately transmitted for review thus resulting on timely access regardless practitioners’ geographical location from one another making them ideal tools for telemedicine consultation during such unprecedented pandemic times like COVID-19 emergency services period we just passed through at 2020 early days..

title: Viral Infections of the Newborn
abstract: Viral infections of the newborn result in significant morbidity and mortality each year. The fetus and newborn are particularly wlnerable to viral infection. The range of expression may vary from no clinical disease to devastating illness and infection occurring before, during, or after birth. Nursing management is determined by the specific viral infection, the severity of the illness, and the unique conditions of the newborn and his/her family. Promising new therapies are on the horizon that may lessen the severity of viral disease. Until such time, the major thrusts of management of neonatal viral disease are prevention of infection and supportive care for the acutely ill newborn.

title: Dietary Selenium Status Regulates the Transcriptions of Selenoproteome and Activities of Selenoenzymes in Chicken Kidney at Low or Super-nutritional Levels
abstract: This study investigates the dietary selenium status, its influence on the transcribed selenoproteome, and how it activates similar activities in chicken kidney as nutrients intake rises. Dietary intakes of selenium are known to be necessary for maintaining a healthy physiological balance due to their common roles as integral components of antioxidant enzymes, involved in production of thyroid hormones and gene regulation. However, discrepancies between dietary supplementation rates have left research looking into whether various amounts will impact cellular levels specifically those active at low or super-nutritional levels in chickens. Through utilising omic technologies transcriptomics and bioinformatics reconstruction was conducted to explore potential shifts within mRNA abundance and the activation adaptations relating respiration patterns during uptake phase. This paper sheds light on knowledge regarding key molecular markers that underpin how certain diets alter metabolism pathways within target tissue types responding under high/low nutrient conditions across time periods both short-term (acute) and constant (chronic). The analysis provides speculating support elucidating quantitative evidence based insights underlying transcripts with distinct activity interactions drawn from comparing chick kidney organs exposed to Selenium enriched vs Se-deficient food medium settings over 48 hours feeding cycle period windows

title: Trends in knowledge of HIV status and efficiency of HIV testing services in sub-Saharan Africa, 2000–20: a modelling study using survey and HIV testing programme data
abstract: This study examines the trends in knowledge of HIV status and the efficiency of HIV testing services in Sub-Saharan Africa from 2000 to 2020. Using survey and HIV testing programme data, a modelling approach was employed to assess how changes over time in access to health care resources associated with testing available were related to improvement or decline in knowledge of an individual's own HIV status. It also aimed at assessing whether these changes had a positive effect on uptake of preventive counselling and treatment for those who tested positive for HIV infection. The results indicate that although there has been significant progress when it comes to increased access to antiretroviral therapy since 2000, more needs to be done if governments are serious about targeting prevention programmes and improving quality outcomes within primary healthcare networks across sub-Saharan Africa. The findings suggest a policy effort should focus not only on expanding coverage but also on creating successful treatments through effective integration into existing community structures as well as strengthening proactive diagnostic tools such as diagnosis tests integrated into village clinical settings.

title: Acute Kidney Injury in the Tropics: Epidemiology, Presentation, Etiology, Specific Diseases, and Treatment
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe clinical condition that poses an increasing burden on the healthcare system, with particular relevance in tropical regions due to their substantially higher rates of AKI. This review seeks to address the epidemiology, presentation, etiology and treatment options currently available for this serious illness within the tropics. An assessment of specific diseases causing acute renal failure will also be discussed as important considerations when diagnosing and treating those affected by AKI in these geopolitical regions. Further research into early interventions for limiting its severity are identified as potential future investigations given its clinical significance amongst communities living in geographical areas facing a variety of environmental health challenges including water scarcity and high ultraviolet intensity exposure. The aim is two-fold; firstly, to increase understanding regarding AKI within the geopolitically qualitative divide known as ‘the tropics’; secondly, raise longer term science policy priorities so further work can strengthen global evidence supporting improved preventative healthcare services for those suffering from exacerbated forms of chronic conditions caused or associated with events leading to AKI development therein.

title: Dengue Fever, Hawaii, 2001–2002
abstract: Autochthonous dengue infections were last reported in Hawaii in 1944. In September 2001, the Hawaii Department of Health was notified of an unusual febrile illness in a resident with no travel history; dengue fever was confirmed. During the investigation, 1,644 persons with locally acquired denguelike illness were evaluated, and 122 (7%) laboratory-positive dengue infections were identified; dengue virus serotype 1 was isolated from 15 patients. No cases of dengue hemorrhagic fever or shock syndrome were reported. In 3 instances autochthonous infections were linked to a person who reported denguelike illness after travel to French Polynesia. Phylogenetic analyses showed the Hawaiian isolates were closely associated with contemporaneous isolates from Tahiti. Aedes albopictus was present in all communities surveyed on Oahu, Maui, Molokai, and Kauai; no Ae. aegypti were found. This outbreak underscores the importance of maintaining surveillance and control of potential disease vectors even in the absence of an imminent disease threat.

title: Proteomic analysis revealed T cell hyporesponsiveness induced by Haemonchus contortus excretory and secretory proteins
abstract: This study presents an analysis of the modulatory effects exerted by excretory and secretory (E/S) proteins from the parasitic nematode Haemonchu contortus, on immune T cells derived from chickens. Through a comprehensive proteomic approach, our research highlights how H. contortus E/S proteins induce hyporesponsiveness in host T cells leading to attenuation of anti-parasitic immunity and providing insights into parasite pathogenic mechanisms. By demonstrating which protein molecules are responsible for immunomodulation in infected hosts, this work provides evidence that may be applicable to other helminth species in poultry or livestock farms with economic impact. Our findings have important implications for vaccine design strategies against this major cause of morbidity around the world.

title: Screening With Reticulocyte Hemoglobin Increased Iron Sufficiency Among NICU Patients
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To increase the rate of iron sufficiency among neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients from 16% to >35% within 12 months of implementing standardized assessment of reticulocyte hemoglobin (retHE). METHODS: We implemented a quality improvement (QI) study to improve iron sufficiency in our out-born level III/IV NICU. We screened 2,062 admissions, of which 622 were eligible based on feeding status at discharge. QI interventions included educational efforts and guideline implementation. Our primary outcome measure was the percentage of patients with their discharge retHE measure within the normal range. We also tracked the process measure of the number of retHE tests performed and a balancing measure of the incidence of elevated retHE among patients receiving iron supplementation. Statistical process control (SPC) charts assessed for special cause variation. RESULTS: The percentage of patients with a retHe within the normal range was significantly increased from a mean of 20% to 39% on SPC chart analysis. We measured significantly more retHE values after guideline implementation (11/mo to 24/mo) and found no cases of elevated retHE among patients receiving iron supplementation. CONCLUSIONS: After the implementation of a standardized guideline, a higher rate of iron sufficiency was found in NICU patients at discharge. This work is generalizable to neonatal populations with the potential for a significant impact on clinical practice.

title: Public Health Data Collection and Sharing Using HIPAA Messages
abstract: Public health information has significant value for doctors, public health officials, epidemiological researchers, the general public, and government agencies. Unfortunately, these data are difficult to obtain and are typically collected on as-needed basis and maintained locally. This localized process unavoidably limits the access to important public health data by its users. Moreover, the diversity of data transmission standards and collection techniques make the collected data less usable. This paper proposes a new standardized public health information system based on the HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) messages, which are the standard transactions between hospitals and insurance companies. In particular, this paper explores the applicability of HIPAA messages as a data source and transmission standard, and proposes a prototype design of a new system to collect and share public health data using HIPAA messages.

title: Self-testing for HIV, HBV, and HCV using finger-stick whole-blood multiplex immunochromatographic rapid test: A pilot feasibility study in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: This pilot feasibility study evaluated the performance of a novel multiplex immunochromatographic rapid test for diagnosing hepatitis viruses B (HBV), C (HCV) and human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), in finger-stick whole blood from participants attending outpatient clinics sub-Saharan Africa, contextualizing an HIV self-testing methodology. Results showed that this diagnostic algorithm was about 95%, 89% and 98% sensitive for detecting HBV, HCV and HIV infections respectively. Additionally, the method conveniently enabled sample collection at home due to its lack of infrastructure requirement; proving useful even when access to health services is limited. Alongside cost considerations this makes it particularly attractive as a viable methodology — on one hand expanding testing options while also steadily driving epidemic control efforts towards goal three of the UNAIDS 90–90–90 framework: Virtually no new transmissions by 2030.  In conclusion, Given its reliability and better acceptability scores characteristic of such user centric tests — this pointof care diagnostic platform could be used to drive scale up strategies needed to reach universal access throughout sub Saharan African countries most heavily burdened with these chronic diseases but where healthcare delivery remains inadequate or non existent in certain areas; empowering citizens with greater autonomy towards their own health outcomes while allowing authorities proper feedback regarding treatment progress hence ultimately aiming towards ending HIV epidemics in East African nations .

title: Rapid RNA Exchange in Aqueous Two-Phase System and Coacervate Droplets
abstract: This article deals with the emerging and potentially revolutionary field of rapid RNA exchange processes taking place in aqueous two-phase systems (ATPS) and coacervate droplets (CD). As living cells contain a high number of RNAs and employ ATPS or CD as components for various biochemical interactions, it is interesting to investigate how these natural conditions affect the observed transfer rates from one molecular component to another. Thus, this study will provide information about the reorganization of RNA molecules in such environments, enabling insight into how best to manipulate them for practical applications. We seek to gain understanding on the effects of phase changes upon receptor/ligand binding in these solutions that can greatly inform efforts towards engineering better biomedicines and therapeutics.

title: The impact of indole-3-lactic acid on immature intestinal innate immunity and development: a transcriptomic analysis
abstract: This study investigates the effects of indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) on immature intestinal innate immunity and development. To do so, a transcriptomic analysis was conducted to evaluate the immunomodulatory capacity of ILA in vitro and its consequences for intestinal organogenesis. In combination with a variety of statistical approaches, this investigation aimed to reveal the distinct transcriptional profile associated with ILA supplementation in immature human colons as well as provide insights into potential supplementary interventions that could be used to modulate an individual's inherent immune responses during prenatal or postnatal stages. The results revealed how specific components within ILA were capable of maintaining optimal levels of key mediators such as toll-like receptor 3 signaling pathways which are integral towards formation and structure integrity within nascent intestines  across early infancy milestones. Additionally noteworthy is how regulating factors like WNT/β -catenin pathway appeared distinctively overexpressed when supplementing preterm infants with ILA thus affording greater insight into translational considerations when crafting nutrition solution geared at safeguarding mucosal health under challenging scenarios typically observed in neonates admitted for tending uncertain GI disorders where prompt host mediated defenses are paramount for ensuing successful regulatory interference processes.

title: Antiviral Activity of Benzavir-2 against Emerging Flaviviruses
abstract: In the present day, emerging flaviviruses pose a significant global health threat due to rapid transmission and severe associated morbidity. Thus, effective antiviral treatments must be quickly established in order to prevent further spread of these diseases. This study aimed to evaluate the antiviral effects of Benzavir-2 against emerging flaviviruses by conducting both in vitro and ex vivo experiments with cell lines that were infected with various relevantly related viruses. The results revealed that Benzavir-2 has potent inhibitory activity against influenza A (H1N1), West Nile fever virus, tick borne encephalitis virus, Zika virus and Influenza B (Victoria lineage). Furthermore, exposure to the drug led to reduced viral titre during incubation times up to 48 hours post infection along with altered morphology resembling apoptosis in infected cells when probed using fluorescence microscopy. These findings suggest that Benzavir-2 may serve as a potential therapeutic option for treating cases of emerging Flavivirus infections.

title: The Way Forward: Potentiating Protective Immunity to Novel and Pandemic Influenza Through Engagement of Memory CD4 T Cells
abstract: Potentially pandemic strains of influenza pose an undeniable threat to human populations. Therefore, it is essential to develop better strategies to enhance vaccine design and predict parameters that identify susceptible humans. CD4 T cells are a central component of protective immunity to influenza, delivering direct effector function and potentiating responses of other lymphoid cells. Humans have highly diverse influenza-specific CD4 T-cell populations that vary in stimulation history, specificity, and functionality. title: Diagnostic workup for ARDS patients
abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is defined by the association of bilateral infiltrates and hypoxaemia following an initial insult. Although a new definition has been recently proposed (Berlin definition), there are various forms of ARDS with potential differences regarding their management (ventilator settings, prone positioning use, corticosteroids). ARDS can be caused by various aetiologies, and the adequate treatment of the responsible cause is crucial to improve the outcome. It is of paramount importance to characterize the mechanisms causing lung injury to optimize both the aetiological treatment and the symptomatic treatment. If there is no obvious cause of ARDS or if a direct lung injury is suspected, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) should be strongly considered to identify microorganisms responsible for pneumonia. Blood samples can also help to identify microorganisms and to evaluate biomarkers of infection. If there is no infectious cause of ARDS or no other apparent aetiology is found, second-line examinations should include markers of immunologic diseases. In selected cases, open lung biopsy remains useful to identify the cause of ARDS when all other examinations remain inconclusive. CT scan is fundamental when there is a suspicion of intra-abdominal sepsis and in some cases of pneumonia. Ultrasonography is important not only in evaluating biventricular function but also in identifying pleural effusions and pneumothorax. The definition of ARDS remains clinical and the main objective of the diagnostic workup should be to be focused on identification of its aetiology, especially a treatable infection. title: Characterization of RNA in Saliva
abstract: The discovery of RNA in saliva, a bodily fluid formerly believed to contain only proteins and lipids, has caused an upheaval in scientific understanding. To facilitate a more holistic comprehension of the role of RNA within saliva and its potential health implications, this study provides an extensive characterization of decisional-relevant sample attributes beneath qualitative minimal criteria. We focus on primary assessment variables including total suspended biomass fractionation, chemical integrity evaluations by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and enzymatic profiles via gel electrophoresis (SDS–PAGE). Through this research we will provide both quantitative evidence for the occurrence of multiple forms of complex molecular life alongside previously unidentified instances in salivary functions that have yet to be realized. Additionally, these fundamental aspects will represent seminal strides towards a better appreciation regarding functional roles taken up by our mouth's many internal constituents.

title: Design, synthesis, heme binding and density functional theory studies of isoindoline-dione-4-aminoquinolines as potential antiplasmodials
abstract: This paper presents a detailed exploration of the structure-function relationship of isoindoline-dione-4-aminoquinolines as potential antimicrobial agents. Through the progressions of design, synthesis, heme binding ability assessment and density functional theory studies on these compounds, extensive property data were obtained which illustrated an increase in biological activity with increasing ring systems modifications. Meanwhile, in vitro antimalarial assays showed that various derivatives possess moderate to good inhibitory activities against chloroquine sensitive and resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains. This research successfully offered novel structural information for drug discovery purposes regarding medical treatment for malaria infection.

title: Interferon induction in swine lymphocyte antigen-defined miniature pigs
abstract: The title of this article is 'Interferon Induction in Swine Lymphocyte Antigen-defined Miniature Pigs'. This study evaluates the interferon (IFN) response of lymphoid cells from miniature pigs with defined alleles for swine leukocyte antigen (SLA). IFN has a critical role in host antiviral immunity, however the complexity and variability within SLAs have posed challenges to predicting responses to specific viral infections. Due to their small size, miniature pigs were chosen as an ideal model animal due to the high level of genetic uniformity achieved through stringent selection criteria. The objective was to characterize IFN production by closely related strains of mini pigs immunized with three vaccine antigens known to induce IFN response in other species. In conclusion, these results indicate that there is significant variation between closely related minipigs concerning their ability to mount an effective IFN response against multiple vaccine antigens.

title: Influence of severity of infection on the effect of appropriate antimicrobial therapy for Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremic pneumonia
abstract: This study examined the impact of the severity of infection on antimicrobial therapy effectiveness in cases of Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) Bacteremic Pneumonia (ABBP). Previous studies have provided conflicting results with respect to proper management and prognosis for ABBP, highlighting an important need for further elucidating appropriate dosage regiments and therapeutic response at different stages of illness progression. Utilizing 290 retrospective patient medical records from two military hospitals, this study utilized semi-quantitative analysis to assess susceptibility to antibiotics and identify predictors relevant to clinical outcomes across five preselected severities determined by clinicians upon diagnosis. The results revealed that there is significant influence on the effect of parenteral antimicrobial treatments for A. baumanii based on initial pathology reports related to severity assessment regardless of treatment timing or method used; ultimately responding positively or negatively depending upon grade parity between diagnosis orders, antibiotic adherence, continuance administration times and patient history scores. These findings provide valuable knowledge towards better understanding contemporary therapeutic protocols currently governing ABBP outbreaks in healthcare facilities throughout the world today.

title: Review—Chemical and Biological Sensors for Viral Detection
abstract: This review focuses on the advancement of chemical and biological sensing technologies and their impact in viral detection. Today, chemicals sensors are increasingly developed to detect presence of harmful viruses at molecular level. Meanwhile, bio-sensing systems allow for effective pathogen analysis within seconds and even analyze specific sequence mutations for improved accuracy in diagnosis. This article discusses current advances in the development of visioning platforms which focus on accurate automatic binding or selective interactions between target molecules from biotropic particles with limited energy requirements. The platform substitutes fluorescent dyes for chromophore receptors thereby enabling easier DNA sequencing with reduced costs as compared to biochemical based methods. In addition, novel approaches based on amplifying nanopores involved in transduction processes provide reliable information about diverse kinds of microorganisms present inside coveted samples; a major advantage being that they can be measured optically without any sophisticated lab instruments. Furthermore, this review also highlights potential applications along with challenges associated with the technology used to create such biosensors and their limitations like false positive rates especially when dealing too small virus copies making their widespread use more complicated than expected

title: Gastroenteritis in Children: A Two-Year Review in Manitoba. I. Etiology
abstract: This paper presents a two-year review of the etiology and epidemiology of gastroenteritis in children aged 0-5 years old in Manitoba. Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the digestive system, which may include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea amongst other symptoms. This study examines previous data on large outbreaks to gain insight into common causes for this affliction among young Manitoban children and inform preventative practices within the province's healthcare system. We conducted a retrospective survey accessing existing provincial databases focusing on identifying sources related to cases arising between May 2016 - 2017 in comparison to incidents reported between May 2018 - 2019. Through our findings we aim to shed light on risk factors associated with gastroenteritis incidence rates across the two study periods.

title: Cocaine and amphetamine-regulated transcript prepropeptide gene (CARTPT) polymorphism interacts with Diet Quality Index-International (DQI-I) and Healthy Eating Index (HEI) to affect hypothalamic hormones and cardio-metabolic risk factors among obese individuals
abstract: BACKGROUND: Epidemiologic studies show that cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript prepropeptide (CARTPT) gene polymorphism modifies diet-obesity relationships. However, the interaction between CARTPT gene polymorphism and diet quality indices have not been investigated yet. The current study was aimed to evaluate the interaction between major dietary indices including Diet Quality Index-International (DQI-I) and Healthy Eating Index (HEI)-2015 and CARTPT gene rs2239670 variants among apparently healthy obese Iranians. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was carried out by employing 288 apparently healthy obese adults aged 20–50 years with a BMI of 30–40 kg/m(2). Diet quality was evaluated by Diet Quality Index-International (DQI-I) and Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015) using a 132-items semi-quantitative validated food frequency questionnaire. The CARTPT gene rs2239670 polymorphism was genotyped by polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR–RFLP) technique. Blood concentrations of glycemic markers, lipid profile, α-melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP) were also measured. ANCOVA multivariate interaction model was used to analyze gene-diet interactions. RESULTS: The significant interactions were identified between CARTPT gene polymorphism and HEI, affecting BMR (P(Interaction) = 0.003), serum glucose (P(Interaction) = 0.009) and high density lipoprotein cholesterol HDL concentrations (P(Interaction) = 0.03) after adjusting for the effects of sex and age. Also we found gene-diet interaction between CARTPT genotypes and DQI-I in terms of fat mass (FM; P(Interaction) = 0.02), waist circumference (WC; P(Interaction) < 0.001), body mass index (BMI; P(Interaction) < 0.001), basal metabolic rate (BMR, P(Interaction) < 0.001), serum fasting glucose (P(Interaction) < 0.01) and AgRP (P(Interaction) = 0.05) in individuals even after adjusting for potential confounders. CONCLUSION: Current study showed the effects of interaction between CARTPT genotype with adherence to HEI and DQI-I scores on obesity-related anthropometric and metabolic risk-factors.

title: Quantitative Phosphoproteomics of Proteasome Inhibition in Multiple Myeloma Cells
abstract: BACKGROUND: The proteasome inhibitor bortezomib represents an important advance in the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM). Bortezomib inhibits the activity of the 26S proteasome and induces cell death in a variety of tumor cells; however, the mechanism of cytotoxicity is not well understood. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We investigated the differential phosphoproteome upon proteasome inhibition by using stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture (SILAC) in combination with phosphoprotein enrichment and LC-MS/MS analysis. In total 233 phosphoproteins were identified and 72 phosphoproteins showed a 1.5-fold or greater change upon bortezomib treatment. The phosphoproteins with expression alterations encompass all major protein classes, including a large number of nucleic acid binding proteins. Site-specific phosphopeptide quantitation revealed that Ser38 phosphorylation on stathmin increased upon bortezomib treatment, suggesting new mechanisms associated to bortezomib-induced apoptosis in MM cells. Further studies demonstrated that stathmin phosphorylation profile was modified in response to bortezomib treatment and the regulation of stathmin by phosphorylation at specific Ser/Thr residues participated in the cellular response induced by bortezomib. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Our systematic profiling of phosphorylation changes in response to bortezomib treatment not only advanced the global mechanistic understanding of the action of bortezomib on myeloma cells but also identified previously uncharacterized signaling proteins in myeloma cells.

title: Exploring the Innate Immunological Response of an Alternative Nonhuman Primate Model of Infectious Disease; the Common Marmoset
abstract: The common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) is increasingly being utilised as a nonhuman primate model for human disease, ranging from autoimmune to infectious disease. In order to fully exploit these models, meaningful comparison to the human host response is necessary. Commercially available reagents, primarily targeted to human cells, were utilised to assess the phenotype and activation status of key immune cell types and cytokines in naive and infected animals. Single cell suspensions of blood, spleen, and lung were examined. Generally, the phenotype of cells was comparable between humans and marmosets, with approximately 63% of all lymphocytes in the blood of marmosets being T cells, 25% B-cells, and 12% NK cells. The percentage of neutrophils in marmoset blood were more similar to human values than mouse values. Comparison of the activation status of cells following experimental systemic or inhalational infection exhibited different trends in different tissues, most obvious in cell types active in the innate immune response. This work significantly enhances the ability to understand the immune response in these animals and fortifies their use as models of infectious disease.

title: Design and Optimization of ECG Modeling for Generating Different Cardiac Dysrhythmias
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of an electrocardiogram (ECG) modeling system for generating different cardiac dysrhythmias. The proposed ECG model is composed of a signal generator, virtual body tissue, and machine learning algorithms. It accurately simulates various types of physiological abnormalities in cardiac events without employing physical metrics or models. In this article, we aim to improve the performance of our ECG model by cross-testing it with data obtained from radiographic scanning experiments conducted on healthy volunteers and multi-dimensional arrays collected from persons suffering from various forms of heart diseases and associated conditions like atrial fibrillation, accelerated junctional rhythms, ventricular tachycardia etc. To conduct these tests effectively we use conventional techniques like interquartile range deviation (IRD), Welch T-test along with newly developed methods such as feature selection based on genetic algorithm optimization approach followed by artificial neural networks. Our experimental results demonstrate that our designed ECG model is appropriate for generating four major classes of arrhythmia plus 21 subclasses found in patients diagnosed with minor irregular beats which has been fully verified both statistically and empirically providing empirical evidence that simulations produced can be \textit{generalized} to real scenarios efficiently.

title: Clinical characteristics of refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children treated with glucocorticoid pulse therapy
abstract: BACKGROUND: To observe the effect of corticosteroids in the treatment of children with refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) under different doses, to summarize the clinical features of children treated with glucocorticoid pulse therapy. METHODS: The clinical data of 125 children with RMPP hospitalized in Tianjin Children’s Hospital from September 2018 to October 2019 were retrospectively analyzed. They were divided into two groups according to the dose of hormone. Compare the clinical features, laboratory findings, and imaging between the two groups, and use meaningful related indicators as ROC curves to find reference indicators for pulse therapy. RESULTS: (1) The median age of the group II was older than that of the group I(P < 0.05). (2) We found more severe presentations, higher incidence of extra-pulmonary complications and more serious radiological findings in group II, which needed oxygen more often, higher the hormone, higher usage rate of gamma globulin, higher usage rate of bronchoscopy, and higher incidence of plastic bronchitis(P < 0.05). (3) WBC, CRP, LDH, FER, D-D dimer, APTT, TT, PCT, IL-6 and the percentage of neutrophils in peripheral blood in Group II were higher than those in Group I(P < 0.05). (4) In ROC curve analysis, CRP, LDH, FER, and neutrophils of leukocyte classification were independent related factors that could be used as valuable predictors of methylprednisolone pulse therapy for RMPP in children. The cut-off values were CRP44.45 mg/L, LDH590IU/L, FER411ng/L, and neutrophils in leukocyte classification were 73.75%, respectively. CONCLUSION: CRP ≥ 44.45 mg/L, LDH ≥ 590 IU/L, FER ≥ 411 ng/L, neutrophil≥73.75%, lung consolidation, and pleural effusion may be predictors that guide the treatment of RMPP with pulse dose of GC.

title: Dendritic cells and Brucella spp. interaction: the sentinel host and the stealthy pathogen
abstract: As dendritic cells (DCs) are among the first cells to encounter antigens, these cells trigger both innate and T cell responses, and are the most potent antigen-presenting cells. Brucella spp., which is an intracellular facultative and stealthy pathogen, is able to evade the bactericidal activities of professional phagocytes. Several studies have demonstrated that Brucella can survive and replicate intracellularly, thereby provoking impaired maturation of DCs. Therefore, the interaction between DCs and Brucella becomes an interesting model to study the immune response. In this review, we first will describe the most common techniques for DCs differentiation in vitro as well as general features of brucellosis. Then, the interaction of DCs and Brucella, including pathogen recognition, molecular mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis, and intracellular trafficking of Brucella to subvert innate response, will be reviewed. Finally, we will debate diversity in immunological DC response and the controversial role of DC activation against Brucella infection.

title: Medical Insurance Information Systems in China: Mixed Methods Study
abstract:
This paper analyzes the provider-to-focusing medical insurance information systems integrated to Chinese hospitals, aiming to explore new and more effective ways of providing health care services. The main focus is on understanding how these systems are being managed and used throughout the country by providers and patients, as well as their ability to improve patient outcomes. In order to understand this complex system, a mixed methods study has been conducted in four major hospitals located in southern China over a two year period. title: Critical physiological and pathological functions of Forkhead Box O tumor suppressors
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the critical physiological and pathological functions of Forkhead Box O (FOXO) tumor suppressors in humans. FOXOs constitute a family of transcription factors well known for regulating various cellular processes including apoptosis, autophagy and cell cycle regulatory pathways. Associated with cancer progression, diverse genetic alterations as well as epigenetic events are known to influence FOXO-mediated pathways at the molecular level leading to development or suppression of tumors. Subsequent investigation into these altered gene expression patterns reveal that modulation of FOXO signaling activities is key to controlling tumor initiation, invasion and metastasis along with supporting further clinical oncology therapeutic studies via identifying novel prognostic biomarkers underlining this mode of regulation within its target cells. Thus, an understanding of the roles played by FOXOs in cancerogenesis can increase our knowledgebase enhancing potential interventions towards preventing this disease altogether thereby providing new insight useful for pursuing better treatment strategies pertinent toward targeting tumorigenesis.

title: Determinants and Drivers of Infectious Disease Threat Events in Europe
abstract: This paper provides an insightful look into the determinants and drivers of infectious disease threat events (IDTEs) in Europe. Utilizing a cross-sectional analysis to examine the rapid emergence, occurrence and transmission of IDTEs across European countries, this study pinpoints why these events have come about and offers potential interventions for limiting their future impacts. By exploring disease surveillance systems, public health policies as well as regional socio-economic factors and access to resources within particular states, this research aims to develop a more comprehensive insights on how IDTEs could be recognized earlier so they can be addressed with effectiveness and efficiency. The implications gleaned from this investigation not only revealswhich nations are vulnerable but also highlights areas for improved capacity building in terms of intergovernmental collaborations between affected states in order to facilitate better preparedness against future situations that threaten both local citizens’ wellbeing as well as global public health security.

title: Immunobiology of Newcastle Disease Virus and Its Use for Prophylactic Vaccination in Poultry and as Adjuvant for Therapeutic Vaccination in Cancer Patients
abstract: Newcastle disease (ND) is one of the most important diseases of poultry worldwide. In the last decades, molecular research has gained a lot of new information about its causative agent, newcastle disease virus (NDV). In poultry industry, certain strains of NDV have been used for preventive vaccination for more than 60 years. NDV has also been applied to cancer patients with beneficial effects for about 50 years, but this is less well known. The molecular basis for these differential effects of NDV in birds and man have been elucidated in the last decades and are explained in this review. The anti-neoplastic and immune-stimulatory properties in non-permissive hosts such as mouse and man have to do with the strong type I interferon responses induced in these foreign species. Additionally, NDV has the potential to break various types of tumor resistances and also to affect liver fibrosis. A main section is devoted to the benefits of clinical application of NDV and NDV-based vaccines to cancer patients. Reverse genetics technology allowed developing NDV into a vector suitable for gene therapy. Examples will be provided in which genetically engineered NDV is being used successfully as vector against new emerging viruses.

title: Long non-coding RNA MEG3 attends to morphine-mediated autophagy of HT22 cells through modulating ERK pathway
abstract: Context: Morphine is an alkaloid isolated from the poppy plants. The addiction of morphine is a very serious social issue. Some long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been proposed to engage in drug addiction. Objective: Whether lncRNA maternally expressed gene 3 (MEG3) attended to morphine-mediated autophagy of mouse hippocampal neuronal HT22 cells was probed. Materials and methods: HT22 cells were subjected to 10 µM morphine for 24 h. Cell autophagy was assessed by measuring LC3-II/LC3-I and Beclin-1 expression. qRT-PCR was carried out to measure MEG3 expression. SiRNA oligoribonucleotides targeting MEG3 (si-MEG3) was transfected to silence MEG3. The orexin1 receptor (OX1R), c-fos, p/t-ERK and p/t-PKC expressions were tested by western blotting. SCH772984 was used as an inhibitor of ERK pathway. Results: Morphine elevated OX1R (2.92 times), c-fos (2.06 times), p/t-ERK (2.04 times) and p/t-PKC (2.4 times), Beclin-1 (3.2 times) and LC3-II/LC3-I (3.96 times) expression in HT22 cells. Moreover, followed by morphine exposure, the MEG3 expression was also elevated in HT22 cells (3.03 times). The silence of MEG3 lowered the Beclin-1 (1.85 times), LC3-II/LC3-I (2.12 times), c-fos (1.39 times) and p/t-ERK (1.44 times) expressions in morphine-treated HT22 cells. Inhibitor of ERK pathway SCH772984 further promoted the influence of MEG3 silence on morphine-caused Beclin-1 (1.97 times) and LC3-II/LC3-I (1.92 times) expressions decreases. Conclusions: Up-regulation of MEG3 attended to the morphine-caused autophagy of HT22 cells might be through elevating c-fos expression and promoting ERK pathway activation. More experiments are also needed in the future to analyse the influence of other lncRNAs in drug addiction.

title: Kinetic Modelling of Infection Tracers [(18)F]FDG, [(68)Ga]Ga-Citrate, [(11)C]Methionine, and [(11)C]Donepezil in a Porcine Osteomyelitis Model
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Positron emission tomography (PET) is increasingly applied for infection imaging using [(18)F]FDG as tracer, but uptake is unspecific. The present study compares the kinetics of [(18)F]FDG and three other PET tracers with relevance for infection imaging. METHODS: A juvenile porcine osteomyelitis model was used. Eleven pigs underwent PET/CT with 60-minute dynamic PET imaging of [(18)F]FDG, [(68)Ga]Ga-citrate, [(11)C]methionine, and/or [(11)C]donepezil, along with blood sampling. For infectious lesions, kinetic modelling with one- and two-tissue-compartment models was conducted for each tracer. RESULTS: Irreversible uptake was found for [(18)F]FDG and [(68)Ga]Ga-citrate; reversible uptake was found for [(11)C]methionine (two-tissue model) and [(11)C]donepezil (one-tissue model). The uptake rate for [(68)Ga]Ga-citrate was slow and diffusion-limited. For the other tracers, the uptake rate was primarily determined by perfusion (flow-limited uptake). Net uptake rate for [(18)F]FDG and distribution volume for [(11)C]methionine were significantly higher for infectious lesions than for correspondingly noninfected tissue. For [(11)C]donepezil in pigs, labelled metabolite products appeared to be important for the analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The kinetics of the four studied tracers in infection was characterized. For clinical applications, [(18)F]FDG remains the first-choice PET tracer. [(11)C]methionine may have a potential for detecting soft tissue infections. [(68)Ga]Ga-citrate and [(11)C]donepezil were not found useful for imaging of osteomyelitis.

title: Weak evidence of country- and institution-related status bias in the peer review of abstracts
abstract: This paper examines weak evidence of status bias in the peer review process, specifically related to countries and institutions. Data from previous study results as well as comparing abstracts from different parts of the world and various universities were used to investigate this issue. The findings suggest that there may be a slight trend for certain academic affiliations to receive better or worse reviews compared with average scores. The implications these findings have on publishing processes are discussed in light of existing theories regarding implicit biases among peer reviewers.

title: Competition-Based Cell Assay Employing Soluble T Cell Receptors to Assess MHC Class II Antigen Processing and Presentation
abstract: Accurate assessment of antigen-specific immune responses is critical in the development of safe and efficacious biotherapeutics and vaccines. Endosomal processing of a protein antigen followed by presentation on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II constitute necessary steps in the induction of CD4+ T cell immune responses. Current preclinical methods for assessing immunogenicity risk consist of in vitro cell-based assays and computational prediction tools. Cell-based assays are time and labor-intensive while in silico methodologies have limitations. Here, we propose a novel cell-based assay capable of investigating an antigen’s endosomal processing and MHC class II presentation capabilities. This novel assay relies on competition between epitopes for MHC class II binding and employs labeled soluble T cell receptors (sTCRs) as detectors of epitope presentation. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1208/s12248-020-00553-x.

title: Detection of enteric adenoviruses with synthetic oligonucleotide probes
abstract: The abilities of hybridization probes to detect all human adenovirus types and to identify enteric adenovirus types were evaluated. The efficiency of hybridization was compared to other tests currently in routine laboratory use on clinical specimens from young children with gastroenteritis, Probes were derived from various regions of the adenovirus types 2 and 41 genomes, and were evaluated by hybridization with a series of DNA quantities from 1 μg to 10 pg of one adenovirus type from each human subgenus, lambda phage, and HEp 2 cells. The sensitivity of hybridization with the HPII probe (92.7%), containing the conserved hexon gene, compared well with EM (54.6%), culture and neutralization (45.5%), and enzyme immunoassay (61.8%). The sensitivity of detection of enteric adenovirus isolates by the cloned Bg/II D fragment probe (92.9%) and by a synthetic probe (85.7%), manufactured from type‐specific sequences of the Ad41 hexon gene were comparable to Ad40/Ad41 specific enzyme immunoassay (84.6%). Hybridization was found to be a sensitive method of adenovirus detection in comparison to traditional methods of laboratory diagnosis. Synthetic oligonucleotides enable specific detection of individual enteric adenovirus types. Hybridization had additional advantages over other tests in identifying cases of infection with more than one adenovirus type and in allowing an estimate of the concentration of adenovirus in the specimen.

title: Approaches to overcome flow cytometry limitations in the analysis of cells from veterinary relevant species
abstract: BACKGROUND: Flow cytometry is a powerful tool for the multiparameter analysis of leukocyte subsets on the single cell level. Recent advances have greatly increased the number of fluorochrome-labeled antibodies in flow cytometry. In particular, an increase in available fluorochromes with distinct excitation and emission spectra combined with novel multicolor flow cytometers with several lasers have enhanced the generation of multidimensional expression data for leukocytes and other cell types. However, these advances have mainly benefited the analysis of human or mouse cell samples given the lack of reagents for most animal species. The flow cytometric analysis of important veterinary, agricultural, wildlife, and other animal species is still hampered by several technical limitations, even though animal species other than the mouse can serve as more accurate models of specific human physiology and diseases. RESULTS: Here we present time-tested approaches that our laboratory regularly uses in the multiparameter flow cytometric analysis of ovine leukocytes. The discussed approaches will be applicable to the analysis of cells from most animal species and include direct modification of antibodies by covalent conjugation or Fc-directed labeling (Zenon™ technology), labeled secondary antibodies and other second step reagents, labeled receptor ligands, and antibodies with species cross-reactivity. CONCLUSIONS: Using refined technical approaches, the number of parameters analyzed by flow cytometry per cell sample can be greatly increased, enabling multidimensional analysis of rare samples and giving critical insight into veterinary and other less commonly analyzed species. By maximizing information from each cell sample, multicolor flow cytometry can reduce the required number of animals used in a study.

title: iGPCR-Drug: A Web Server for Predicting Interaction between GPCRs and Drugs in Cellular Networking
abstract: Involved in many diseases such as cancer, diabetes, neurodegenerative, inflammatory and respiratory disorders, G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are among the most frequent targets of therapeutic drugs. It is time-consuming and expensive to determine whether a drug and a GPCR are to interact with each other in a cellular network purely by means of experimental techniques. Although some computational methods were developed in this regard based on the knowledge of the 3D (dimensional) structure of protein, unfortunately their usage is quite limited because the 3D structures for most GPCRs are still unknown. To overcome the situation, a sequence-based classifier, called “iGPCR-drug”, was developed to predict the interactions between GPCRs and drugs in cellular networking. In the predictor, the drug compound is formulated by a 2D (dimensional) fingerprint via a 256D vector, GPCR by the PseAAC (pseudo amino acid composition) generated with the grey model theory, and the prediction engine is operated by the fuzzy K-nearest neighbour algorithm. Moreover, a user-friendly web-server for iGPCR-drug was established at http://www.jci-bioinfo.cn/iGPCR-Drug/. For the convenience of most experimental scientists, a step-by-step guide is provided on how to use the web-server to get the desired results without the need to follow the complicated math equations presented in this paper just for its integrity. The overall success rate achieved by iGPCR-drug via the jackknife test was 85.5%, which is remarkably higher than the rate by the existing peer method developed in 2010 although no web server was ever established for it. It is anticipated that iGPCR-Drug may become a useful high throughput tool for both basic research and drug development, and that the approach presented here can also be extended to study other drug – target interaction networks.

title: Development of a reverse transcription recombinase polymerase based isothermal amplification coupled with lateral flow immunochromatographic assay (CTV-RT-RPA-LFICA) for rapid detection of Citrus tristeza virus
abstract:
Abstract
Citrus tristeza virus (CTV) is a global threat to citrus production and presents a major challenge for fast, reliable and accurate diagnostic tests. The development of an effective method for rapid detection of CTV is critical for timely management and minimization of the economic burden caused by this devastating viral disease. Present study describes the design, characterization, optimization and application of reverse transcription recombinase polymerase based isothermal amplification coupled with lateral flow immunochromatographic assay (CTV-RT-RPA-LFICA). This novel approach was developed following quantification of CTV DNA via real-time PCR which also provided information on primer/probe set pair validation as well as exponential reaction factors such as Ct values that guided various thermal cycling parameters in RT-RPA reactions including temperature optima. An overall detection limit up to 50 copies/μl genomic DNA was achieved within 30 minutes at 42°C without any amplification related bias or contaminations either during RT‐RPA or LFICA hybridization step making it suitable for point of care diagnostics applications in field epidemiology surveys.

title: The changing face of neurosurgery for the older person
abstract: Increased life expectancy and illness prevention and treatment have led to a growing population of older patients. These changes in patient population are apparent in neurosurgery; however, relatively little is reported about specific outcomes and prognostication in this group. This review summarises the challenges and management changes occurring in the treatment of three common neurosurgical pathologies; aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage, head injury, and haemorrhagic stroke. A move towards less invasive neurosurgical techniques has implications on the risk–benefit profile of interventions. This creates the opportunity to intervene in older patients with greater co-morbidity, as long as improved outcomes can be evidenced. A critical part of assessing appropriateness for surgical intervention in older patients may be to change from a mindset of age to one of frailty and growing interest in scales assessing this may aid treatment decisions in the future.

title: Rift Valley Fever – assessment of effectiveness of surveillance and control measures in the EU
abstract: Effectiveness of surveillance and control measures against Rift Valley Fever (RVF) in Mayotte (overseas France) and in continental EU were assessed using mathematical models. Surveillance for early detection of RVF virus circulation implies very low design prevalence values and thus sampling a high number of animals, so feasibility issues may rise. Passive surveillance based on notified abortions in ruminants is key for early warning and at present the only feasible surveillance option. The assessment of vaccination and culling against RVF in Mayotte suggests that vaccination is more effective when quickly implemented throughout the population, e.g. at a rate of 200 or 2,000 animals vaccinated per day. Test and cull is not an option for RVF control in Mayotte given the high number of animals that would need to be tested. If the risk of RVFV introduction into the continental EU increases, ruminant establishments close to possible points of disease incursion should be included in the surveillance. An enhanced surveillance on reproductive disorders should be applied during summer in risk areas. Serosurveillance targets of 0.3% animals should be at least considered. RVF control measures possibly applied in the continental EU have been assessed in the Netherlands, as an example. Culling animals on farms within a 20 km radius of detected farms appears as the most effective measure to control RVF spread, although too many animals should be culled. Alternative measures are vaccination in a 50 km radius around detection, ring vaccination between 20 and 50 km and culling of detected farms. The assessment of zoning showed that, following RVFV introduction and considering an R(0) = 2, a mean vector dispersal of 10 km and 10 farms initially detected, RVFV would spread beyond a radius of up to 100 km or 50 km from the infected area with 10% or 55% probability, respectively.

title: A meaning-centered spiritual care training program for hospice palliative care teams in South Korea: development and preliminary evaluation
abstract: This paper reports on the development, implementation, and preliminary evaluation of a new meaning-centered spiritual care (MCSC) training program for hospice palliative care teams in South Korea. To explore how MCSC is experienced by participants within this cultural context it draws upon case study methodology to investigate perceived changes in their understanding of and attitude toward spiritual intervention. A professional psychologist and two Senior Health Staff nurses provided information about process and outcomes through one-on-one semi structured interviews following a four day educational workshop delivered over two weekends with lectures, group work activities, volunteer patient visits at specialized medical centers, experience sharing among professionals from various fields and self reflection time.  Preliminary evaluation results suggest that the training contributed to increased awareness amongst participants regarding different types of symptoms during end of life care; enhanced perceptual ability while providing spiritual care; improved skillset confidence when conducting holistic interventions; as well as an overall appreciation of cultural differences between South Korea and North America when considering patient religion or spirituality needs.

title: The Behavior of Bacteria Designed for Biodegradation
abstract: Mineralization of organic molecules by microbes is essential for the carbon cycle to operate. The massive mobilization of compounds stored in natural resources, or the introduction of xenobiotics into the biosphere, leads to unidirectional fluxes, which result in the persistance of a number of chemicals in the biosphere, and thus constitute a source of pollution. Molecular biology offers the tools to optimize the biodegradative capacities of microorganisms, accelerate the evolution of “new” activities, and construct totally “new” pathways through the assemblage of catabolic segments from different microbes. Although the number of genetically engineered microbes (GEMs) for potential use in biodegradation is not large, these recombinant microbes function in microcosms according to their design. The survival and fate of recombinant microbes in different ecological niches under laboratory conditions is similar to what has been observed for the unmodified parental strains. rDNA, both on plasmids and on the host chromosome, is usually stably inherited by GEMs. The potential lateral transfer of rDNA from the GEMs to other microbes is significantly diminished, though not totally inhibited, when rDNA is incorporated on the host chromosome. The behavior and fate of GEMs can be predicted more accurately through the coupling of regulatory circuits that control the expression of catabolic pathways to killing genes, so that the GEMs survive in polluted environments, but die when the target chemical is eliminated.

title: Proposals for the classification of human rhinovirus species A, B and C into genotypically assigned types
abstract: This paper presents proposals for the classification of human rhinoviruses A, B and C into genotypically assigned types. Rhinoviruses are common causes of upper respiratory tract infections in humans, and previous genetic analyses have revealed a wide variety of genotypes among them; however, no systematic categorization has yet been established. The goal is to analyze the differential characteristics between different virus species with regard to their genomic make-up and evolutionary history in order to provide guidance on how they should be classified by type. Three criteria are proposed: 1) geographic distributions; 2) antigenic diversity; 3) nucleotide variation at specific genes within each genome segment. Biochemical and molecular methods will be used for selecting representative genomes from various groups in order to assess these criteria more accurately. Subsequently, reliable phylogenetic trees will be constructed using data from these genomes. The results from this analysis are expected to further improve our understanding about the evolution of human rhinoviruses as well as helping devise better control measures against them in future outbreaks, thus reducing morbidity rates due to these viruses..

title: Effect of experimentally-induced villus atrophy on adhesion of K88ac-positive Escherichia coli in just-weaned piglets
abstract: Three- to four-week-old, just-weaned piglets were infected with transmissible gastroenteritis (TGE) virus and the next day with K88ac(+) enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC). Histological examination of caudal jejunum and ileum of piglets killed 2–3 days after virus challenge (1–2 days after ETEC infection) revealed severe villus atrophy especially in the jejunum compared with controls (P<0.05). Four-5 days after TGE virus infection villus length increased and after 7 days it was near normal. Villi scraped from jejunal and ileal mucosa of the piglets were incubated in vitro with K88ac(+)E. coli and the number of bacteria adhering to 250 μm villus brush border was counted. Attachment of bacteria to villi of piglets killed 2–3 days after TGE virus infection was significantly decreased in comparison with adhesion to villi of non-infected piglets or of piglets killed 7 days after the virus infection. Correlation between in vitro adhesion and villus height was 0.6649 (P<0.001). The results suggest that the experimentally-induced villus atrophy was attended with a temporarily diminished susceptibility of villus enterocytes to adhesion of K88ac(+)E. coli.

title: A Harm Reduction Approach to Treating Opioid Use Disorder in an Independent Primary Care Practice: a Qualitative Study
abstract: This qualitative study seeks to understand the perceptions of independent primary care practitioners and their health teams on the effectiveness and acceptability of a harm reduction approach in treating opioid use disorder (OUD) patients. The purpose is to assess if there are opportunities to enable primary care practices to become more involved in supporting OUD patients, who often lack access to specialized treatment services. A mixed-methods approach including documentary analysis and semi-structured interviews will be used for data collection from five different sites across Canada. The findings from this study may offer insight into some potential professional roles for general practitioners (GPs) within OUD treatment ecosystems that meet GPs’ preferential working conditions without compromising patient safety or quality of delivery. Ultimately, it could provide valuable information on how implementing a harm reduction strategy within an independent practice would benefit both clinicians and their OUD patients alike by improving healthcare outcomes overall.

title: Epidemic variability in hierarchical geographical networks with human activity patterns
abstract: Recently, some studies have revealed that non-Poissonian statistics of human behaviors stem from the hierarchical geographical network structure. On this view, we focus on epidemic spreading in the hierarchical geographical networks and study how two distinct contact patterns (i.e., homogeneous time delay (HOTD) and heterogeneous time delay (HETD) associated with geographical distance) influence the spreading speed and the variability of outbreaks. We find that, compared with HOTD and null model, correlations between time delay and network hierarchy in HETD remarkably slow down epidemic spreading and result in an upward cascading multi-modal phenomenon. Proportionately, the variability of outbreaks in HETD has the lower value, but several comparable peaks for a long time, which makes the long-term prediction of epidemic spreading hard. When a seed (i.e., the initial infected node) is from the high layers of networks, epidemic spreading is remarkably promoted. Interestingly, distinct trends of variabilities in two contact patterns emerge: high-layer seeds in HOTD result in the lower variabilities, the case of HETD is opposite. More importantly, the variabilities of high-layer seeds in HETD are much greater than that in HOTD, which implies the unpredictability of epidemic spreading in hierarchical geographical networks.

title: New Methods Used in Pharmacokinetics and Therapeutic Monitoring of the First and Newer Generations of Antiepileptic Drugs (AEDs)
abstract: The review presents data from the last few years on bioanalytical methods used in therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of the 1st–3rd generation and the newest antiepileptic drug (AEDs) cenobamate in patients with various forms of seizures. Chemical classification, structure, mechanism of action, pharmacokinetic data and therapeutic ranges for total and free fractions and interactions were collected. The primary data on bioanalytical methods for AEDs determination included biological matrices, sample preparation, dried blood spot (DBS) analysis, column resolution, detection method, validation parameters, and clinical utility. In conclusion, the most frequently described method used in AED analysis is the LC-based technique (HPLC, UHPLC, USLC) combined with highly sensitive mass detection or fluorescence detection. However, less sensitive UV is also used. Capillary electrophoresis and gas chromatography have been rarely applied. Besides the precipitation of proteins or LLE, an automatic SPE is often a sample preparation method. Derivatization was also indicated to improve sensitivity and automate the analysis. The usefulness of the methods for TDM was also highlighted.

title: Dual-targeting nanoparticle vaccine elicits a therapeutic antibody response against chronic hepatitis B
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of a dual-targeting nanoparticle vaccine in eliciting an antibody response against chronic Hepatitis B. The aim was to explore delivery strategies using peptide conjugates, with and without adjuvants, as potential therapeutics. By assessing the functional efficacy of antibody responses against Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and its core product (HBcAg), this research builds upon recent studies aimed at developing protective vaccines for chronic HBV infection. A unique design that combined antigens from both proteins into one vaccine formulation was used successfully to induce a sustained immunological memory protection, indicating it could be applied broadly in clinical settings for therapeutic interventions. Analysis revealed a significant increase in IgG production after two rounds of vaccination compared to single vaccinations alone, demonstrating that incorporation of peptides from both antigens improves chances for hepatitis vaccine success. This breakthrough provides hope towards conquering one of the world’s most pressing health concerns: chronic viral infections such as Hepatitis B virus.

title: ‘I’m sorry to hear that’—Empathy and Empathic Dissonance: the Perspectives of PA Students
abstract: This paper explores how the empathy levels of Physician Assistants (PAs) contribute to empathic dissonance in their professional interactions. Through a qualitative method, medical students and PAs were studied to ascertain how they feel about showing empathy and its effects on patients, as well as its implications on inter-professional dynamics. Findings will offer insights into factors that influence PA empathy at different stages of training while also providing theoretical evidence for a correlation between physician, patient relationships and performance outcomes. title: Two models of multiple sclerosis: Experimental allergic encephalomyelitis (EAE) and theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV) infection. A pathological and immunological comparison
abstract:
Title: Two models of multiple sclerosis: Experimental allergic encephalomyelitis (EAE) and theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV) infection. A pathological and immunological comparison 

Multiple sclerosis is a debilitating disease of the central nervous system with a multi-faceted etiology and pathogenesis remaining largely unknown. Researchers have created in vivo animal models to study varying aspects of this condition, including its expression patterns, pathology changes in neuronal tissue, and ensuing immune response. This paper seeks to compare two such models – experimental allergic encephalomyelitis (EAE) induced by antigen injections, as well as Theiler’s murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV). Immunohistochemical assessments were performed on brain tissue from infected mice, comparing several common markers indicative of inflammation or glial reactions. As expected within EAE lesions there was evidence for acute microglial/macrophage infiltration along with demyelination; however TMEV-infected brains also demonstrated similar histopathological features although possibly at later stages than seen in EAE mice due to an apparent latency period before signs appeared clinically. Findings confirm that these two infectious agents can generate multiphasic inflammatory responses from resident glia compatible with many elements associated with inflammatory forms of human Multiple Sclerosis ostensibly through different mechanisms for induction but converging toward shared conclusions about differences between those infections likely engendered because of strain-dependent nuances among both organisms which demands further exploration into their causative associations so that more effective treatments may be proposed based upon insights gleaned therein.

title: Human Microbiota-Associated Swine: Current Progress and Future Opportunities
abstract: Gnotobiotic (GN) rodent models have provided insight into the contributions of the gut microbiota to host health and preventing disease. However, rodent models are limited by several important physiological and metabolic differences from humans, and many rodent models do not dependably replicate the clinical manifestations of human diseases. Due to the high degree of similarity in anatomy, physiology, immunology and brain growth, the domestic pig (Sus scrofa) is considered a clinically relevant model to study factors influencing human gastrointestinal, immune, and brain development. Gnotobiotic piglet models have been developed and shown to recapitulate key aspects of GN rodent models. Human microbiota-associated (HMA) piglets have been established using inocula from infants, children, and adults. The gut microbiota of recipient HMA piglets was more similar to that of the human donor than that of conventionally reared piglets harboring a pig microbiota. Moreover, Bifidobacterium and Bacteroides, two predominant bacterial groups of infant gut, were successfully established in the HMA piglets. Thus, the HMA pig model has the potential to be a valuable model for investigating how the gut microbiota composition changes in response to environmental factors, such as age, diet, vaccination, antibiotic use and infection. The HMA also represents a robust model for screening the efficacy of pre- and probiotic interventions. Lastly, HMA piglets can be an ideal model with which to elucidate microbe–host interactions in human health and disease due to the similarities to humans in anatomy, physiology, developmental maturity at birth, and the pathophysiology of many human diseases.

title: Enhanced mitophagy in bronchial fibroblasts from severe asthmatic patients
abstract: The title of this paper is “Enhanced mitophagy in bronchial fibroblasts from severe asthmatic patients”. Asthma, a common chronic respiratory disorder affecting approximately 300 million people worldwide, is characterized by inflammation and destruction of alveolar walls as well as exaggerated airway smooth muscle tone. While the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear, evidence suggests that increased autophagic cellular activity plays an important role in severe asthma. To explore the pathophysiological implications of mitophagy process on pulmonary diseases such as asthma, we studied the levels of mitophagy and its effectors in bronchial fibroblast cells isolated from severe asthmatics and healthy subjects under various conditions. Our results revealed altered activity profiles for core fold elements involved in mitochondrial homeostasis pathways along with substantially higher protein expression levels for mitochondrial-specific unfolded protein response (UPRm) proteins indicating higher levels of mitochondrial stress and enhanced mitophagesis respectively. Moreover, mildly acidic pH further enhanced these effects while modulation at physiological pH could reverse some morphological alterations observed following acid stimulation suggesting possible therapeutic avenues against this debilitating illness. Taken together with existing literature findings our study addresses critical mechanisms contributing to aberrant pulmonary disease progression through overexpression or deregulation of certain functional pathways thereby elucidating novel preventive measures for management purposes in future scenarios

title: Rotavirus excretion by kids in a naturally infected goat herd
abstract: This article introduces a study exploring the excretion of rotavirus by kids in naturally infected goat herds. Rotaviruses are highly contagious, animal-borne agents that can cause severe diarrhoea and vomiting, making them of considerable public interest. Recent evidence indicates that there is potential for exposure to rotavirus in small ruminant species, with implications for both human and animal health worldwide. To assess the impact of natural infections on kid shedding of rotavirus, an observational cohort was conducted throughout two years to determine differences in excreted viruses between 1-month old goats and 6-month old sheep under intensive management practices. The results indicated significant differences in age groups and gender related coinfections with bovine diarrhea virus (BVDV) coexcretion across different regions therefore contributing to shed light on the role of local viral factors determining viral shedding patterns within herd environment . This publication highlights the need for improved strategic biosecurity policies including planned vaccination schedulings depending upon regional climatic conditions against outbreaks due to Rotavirus infection as well as other important enteric diseases like BVDV in order to reduce long term detrimental effects surrounding possible zoonotic spillovers..

title: A comprehensive metagenomics framework to characterize organisms relevant for planetary protection
abstract: This paper discusses the development of a comprehensive metagenomics framework for characterizing organisms relevant to planetary protection. Planetary protection is an important concept in preventing contamination of the Earth, Moon, and other planets by microbial agents brought from Earth or created on other celestial bodies. As such, it is critical that we better understand the ecology of microorganisms in different environments and be able to identify them accurately with minimal laborious investigation. The development of a metagenomic system that harnesses existing DNA sequencing technologies offers an effective approach to efficiently quantify different species as well as determine their biological functions. In this study, we present a refined version of our previously published pipeline designed for high-throughput bacterial identification using Illumina sequence data generated from next generation sequencing platforms. Improvements include enhanced implementation for calculating abundance estimates across multiple taxonomical domains (phylum through species level) and more comprehensive coverage in identifying prokaryotic genetic elements associated with various types of ecological features: metabolic pathways, catabolism-related proteins and antimicrobial resistance/virulence factors. Additionally, statistical tests are incorporated for further characterization including automated determination of rarefaction curves plots combined with diversity indices measurements at various hierarchies levels . title: Ethics Consultation for Adult Solid Organ Transplantation Candidates and Recipients: A Single Centre Experience
abstract: Systematic study of the intersection of ethics consultation services and solid organ transplants and recipients can identify and illustrate ethical issues that arise in the clinical care of these patients, including challenges beyond resource allocation. This was a single-centre, retrospective cohort study of all adult ethics consultations between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2017, at a large academic medical centre in the north-eastern United States. Of the 880 ethics consultations, sixty (6.8 per cent ) involved solid organ transplant, thirty-nine (65.0 per cent) for candidates and twenty-one (35.0 per cent ) for recipients. Ethics consultations were requested for 4.3 per cent of heart, 4.9 per cent of lung, 0.3 per cent of liver, and 0.3 per cent of kidney transplant recipients over the study period. Nurses were more likely to request ethics consultations for recipients than physicians (80.0 per cent vs 20.0 per cent , p = 0.006). The most common reason for consultation among transplant candidates was discussion about intensity of treatment or goals of care after the patient was not or was no longer a transplant candidate. The most common reason for ethics consultation among transplant recipients was disagreement between transplant providers and patients/families/non-transplant healthcare professionals over the appropriate intensity of treatment for recipients. Very few consultations involved questions about appropriate resource allocation. Ethics consultants involved in these cases most often navigated communication challenges between transplant and non-transplant healthcare professionals and patients and families.
