title: Preclinical evaluation of AT-527, a novel guanosine nucleotide prodrug with potent, pan-genotypic activity against hepatitis C virus
abstract: Despite the availability of highly effective direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens for the treatment of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, sustained viral response (SVR) rates remain suboptimal for difficult-to-treat patient populations such as those with HCV genotype 3, cirrhosis or prior treatment experience, warranting development of more potent HCV replication antivirals. AT-527 is the hemi-sulfate salt of AT-511, a novel phosphoramidate prodrug of 2’-fluoro-2’-C-methylguanosine-5'-monophosphate that has potent in vitro activity against HCV. The EC(50) of AT-511, determined using HCV laboratory strains and clinical isolates with genotypes 1–5, ranged from 5–28 nM. The active 5'-triphosphate metabolite, AT-9010, specifically inhibited the HCV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. AT-511 did not inhibit the replication of other selected RNA or DNA viruses in vitro. AT-511 was approximately 10-fold more active than sofosbuvir (SOF) against a panel of laboratory strains and clinical isolates of HCV genotypes 1–5 and remained fully active against S282T resistance-associated variants, with up to 58-fold more potency than SOF. In vitro, AT-511 did not inhibit human DNA polymerases or elicit cytotoxicity or mitochondrial toxicity at concentrations up to 100 μM. Unlike the other potent guanosine analogs PSI-938 and PSI-661, no mutagenic O(6)-alkylguanine bases were formed when incubated with cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and AT-511 had IC(50) values ≥25 μM against a panel of CYP enzymes. In hepatocytes from multiple species, the active triphosphate was the predominant metabolite produced from the prodrug, with a half-life of 10 h in human hepatocytes. When given orally to rats and monkeys, AT-527 preferentially delivered high levels of AT-9010 in the liver in vivo. These favorable preclinical attributes support the ongoing clinical development of AT-527 and suggest that, when used in combination with an HCV DAA from a different class, AT-527 may increase SVR rates, especially for difficult-to-treat patient populations, and could potentially shorten treatment duration for all patients.

title: Effect of HA330 resin-directed hemoadsorption on a porcine acute respiratory distress syndrome model
abstract: BACKGROUND: Blood purification is an emerging approach to dampening the cytokine storm. This study aims to assess the efficacy of HA330 resin-directed hemoadsorption (HA) on endotoxin-induced porcine acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) model. METHODS: Twenty-four Chinese domestic pigs were allocated into saline group receiving intravenous infusion of saline (N = 6) and endotoxin group receiving intravenous infusion of LPS (N = 18). When ALI model was initially diagnosed, six pigs in the LPS and saline group were killed for BALF and histopathological analysis. The remaining 12 pigs in LPS group received 3-h HA (N = 6) or HA-sham (N = 6) treatment, respectively. Following another 5-h observation, animals were killed. Variables on hemodynamics, blood gases and lung mechanics were recorded at a series of time points. Differentially expressed cytokines and proteins were determined by ELISA and proteomics. RESULTS: HA treatment significantly improved injured oxygenation induced by LPS. HA also partially improved the barrier permeability and reduced lung edema and inflammation/injury induced by LPS infusion. Proteomic analysis showed the differentially expressed proteins between HA- and HA-sham-treated groups mostly belonged to the categories of acute inflammation/immune response, and proteolysis. CONCLUSIONS: Hemoadsorption improved ARDS possibly by blunting the cytokine storm and by restoring homeostasis of the disordered proteome milieu in the exudative phase. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (doi:10.1186/s13613-017-0287-0) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

title: Database resources of the National Center for Biotechnology Information
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to discuss the Database Resources of the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). This resource is one of the premier sources for biotechnological and genomic data. Established by the United States National Institutes of Health in 1988, NCBI has become a global leader in its field, providing essential support to ongoing research into genetic diseases, potential treatments and much more. Herein, we review NCBI's comprehensive collection of bioinformatics databases and explore how they can be used by scientists from various disciplines to aid their research processes. We highlight specific areas where these databases are critical such as disease-causing genes identification or drug target validation and explain how each type within NCBI contributes something unique towards providing an understanding into genetic causation. The discussion further introduces other freely available toolkits developed with these databases that automate laborious tasks for researchers working on sequence analysis projects through graphical user interfaces or command line options as per necessity

title: Clinical features, complications and atypical manifestations of children with severe forms of dengue hemorrhagic fever in South India
abstract: This study focused on the clinical features, complications, and atypical manifestations of children with severe forms of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) in South India. Despite continued efforts to reduce disease incidence through control measures, DHF remains a common occurrence in this region. Aims were to better understand the spectrum of DHF presentation among pediatric patients and examine associated risk factors for negative outcomes such as death or organ failure. A prospective cohort analysis was conducted over seven years, involving 168 hospitalized children aged 6 months to 12 years diagnosed with severe DHF based on World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. title: Blockage of Store-Operated Ca(2+) Influx by Synta66 is Mediated by Direct Inhibition of the Ca(2+) Selective Orai1 Pore
abstract: SIMPLE SUMMARY: Store-operated calcium channels constituted from the proteins Orai and STIM are important targets for development of new drugs, especially for the treatment of auto-immune diseases. Also, interference with channel function is linked to reduced cancer cell progression, making these channels potential targets for anti-cancer drug development. Therefore, inhibitors need to be evaluated for both their binding selectivity and their potential to interfere with cancer progression. Here, we investigated the inhibitor Synta66 and determined its site of binding via both patch clamp recordings and computational approaches and evaluated its potency as anti-cancer agent in glioblastoma multiforme cells. Our findings show that Synta66 is a highly selective ligand to the Orai1 pore and efficiently blocks store operated calcium entry in glioblastoma cells. Still, in the tested cell lines, Synta66 did not reduce cell viability. We therefore suggest Synta66 as a precise tool to observe interference of store-operated Orai1 channel function in vitro and of resulting downstream effects. ABSTRACT: The Ca(2+) sensor STIM1 and the Ca(2+) channel Orai1 that form the store-operated Ca(2+) (SOC) channel complex are key targets for drug development. Selective SOC inhibitors are currently undergoing clinical evaluation for the treatment of auto-immune and inflammatory responses and are also deemed promising anti-neoplastic agents since SOC channels are linked with enhanced cancer cell progression. Here, we describe an investigation of the site of binding of the selective inhibitor Synta66 to the SOC channel Orai1 using docking and molecular dynamics simulations, and live cell recordings. Synta66 binding was localized to the extracellular site close to the transmembrane (TM)1 and TM3 helices and the extracellular loop segments, which, importantly, are adjacent to the Orai1-selectivity filter. Synta66-sensitivity of the Orai1 pore was, in fact, diminished by both Orai1 mutations affecting Ca(2+) selectivity and permeation of Na(+) in the absence of Ca(2+). Synta66 also efficiently blocked SOC in three glioblastoma cell lines but failed to interfere with cell viability, division and migration. These experiments provide new structural and functional insights into selective drug inhibition of the Orai1 Ca(2+) channel by a high-affinity pore blocker.

title: Correcting the Actual Reproduction Number: A Simple Method to Estimate R(0) from Early Epidemic Growth Data
abstract: The basic reproduction number, R(0), a summary measure of the transmission potential of an infectious disease, is estimated from early epidemic growth rate, but a likelihood-based method for the estimation has yet to be developed. The present study corrects the concept of the actual reproduction number, offering a simple framework for estimating R(0) without assuming exponential growth of cases. The proposed method is applied to the HIV epidemic in European countries, yielding R(0) values ranging from 3.60 to 3.74, consistent with those based on the Euler-Lotka equation. The method also permits calculating the expected value of R(0) using a spreadsheet.

title: Long-term follow-up of autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for refractory juvenile dermatomyositis: a case-series study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To follow up the refractory juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT) in a long time and to investigate whether AHSCT is effective and safe to treat refractory JDM. METHODS: We collected the AHSCT and follow-up data of three patients with refractory JDM who received autologous peripheral blood CD34+ cell transplantation in our hospital between June 2004 and July 2015. Those data include: hight, weight, routine blood and urine tests, ESR, CK, ALT, AST, LDH, renal functional tests, lymphocyte subpopulations, HRCT and muscle MRI. The last follow-up was done in June 2017. RESULTS: All three patients had complete remission and could stop prednisone after 3–12 months. None of them relapsed at 144, 113 and 23 months follow-up. Twelve months after their AHSCT, all of their monitoring indexes have returned to normal and they have stopped all medications. Until the date of this article, none of them relapsed or need medicine. CONCLUSION: Our study suggests that AHSCT is safe and effective in treating refractory JDM, and it can provides long term drug-free survival. However, more cases are needed for further confirmation.

title: Prediction Model of Deep Learning for Ambulance Transports in Kesennuma City by Meteorological Data
abstract: This study presents a prediction model of deep learning for ambulance transports in Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan based on meteorological data. This paper proposes to implement an artificial neural network with multiple hidden layers to predict the number of ambulance transports from forecasted or actual meteorological conditions. The input variables are air temperature and pressure, wind speed and direction, relative humidity and cloud cover. To evaluate the efficacy of this proposed model’s predictive capabilities versus existing models used by transportation agencies in town, we conducted a comparative analysis using two sets of data: one simulating possible patterns observed under various weather conditions in Kesennuma City between 2010-2015 (the training dataset) and one containing observations collected during 2016-2017 (the test dataset). Our results demonstrate that the proposed prediction model outperforms current models when trained against the simulation data. Furthermore, when tested against the independent observation data set found significant improvement despite some areas requiring further fine tuning. This novel development could prove useful as either an alternative to or complement existing prediction methods employed by transportation systems in town due to its functional application potential pertaining specifically towards geographical environments similar to those encountered within Katsunuma city limits making it structurally cost efficient than traditional forecasting applications involving hand labor or large infrastructural equipment investments.

title: Functional Limitations of Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cells Limit Type I Interferon, T Cell Responses and Virus Control in Early Life
abstract: This article explores the functional limitations of plasmacytoid dendritic cells that limit type I interferon, T cell responses and virus control in early life. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) are recognized as critical effector immune cells with a central role in initiating early antiviral immunity. In addition to their potential role in adjuvant activity and other immunomodulatory functions, pDCs also possess numerous features that suggest an important capacity for regulating host immune homeostasis during acute viral infections. However, evidence suggests that pDC numbers and function significantly diminish with increasing age due to both environmental influences such as aging-associated stressors or chronic inflammation and intrinsic mechanisms associated with age-related changes in gene expression. As a result, specific populations of individuals, like infants and young children most vulnerable to infection at this developmental stage may be inadequately defended these against impacting viruses at an increased risk for severe outcomes due to impaired innate anti-viral defences which impair response to vaccines or treatments thereof. This study reviews current knowledge on the ability of pDCs provide appropriate level of defence against life threatening viruses via optimal production of Interferons thus providing insight into improved clinical treatments suitable especially for those considered most vulnerable including neonates or premature infants exposed to infection hours after birth.

title: Protection against feline infectious peritonitis by intranasal inoculation of a temperature-sensitive FIPV vaccine
abstract: This study highlights a novel approach to immunizing house cats against feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) utilizing intranasal inoculation of a temperature-sensitive FIPV vaccine. To test this hypothesis, we conducted an experiment with 15 healthy cats ranging in age from one-to-three years old over the course 10 weeks. We have discovered that 80% of cats administered intranasal FIPV vaccine are completely protected against all forms of FIP until 24 weeks post vaccination as opposed to zero protection in the control group when exposed to wild type virus after 26th week post vaccination. Our results suggest that this method can provide effective and long-term protection for house cats against severe forms of FIP infections which was not observed within the reported studies before. This approach opens up new directions for vaccinating pet cats against life threatening diseases like FIP without any adverse reactions and has potential implications on other animal populations worldwide.

title: Symptom clusters in cancer patients: An Italian survey to validate and describe unwarranted clinical variation, inequality in access to healthcare, knowledge, and risk of malpractice
abstract: This paper explores the symptom clusters in cancer patients and Italy's healthcare framework to validate, describe and assess unwarranted clinical variation, lack of access to healthcare services, knowledge, and risk of malpractice. Drawing upon empirical data collected from an original survey conducted with 60 Italian cancer patients at 11 hospitals spread across 7 regions as well as separately interviews with 10 oncologists plus 5 expert radiologists practising over 6-months period (November 2019 - April 2020), this research will draw attention to the predictors linking symptom cluster variations by socio demographic factors present in Italian society such as gender/ethnicity, educational attainment etc., providing a comprehensive evidence based analysis for stakeholders in identifying what approaches are necessary for successful action plan delivery concerning unmet needs resulting from geographic disparities within hospitals regarding access to health care among cancer patient populations. Furthermore aimed outcomes will be sought addressing pressing issues like how improvements can be affected when considering socio economic inequalities among cancer patient populations that may lead to better prevention strategies while reducing risks of medical malpractice noncompliance through focused collaborative work between practitioners and other professionals involved.

title: Ambulatory and stationary healthcare use in survivors of ARDS during the first year after discharge from ICU: findings from the DACAPO cohort
abstract: This study describes the healthcare utilization of survivors of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) during their first post-intensive care unit (ICU) year. Using data from Eindhoven Cohort on Acute Disease and Post-Intensive Care Outcome (DACAPO), ambulatory care visits as well as readmissions to stationary health units were evaluated in 328 ARDS survivors admitted at ICUs between October 2017 and November 2019. Findings showed considerable higher use of both ambulatory and stationary care in the first 12 months after discharge when compared with pre-discharge usage. Survivors visited primary centers 5.6 days/year, suggesting frequent monitoring by family physicians, along with 3-4 times hospital stationery visits due to secondary events such as sepsis or new episodes of organ failure necessitating treatment for recurrences or comorbidities development.. Our results show that ARDS patients require long term support specifically tailored towards this population's needs which goes beyond traditional approaches to treat comorbid conditions only associated with other diseases,. Key implications for healthcare practice are discussed herein citing potential adaptation strategies according with infrastructure patient surveillance systems currently applied across Europe.

title: Preparedness of community-based organisations in biohazard: reliability and validity of an assessment tool
abstract: The purpose of this study was to develop a tool for community-based health organisations (CBHOs) to evaluate the preparedness in biohazards concerning epidemics or bioterrorism. We searched concepts on partnerships of CBHOs with health systems in guidelines of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and literature. Then, we validated the researcher-made tool by face validity, content validity, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and criterion validity. Data were collected by sending the tool to 620 CBHOs serving under supervision of Iran’s ministry of health. Opinions of health professionals and stakeholders in CBHOs were used to assess face and content validity. Factor loads in EFA were based on three-factor structure that verified by CFA. We used SPSS V.18 and Mplus7 software for statistical analysis. About 105 health-based CBHOs participated. After conducting face validity and calculating content validity ratio and content validity index, we reached 54 items in the field of planning, training and infrastructure. We conducted construct validity using 105 CBHOs. Three items exchanged between the fields according to factor loads in EFA, and CFA verified the model fit as Comparative Fit Index, Tucker-Lewis index and root mean square error of approximation were 0.921, 0918 and 0.052, respectively. The Cronbach’s of the whole tool was 0.944. Spearman correlation coefficient confirmed criterion validity as coefficient was 0.736. Planning, training and infrastructure fields are the most important aspects of preparedness in health-based CBHOs. Applying the new assessment tool in future studies will show the weaknesses and capabilities of health-based CBHOs in biohazard and clear necessary intervention actions for health authorities.

title: Global Regulatory Landscape for Aggregate Safety Assessments: Recent Developments and Future Directions
abstract: Notwithstanding successful harmonization efforts, the global regulatory framework governing product safety is complex and continually evolving, as evidenced by additional regional guidance and regulations. In this regulatory review, we provide an overview from both global and regional perspectives. A historical perspective, with a focus on recent developments, enables identification of important long–term trends, such as a shift from single–case medical review of serious adverse events to an interdisciplinary evaluation of aggregate data for the purpose of judging product causality and informing benefit–risk assessments. We will show how these trends lead to opportunities for closer interdisciplinary collaboration, for bridging the gap between preand postmarketing surveillance, and for a more proactive determination of patient populations with a positive benefit–risk profile for product use. We will conclude by pointing to ongoing and future work that seeks to provide specific solutions for ongoing aggregate safety evaluation.

title: A study on the relationships of place attachment and individual attributes of residents in different vulnerable districts in Taipei, Taiwan
abstract: Under the impact of climate change, Taiwan, an island state, has faced the challenges of extreme weather events in recent years. Based on previous studies on climate change and vulnerability in Taipei, Taiwan, this study explores the correlations between place attachment and individual attributes of residents in different vulnerable areas in Taipei. First, this study investigates the integrated vulnerability (IV) of 12 districts of Taipei by overlaying natural vulnerability (NV) and social vulnerability (SV). This study selects four districts with high IV and low IV in Taipei, and with a large proportion of flooded areas, as the study sites. Second, a questionnaire survey (600 respondents) is conducted to examine the correlations between place attachment and the individual attributes of the respondents (age, residence duration, disaster experience, and education) in the four districts. Third, factor analyses are carried out to categorize place attachment into four factors: “security,” “familiarity,” “belongingness,” and “rootedness.” Finally, whether different factors have different relationships with place attachment are elucidated. The results show no consistent correlations between place attachment and individual attributes in areas with different vulnerabilities. Furthermore, by comparing the correlations before and after factor analyses of place attachment, among the four factors of place attachment (security, familiarity, belongingness, rootedness), there are no factors significantly relating to overall place attachment. This study further examines the mediator effect between risk experience and place attachment. The results show no mediator effects in the relationships of “perception → place attachment → coping behavior” and “attitude → place attachment → coping behavior.” Follow-up studies can elucidate factor analyses of place attachment and examine the effect of geographical scale (neighborhood, district, and city) on place attachment.

title: Yeast display platform technology to prepare oral vaccine against lethal H7N9 virus challenge in mice
abstract: This paper presents a study on the use of yeast display platform technology to prepare oral vaccine against lethal H7N9 virus challenge in mice. Novel strategies combining gene cloning, directed evolution and computational protein design enabled the scientists to discover an effective antigenic epitope from NS1 pseudotyped A/H7N9 influenza virus for preventing pulmonary damage and morbidity in mice. Analysis by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, immunoglobulin G flow cytometry, lung homogenate viral titers assay as well as histopathological examination revealed that successful elicitation of functional antibody responses using this vaccine effectively regarded as long-term protection against lethal H7N9 infection and thus promising resources to control influenza pandemics.

title: An example of clinical inertia in geriatrics
abstract: Clinical inertia is an understudied issue in geriatrics among health-care providers, with distinct ramifications for the elderly population. This paper presents an example of clinical inertia faced by a middle-aged female patient admitted to a nursing home due to frailty and advanced age; this case illustrates how inappropriate medical interventions can negatively impact a patient’s long-term care plan and quality of life. By examining the woman’s course of treatment, her failure to adhere to prescribed protocols, and physician decisions at play throughout her stay in the facility, we are able to gain insight into the broader issue of insufficient communication between healthcare providers and issues related directly or indirectly with clinical inertia. Through recognition of key symptoms associated with potential adverse outcomes early on in her hospital stay as well as better collaboration among involved personnel, it is posited that further escalation could have been prevented. Notably, greater attention needs be given towards decreasing mental misrepresentations which challenge current studies regarding appropriate healthcare utilization within geriatric settings. title: Burnout, anxiety and depression risk in medical doctors working in KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa: Evidence from a multi-site study of resource-constrained government hospitals in a generalised HIV epidemic setting
abstract: 'Burnout, Anxiety and Depression Risk in Medical Doctors Working in KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa: Evidence from a Multi-Site Study of Resource-Constrained Government Hospitals in a Generalised HIV Epidemic Setting'. This study examined the prevalence of burnout, anxiety symptoms, and depression among medical doctors working within the resource-constrained government hospitals located within KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. Data were collected through face to face interviews with 441 participants using validated tools measuring mental health outcomes containing three subscales each for burnout (emotional exhaustion, cynicism and reduced efficacy), anxiety (psychological distress) and depressive symptoms (difficulty concentrating). Our results show that 63.04% of medical doctors have moderate levels or higher on emotional exhaustion scale; 37.02 % have moderate levels or higher on cynicism scale; 55.34% have moderately high to extremely high level risk scores associated with developing depressive disorder along with 34.14 % having moderately low to extremely low level anxiety symptom severity. The findings provide some evidence into the need for greater understanding of psychological effects upon healthcare professionals during epidemics such as HIV pandemic particularly those working within limited resources countries like South Africa so that appropriate interventions may be developed to enhance their wellbeing and performance at work place environment leading potentially improved patient care outcome due to better availability staff resulting from reduction in unnecessary absenteeism related mental illness issues .

title: Fluorine makes a difference
abstract: This article explores the effect of Fluoride on periapical disease and its impact on dental health. It investigates fluoride levels in different populations across the globe, as well as their effectiveness towards oral hygiene habits and periodontal cases. Results confirmed that increased consumption of fluoridated products substantially decreased tooth decay rates compared to non-fluoridated counterparts, with positive implications for those seeking more effective preventative care options.

title: A Strain-Specific Inhibitor of Receptor-Bound HIV-1 Targets a Pocket near the Fusion Peptide
abstract: This study examines the potential of novel inhibitors as a promising strategy for HIV-1 therapy. We present the discovery of a strain-specific inhibitor (SMXRXD16), showing that it binds to the receptor binding site on HIV-1 and targets a pocket close to the fusion peptide. Computational docking studies suggest efficacy in inhibiting virus infectivity, while biochemical assays demonstrate disease inhibition in vitro. In vivo testing showed partial protection from infection when compared to untreated control mice. We evaluate SMXRXD16's therapeutic utility by highlighting its ability to inhibit viral activities without causing collateral damage or forming drug resistance, making it an attractive therapeutic option for consideration against various strains of HIV-1 using further preclinical evaluation and clinical trials.

title: Actin cytoskeletal inhibitor 19,20-epoxycytochalasin Q sensitizes yeast cells lacking ERG6 through actin-targeting and secondarily through disruption of lipid homeostasis
abstract: This paper aims to explore the effects of 19,20-epoxycytochalasin Q (ECQ), an actin cytoskeletal inhibitor, on yeast cells lacking ERG6. Through a series of experiments including gene expression analysis and liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry, we demonstrate that ECQ induces a unique form of cellular stress in yeast cells which leads to its selectivity towards these mutant variants. The results indicate that ECQ sensitizes yeast cells through two distinct mechanisms: firstly by targeting actins and secondly by disrupting lipid homeostasis. We also discuss our findings within the broader context of molecular pathways regulating essential cellular functions such as organization, polarization and metabolism for optimal fitness. Our data suggest a novel pathway linking actin dysfunction caused by ECQ treatment and perturbation in metabolic processes contributing to sensitivity towards drugs important for cancer therapy development or antivirulence strategies.

title: Modeling the effect of comprehensive interventions on Ebola virus transmission
abstract: Since the re-emergence of Ebola in West Africa in 2014, comprehensive and stringent interventions have been implemented to decelerate the spread of the disease. The effectiveness of interventions still remains unclear. In this paper, we develop an epidemiological model that includes various controlling measures to systematically evaluate their effects on the disease transmission dynamics. By fitting the model to reported cumulative cases and deaths in Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia until March 22, 2015, we estimate the basic reproduction number in these countries as 1.2552, 1.6093 and 1.7994, respectively. Model analysis shows that there exists a threshold of the effectiveness of isolation, below which increasing the fraction of latent individuals diagnosed prior to symptoms onset or shortening the duration between symptoms onset and isolation may lead to more Ebola infection. This challenges an existing view. Media coverage plays a substantial role in reducing the final epidemic size. The response to reported cumulative infected cases and deaths may have a different effect on the epidemic spread in different countries. Among all the interventions, we find that shortening the duration between death and burial and improving the effectiveness of isolation are two effective interventions for controlling the outbreak of Ebola virus infection.

title: Influenza A Virus on Oceanic Islands: Host and Viral Diversity in Seabirds in the Western Indian Ocean
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of Influenza A Virus (IAV) on oceanic islands, host and viral diversity in seabirds dwelling in the Western Indian Ocean. IAV is one of the most common infectious agents affecting birds and can be established as an important factor influencing host health, demography and species composition on remote offshore islands. We examine which bird species are affected by IAV infection and analyse potential environmental drivers underlying disease prevalence among distinct species across multiple island sites. We collected samples from different types of seabirds inhabiting six archipelagos within the Western Indian Ocean between 2018-2020 to determine their genetic variation using molecular tools. Our findings provide invaluable insights into how fine scale epidemiological processes are influenced by movements, environmental conditions and long-term stability for conservation management strategies aimed at reducing transboundary threats.

title: Infections in neutropenic patients I: Aetiology
abstract: This study provides an insight into the aetiology of infections in neutropenic patients. The effects of neutropenia on patient vulnerability, risk factors specific to immunocompromised individuals and infection sources are evaluated. Research on how to identify which infections these patients are most susceptible to is also explored. By understanding the principal causes of infection, healthcare providers may work towards effective prevention measures and improved outcomes for this at-risk population.

title: Effects of certain stress factors on the re-excretion of infectious laryngotracheitis virus from latently infected carrier birds
abstract: Experiments were set up to assess the effects of ‘natural’ and ‘artificial’ stresses on the re-excretion of infectious laryngotracheitis (ilt) virus in latently infected chickens recovered from the acute phase of the disease. The stresses were rehousing with the addition of ilt-free contact birds, corticosteroid treatment and the onset of lay. The contact birds were also monitored for transmission of the virus from the carrier birds. Rehousing with unfamiliar birds induced ilt virus shedding in one of five birds and there was evidence of transmission from this bird to its mate. The onset of lay had a significant effect on the overall shedding rates of the carrier birds. Nine of 10 birds shed virus after onset of lay compared with only two in the three-and-a-half weeks before, and there was a highly significant increase (P<0·001) in the overall number of virus isolations during this period. Corticosteroid treatment did not affect virus shedding. These results may explain some of the apparently spontaneous outbreaks of ilt which occur in the field.

title: Cauda equina syndrome in an obese pregnant patient secondary to double level lumbar disc herniation – A case report and review of literature
abstract: This case report examines a unique patient presentation of Cauda Equina Syndrome (CES) in an obese pregnant woman with double level lumbar disc herniation. CES is a rare yet serious form of nerve root compression, which can lead to varying levels of paralysis and loss of sensation if not addressed promptly. Despite the growing prevalence of obesity worldwide, limited reports have described this condition in obese pregnancy resulting from lumbar spinal disease. This paper presents diagnosis, treatment procedure as well as clinical outcome following management intervention while contextualizing it within current understanding drawn from the published evidence base provided via systematic review and comprehensive literature search.  The findings have important practical implications for anticipating adverse effects related to obesity during pregnancy that could potentially decrease obstetric morbidity outcomes through diligent clinician attentiveness.

title: Association of Mobile Instant Messaging Chat Group Participation With Family Functioning and Well-Being: Population-Based Cross-sectional Study
abstract: This study focuses on the implications of mobile instant messaging (MIM) chat group participation for family functioning and well-being. In an effort to better understand its potential risks, benefits, and health outcomes, we present a population-based cross-sectional study of family members who frequently participate in MIM chat groups in China. Our objective is to evaluate the associations between MIM chat group participation with family functioning and well-being. A total sample size of 1,800 participants from 39 cities were used in this study; they completed online questionnaires containing demographic information as well as scales designed to measure psychological awareness and self-reports on family relationships. Additionally, general ratings of their overall subjective mental states were assessed through interviews administered by trained researchers. Results revealed that frequent involvement with MIM chat groups was associated with poorer intrafamilial communication quality, weaker bonds among family members, reduced satisfaction or enjoyment within families’ social contexts/activities, higher depressive symptoms experiences as reported by interviewees as well lower perceived levels of personal physical health status compared with counterparts reporting limited use/engagement in such activities. These findings cannot be explained entirely by traditional offline factors alone and imply a need for further research into moderation effects across cultures regarding the utilization of modern digital resources for facilitating access to clan activities either inside or outside homescan potentially impact formative nuisances at both micro level (intrafamily), meso level (neighbourhoods etc.), macro level(social systems)and transcending beyond community networks .

title: Clinical Features of Severe Influenza A (H1N1) Virus Infection
abstract: This study presents an assessment of the clinical features of influenza A (H1N1) virus infection in order to gain a deeper understanding of this highly contagious pathogen and its associated risks to public health. The scientific data gathered from patients with H1N1 reveals that the severity of this virus is not limited to individuals with only mild symptoms, as more serious manifestations exist that could potentially lead to severe morbidity and mortality. This paper provides insights into which clinical characteristics are predictive for those suffering from severe infections, so that appropriate preventative measures may be undertaken before development of systemic illness or critical illness occur.

title: Production, Characterization and Applications for Toxoplasma gondii-Specific Polyclonal Chicken Egg Yolk Immunoglobulins
abstract: This paper examines the production and characterization of polyclonal chicken egg yolk immunoglobulins specific to Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii) with a focus on their potential applications in diagnosis, therapy and vaccination. Recent studies suggest that these polyclonal antibodies are an attractive alternative to monoclonal antibody-based products due to their relative affordability, broad range of epitopes recognized by large number of B cells and enhanced safety profiles when compared to small molecules or viral vectors-associated vaccines. Additionally, they have been used in several clinical trials involving humans without significant side effects reported so far. Here we present a comprehensive description of the process for producing these IgYs as well as physicochemical characterization based on aggregation tests and their application potential against T. gondii antigens from different strains presenting atypical forms including either non replicative or cyst states which could be implicated in drug resistance playing crucial role in veterinary clinics performances together with the food safety issues related by its presence into meat derived products.

title: Filovirus Research in Gabon and Equatorial Africa: The Experience of a Research Center in the Heart of Africa
abstract: This article presents a review of the experience of Gabon's Centre International de Recherches Medicales (CIRMF) in filovirus research between 2006 and 2016. Located in central Equatorial Africa, CIRMF has been at the forefront of simian and human-associated viral hemorrhagic fever studies in this region during this time period. Benefits to the advancement of scientific knowledge, clinical care development and disease management are discussed as well as how economic drivers may impact future progress. Researchers from CIRMF have made several important field discoveries on transmission dynamics, virology, diagnostics instrumentation, pathogenesis and therapeutics that provide new insights for understanding filoviral infections across Central Africa. The findings will open up opportunities for collaborations among international researchers to explore further avenues towards improved filovirus control strategies worldwide by utilizing local resources available at CIRMF centre.

title: Development and Testing of an Abbreviated Numeracy Scale: A Rasch Analysis Approach
abstract: Research has demonstrated that individual differences in numeracy may have important consequences for decision making. In the present paper, we develop a shorter, psychometrically improved measure of numeracy—the ability to understand, manipulate, and use numerical information, including probabilities. Across two large independent samples that varied widely in age and educational level, participants completed 18 items from existing numeracy measures. In Study 1, we conducted a Rasch analysis on the item pool and created an eight‐item numeracy scale that assesses a broader range of difficulty than previous scales. In Study 2, we replicated this eight‐item scale in a separate Rasch analysis using data from an independent sample. We also found that the new Rasch‐based numeracy scale, compared with previous measures, could predict decision‐making preferences obtained in past studies, supporting its predictive validity. In Study, 3, we further established the predictive validity of the Rasch‐based numeracy scale. Specifically, we examined the associations between numeracy and risk judgments, compared with previous scales. Overall, we found that the Rasch‐based scale was a better linear predictor of risk judgments than prior measures. Moreover, this study is the first to present the psychometric properties of several popular numeracy measures across a diverse sample of ages and educational level. We discuss the usefulness and the advantages of the new scale, which we feel can be used in a wide range of subject populations, allowing for a more clear understanding of how numeracy is associated with decision processes. title: Therapeutic Uses of Red Macroalgae
abstract: This study explores the therapeutic applications of Red Macroalgae as an effective treatment for a wide array of medical ailments. It examines the unique biochemical properties that make this material an attractive option for many forms of health related issues and describes potential avenues for further research. This article reviews existing literature on the topic, recounting findings from experiments conducted to evaluate whether or not Red Macroalgae can be used effectively in treating various diseases. The results of these studies are discussed along with any relevant limitations, to provide insight into both positive and negative impacts associated with utilization of this material as a form of therapy or remedy. Finally, implications regarding future research directions in this field are suggested. Ultimately, it is hoped that this analysis will firm up our understanding on how best to develop suitable treatments utilizing Red Macroalgae while informing practitioners regarding its usefulness as a viable alternative medicinal source.

title: Thinking Beyond HLH: Clinical Features of Patients with Concurrent Presentation of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis and Thrombotic Microangiopathy
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a syndrome of excessive immune system activation driven mainly by high levels of interferon gamma. The clinical presentation of HLH can have considerable overlap with other inflammatory conditions. We present a cohort of patients with therapy refractory HLH referred to our center who were found to have a simultaneous presentation of complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). Twenty-three patients had therapy refractory HLH (13 primary, 4 EVB-HLH, 6 HLH without known trigger). Sixteen (69.6%) met high-risk TMA criteria. Renal failure requiring renal replacement therapy, severe hypertension, serositis, and gastrointestinal bleeding were documented only in patients with HLH who had concomitant complement-mediated TMA. Patients with HLH and without TMA required ventilator support mainly due to CNS symptoms, while those with HLH and TMA had respiratory failure predominantly associated with pulmonary hypertension, a known presentation of pulmonary TMA. Ten patients received eculizumab for complement-mediated TMA management while being treated for HLH. All patients who received the complement blocker eculizumab in addition to the interferon gamma blocker emapalumab had complete resolution of their TMA and survived. Our observations suggest co-activation of both interferon and complement pathways as a potential culprit in the evolution of thrombotic microangiopathy in patients with inflammatory disorders like refractory HLH and may offer novel therapeutic approaches for these critically ill patients. TMA should be considered in children with HLH and multi-organ failure, as an early institution of a brief course of complement blocking therapy in addition to HLH-targeted therapy may improve clinical outcomes in these patients. title: Antimicrobial de-escalation as part of antimicrobial stewardship in intensive care: no simple answers to simple questions—a viewpoint of experts
abstract: Antimicrobial de-escalation (ADE) is defined as the discontinuation of one or more components of combination empirical therapy, and/or the change from a broad-spectrum to a narrower spectrum antimicrobial. It is most commonly recommended in the intensive care unit (ICU) patient who is treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics as a strategy to reduce antimicrobial pressure of empirical broad-spectrum therapy and prevent antimicrobial resistance, yet this has not been convincingly demonstrated in a clinical setting. Even if it appears beneficial, ADE may have some unwanted side effects: it has been associated with prolongation of antimicrobial therapy and could inappropriately be used as a justification for unrestricted broadness of empirical therapy. Also, exposing a patient to multiple, sequential antimicrobials could have unwanted effects on the microbiome. For these reasons, ADE has important shortcomings to be promoted as a quality indicator for appropriate antimicrobial use in the ICU. Despite this, ADE clearly has a role in the management of infections in the ICU. The most appropriate use of ADE is in patients with microbiologically confirmed infections requiring longer antimicrobial therapy. ADE should be used as an integral part of an ICU antimicrobial stewardship approach in which it is guided by optimal specimen quality and relevance. Rapid diagnostics may further assist in avoiding unnecessary initiation of broad-spectrum therapy, which in turn will decrease the need for subsequent ADE.

title: Prevalence of neutralising antibodies to Berne virus in animals and humans in Vellore, South India
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the prevalence of antibodies to Berne virus in both animals and humans living in Vellore, South India. It offers a comprehensive insight into the rate of infection as well as exploring risk factors associated with individuals who present with evidence of neutralizing antibodies.

title: Biosynthesis of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) in Bacillus aryabhattai and cytotoxicity evaluation of PHBV/poly(ethylene glycol) blends
abstract: The study described poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) accumulation in Bacillus aryabhattai PHB10 for the first time and evaluated the polymer induced cytotoxicity in-vitro with PHBV/poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) blends. The B. aryabhattai strain produced 2.8 g/L PHBV, equivalent to 71.15% of cell dry mass in a medium supplemented with propionic acid, after 48 h incubation. The optimum temperature and pH for the copolymer accumulation was 31 °C and 7, respectively. The gas chromatography–mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance analyses confirmed the polymer obtained as PHBV. The differential scanning calorimetry analysis revealed that the melting point of the material as 90 °C and its thermal stability up to 220 °C. The average molecular weight (Mn) and polydispersity index of the sample was estimated by gel permeation chromatography analysis and observed as 128.508 kDa and 2.82, respectively. The PHBV showed tensile strength of 10.3 MPa and elongation at break of 13.3%. The PHBV and their blends with PEG were tested for cytotoxicity on human keratinocytes (HaCaT cells) and the cells incubated with PHBV/PEG2kDa blends were 99% viable, whereas with the PHBV alone showed comparatively higher cytotoxicity. The significant improvement in the cell viability of PHBV/PEG2kDa blends indicates its potential as a candidate for skin graft applications.

title: The B‐cell system of human mucosae and exocrine glands
abstract: The B-cell system of human mucosae and exocrine glands has long been a mystery to scientists, yet new evidence suggests that this is likely a key component in the regulation of mucosal immunity. Previous studies have shed light on the role of B-cells in antigen presentation as well as effector responses such as antibody production. Recently, using an RNA-sequencing approach across several different sites from multiple individuals we have identified a specific transcriptional signature for these cell populations within human mucosal tissues and exocrine glands. Our data demonstrates the presence of distinct subpopulations with contrasting features suggesting subtle regionalization or organ-specific differences in function. Notably our findings point towards differential involvement between local tissue resident versus systemic IgA+ B cells across various surface epithelia, suggesting dynamic changes dependent on anatomical site which may be essential to understanding beneficial immune responses associated with protection against invading pathogens at both localised sites and more distal locations within the body. Such insights could identify targets for therapeutic approaches involved in improving host defense mechanisms leading to better control of infectious diseases such as HIV or COVID infections, while also providing an opportunity to develop interventions aimed at reducing inflammation driven allergy disorders relevant in modern times.

title: Mechanisms and pathways to impact in public health research: a preliminary analysis of research funded by the National Institute for Health Research (NIHR)
abstract: This study presents a preliminary analysis of research funded by the National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) and examines the mechanisms and pathways to impact developed in studies aimed at improving public health outcomes. Despite increased investment in public health research, there is still limited evidence regarding how activities are designed to secure an effect beyond academic outputs. To address this gap, NIHR's support was used as a case study to explore how researchers and stakeholders go about developing value from individual projects, with a particular focus on health services delivery improvement or wider population-level change. Drawing upon company directories data sources encompassing over 1,400 estimated NIHR investments between 2012-2018, qualitative interviews veering around key themes were conducted with those involved across all stages of the funding process including information providers and end-users. Findings indicated that while some grant holders utilised general performance criteria alongside specific patient/public involvement metrics supplied by their funder; others had applied their own self-defined benchmarks that could be personalised towards different stakeholder interests/environmental influences outside immediate examination scope. Moreover, perceived improvements raised during interviewwere founded upon co-productive pathways unique per area under consideration yet often enabled through proactive collaborations nor exclusive partnerships driven in part by NIHRI’s broad established network(s). This paper hence calls attention to amplifying understandings relating participatory efforts ability delving inwardly into components crucial for understanding complex practices known for their proficiency attaining effective interventions prevalent within contemporary policy contexts

title: Pancreatitis and Pancreatic Pseudocyst
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the relationship between pancreatitis and pancreatic pseudocyst. A focus is placed on the epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, diagnosis and clinical management of this dual pathology. The research encompasses analysis of literature from retrospective studies as well as prospective trials in order to draw conclusions about best practices for dealing with associated complications. This knowledge may help clinicians in providing better patient-centered care regarding pancreatitis and its related conditions.

title: Design of the first highly potent and selective aminopeptidase N (EC 3.4.11.2) inhibitor
abstract: A series of phosphinic compounds mimicking the transition state of substrates hydrolysed by aminopeptidase N (EC 3.4.11.2) were synthesized. These new compounds have potent inhibitory activities with Ki values in the nanomolar range. These derivatives behave as the most potent APN inhibitors designed to date.

title: SUMO fusion system facilitates soluble expression and high production of bioactive human fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)
abstract: As a key humoral regulator of phosphate homeostasis and its involvement in the pathogenesis of human disease, human fibroblast growth factor 23 (hFGF23) has become a particularly attractive therapeutic target. To prepare soluble and bioactive recombinant human FGF23 to meet the increasing demand in its pharmacological application, small ubiquitin-related modifier (SUMO)-FGF23 fusion gene and FGF23 non-fusion gene were amplified by standard PCR methods and cloned into vector pET-22b and pET-3c, then transformed into Escherichia coli Rosetta (DE3) and BL21 (DE3). The best combination of plasmid and host strain was screened, and only Rosetta (DE3)/pET-SUMO-FGF23 was screened for rhFGF23 protein expressed. The average bacterial yield and the soluble expression level of recombinant hFGF23 of three batches attained 687 ± 18 g and 30 ± 1.5%, respectively, after treatment with 0.4 mM isopropyl-thio-β-galactopyranoside for 19 h at 16 °C in a 30-L fermentor, after which it was purified by DEAE Sepharose FF and nickel nitrilotriacetic acid affinity chromatography. Once cleaved by the SUMO protease, the recombinant human FGF23 was released from the fusion protein. The purity of rFGF23 was shown by high performance liquid chromatography to be greater than 90% and the yield was 60 ± 1.5 mg/L. In vitro data showed that the purified rFGF23 can induce the phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinases in the glioma U251 cell. The results of in vivo animal experiments also showed that rFGF23 could decrease the concentration in the plasma of normal rats fed with a fixed formula diet. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (doi:10.1007/s00253-011-3864-4) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

title: The EU-TOPIA evaluation tool: An online modelling-based tool for informing breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening decisions in Europe
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aiming to support European countries in improving their breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer (CRC) screening programmes, the EU-TOPIA consortium has developed an online user-friendly tool (the EU-TOPIA evaluation tool; https://miscan.eu-topia.org) based on the Microsimulation Screening Analysis (MISCAN) model. METHODS: We designed an online platform that allows stakeholders to use their country-specific data (demographic, epidemiological, and cancer screening information) to quantify future harms and benefits of different cancer screening scenarios in their country. Current cancer screening programmes and impacts of potential changes in screening protocols (such as extending target ages or increasing screening attendance) can be simulated. Results are scaled to the country-specific population. To illustrate the tool, we used the tool to simulate two different CRC screening scenarios in the Netherlands: biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in ages 55–75 and colonoscopy every ten years in ages 55–75. Data from the Dutch screening programme was used to inform both scenarios. RESULTS: A total of 482,700 CRC cases and 178,000 CRC deaths were estimated in the Netherlands with FIT screening (for individuals aged 40–100 years, 2018–2050), with 47.3 million FITs performed (1.92 million positives of which 1.64 million adhered to diagnostic colonoscopy). With colonoscopy screening, CRC incidence and mortality were, respectively, up to 17% and 14% lower than in the current FIT screening programme, requiring, however, a colonoscopy demand that was 7-fold higher. CONCLUSIONS: Our study presents an essential online tool for stakeholders and medical societies to quantify estimates of benefits and harms of early cancer detection in Europe.

title: Pneumonia in the Cancer Patient
abstract: Pneumonia remains a life threatening and common complication in patients with cancer. This paper reviews the incidence and risk factors associated with pneumonia development, as well as discusses evidence-based interventions for prevention and management of this condition in the oncology population. A systematic review was conducted to identify pertinent research studies including randomized clinical trials from existing published literature from 2000 to 2019 using databases such as MEDLINE, Embase and Cochrane Library. Analyses were focused on outcomes related to patient safety regarding therapy for Pneumonia occurrence that may be captured by healthcare providers including mortality rate, frequency of re-hospitalization or complications among those affected by cancer. The findings suggest an overall increase in risk of pneumonia due to bacteria or viral infections although preventive measures have lead to improved management outcomes under certain circumstances; however more evidence is needed concerning disease transmission between hospitalized patients. Thus, further prospective controlled indepth studies are necessary to determine optimal approaches towards enhancing quality of care while lessening burden on health systems due to increased morbidity and mortality rates associated with Pneumonia amongst those afflicted by cancer specifically while exploring proper guidelines for screening choices amongst healthcare practitioners during regular follow up along various stages through their treatments trajectories.

title: Applications, challenges, and needs for employing synthetic biology beyond the lab
abstract: Synthetic biology holds great promise for addressing global needs. However, most current developments are not immediately translatable to ‘outside-the-lab’ scenarios that differ from controlled laboratory settings. Challenges include enabling long-term storage stability as well as operating in resource-limited and off-the-grid scenarios using autonomous function. Here we analyze recent advances in developing synthetic biological platforms for outside-the-lab scenarios with a focus on three major application spaces: bioproduction, biosensing, and closed-loop therapeutic and probiotic delivery. Across the Perspective, we highlight recent advances, areas for further development, possibilities for future applications, and the needs for innovation at the interface of other disciplines.

title: Incidental Findings in TMJ Imaging
abstract: For years, the conventional imaging modalities are generally used in dental practice routine. They provide precious information about dentomaxillofacial region; they also have some limitations such as superimpositions, magnifications, distortions, and low-image quality. Because of these limitations, some pathologies, calcifications, and anatomical variations may be missed. Any findings on a radiographic image which are not related to the research areas of interest could be a description of “incidental findings.” Calcifications are one of these incidental findings. They are asymptomatic and also common in TMJ images. Although most of the calcifications require no treatment, correct identification will reduce further diagnostic assessments. Incidental findings on TMJ images were rare, while examining images for temporomandibular disorders and associated issues, it is important not only to examine the TMJ structures but also to look at the nearby anatomical features to check for evidence of incidental findings pathologies that may have mimicked signs and symptoms of TMJ disorders.

title: Molecular and Cellular Effects of Chemical Chaperone—TUDCA on ER-Stressed NHAC-kn Human Articular Chondrocytes Cultured in Normoxic and Hypoxic Conditions
abstract: This study examines the molecular and cellular effects of chemical chaperone TUDCA on ER-stressed NHAC-kn human articular chondrocytes cultured under normoxic and hypoxic conditions. The objective was to explore the protective role of TUDCA in reducing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, modulating oxidative stress responses, as well as its effect on cell viability/proliferation both in normoxia and hypoxia. Analyses were conducted with quantitative real Time Polymerase Chain Reaction (qRT-PCR), Western Blotting, Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Production Assay and Cell Counting Kit8 (CCK-8) assays which revealed that TUDCA reduced expressions of ER Stress Markers BiP gene/protein while exerting a mild antioxidant effect. In addition, CCK– 8 assay showed improved cell counts compared to control in both normoxic treatment groups whereas a moderate increase was only observed after 48 h of hypoxic culture with or without drug exposure. Thus we demonstrated that application of exogenous chemical chaperone is beneficial for protecting human articular chondrocytes from ER induced damage involving reduction of mRNA expression levels for two key eukaryotic translation initiation factor subunits 5B & 4EBP1 as well as increased perilipin 1 expression following stress stimulus .

title: Genomic Epidemiology Analysis of Infectious Disease Outbreaks Using TransPhylo
abstract: This study provides an analysis of the genomic epidemiology of infectious disease outbreaks using TransPhylo, a novel technique that uses Next Generation Sequencing-derived bacterial genome data to rapidly determine transmission between infected individuals. The first part of this paper examines the advantages and disadvantages of using the tool on outbreak scenarios such as HIV, influenza and salmonella infections. Furthermore, we develop a comprehensive framework for assessing how well this technology can be used in practical settings by highlighting its accuracy and limitations when it comes to identifying individual patient sources for potentially dispersed bacteria according to host demographic data. This framework is evaluated through extensive case studies simulating outbreaks from several different pathogens including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Escherichia coli O157:H7 (E. coli), Yersinia pestis ( plague), and Streptococcus pyogenes (scarlet fever). Finally, our findings demonstrate that TransPhylo is highly efficient in tracing interpatient transmissions during disease outbreaks efficiently at low cost while providing high levels of confidence in source detection results due to improved accuracy compared with existing methods like MLST-based approaches.

title: How do we … integrate pathogen reduced platelets into our hospital blood bank inventory?
abstract: For more than 50 years there has been an ongoing effort to combat transfusion‐transmitted infections and provide patients with the safest possible blood. This initiative has driven much of the research within the transfusion community. Initial methods included screening donors for travel histories to banned areas and for high‐risk behaviors, but pathogen‐specific assays performed at the collection and manufacturing sites also have become key factors in assuring blood safety. Many of these have focused on donor and laboratory‐based screening for transfusion‐transmitted diseases, as evidenced by the hepatitis and human immunodeficiency virus screening in the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s. More recently, this effort has expanded to develop donor screening assays to identify other blood‐borne pathogens, such as Zika and West Nile viruses and Babesia. Bacterial contamination of units of platelets (PLTs), however, remains a significant concern. In recent years, the Food and Drug Administration has approved rapid tests to identify bacterially contaminated PLT units in the blood bank before transfusion. Other supplemental methods have been developed, however, that aim to inactivate blood‐borne pathogen(s) present in the blood product, rather than to rely on our ability to identify and interdict contaminated and infected components. Pathogen reduction technology, as this is referred to, provides a proactive way to further reduce the risk posed by transfusion‐transmitted infections.

title: A novel, cell-specific attenuation of a herpes simplex virus type 1 infection in vivo
abstract: We have observed a cell-specific attenuation of herpes simplex virus type 1 strain 17syn+ in vivo that was dependent upon the cell type used to grow the virus. Direct corneal infection of rabbits with 17syn+ propagated in Vero cells caused 60% (6 of 10) to develop severe central nervous system (CNS) disease as evidenced by seizures and/or paralysis; all neurologically impaired rabbits died. In contrast, infection of rabbits with 17syn+ propagated in BHK-21 cells induced seizures and was fatal in 10% (1 of 10). The cell-specific attenuation of a 17syn+ occurred after one growth cycle in BHK-21 cells. To determine whether the decreased virulence of the BHK-21 cell-grown virus correlated with a less severe CNS inflammatory reaction, CNS tissues from rabbits infected with 17syn+ grown in Vero and BHK-21 cells were compared. Histopathological analyses revealed no differences in the location or severity of inflammatory lesions from rabbits infected with virus grown in either cell type. Virus-induced corneal disease was less dependent upon the cell type used to propagate the virus as there were no significant differences in the type or severity of observed corneal lesions. Possible explanations based on differences between Vero and BHK-21 cells are discussed.

title: δ-secretase in neurodegenerative diseases: mechanisms, regulators and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of δ-secretase and its role in neurodegenerative diseases. δ-Secretase is an intramembrane proteolytic enzyme that cleaves several substrates within the human brain, making it a potential target for therapeutics. In this review, we analyze recent investigations into the biology of δ-secretase and address topics such as its mechanisms, regulators and possible therapeutic interventions. Furthermore, we discuss existing issues related to therapy research on δ-secretase and suggest some possible strategies for drug development targeting this molecule. This work offers new insights into our comprehension of how neurological processes may be affected by defective regulation of δ-secretase activity in various diseases that affect neuronal breakdown or alteration such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The identification of small molecules as inhibitors or activators able to correct aberrant proteolysis could pave the way towards improved pharmacotherapeutic options in these devastating disorders

title: Approaches for patients with very high MELD scores
abstract: Approaches to care for patients with elevated MELD (Model of End-stage Liver Disease) scores remain highly contested, and it is not yet clear which treatments are most effective. This publication reviews several outreach strategies utilized by current liver units when caring for those who have an extremely high MELD score, one that surpasses the traditional “terminal” threshold greatly. Comparison studies between these various approaches and their outcomes have been conducted in an effort to implement more effective models of palliative care for these cases, as well as adding research gaps within this field which need to be further examined. Contemporary medical advancements related to different therapies available and changes in diet or lifestyle specific to such cases will also be discussed from a comprehensive interdisciplinary perspective. Evidence-based protocols created based on previous clinical results will offer direction for healthcare professionals both treating and monitoring individuals at risk of endstage liver disease progression in order to prevent the development of critical symptoms associated with cirrhosis before they become irreversible or terminal. We hope that through exploring existing data regarding new treatments along with possible patient rehabilitative activities best devices can be suggested while reinforcing relevant theories proposed by leading physicians into practice so that lasting improvements in prognosis can become abundantly available across all branches responsible for providing hepatology services worldwide

title: Adult-Onset Still’s Disease
abstract: This study examines Adult-Onset Still’s Disease (AOSD), a rare form of inflammatory arthritis. It is notable for its prodromal symptoms such as high fever and rash, which can indicate both infection or autoimmunity. This investigation will investigate the test methods used to diagnose AOSD, newly-developed treatments and potential risk factors for patients with this condition. The importance of accurately identifying AOSD so that appropriate therapy can be initiated without delay will be discussed in depth along with an evaluation of the most effective care options from a clinical perspective.

title: Use of Network Analysis and Spread Models to Target Control Actions for Bovine Tuberculosis in a State from Brazil
abstract: Livestock movements create complex dynamic interactions among premises that can be represented, interpreted, and used for epidemiological purposes. These movements are a very important part of the production chain but may also contribute to the spread of infectious diseases through the transfer of infected animals over large distances. Social network analysis (SNA) can be used to characterize cattle trade patterns and to identify highly connected premises that may act as hubs in the movement network, which could be subjected to targeted control measures in order to reduce the transmission of communicable diseases such as bovine tuberculosis (TB). Here, we analyzed data on cattle movement and slaughterhouse surveillance for detection of TB-like lesions (TLL) over the 2016–2018 period in the state of Rio Grande do Sul (RS) in Brazil with the following aims: (i) to characterize cattle trade describing the static full, yearly, and monthly snapshots of the network contact trade, (ii) to identify clusters in the space and contact networks of premises from which animals with TLL originated, and (iii) to evaluate the potential of targeted control actions to decrease TB spread in the cattle population of RS using a stochastic metapopulation disease transmission model that simulated within-farm and between-farm disease spread. We found heterogeneous densities of premises and animals in the study area. The analysis of the contact network revealed a highly connected (~94%) trade network, with strong temporal trends, especially for May and November. The TLL cases were significantly clustered in space and in the contact network, suggesting the potential for both local (e.g., fence-to-fence) and movement-mediated TB transmission. According to the disease spread model, removing the top 7% connected farms based on degree and betweenness could reduce the total number of infected farms over three years by >50%. In conclusion, the characterization of the cattle network suggests that highly connected farms may play a role in TB dissemination, although being close to infected farms was also identified as a risk factor for having animals with TLL. Surveillance and control actions based on degree and betweenness could be useful to break the transmission cycle between premises in RS.

title: Childhood Tuberculosis Presenting with Haemophagocytic Syndrome
abstract: This study examines the case of a six-year-old child with an atypical presentation of tuberculosis and associated haemophagocytic syndrome (HPS). The investigations showed that childhood tuberculosis in a low endemic country was complicated by HPS, transformed into macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) after immunosuppressive treatment. This paper aims to define the clinical features at diagnosis, discuss unconventional presentations and highlight management challenges for subspecialists treating MAS patients. Further research is required to identify genetic associations between MAS/HPS reactivation due to emerging primary infections such as tuberculous mycobacteria or other pathogens triggering TB‐like clinical manifestations.

title: Centenarians in nursing homes during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract:
This article examines the effects of COVID-19 on the centenarian population in nursing homes. Despite making up an increasingly large portion of those living in elderly care settings, research into this group's protection is lagging behind other age groups. The study aims to review what strategies have been employed by nursing homes to protect centenarians during the pandemic, how well these strategies are working and any lessons that should be learned for future regional or global responses. Data was collected from ten different Chinese institutions with centenarian populations in December 2020; interviews were conducted alongside open surveys with staff and relatives through online platforms such as WeChat. Results suggested that although nurses had successfully implemented a range of preventive measures following public health guidance, certain areas require further attention including inadequate control over infectious sources outside healthcare facilities, insufficient quarantine resources and lack of clear medical guidance for family members who may visit centenarians during lock down periods. Consequently, it is recommended that there needs to be greater emphasis placed on implementing preventative measures within both local government bodies and individual healthcare facilities as well as better protocols put in place for when situations arise where they can provide prompt services while protecting their more vulnerable residents.

title: Identification of RNA Binding Proteins Associated with Dengue Virus RNA in Infected Cells Reveals Temporally Distinct Host Factor Requirements
abstract: BACKGROUND: There are currently no vaccines or antivirals available for dengue virus infection, which can cause dengue hemorrhagic fever and death. A better understanding of the host pathogen interaction is required to develop effective therapies to treat DENV. In particular, very little is known about how cellular RNA binding proteins interact with viral RNAs. RNAs within cells are not naked; rather they are coated with proteins that affect localization, stability, translation and (for viruses) replication. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Seventy-nine novel RNA binding proteins for dengue virus (DENV) were identified by cross-linking proteins to dengue viral RNA during a live infection in human cells. These cellular proteins were specific and distinct from those previously identified for poliovirus, suggesting a specialized role for these factors in DENV amplification. Knockdown of these proteins demonstrated their function as viral host factors, with evidence for some factors acting early, while others late in infection. Their requirement by DENV for efficient amplification is likely specific, since protein knockdown did not impair the cell fitness for viral amplification of an unrelated virus. The protein abundances of these host factors were not significantly altered during DENV infection, suggesting their interaction with DENV RNA was due to specific recruitment mechanisms. However, at the global proteome level, DENV altered the abundances of proteins in particular classes, including transporter proteins, which were down regulated, and proteins in the ubiquitin proteasome pathway, which were up regulated. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: The method for identification of host factors described here is robust and broadly applicable to all RNA viruses, providing an avenue to determine the conserved or distinct mechanisms through which diverse viruses manage the viral RNA within cells. This study significantly increases the number of cellular factors known to interact with DENV and reveals how DENV modulates and usurps cellular proteins for efficient amplification.

title: Natural Pig Plasma Immunoglobulins Have Anti-Bacterial Effects: Potential for Use as Feed Supplement for Treatment of Intestinal Infections in Pigs
abstract: There is an increasing demand for non-antibiotics solutions to control infectious disease in intensive pig production. Here, one such alternative, namely pig antibodies purified from slaughterhouse blood was investigated in order to elucidate its potential usability to control post-weaning diarrhoea (PWD), which is one of the top indications for antibiotics usage in the pig production. A very cost-efficient and rapid one-step expanded bed adsorption (EBA) chromatography procedure was used to purify pig immunoglobulin G from slaughterhouse pig plasma (more than 100 litres), resulting in >85% pure pig IgG (ppIgG). The ppIgG thus comprised natural pig immunoglobulins and was subsequently shown to contain activity towards four pig-relevant bacterial strains (three different types of Escherichia coli and one type of Salmonella enterica) but not towards a fish pathogen (Yersinia ruckeri), and was demonstrated to inhibit the binding of the four pig relevant bacteria to a pig intestinal cell line (IPEC-J2). Finally it was demonstrated in an in vivo weaning piglet model for intestinal colonization with an E. coli F4+ challenge strain that ppIgG given in the feed significantly reduced shedding of the challenge strain, reduced the proportion of the bacterial family Enterobacteriaceae, increased the proportion of families Enterococcoceae and Streptococcaceae and generally increased ileal microbiota diversity. Conclusively, our data support the idea that natural IgG directly purified from pig plasma and given as a feed supplement can be used in modern swine production as an efficient and cost-effective means for reducing both occurrence of PWD and antibiotics usage and with a potential for the prevention and treatment of other intestinal infectious diseases even if the causative agent might not be known.
