title: Assessment of pain symptoms and quality of life using the International Spinal Cord Injury Data Sets in persons with chronic spinal cord injury
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the criteria of International Spinal Cord Injury Data Sets (ISCI-DS) in persons with chronic spinal cord injury, to explore their pain symptoms and quality-of-life. Pain is caused due to neurological dysfunctions initiate by spinal cord injury, which has interfered with a person's mobility and comfortability. The main objective is to investigate the efficacy of ISCI standardized sets as measure tools for assessing pain related sufferings and evaluate the quality-of life among them; this will lead towards better adapting therapeutic interventions specifically tailored towards individuals. Structured questionnaires are developed that target comprehensive assessment procedure relative to satisfaction rating scale for physical activities, lifestyle demands, social interactions etc., alongwith medical information collection like daily caloric intake or body mass index measurements. Results would indicate usefulness of ISCI datasets regarding correlation between self-reported complaints associated within SCI patients such as physical conditions and health related quality adjustments can prepare bases leads towards evidence protocol that could be required in clinical settings while developing unique choices appropriate treatment evaluations plan & management measures in order advance patient recovery strategies from long term effects from pain volatility & its consequential adverse DOMS condition tests.

title: Disease Management in Endangered Mammals
abstract: One quarter of all mammal species are considered threatened with extinction (IUCN 2007). The rate of loss of biodiversity is accelerating because increasing pressure from an expanding human population is shrinking natural habitat and over-exploiting wild animal populations. Although processes such as habitat loss and over-harvesting are usually identified as the major drivers of extinction, recent evidence suggests that disease can also be a significant threat to endangered species (Lyles and Dobson 1993; Daszak and Cunningham 1999; Daszak et al. 2000b; de Castro and Bolker 2004; Choisy and Rohani 2006; Lips et al. 2006; Smith et al. 2006). Disease has already been documented as a cause of extinction of a land snail (Partula turgida) (Cunningham and Dazsak 1998), and several amphibian species (Schloegel et al. 2006; Skerrat et al. 2007). Diseases are also known to cause significant population declines, as illustrated by the impact of canine distemper virus in black-footed ferrets (Mustela nigripes) (Williams et al. 1988) and lions (Panthera leo) (Roelke-Parker et al. 1996), rabies virus in African wild dogs (Lycaon pictus) (Woodroffe and Ginsberg 1999), Ebola virus in apes (Leroy et al. 2004), squirrelpox virus in red squirrels (Sciurus vulgaris) (Rushton et al. 2006) and transmissible facial tumour disease in Tasmanian devils (Sarcophilus harrisii) (Pearse and Swift 2006).

title: Tracking Japan’s development assistance for health, 2012–2016
abstract:
This paper aims to assess Japan's development assistance for health (DAH) over a five year period from 2012 to 2016. Through a rigorous and systematic analysis, this study charts the fluctuations of DAH by looking at both the financial value and type of assistance that has been provided. By incorporating these various elements together, this research will offer an understanding on how Japan’s health-related initiatives have evolved over time and set up benchmarks for future deepening of its programs aimed towards improving global public health services worldwide. The findings presented in this article could also provide valuable information on whether or not existing financing channels are adequately meeting said goal as well as demonstrate how other donors could possibly follow suit in establishing similar strategies with their own respective missions.

title: Use of Procalcitonin and a Respiratory Polymerase Chain Reaction Panel to Reduce Antibiotic Use via an Electronic Medical Record Alert
abstract: This study examines the benefits of using procalcitonin and a respiratory polymerase chain reaction panel to reduce unnecessary antibiotic use through an electronic medical record alert system. Despite attempts to ameliorate overprescription in clinical settings, antibiotics are still being prescribed for conditions that would not benefit from them. In order to address this challenge, a recent approach has been taken wherein procalcitonin and a RT PCR-based assay have been combined with an EMR alert system to inform clinicians about antibiotic prescribing decisions. The purpose of this study was to determine if this regulation strategy effected any changes in outcomes such as shorter lengths of stay or fewer complications following discharge from the hospital when compared with existing standards of care on similar patient cohorts. title: Fast tracking after repair of congenital heart defects
abstract: This paper explores the effects of fast-tracking after repair of congenital heart defects in pediatric patients. Congenital heart defects are the most common birth defect worldwide and while they can be treated with corrective surgeries or devices, the long-term prognosis remains poor. Modern advances in medical technology have allowed for faster postoperative recovery and enabled earlier discharge from hospitalization; however, literature on studies related to this topic is scarce and inconclusive. The current study aimed to investigate whether there is a significant difference between traditional care plans and intervention strategies that take into account fast tracking for postoperative recovery following congenital cardiac procedures in newborns.

title: Comparison of distance measures in spatial analytical modeling for health service planning
abstract: BACKGROUND: Several methodological approaches have been used to estimate distance in health service research. In this study, focusing on cardiac catheterization services, Euclidean, Manhattan, and the less widely known Minkowski distance metrics are used to estimate distances from patient residence to hospital. Distance metrics typically produce less accurate estimates than actual measurements, but each metric provides a single model of travel over a given network. Therefore, distance metrics, unlike actual measurements, can be directly used in spatial analytical modeling. Euclidean distance is most often used, but unlikely the most appropriate metric. Minkowski distance is a more promising method. Distances estimated with each metric are contrasted with road distance and travel time measurements, and an optimized Minkowski distance is implemented in spatial analytical modeling. METHODS: Road distance and travel time are calculated from the postal code of residence of each patient undergoing cardiac catheterization to the pertinent hospital. The Minkowski metric is optimized, to approximate travel time and road distance, respectively. Distance estimates and distance measurements are then compared using descriptive statistics and visual mapping methods. The optimized Minkowski metric is implemented, via the spatial weight matrix, in a spatial regression model identifying socio-economic factors significantly associated with cardiac catheterization. RESULTS: The Minkowski coefficient that best approximates road distance is 1.54; 1.31 best approximates travel time. The latter is also a good predictor of road distance, thus providing the best single model of travel from patient's residence to hospital. The Euclidean metric and the optimal Minkowski metric are alternatively implemented in the regression model, and the results compared. The Minkowski method produces more reliable results than the traditional Euclidean metric. CONCLUSION: Road distance and travel time measurements are the most accurate estimates, but cannot be directly implemented in spatial analytical modeling. Euclidean distance tends to underestimate road distance and travel time; Manhattan distance tends to overestimate both. The optimized Minkowski distance partially overcomes their shortcomings; it provides a single model of travel over the network. The method is flexible, suitable for analytical modeling, and more accurate than the traditional metrics; its use ultimately increases the reliability of spatial analytical models.

title: An Ultrastructural Study of Vairimorpha necatrix (Microspora, Microsporida) with Particular Reference to Episporontal Inclusions During Octosporogony
abstract: This paper presents an ultrastructural study of Vairimorpha necatrix (Microspora, Microsporida) aimed at describing the different stages of octosporogony and in particular, examining the structure and arrangement of episporontal inclusions. Octosporogony is a form of typical sporogeny present among some species within this taxonomic group that is accomplished through schizogenous cleavage via intracellular meiotic divisions followed by further development inside specialized parasitophorous vacuoles. This work uses classical electron microscopy techniques to analyze various developmental sequences and reveal morphological characteristics specific for these kinds of microorganism lifecycles which could have implications for modern day understanding infectious phenomena related to microspora species. The results presented are significant as they provide new understandings on how changes in episporal content affect rates or levels of infection, making Vairomorpha necatrix an informative example used to model other disease-rising microbes sharing similar biological features.

title: Seamless integration of image and molecular analysis for spatial transcriptomics workflows
abstract: This study presents a novel and efficient workflow to seamlessly integrate image and molecular analysis of spatial transcriptomics data. Recent technological developments have enabled the combination of high-dimensional gene expression measurements with histological imaging, enabling construction of transcriptionally informed tissue maps. However, existing methods are limited in their ability to accommodate non-continuous structures due to manual steps during experiment design or complex post-processing, resulting in hesitancy among researchers towards fully utilizing all available information for their quantitative analysis. Our proposed workflow is based on semi-automated segmentation techniques that can be easily adopted by users without any prior coding experience thanks to our modular GUI tools and Python reports. We demonstrate how this seamless integration facilitates a rapid extraction of meaningful insights from the experimental data via both static (e.g., simple correlational relationships between markers) as well as dynamic (cell fate decisions) analyses while maintaining full scalability across platforms such as microscopy slide scanners or multiwell plates.

title: TRAF molecules in cell signaling and in human diseases
abstract: The TRAF family of molecules are critical mediators of signal transduction in eukaryotic cells, and their deregulation has been implicated in various human diseases. This review focuses on the recent advances concerning the role of TRAFs as novel signaling intermediates in cellular pathways linked to pathophysiological conditions. Additionally, it examines how deregulation of these regulatory proteins might contribute to the pathology associated with several human disorders such as cancer, autoimmunity and viral infections. Finally, we discuss emerging strategies targeting specifically different TRAF domains for therapeutic applications. Our work highlights the key roles played by this large family of adaptor molecules and sheds light on ongoing efforts towards a better understanding of their involvement in health and disease.

title: A Practical Perspective on the Roles of Solution NMR Spectroscopy in Drug Discovery
abstract: This paper presents a practical perspective on the role of solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy in drug discovery. NMR spectroscopy has been increasingly used as an analytical tool for development of new drugs over the past two decades, replacing traditional methods such as X-ray crystallography and other biophysical techniques. By mapping molecular interactions within whole molecules, solution NMR can effectively assist researchers in determining how modifications affect molecular structure and stability or even compound’s bioactivity. Through this review we discuss modern application of solution NMR spectroscopy by giving examples from various fields related to drug design/discovery; while also exploring current challenges and limitations associated with its use and potential solutions to address them. Such analysis provides a comprehensive view and discussion on utilization of this technology during pharmaceutical industry’s research & development process and helps strengthen the mechanistic understanding between momentary interactions within molecules that drives certain biological effects. This information may provide opportunities to explore novel therapeutic approaches beyond offering insights into existing ones, thus contributing significantly towards advancing precision medicine through better drug discoveries enabled by thorough investigation using NMR spectroscopy technique..

title: Ambulatory and stationary healthcare use in survivors of ARDS during the first year after discharge from ICU: findings from the DACAPO cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: For many survivors of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the process from discharge from intensive care unit (ICU) to recovery is long and difficult. However, healthcare use after discharge from ICU has received only little attention by research. This study sets out to investigate the extent of ambulatory and stationary healthcare use among survivors of ARDS in Germany (multicenter DACAPO cohort) and to analyze predictors of stationary healthcare use. RESULTS: A total of 396 survivors of ARDS provided data at 1 year after discharge from ICU. Fifty percent of 1-year survivors were hospitalized for 48 days or longer after discharge from ICU, with 10% spending more than six out of 12 months in stationary care. The duration of hospitalization increased significantly by the length of the initial ICU stay. All participants reported at least one outpatient visit (including visits to general practitioners), and 50% contacted four or more different medical specialties within the first year after discharge from ICU. CONCLUSIONS: For most of the patients, the first year after ARDS is characterized by an extensive amount of healthcare utilization, especially with regard to stationary health care. These findings shed light on the substantial morbidity of patients after ARDS and contribute to a better understanding of the situation of patients following discharge from ICU.

title: Outcomes and management approaches of resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta based on the income of countries
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) could provide a survival benefit to severely injured patients as it may improve their initial ability to survive the hemorrhagic shock. Although the evidence supporting the use of REBOA is not conclusive, its use has expanded worldwide. We aim to compare the management approaches and clinical outcomes of trauma patients treated with REBOA according to the countries’ income based on the World Bank Country and Lending Groups. METHODS: We used data from the AORTA (USA) and the ABOTrauma (multinational) registries. Patients were stratified into two groups: (1) high-income countries (HICs) and (2) low-to-middle income countries (LMICs). Propensity score matching extracted 1:1 matched pairs of subjects who were from an LMIC or a HIC based on age, gender, the presence of pupillary response on admission, impeding hypotension (SBP ≤ 80), trauma mechanism, ISS, the necessity of CPR on arrival, the location of REBOA insertion (emergency room or operating room) and the amount of PRBCs transfused in the first 24 h. Logistic regression (LR) was used to examine the association of LMICs and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 817 trauma patients from 14 countries were included. Blind percutaneous approach and surgical cutdown were the preferred means of femoral cannulation in HICs and LIMCs, respectively. Patients from LMICs had a significantly higher occurrence of MODS and respiratory failure. LR showed no differences in mortality for LMICs when compared to HICs; neither in the non-matched cohort (OR = 0.63; 95% CI: 0.36‑1.09; p = 0.1) nor in the matched cohort (OR = 1.45; 95% CI: 0.63‑3,33; p = 0.3). CONCLUSION: There is considerable variation in the management practices of REBOA and the outcomes associated with this intervention between HICs and LMICs. Although we found significant differences in multiorgan and respiratory failure rates, there were no differences in the risk-adjusted odds of mortality between the groups analyzed. Trauma surgeons practicing REBOA around the world should joint efforts to standardize the practice of this endovascular technology worldwide.

title: Relevance of Autophagy Induction by Gastrointestinal Hormones: Focus on the Incretin-Based Drug Target and Glucagon
abstract: The biology of autophagy in health and disease conditions has been intensively analyzed for decades. Several potential interventions can induce autophagy in preclinical research; however, none of these interventions are ready for translation to clinical practice yet. The topic of the current review is the molecular regulation of autophagy by glucagon, glucagon-like peptide (GLP)-1 and the GLP-1-degrading enzyme dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4). Glucagon is a well-known polypeptide that induces autophagy. In contrast, GLP-1 has been shown to inhibit glucagon secretion; GLP-1 also has been related to the induction of autophagy. DPP-4 inhibitors can induce autophagy in a GLP-1–dependent manner, but other diverse effects could be relevant. Here, we analyze the distinct molecular regulation of autophagy by glucagon, GLP-1, and DPP-4 inhibitors. Additionally, the potential contribution to autophagy by glucagon and GLP-1 after bariatric surgery is discussed.

title: Income-Generating Processes of Free Web-Based Digital Health Tools to Engage Patients: Qualitative Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: In recent years, digital tools have become a viable means for patients to address their health and information needs. Governments and health care organizations are offering digital tools such as self-assessment tools, symptom tracking tools, or chatbots. Other sources of digital tools, such as those offered through patient platforms, are available on the internet free of charge. We define patient platforms as health-specific websites that offer tools to anyone with internet access to engage them in their health care process with peer networks to support their learning. Although numerous social media platforms engage users without up-front charges, patient platforms are specific to health. As little is known about their business model, there is a need to understand what else these platforms are trying to achieve beyond supporting patients so that patients can make informed decisions about the benefits and risks of using the digital tools they offer. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to explore what patient platforms are trying to achieve beyond supporting patients and how their digital tools can be used to generate income. METHODS: Textual and visual data collected from a purposeful selection of 11 patient platforms from September 2013 to August 2014 were analyzed using framework analysis. Data were systematically and rigorously coded and categorized according to key issues and themes by following 5 steps: familiarizing, identifying a thematic framework, indexing, charting, and mapping and interpretation. We used open coding to identify additional concepts not captured in the initial thematic framework. This paper reports on emergent findings on the business models of the platforms and their income-generating processes. RESULTS: Our analysis revealed that in addition to patients, the platforms support other parties with interests in health and information exchanges. Patient platforms did not charge up-front fees but generated income from other sources, such as advertising, sponsorship, marketing (eg, sending information to users on behalf of sponsors or providing means for sponsors to reach patients directly), supporting other portals, and providing research services. CONCLUSIONS: This study reports on the mechanisms by which some patient platforms generate income to support their operations, gain profit, or both. Although income-generating processes exist elsewhere on social media platforms in general, they pose unique challenges in the health context because digital tools engage patients in health and information exchanges. This study highlights the need to minimize the potential for unintended consequences that can pose health risks to patients or can lead to increased health expenses. By understanding other interests that patient platforms support, our findings point to important policy implications, such as whether (and how) authorities might protect users from processes that may not always be in their best interests and can potentially incur costs to the health system.

title: Deep sequencing of primary human lung epithelial cells challenged with H5N1 influenza virus reveals a proviral role for CEACAM1
abstract: This study examines the effects of an influenza virus (H5N1) on primary human lung epithelial cells. Using deep sequencing, data from this preclinical medicine study reveals a previously unknown proviral role for CEACAM1 gene in response to this viral pathogen. By elucidating the mechanism by which virus interacts with cells and how genes can affect outcomes, we gain insight into developing new therapeutic approaches to address infection risks associated with H5N1 influenza virus. Through increased understanding of molecular pathways involved in population-level health events, findings from this research are valuable for informing public health decisions and potential clinical interventions.

title: Cardiac biomarkers in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis seeks to investigate the role of cardiac biomarkers in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The objective is to examine the clinical utility, safety profile, and other relevant outcomes associated with perioperative cardiac markers for risk stratification among this unique patient population. Perioperative cardiac troponin T levels have already been identified as important predictors of mortality among ARDS patients. However, there remain various unanswered questions regarding the overall risk stratification benefits that meticulous measurement of other established biomarkers may provide clinicians when assessing individuals suffering from ARDS. A comprehensive literature search was conducted which included studies published between 2007–2019 indexed on PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE databases. title: Adjunct low-dose ketamine infusion vs standard of care in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients at a Tertiary Saudi Hospital (ATTAINMENT Trial): study protocol for a randomized, prospective, pilot, feasibility trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: A noticeable interest in ketamine infusion for sedation management has developed among critical care physicians for critically ill patients. The 2018 Pain, Agitation/sedation, Delirium, Immobility, and Sleep disruption guideline suggested low-dose ketamine infusion as an adjunct to opioid therapy to reduce opioid requirements in post-surgical patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). This was, however, rated as conditional due to the very low quality of evidence. Ketamine has favorable characteristics, making it an especially viable alternative for patients with respiratory and hemodynamic instability. The Analgo-sedative adjuncT keTAmine Infusion iN Mechanically vENTilated ICU patients (ATTAINMENT) trial aims to assess the effect and safety of adjunct low-dose continuous infusion of ketamine as an analgo-sedative compared to standard of care in critically ill patients on mechanical ventilation (MV) for ≥ 24 h. METHODS/DESIGN: This trial is a prospective, randomized, active controlled, open-label, pilot, feasibility study of adult ICU patients (> 14 years old) on MV. The study will take place in the adult ICUs in the King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Center (KFSH&RC), Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and will enroll 80 patients. Patients will be randomized post-intubation into two groups: the intervention group will receive an adjunct low-dose continuous infusion of ketamine plus standard of care. Ketamine will be administered over a period of 48 h at a fixed infusion rate of 2 μg/kg/min (0.12 mg/kg/h) in the first 24 h followed by 1 μg/kg/min (0.06 mg/kg/h) in the second 24 h. The control group will receive standard of care in the ICU (propofol and/or fentanyl and/or midazolam) according to the KFSH&RC sedation and analgesia protocol as clinically appropriate. The primary outcome is MV duration until ICU discharge, death, extubation, or 28 days post-randomization, whichever comes first. DISCUSSION: The first patient was enrolled on 1 September 2019. As of 10 October 2019, a total of 16 patients had been enrolled. We expect to complete the recruitment by 31 December 2020. The findings of this pilot trial will likely justify further investigation for the role of adjunct low-dose ketamine infusion as an analgo-sedative agent in a larger, multicenter, randomized controlled trial. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04075006. Registered on 30 August 2019. Current controlled trials: ISRCTN14730035. Registered on 3 February 2020.

title: Post-transcriptional regulation of antiviral gene expression by N6-methyladenosine
abstract: The post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression is a fundamental process by which cells determine the level and rate of viral response. In this study, we focus on N6-methyladenosine (m6A), an epigenetic modification that occurs predominantly in the transcribed RNA strands and has been implicated in regulating antiviral gene expression in plants. We further characterize m6A modifications may mediate post-transcriptional control mechanisms to govern diverse aspects such as protein synthesis, mRNA stability, translational efficiency and other molecular functions critical to plant defense against viruses. Our results provide important insights into how m6A modulates plant immunity against viral infections and suggest potential routes for therapeutic intervention.

title: A mathematical representation of protein binding sites using structural dispersion of atoms from principal axes for classification of binding ligands
abstract: Many researchers have studied the relationship between the biological functions of proteins and the structures of both their overall backbones of amino acids and their binding sites. A large amount of the work has focused on summarizing structural features of binding sites as scalar quantities, which can result in a great deal of information loss since the structures are three-dimensional. Additionally, a common way of comparing binding sites is via aligning their atoms, which is a computationally intensive procedure that substantially limits the types of analysis and modeling that can be done. In this work, we develop a novel encoding of binding sites as covariance matrices of the distances of atoms to the principal axes of the structures. This representation is invariant to the chosen coordinate system for the atoms in the binding sites, which removes the need to align the sites to a common coordinate system, is computationally efficient, and permits the development of probability models. These can then be used to both better understand groups of binding sites that bind to the same ligand and perform classification for these ligand groups. We demonstrate the utility of our method for discrimination of binding ligand through classification studies with two benchmark datasets using nearest mean and polytomous logistic regression classifiers.

title: Population implications of the deployment of novel universal vaccines against epidemic and pandemic influenza
abstract: This study investigates the population implications of deploying a novel universal influenza vaccine with the aim of controlling epidemics and pandemics. Building on previous findings in public health research, this manuscript will examine how new vaccination procedures could lessen transmission rates and ultimately reduce mortality across different age groups by mostly targeting high risk demographic populations. It also aims to explore how variations in regional population structure could affect implementation strategies. Furthermore, social equity issues related to access and availability are going to be addressed as well. By taking into account such key elements impacting vaccine effectiveness, this paper intends to provide valuable insights which can help inform an evidence-based approach towards increasing disease prevention and control efforts against global flu outbreaks.

title: Ligand Clouds around Protein Clouds: A Scenario of Ligand Binding with Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) were found to be widely associated with human diseases and may serve as potential drug design targets. However, drug design targeting IDPs is still in the very early stages. Progress in drug design is usually achieved using experimental screening; however, the structural disorder of IDPs makes it difficult to characterize their interaction with ligands using experiments alone. To better understand the structure of IDPs and their interactions with small molecule ligands, we performed extensive simulations on the c-Myc(370–409) peptide and its binding to a reported small molecule inhibitor, ligand 10074-A4. We found that the conformational space of the apo c-Myc(370–409) peptide was rather dispersed and that the conformations of the peptide were stabilized mainly by charge interactions and hydrogen bonds. Under the binding of the ligand, c-Myc(370–409) remained disordered. The ligand was found to bind to c-Myc(370–409) at different sites along the chain and behaved like a ‘ligand cloud’. In contrast to ligand binding to more rigid target proteins that usually results in a dominant bound structure, ligand binding to IDPs may better be described as ligand clouds around protein clouds. Nevertheless, the binding of the ligand and a non-ligand to the c-Myc(370–409) target could be clearly distinguished. The present study provides insights that will help improve rational drug design that targets IDPs.

title: Tight junctions in pulmonary epithelia during lung inflammation
abstract: This article provides an overview of the role that tight junctions (TJs) play in mediating pulmonary inflammatory responses. TJs are a specialized form of cell-cell junctions found in epithelial cells, which control permeability and regulate the passage of water and solutes between epithelial layers by forming impermeable barriers. Recent studies have begun to explore how changes to TJ integrity at the site of inflammation may affect passive transport mechanisms such as transcytosis that are essential for maintaining proper lung function. Evidence shows increased leukocyte infiltration due to decreased TJ sealing contributes significantly to airway obstruction resulting from excessive mucus production, leading to severe respiratory distress during acute lung injury. This article aims to discuss aberrations occurring in TJ architecture under different pulmonic pathological conditions and its systemic effects on overlying electrophysiologic processes regulating pulmonary immune homeostasis.

title: Soluble Form of Canine Transferrin Receptor Inhibits Canine Parvovirus Infection In Vitro and In Vivo
abstract: Canine parvovirus (CPV) disease is an acute, highly infectious disease threatening the dog-raising industry. So far there are no effective therapeutic strategies to control this disease. Although the canine transferrin receptor (TfR) was identified as a receptor for CPV infection, whether extracellular domain of TfR (called soluble TfR (sTfR)) possesses anti-CPV activities remains elusive. Here, we used the recombinant sTfR prepared from HEK293T cells with codon-optimized gene structure to investigate its anti-CPV activity both in vitro and in vivo. Our results indicated that codon optimization could significantly improve sTfR expression in HEK293T cells. The prepared recombinant sTfR possessed a binding activity to both CPV and CPV VP2 capsid proteins and significantly inhibited CPV infection of cultured feline F81 cells and decreased the mortality of CPV-infected dogs, which indicates that the sTfR has the anti-CPV activity both in vitro and in vivo.

title: New quality and quantity indices in science (NewQIS): results of the first decade—project progress review
abstract: This review provides an overview of the findings and progress made while developing NewQIS, a novel set of quality and quantity indices in science. NewQIS was initially proposed over 10 years ago with the goal of measuring research productivity accurately, reliably and consistently for comparison purposes among different scientific disciplines. This project has introduced multiple criteria beyond traditional output metrics (e.g., publication count) that measure the wider impact of academic output on society and other stakeholders (e.g., public engagement). After a decade-long study, this review examines how these measures have influenced scholarly communications by charting advancements such as introducing more robust indicators from diverse sources like online bibliographic databases as well as social media data. Significantly, it demonstrates how NewQIS can help institutions to monitor civilizational prospects associated with values such as freedom or justice that rely heavily on knowledge created through modern science communication platforms which often go unaccounted for within existing metrics used to assess performance outcomes in academia.

title: Expression profiling of microRNAs in lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury after hypothermia treatment
abstract: We investigated the expression profiles of miRNAs in acute lung injury (ALI) rats after hypothermia treatment. ALI rats were induced with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and maintained with hypothermia (HT) or normothermia (NT) for 6 hours. HT attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration in the lung and improved biochemical indicators of multi-organ dysfunction. Nineteen miRNAs were significantly differentially expressed in the HT group compared with the NT group. miR-142, miR-98, miR-541, miR-503, miR-653, miR- 223, miR-323 and miR-196b exhibited opposite patterns of expression between the two groups. These dysregulated miRNAs were mainly involved in the immune and inflammatory response on functional annotation analyses. This study shows that HT has lung protective effects and influences expression profiles of miRNAs in ALI. And dysregulated miRNAs after HT modulate the immune and inflammation in ALI. These results suggest that dysregulated miRNAs play a role in the mechanism of the lung protective effects of HT in ALI.

title: Universal evolutionary selection for high dimensional silent patterns of information hidden in the redundancy of viral genetic code
abstract: This paper explores the implications of the discovery that evolutionary selection supports universal patterns of information embedded within viral genetic code. Known as ‘silent patterns’, these elements are primarily manifested in higher dimensions which can make them difficult to discern and define. To better understand how this phenomenon is applicable across numerous organisms, a comprehensive evaluation was conducted analyzing several strands of DNA for coding and non-coding segments. Results show that conspicuous levels of information redundancy exist at various lengths throughout viruses; further illuminating their importance in successful propagation and transmission over long periods of time. Findings indicate there is a consistent evolutionary force preserving characteristic features within the redundant sections along different branches within the genealogy tree — suggesting they contain vital adaptive advantages essential for survival and adaptation into new environments by encoding additional attributes beyond basic genes expressed biologically. These relationships suggest an important role for silent patterns beyond traditional sources or constraints leading to practical applications where understanding higher dimensional optimization blocks will be beneficial when designing future products such as improved antiviral treatments or prevention strategies targeting possible outbreaks on global scales.

title: Well-Being at Work after Return to Work (RTW): A Systematic Review
abstract: Background: Employees’ well-being at work after the return to work (RTW) is considered a key aspect of rehabilitation and maintenance of workability. This systematic review aimed at identifying the common psychosocial factors that predict the subjective and psychological well-being in RTW processes after having a long-standing health problem or disability. Objective: To evaluate the subjective and psychological well-being at work of employees with chronic or long-standing health problems or those returning to work after any cause of disability. Data source: Systematic review of articles published in English or Spanish using PsycINFO, PsycARTICLES, MEDLINE, Psychology, and Behavioral Sciences Collection, and Pubpsych. An additional study was identified by contacting expert academics in the field. The search equations used included terms such as Return to Work, Long-Standing Health Problems or Disability, Work Health Balance, and job satisfaction or subjective well-being. Eligibility criteria for the studies: Studies that included a measure of employees’ well-being at work following return to work were selected for the review. Evaluation of the studies and synthesis methods: The studies were selected using predefined fields which included quality criteria. Results: Of the 264 articles returned by the initial search, a total of 20 were finally selected. Results were organized around the three different theoretical approaches for understanding RTW and its antecedents and consequences: (a) RTW and autonomy at work have a positive effect on psychological well-being; (b) job demand is linked to less job satisfaction, whereas a higher level on the work–health balance is associated with job satisfaction and work engagement; (c) internal and external support is linked to job satisfaction in the case of a disease. Limitations: The evidence provided by the results is restricted by the limited availability of studies focusing on well-being at work following return to work. Moreover, the studies identified are of different kinds, thereby preventing comparisons. Conclusions and implications of the main findings: Employees’ subjective well-being after return to work has received very little attention to date. Given its importance in the current configuration of the labor market, it should be the object of more research.

title: A revision of the western Palaearctic species of Urophora Robineau‐Desvoidy (Diptera: Tephritidae)
abstract: Abstract A key is provided to twenty‐four western Palaearctic species of Urophora Robineau‐Desvoidy. The hosts of twenty‐three species which attack Asteraceae are listed, including those being used or investigated as possible weed biocontrol agents. The species are divided into four species groups and the differing host relationships and types of galls induced by these groups are discussed. U.lopholomae sp.n. and U.affinis ssp. calcitrapae ssp.n., associated with Centaurea (Lopholoma) spp. and C. (Calcitrapa) spp. respectively, are described. U. algerica (Hering) and U.sjumorum (Rohdendorf) are both treated as subspecies of U. quadrifasciata (Meigen). U.pontica is given full specific status and U.hispanica is removed from synonymy. The following new synonymies are made (junior synonyms in parentheses): U. angustifascia (Hering) (=Euribia phaeocera Hering); U. cardui (Linnaeus) (=U. reaumurii Robineau‐Desvoidy, lectotype designated); U. jaceana (Hering) (=E.conyzae Hering); U.maura (Frauenfeld) (=E. tecta Hering); U. mauritanica Macquart (=U. lejura Rondani, Trypeta macrura Loew); U.solstitialis (Linnaeus) (=E.sonderupi Hering, U. veruata Rondani); U.stylata (Fabricius) (=E.pia Hering, U. vulcaanica Rondani); U. terebrans (Loew) (=E. approximata Hering, T. eriolepidis Loew, E. manni Hendel). The possibility that U. quadrifasciata is a species complex is discussed; it is also suggested that U.affinis and U.jaceana represent the morphological extremes of a complex. The misuse of the name Musca stylata Fabricius in the genus Myopites Blot is noted.

title: Transcriptional host–pathogen responses of Pseudogymnoascus destructans and three species of bats with white-nose syndrome
abstract: This scientific journal aims to investigate the transcriptional host–pathogen responses of Pseudogymnoascus destructans, a newly identified species associated with white-nose syndrome (WNS) in three species of bats. In recent years, WNS has emerged as one of the most devastating wildlife epidemics endangering bat populations in North America and Europe. This deadly fungal infection not only causes significant mortality among affected species but also changes their natural habitats and behavior patterns, causing far-reaching ecological effects on surrounding ecosystems. title: Buccal Bone Changes Around First Permanent Molars and Second Primary Molars after Maxillary Expansion with a Low Compliance Ni–Ti Leaf Spring Expander
abstract: This paper aims to explore the changes in buccal bone levels of first permanent and second primary molars in children treated with a Low Compliance Ni–Ti leaf spring expander for maxillary expansion. In order to achieve an accurate evaluation, Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) images were used to assess the changes before, during and after treatment. 27 children treated with the device between 10-12 years of age were selected from a sample population of over 200 children from private orthodontic clinics located across Brazil. Results showed significant differences between measurements taken before and after expansion, indicating that an increase on buccal bone level was observed mainly at lower regions around both types of teeth analyzed. These findings provide evidence for improved clinical management protocols when using this type of expanders due to its low compliance characteristics.

title: Innovative Drug Treatments for Viral and Autoimmune Myocarditis
abstract: This article examines the prospect of novel drug treatments for viral and autoimmune myocarditis, a life-threatening disease initiated by inflammation of the heart muscle. Existing therapies rely on inhibiting immune activity or attacking viruses from the onset; however, their effectiveness is limited. Novel treatment approaches may offer the potential to successfully target this multifaceted pathologic state with greater precision. Through an exploration of current literature, clinical data and preclinical investigations, this paper will provide insight into plausible therapeutic strategies that are being developed in order to improve patient outcome associated with myocarditis. In conclusion, advances made in drug design should facilitate earlier detection and improved management approaches which can reduce mortality rates in patients suffering from both viral and autoimmune forms of myocarditis.

title: Effectiveness of Integrated HIV Prevention Interventions among Chinese Men Who Have Sex with Men: Evaluation of a 16-City Public Health Program
abstract:
The HIV/AIDS pandemic has disproportionately impacted vulnerable populations including men who have sex with men (MSM). To address this, the Chinese government implemented an integrated 16-city public health program to increase access to and effectiveness of prevention interventions for MSM. This paper evaluates the impact of that program on reducing HIV prevalence among identified participant groups in representative cities. 

We begin by conducting a comprehensive review of existing datasets examining relevant factors and sociocultural differences. Building from those findings, we use a mixed methods quantitative analysis to evaluate whether planning-level changes successfully translated into actionable outcomes at both the individual level and citywide scale. Our results are then used to assess success levels and make recommendations for future integrated prevention strategies. The study provides valuable insights into public health policy efficacy in highly populated areas around China as well as identify potential obstacles which hinder effective implementation of such strategies within high risk communities like MSM populations living in urban settings across China.

title: Protein Disulfide Isomerase and Host-Pathogen Interaction
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) production by immunological cells is known to cause damage to pathogens. Increasing evidence accumulated in the last decade has shown, however, that ROS (and redox signals) functionally regulate different cellular pathways in the host-pathogen interaction. These especially affect (i) pathogen entry through protein redox switches and redox modification (i.e., intra- and interdisulfide and cysteine oxidation) and (ii) phagocytic ROS production via Nox family NADPH oxidase enzyme and the control of phagolysosome function with key implications for antigen processing. The protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) family of redox chaperones is closely involved in both processes and is also implicated in protein unfolding and trafficking across the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and towards the cytosol, a thiol-based redox locus for antigen processing. Here, we summarise examples of the cellular association of host PDI with different pathogens and explore the possible roles of pathogen PDIs in infection. A better understanding of these complex regulatory steps will provide insightful information on the redox role and coevolutional biological process, and assist the development of more specific therapeutic strategies in pathogen-mediated infections.

title: A Component Analysis of the Mindfulness-Based Positive Behavior Support (MBPBS) Program for Mindful Parenting by Mothers of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Mindfulness-Based Positive Behavior Support (MBPBS) has been shown to be effective in reducing stress and burnout in parents and professional caregivers of children and adolescents with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The aim of this study was to assess the comparative effects of the mindfulness (MB) and positive behavior support (PBS) components against the MBPBS program for mindful parenting. METHODS: The study utilized a three-arm randomized controlled trial design, with a 10-week pre-treatment control condition, 30 weeks of intervention, and 3 years of post-intervention follow-up. Mothers of children with ASD were randomly assigned to the MB, PBS, and MBPBS conditions and provided 3 days of training specific to each condition. The effects of these programs were assessed on the mothers (i.e., training attendance, meditation time, perceived psychological stress) and spillover effects were assessed on their children with ASD (i.e., aggression, disruptive behavior, compliance with mothers’ requests). RESULTS: Mothers in the MBPBS condition reported greater reductions in perceived psychological stress, followed by those in the MB condition, and with no significant changes reported by those in the PBS condition. Reduction in the children’s aggression and disruptive behavior followed a similar pattern, with most to least significant reductions being in MBPBS, MB, and PBS condition, respectively. Significant increases in compliance (i.e., responsiveness to mothers’ requests) were largest in the MBPBS condition, followed by MB, and then PBS. Changes across all variables for both mothers and their children were maintained for 3 years post-intervention. After time and training type were controlled for, meditation time was a significant predictor in reducing aggressive and disruptive behaviors, and in enhancing compliance of the children with mothers’ requests. CONCLUSIONS: Positive outcomes for mothers and their children with ASD were significantly greater in the MBPBS condition, followed by the MB condition, and least in the PBS condition. MBPBS appears to be an effective mindful parenting program on the assessed variables.

title: Serologic Markers for Ebolavirus Among Healthcare Workers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: This study investigates the presence of serologic markers for Ebolavirus among healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Ebola virus disease is a highly-infectious viral hemorrhagic fever known to cause mortality rates as high as 90%. Outbreaks in West Africa and DRC have highlighted the need for heightened surveillance especially among healthcare facilities. To evaluate risk levels, this study analyzes serum samples from 127 Congolese health care workers collected over a period of four months. Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assays (ELISAs) are employed to measure humoral immune response with each participant providing written informed consent prior to their inclusion. This cross sectional epidemiological study seeks to investigate if Healthcare Workers in the DRC have been exposed or infected by Eblovirus and assess correlations between demographic data and ELISA results in order to better understand potential risk factors associated with infection.

title: Effects and safety of tanreqing injection on viral pneumonia: A protocol for systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effects and safety of Tanreqing injection on viral pneumonia by conducting a systematic review and meta-analysis. Viral pneumonia, one of the most dangerous infectious diseases worldwide, is associated with high rates of mortality. Recently, an effective new preventive treatment based on ancient Chinese herbal medicine, called Tanreqing injection (TTQ), has proven successful in decreasing symptoms related to viral pneumonia. This systematic review and meta-analysis intends to assess the efficacy and safety profile of TTQ by comparing it with conventional treatments like antibiotics and antiviral drugs as prescribed for treating viral pneumonia. A literature search will be conducted within relevant databases such as Medline/PubMed, Embase/Cochrane Library etc., identifying randomized control trials (RCTs) that have included patients diagnosed clinically or radiologically with viral pneumonia. The primary outcomes measures include safety parameters including adverse drug reactions while secondary outcomes measure clinical effectiveness evaluated through criteria like virus clearance time or proportion of cured cases without relapse rate whereas vital sign variations from baseline values constitute supportive variables throughout this analysis process. Thus our findings may optimistically help demonstrate whether TTQ can be used for routine management - both as therapeutic liniment & as an adjunct therapy - for treating different types of acute & chronic infection caused by various strains of viruses leading to severe respiratory condition commonly known as septic virus lung disease or ‘pneumonia’ in modern era parlance..

title: Microbial Electrochemical Systems: Principles, Construction and Biosensing Applications
abstract: This paper outlines an overview of microbial electrochemical systems (MES) – a vibrant and fast-growing field in environmental engineering. With the development of novel techniques, these systems are now being applied to various industrial and medical tasks such as biosensing. This review explores the fundamentals of MES, including principles of operation, construction guidelines, and available biosensing applications. A comparative analysis between traditional sensors and mimetic bioelectrochemical systems approaches is also presented along with their respective advantages in terms of performance capabilities. By introducing innovative ways to construct biosensors based on cutting-edge research methods, this report provides readers with valuable insight into how MES can be used for real world problems encountered by professionals across diverse sectors.

title: Effect of plasma vitamin C levels on Parkinson’s disease and age at onset: a Mendelian randomization study
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between plasma vitamin C levels, Parkinson’s disease (PD) and age at onset using Mendelian randomization. It has been postulated that oxidative stress caused by a lack of antioxidant nutrients could increase one's risk for PD, but less is known about how vitamin C levels specifically impact their risk. To examine this hypothesis more closely, researchers have conducted a Mendelian randomization study on 2097 participants with genetically-determined plasma concentrations of vitamin C and 7093 control individuals. Upon analysis, they found an inverse correlation between plasma vitamin C levels and PD development before 70 years of age; compared to those in the lowest quintile of vitamincC levelsthe highest quintile was associated with a 54% lower odds-ratio for developing PD. Furthermore, every 1 SD increase in log-transformed plasma Vitamin levels was associated with an 11% decreased odds ratio for adolescent/young adult onset disease (<40). This illustrates that higher serum Vitamin concentrations may reduce susceptibility to develop PD prior to 70 years old as well as protect against early onset cases occurring before the age of 40. Overall these findings suggest cause for further efficacy testing into whether or not increasing dietary intake or supplementation could help reduce one's likelihood for early stage Parkinson's development due factors such as reduced oxidative stress and improved neuronal health.

title: Etiological, epidemiological, and clinical features of acute diarrhea in China
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the etiological, epidemiological and clinical features associated with acute diarrhea in China. Acute diarrhea remains a major public health concern in this region due to its potential impact on morbidity, mortality, and hospitalization rates among minority populations. To gain insight into this critical problem, we performed a comprehensive review of published literature on the subject to investigate trends related to causative agents and exacerbated factors. The results drew attention to various pathogens as well as dietary or environmental characteristics which may lead to significant outbreaks that may affect even vulnerable patient groups such as children or elderly individuals. Furthermore, evidence regarding socio-economic variables has been provided that can influence both the symptomatic outcome for patients suffering from acute cases of travelers’ diarrhea but also long term consequences including disruption in quality-of-life issues or disproportionate burden within certain potentially at-risk communities. As such, further research based upon these preliminary findings is important for facilitating adequate policy implementation and treatment strategy development across different age groups across urbanized areas of China where incidence numbers are expectedly increasing over time.

title: Progress in the Development of Eukaryotic Elongation Factor 2 Kinase (eEF2K) Natural Product and Synthetic Small Molecule Inhibitors for Cancer Chemotherapy
abstract: Eukaryotic elongation factor 2 kinase (eEF2K) has emerged as an important target for cancer chemotherapy, particularly given the promising initial results in clinical trials. This paper discusses recent progress in the development of natural product and synthetic small-molecule inhibitors of eEF2K for use in cancer therapies due to their ability to induce cell death and prevent tumour progression. First, it reviews existing literature on this topic with evidence from investigations into drugs such as PMI 60004 and Resveratrol Synthesis inhibitors that suggest potential efficacy. This is followed by a focus on determining active substances involved in these compounds which can be isolated from natural sources or produced synthetically along with biophysical characterization protocols used to further confirm binding interactions between biochemical pathways associated with eEF2K inhibition and anticancer agents. Finally, methods are discussed which address challenges like formulation stability and biological activity to ensure potency against different disease states while limiting undesirable side effects on healthy cells. Taken together, this review provides new insights into the prospective therapeutic value of selected compounds which are capable of inhibiting eEF2K antiproliferative capacity thereby offering promise for enhanced cancer treatment outcomes.

title: Uncommon cause of cardiac tamponade in a young man
abstract: This paper explores an uncommon cause of cardiac tamponade in a young man. A 44-year-old male was admitted to the emergency department with chest pain and dyspnea. Initial labs, radiological investigations and echocardiographic studies revealed the presence of pericardial effusion causing extensive right ventricular collapse leading to cardiac tamponade as a result of drug ingestion. He had few episodes prior months due to deliberate self-poisoning with two antihypertensive drugs known as clonidine and propranolol resulting in acute intoxication. To our surprise this unusual combination was found out to be responsible for inducing rapid progression from mild pericardial effusion up till severe grade IV contusive tamponade. This study highlights an extremely uinique cause of cardiac pump failure requiring ever vigilant diagnosis in such cases which may otherwise turn fatal without immediate intervention .

title: Matrix stiffness modulates infection of endothelial cells by Listeria monocytogenes via expression of cell surface vimentin
abstract: Extracellular matrix stiffness (ECM) is one of the many mechanical forces acting on mammalian adherent cells and an important determinant of cellular function. While the effect of ECM stiffness on many aspects of cellular behavior has been studied previously, how ECM stiffness might mediate susceptibility of host cells to infection by bacterial pathogens is hitherto unexplored. To address this open question, we manufactured hydrogels of varying physiologically relevant stiffness and seeded human microvascular endothelial cells (HMEC-1) on them. We then infected HMEC-1 with the bacterial pathogen Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) and found that adhesion of Lm to host cells increases monotonically with increasing matrix stiffness, an effect that requires the activity of focal adhesion kinase (FAK). We identified cell surface vimentin as a candidate surface receptor mediating stiffness-dependent adhesion of Lm to HMEC-1 and found that bacterial infection of these host cells is decreased when the amount of surface vimentin is reduced. Our results provide the first evidence that ECM stiffness can mediate the susceptibility of mammalian host cells to infection by a bacterial pathogen.

title: Molecular screening of pathogenic Escherichia coli strains isolated from dairy neonatal calves in Cordoba province, Argentina
abstract: The aim of this study was to perform a current molecular characterization of bovine pathogenic Escherichia coli strains isolated from random samplings in Argentinean dairy farms. Rectal swabs were obtained from 395 (63.7 %) healthy and 225 (36.3 %) diarrheic calves, belonging to 45 dairy farms in Cordoba Province, Argentina. E. coli isolates were examined for virulence genes (f5, f41, f17, sta, stb, lt, eae, vt) using PCR and the prevalence of E. coli virulence profiles was spatially described in terms of spatial distribution. A total of 30.1 % isolates were found to be positive for at least one of the virulence genes. Depending on the different gene combinations present, 11 virulence profiles were found. Most of the isolates analyzed had a single gene, and no combination of fimbrial and enterotoxin gene was predominant. There was no association between the frequency and distribution of E. coli virulence genes and calf health status. Most of the virulence profiles were compatible with ETEC strains and showed a homogeneous distribution over the sampled area. A clustering pattern for E. coli virulence profiles could not be recognized. This work provides updated information on the molecular characterization of pathogenic E. coli strains from dairy herds in Cordoba, Argentina. These findings would be important to formulate prevention programs and effective therapies for diarrhea in calves caused by E. coli.

title: Molecular pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus
abstract: This article presents an overview of the molecular pathogenesis underlying systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by autoreactive B and T cells that attack anatomic, functional and immunologic components of the host. Using in-depth review and analysis, this paper investigates how abnormal activation of epigenetic processes has been implicated as playing a pivotal role in SLE pathogenesis. title: “Non-Essential” Proteins of HSV-1 with Essential Roles In Vivo: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Viruses encode for structural proteins that participate in virion formation and include capsid and envelope proteins. In addition, viruses encode for an array of non-structural accessory proteins important for replication, spread, and immune evasion in the host and are often linked to virus pathogenesis. Most virus accessory proteins are non-essential for growth in cell culture because of the simplicity of the infection barriers or because they have roles only during a state of the infection that does not exist in cell cultures (i.e., tissue-specific functions), or finally because host factors in cell culture can complement their absence. For these reasons, the study of most nonessential viral factors is more complex and requires development of suitable cell culture systems and in vivo models. Approximately half of the proteins encoded by the herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) genome have been classified as non-essential. These proteins have essential roles in vivo in counteracting antiviral responses, facilitating the spread of the virus from the sites of initial infection to the peripheral nervous system, where it establishes lifelong reservoirs, virus pathogenesis, and other regulatory roles during infection. Understanding the functions of the non-essential proteins of herpesviruses is important to understand mechanisms of viral pathogenesis but also to harness properties of these viruses for therapeutic purposes. Here, we have provided a comprehensive summary of the functions of HSV-1 non-essential proteins.

title: Activity data from wearables as an indicator of functional capacity in patients with cardiovascular disease
abstract: BACKGROUND: Smartphone and wearable-based activity data provide an opportunity to remotely monitor functional capacity in patients. In this study, we assessed the ability of a home-based 6-minute walk test (6MWT) as well as passively collected activity data to supplement or even replace the in-clinic 6MWTs in patients with cardiovascular disease. METHODS: We enrolled 110 participants who were scheduled for vascular or cardiac procedures. Each participant was supplied with an iPhone and an Apple Watch running the VascTrac research app and was followed for 6 months. Supervised 6MWTs were performed during clinic visits at scheduled intervals. Weekly at-home 6MWTs were performed via the VascTrac app. The app passively collected activity data such as daily step counts. Logistic regression with forward feature selection was used to assess at-home 6MWT and passive data as predictors for “frailty” as measured by the gold-standard supervised 6MWT. Frailty was defined as walking <300m on an in-clinic 6MWT. RESULTS: Under a supervised in-clinic setting, the smartphone and Apple Watch with the VascTrac app were able to accurately assess ‘frailty’ with sensitivity of 90% and specificity of 85%. Outside the clinic in an unsupervised setting, the home-based 6MWT is 83% sensitive and 60% specific in assessing “frailty.” Passive data collected at home were nearly as accurate at predicting frailty on a clinic-based 6MWT as was a home-based 6MWT, with area under curve (AUC) of 0.643 and 0.704, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this longitudinal observational study, passive activity data acquired by an iPhone and Apple Watch were an accurate predictor of in-clinic 6MWT performance. This finding suggests that frailty and functional capacity could be monitored and evaluated remotely in patients with cardiovascular disease, enabling safer and higher resolution monitoring of patients.

title: Viral RNA switch mediates the dynamic control of flavivirus replicase recruitment by genome cyclization
abstract: Viral replicase recruitment and long-range RNA interactions are essential for RNA virus replication, yet the mechanism of their interplay remains elusive. Flaviviruses include numerous important human pathogens, e.g., dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV). Here, we revealed a highly conserved, conformation-tunable cis-acting element named 5′-UAR-flanking stem (UFS) in the flavivirus genomic 5′ terminus. We demonstrated that the UFS was critical for efficient NS5 recruitment and viral RNA synthesis in different flaviviruses. Interestingly, stabilization of the DENV UFS impaired both genome cyclization and vRNA replication. Moreover, the UFS unwound in response to genome cyclization, leading to the decreased affinity of NS5 for the viral 5′ end. Thus, we propose that the UFS is switched by genome cyclization to regulate dynamic RdRp binding for vRNA replication. This study demonstrates that the UFS enables communication between flavivirus genome cyclization and RdRp recruitment, highlighting the presence of switch-like mechanisms among RNA viruses. title: Economic Burden and Health Care Access for Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Diseases in China: Web-Based Survey Study
abstract: This study presents the results of a web-based survey to evaluate the economic burden and health care access of patients with inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) in China. In recent years, IBD has been increasingly prevalent due to environmental factors and lifestyle changes. Previous studies have documented the challenges associated with accessing healthcare services for those affected by IBD, however such information is rarely detailed or systematically recorded in China due to longstanding healthcare disparities between urban and rural areas. The objective of this survey was to collect comprehensive sociodemographic data from Chinese IBD patients regarding their medical costs, usage of healthcare services, satisfaction levels with existing treatment plans, and awareness about available treatments for their condition. In addition to providing valuable insight into patient needs related to management of a chronic condition like IBD, these findings can also inform strategies for improved delivery at lower cost within the Chinese healthcare system as well as policies that support quality access for all patients regardless of geographical location or financial status.

title: The Impact of Infectious Diseases on the Development of Africa
abstract:
The Impact of Infectious Diseases on the Development of Africa 
Immunization, access to healthcare and welfare, efficient management of resources are some of the cornerstones for achieving sustainable economic growth and development. Although there has been significant progress in these areas over recent decades, much of Sub-Saharan Africa continues to lag behind other regions. This can be attributed to a number of contributing factors such as poverty and government instability however another central issue is infectious diseases which have had an outsize impact on health and mortality outcomes throughout the region. This paper aims to explore the association between infectious diseases and their effects on infrastructure, life expectancy, productivity levels and economic output in Sub-Saharan Africa both before and after interventions by various international organizations such as United Nations Development Program (UNDP), Global Fund (GF) etc., through employing qualitative research techniques compiled from secondary literature sources that highlight successes or failures experienced in each local context. It is hoped that any lessons learned will go towards crafting novel approaches for mitigating these problems in future policy formulation thereby driving inclusive development within African countries with a strong emphasis equity & quality service delivery irrespective socioeconomic status or geographical locations.

title: Hydrocortisone and bronchopulmonary dysplasia: variables associated with response in premature infants
abstract: This study examines the variables associated with response to hydrocortisone therapy for bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) in premature infants. BPD is a common, chronic lung disorder that can affect the development and function of an infant’s lungs, often resulting from prematurity. Previous studies show conflicting results regarding whether age at first dose and maximal dose of hydrocortisone affects long-term outcomes among these neonates. In order to assess this question, we will survey a sample of children aged 5-8 years who have been treated with hydrocortisone during their infancy and analyze the links between dosage and long-term health outcomes related to BPD severity. The findings of this research may provide critical evidence on dosing strategies that could potentially improve survival rate and health prognosis in preterm babies born with BPD.

title: People With Advanced Cancer: The Process of Living Well With Awareness of Dying
abstract: This paper examines how individuals with advanced cancer create pathways for envisioning and enacting meaningful lives, despite their illness. Drawing on one-on-one semi-structured interviews with nine people living with advanced cancer, the study identifies practices of enculturation as essential to living well in awareness of dying. Through cultural activities framed by being ‘alive’ and a focus on maintaining consciousness while reorientating one's relationships, participants demonstrate courage, grace and resilience in responding to illness. To broaden our understanding of life amidst disease trajectories through to death this research foregrounds narratives that seek to normalize dialogue around end–of–life needs.

title: Overexpression of an apple LysM-containing protein gene, MdCERK1–2, confers improved resistance to the pathogenic fungus, Alternaria alternata, in Nicotiana benthamiana
abstract:
Title: Overexpression of MdCERK1–2 Gene Enhances Resistance against Alternaria alternata in Nicotiana benthamiana 
The immense crop losses caused by plant bacterial and fungal pathogens have been a major concern, spurring efforts to develop pathogen resistant varieties. The emerging evidence from transcriptome analyses has demonstrated the importance of LysM-containing proteins (LysM-CPs) in context to the recognition and signaling of an array of microbe associated molecular patterns (MAMPs), thereby inducing host resistance. Here we report that overexpression of apple LysM-CP gene, MdCERK1–2 in Nicotiana benthamina significantly enhances its resistance against Alternaria alternata pathogen which causes early blight disease on its leaves. Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis revealed higher expression levels for MdCERK1–2 messenger RNA upon inoculation with A. alternata compared to noninoculated control plants as well as upregulation at different time points post infection. Phenotypic evaluations indicated that over expression conferred enhanced protection against symptoms such as necrotic spots on inoculated leaves along with lesser area under earliness lesion progression curves representing lower lesions count than control infected lines. Further investigations suggested the defense related genes are upregulated earlier when MdCEKR1–2 gene was constitutively expressed suggesting it’s involvement in priming host immune response machinery prior attempted microbial infiltration which translates into improved resistance capacity; thus deploying this strategy could be useful for improving crop yield/productivity owing to reduced disease consequences caused due to susceptible varieties having deficient or poor interaction between MAMP receptors like MdCERK12 and effector molecules employed by microbes used for colonization process during inducing diseases

title: Cardiorespiratory behavior of preterm infants receiving continuous positive airway pressure and high flow nasal cannula post extubation: randomized crossover study
abstract: The present study examines the cardiorespiratory behavior of preterm infants receiving either continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or a high flow nasal cannula (HFNC) post extubation. Prematurity is early birth that can lead to significant health concerns for developing infants, including the struggle to breathe and maintain adequate oxygen levels. During hospitalization, premature babies may be intubated and kept on a ventilator in order to support their breathing; however, this process carries the risk of causing further damage due frequent tube removal and insertion. Therefore, we investigated how two non-invasive methods – CPAP and HFNC – affect cardiorespiratory function among preterm infants shortly after completion of mechanical ventilation. This randomized crossover study had each infant receive 24 hours of CPAP followed by 48 hours of HFNC as well as vice versa for comparison purposes in order to assess behavior related differences between these interventions following extubation. The findings from this study will be critical in determining which method has better clinical outcomes when used immediately after discarding the ventilator machine in preterm patients, providing valuable implications for care practices with this delicate population.

title: Validation of the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire in Korean Older Adults(*)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate psychometric properties of the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire (MCTQ) in a sample of Korean older adults. METHODS: One-hundred ninety two participants aged 65 and over completed interview-based questionnaires about chronotype, insomnia, depression, and anxiety. Additionally, a small subset of subjects completed a 7-day sleep diary and actigraphy measurements. RESULTS: Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ) scores were significantly negatively correlated with Midpoint of sleep on free days corrected for sleep debt accumulated through weekdays (MSFsc) (r=-0.45, p<0.01) assessed by the MCTQ. MSFsc using the MCTQ was significantly positively correlated with MSFsc assessed by both the sleep diary (r=0.74, p<0.05) and actigraphy (r=0.76, p<0.05). Additionally, MSFsc assessed by the MCTQ was significantly positively correlated with insomnia (r=0.26, p<0.01), depression (r=0.25, p<0.01), and anxiety (r=0.18, p<0.05). Finally, based on MEQ scores, we derived a cut-off score for the MCTQ that distinguishes morning type and other types (intermediate/evening types) in older adults. CONCLUSION: The results of these studies supported the validity of the MCTQ in Korean older adults. Additionally, while sleep rhythms in elder adults may be more advanced, eveningness tendency may be still important and indicative of sleep and psychological disturbance.

title: Capsid-deficient alphaviruses generate propagative infectious microvesicles at the plasma membrane
abstract: Alphavirus budding is driven by interactions between nucleocapsids assembled in the cytoplasm and envelope proteins present at the plasma membrane. So far, the expression of capsid and envelope proteins in infected cells has been considered an absolute requirement for alphavirus budding and propagation. In the present study, we show that Semliki Forest virus and Sindbis virus lacking the capsid gene can propagate in mammalian and insect cells. This propagation is mediated by the release of infectious microvesicles (iMVs), which are pleomorphic and have a larger size and density than wild-type virus. iMVs, which contain viral RNA inside and viral envelope proteins on their surface, are released at the plasma membrane and infect cells using the endocytic pathway in a similar way to wild-type virus. iMVs are not pathogenic in immunocompetent mice when injected intravenously, but can infect different organs like lungs and heart. Finally, we also show that alphavirus genomes without capsid can mediate the propagation of heterologous genes, making these vectors potentially interesting for gene therapy or vaccination studies. The minimalist infectious system described in this study shows that a self-replicating RNA able to express membrane proteins with binding and fusion properties is able to propagate, providing some insights into virus evolution. title: Quantifying heterogeneous contact patterns in Japan: a social contact survey
abstract: This paper presents a study of quantifying heterogeneous contact patterns in Japan using a social contact survey. The objective of the survey was to evaluate and compare levels of physical contacts among different groups based on age, gender, occupation, educational attainment and socio-economic status. To achieve this goal, survey participants were asked to record all physical contacts for one full month and their demographic information was collected as well. For analysis purposes the data obtained from the survey was coded according to specific criteria from both population size estimates published by local municipalities in Japan and internationally accepted classifications related to health behavior science. By comparing the results of our research with existing databases it has been possible to identify varying levels of social contacts across different population segments while giving emphasis on measuring inequalities due to differences such as age or gender during particular periods or conditions (e.g., working hours). Moreover, our findings provide precious insights regarding how heterogeneous contact patterns influence behaviors that can affect public health during times of crisis response strategies like those implemented following natural disasters like earthquakes or floods.
