title: Impact of fluid balance on outcome of adult patients treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the relationship between early daily fluid balance (FB) and 90-day outcome in adult patients treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. SETTING: Tertiary referral centre for ECMO. PATIENTS: 115 patients treated with ECMO for refractory heart failure and 57 patients treated with ECMO for refractory respiratory failure. METHODS: We analysed the association between early daily FB versus hospital and 90-day mortality using multivariable logistic regression model, Cox proportional-hazards model and propensity score. RESULTS: We obtained detailed demographic, clinical, and biochemical data, daily FB, and continuous renal replacement days. Fifty-seven per cent of patients had acute kidney injury (AKI) at ECMO initiation, and 60 % (n = 103) of patients received continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) during ECMO course, beginning at a median of 1 (0–3.5) days after ECMO initiation. Overall 90-day mortality was 24 %. Survivors exhibited lower daily FB from day 3 to day 5. After adjustments, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) III, CRRT during the first 3 days, major bleeding event at day 1 and positive FB on day 3 were independent predictors of 90-day mortality. Positive FB at ECMO day 3 remained an independent predictor of hospital and 90-day mortality, regardless of the statistical model used or the inclusion of a propensity score to have positive FB. CONCLUSIONS: Positive FB at ECMO day 3 is an independent predictor of 90-day mortality. Further interventional studies aimed at testing the value of strategy of tight control of FB during the early ECMO period are now warranted. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (doi:10.1007/s00134-014-3360-2) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

CONCLUSIONS: Positive FB at ECMO day 3 is an independent predictor of 90-day mortality. title: All Hands on Deck: Transdisciplinary Approaches to Emerging Infectious Disease
abstract: The increasing burden of emerging infectious diseases worldwide confronts us with numerous challenges, including the imperative to design research and responses that are commensurate to understanding the complex social and ecological contexts in which infectious diseases occur. A diverse group of scientists met in Hawaii in March 2005 to discuss the linked social and ecological contexts in which infectious diseases emerge. A subset of the meeting was a group that focused on “transdisciplinary approaches” to integrating knowledge across and beyond academic disciplines in order to improve prevention and control of emerging infections. This article is based on the discussions of that group. Here, we outline the epidemiological legacy that has dominated infectious disease research and control up until now, and introduce the role of new, transdisciplinary and systems-based approaches to emerging infectious diseases. We describe four cases of transboundary health issues and use them to discuss the potential benefits, as well as the inherent difficulties, in understanding the social–ecological contexts in which infectious diseases occur and of using transdisciplinary approaches to deal with them.

title: Maternal and fetal outcomes of dengue fever in pregnancy: a large prospective and descriptive observational study
abstract: This manuscript describes a large prospective and descriptive observational study of maternal and fetal outcomes in pregnancy complicated by dengue fever. Dengue is a serious viral disease that can lead to severe and potentially fatal complications during pregnancy, yet little is known about the effects on both mother and child. This research was conducted in Chiang Mai province, Thailand from 2010 - 2014 in order to evaluate long-term effects of acute dengue infection during pregnancy on mothers and fetuses for whom no antenatal treatment was administered. We enrolled 151 pregnant women with confirmed laboratory diagnosed primary or secondary dengue fever early before the 24th week of gestation. We followed up up until 6-weeks postpartum to document any adverse events related to mother’s organ system as well as fetal outcomes at delivery such as intrauterine growth restriction or preterm birth at less than 37 weeks gestational age (GA). Herein we report baseline characteristics of participants, risk factors associated with these particular outcomes along with their prevalence rates observed following exposures

title: Immunosuppressive potential of fowl adenovirus serotype 4
abstract: This abstract outlines the findings of an exploration into the immunosuppressive potential of Fowl Adenovirus Serotype 4 (FAdV-4). A comprehensive analysis was conducted to identify whether FAdV-4 has a role in the suppression of chicken defense without compromising its nutritional integrity. Results from this research have demonstrated that FAdV-4 can be reliably used as an immunosuppressive agent while preserving critical host physiological characteristics. Specifically, morphological and biochemical parameters were measured to track how FAdV-4 induced immune responses at both cellular and systemic levels and did not produce any significant changes in nutrient absorption capacity by chickens. These results highlight the ability of FAdV-4 to safely reduce markers associated with different types of immunity while maintaining the optimum nutritional value required for healthful growth and development.

title: Evidence of the effect of primary care expansion on hospitalizations: Panel analysis of 143 municipalities in the Brazilian Amazon
abstract: This article analyses the effect of primary care expansion on hospitalizations in 143 municipalities situated in the Brazilian Amazon region. The expansion of primary health care services has been suggested as a valid approach to reduce avoidable hospitalisations, yet there is limited evidence which supports this hypothesis. Therefore, this study reviews available data and investigates whether an increase in access to primary healthcare services reduces rates of hospitalization among individuals living within Brazilian Amazon municipalities. Employing panel analysis techniques, it was possible to determine that increased access to quality primary health services does indeed lower the number of emergency department visits for preventable health events associated with well-known risk factors such as age and gender differences. Moreover, results from this research suggest that large investments into regional public health infrastructures would further contribute towards better population outcomes—regardless of local socioeconomic conditions or demographics—thus reinforcing the importance of providing comprehensive preventive practices across rural areas.

title: Management of chickenpox in pregnant women: an Italian perspective
abstract: This article provides a unique overview of the current management of chickenpox in pregnant women from an Italian perspective. Chickenpox, caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV), is a highly contagious disease which can result in serious complications for the mother and her unborn child if not treated effectively. During pregnancy, the immune system of the woman is often weakened, increasing their susceptibility to infections such as chickenpox. Therefore, early diagnosis and proper treatment are essential steps towards mitigating risks associated with maternal-fetal transmission of VZV. An observational study was conducted among 500 pregnant Italian women diagnosed with primary or secondary infection due to chickenpox; clinical findings, risk factors involved and drug treatments were also assessed along with postnatal outcomes reported at 4 weeks post delivery. Results indicated that pregnant women administered antiviral drugs during the initial episode demonstrated significantly lower rates of placental abruption compared to those who received antibiotic therapy only up until 36 weeks gestation stage while infants born prematurely exhibited similar immunological responses regardless of therapeutic interventions adopted by their mothers prenatally . This finding suggests antiviral medications may be effective at controlling VZV replication within heavy immunosuppressive conditions encountered during late Gestations stages despite prolonged administration duration often recommended for such cases. Furthermore our data indicates monitoring viral titers both prior/during labor should be suggested as avoid further spreading in health care settings

title: What’s the point? Domestic dogs’ sensitivity to the accuracy of human informants
abstract: In this study, we investigate the extent to which domestic dogs are sensitive to the accuracy of human informants. To what degree do they form opinions based on individual experiences as opposed to relying on generic information from humans? We apply methodology informed by cognitive science and communication theory, in order to assess how accurately dogs interpret human communication. We find that domestic dogs are able to use prior experience with human behaviour to inform their responses and make decisions about object location based on an assessment of informant accuracy. Our results demonstrate that domestic dogs possess a sophisticated capacity for detecting truth-telling behaviour from communicating agents and can quickly adapt their behavioural response accordingly. Our research progresses existing theories concerning animal cognition, providing evidence for the presence of advanced interpretive skills among domesticated species beyond primates.

title: The accuracy of nurses' estimates of their absenteeism
abstract:
This article examines the accuracy of nurses’ estimates of their absenteeism in the workplace. Absenteeism is a serious problem for hospitals, resulting in disruption to services and costs due to both direct and indirect causes. Comparing instances where employees report themselves absent with official records can provide important insight into this phenomenon. Using a large population database, this study stresses the importance of recognizing small differences among estimations which have significant cost implications for hospital managers over time. 

The data was collected from approximately 10,000 registered nurse absences according to their self-reports between 2005 and 2011 at four acute care teaching hospitals located on different geographic locations in the United States. Subsequent analysis revealed that registered nurses underestimate their own absenteeism rate by 0.002%. The results highlight additional evidence that healthcare systems rely heavily on information provided by its employees without taking into consideration discrepancies that may exist between reported and actual absence rates, thus overestimating budgeting forecasts used for day-to-day operations of health organizations across the country..

title: Comparison of clinical outcomes between laparoscopic and open surgery for left-sided colon cancer: a nationwide population-based study
abstract: The role of laparoscopic surgery for left-sided colon cancer has been supported by the results of randomized controlled trials. However, its benefits and disadvantages in the real world setting should be further assessed with population-based studies.The hospitalization data of patients undergoing open or laparoscopic surgery for left-sided colon cancer were sourced from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database. Patient and hospital characteristics and perioperative outcomes including length of hospital stay, operation time, opioid use, blood transfusion, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and use of mechanical ventilation were compared. The overall survival was also assessed. Patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery had shorter hospital stay (p < 0.0001) and less demand for opioid analgesia (p = 0.0005). Further logistic regression revealed that patients undergoing open surgery were 1.70, 2.89, and 3.00 times more likely to have blood transfusion, to be admitted to ICU, and to use mechanical ventilation than patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery. Operations performed in medical centers were also associated with less adverse events. The overall survival was comparable between the 2 groups.With adequate hospital quality and volume, laparoscopic surgery for left-sided colon cancer was associated with improved perioperative outcomes. The long-term survival was not compromised.

title: Ecological Niche Modeling: An Introduction for Veterinarians and Epidemiologists
abstract:
This study outlines the potential success of Ecological Niche Modeling (ENM) as a risk assessment tool, using an interdisciplinary approach to analyze disease dynamics and predicting regional impacts. ENM is a powerful predictive tool that combines environmental data with population data and biogeographic principles, allowing for comprehensive assessments of the spread of zoonotic diseases. Veterinarians and epidemiologists need this method to accurately predict where disease outbreaks are most likely, understand how these can vary both seasonally and geographically and ultimately inform effective preventive measures in order to protect public health. 

The purpose of this paper is twofold: firstly, it presents a review of existing literature exploring ENM capabilities for veterinary science applications; secondly, it assesses the utility of ENM by conducting empirical research on several case studies related to animal health management. This paper provides detailed insight into best practices employed by practitioners when using ENMs combined with guidance specific to veterinarians or epidemiologists. It also highlights key challenges associated with certain ENMS models and offers valuable recommendations on how they could be improved upon through better user training or advanced technology such as Cloud Computing Solutions (CCS).Overall, this article seeks provide progressive strategies encouraging further development within their respective fields so that market-leading techniques may continue strengthen our understanding around ‘One Health’ concepts - improving the sustainability in human-animal long term relationships networking region wide activities together through consolidated knowledge sharing initiatives for all concerned stakeholders ultimately leading us towards healthier ecosystems worldwide.: 'Ecological Niche Modeling: An Introduction for Veterinarians and Epidemiologists'

title: Chemokines as Molecular Targets for Therapeutic Intervention
abstract: Despite the youth of the chemokine field, many antagonists of chemokine function have already been identified and tested at the preclinical level. These include neutralizing antibodies, peptidyl and non-peptidyl antagonists and non-specific immunosuppressive agents. These early studies suggest that chemokine agonists have the potential to regulate many diseases, ranging from HIV-1 infection and tumor growth to acute and chronic inflammation. Clinical application will depend on pharmaceutical development. Great strides have been made in defining structural domains of the chemokines involved in receptor binding and activation. The identification of receptors is rapidly progressing, but with 50 potential ligands and 15 characterized receptors, it is obvious that additional molecular studies are needed. The intriguing observation that several pathogens either use chemokine receptors as entry portals or produce chemokine decoys to subvert the immune system suggests that there is much to be learned about the immune system from studies of “virokines.” Future studies should lead to the discovery and design of more effective inhibitors and antagonists with therapeutic benefit.

title: 6-O-angeloylplenolin exerts neuroprotection against lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo
abstract: Neuroinflammation is one of the critical events in neurodegenerative diseases, whereas microglia play an important role in the pathogenesis of neuroinflammation. In this study, we investigated the effects of a natural sesquiterpene lactone, 6-O-angeloylplenolin (6-OAP), isolated from the traditional Chinese medicine Centipeda minima (L.) A.Br., on neuroinflammation and the underlying mechanisms. We showed that treatment with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) caused activation of BV2 and primary microglial cells and development of neuroinflammation in vitro, evidenced by increased production of inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β, the phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of NF-κB, and the transcriptional upregulation of COX-2 and iNOS, leading to increased production of proinflammatory factors NO and PGE(2). Moreover, LPS treatment induced oxidative stress through increasing the expression levels of NOX2 and NOX4. Pretreatment with 6-OAP (0.5−4 μM) dose-dependently attenuated LPS-induced NF-κB activation and oxidative stress, thus suppressed neuroinflammation in the cells. In a mouse model of LPS-induced neuroinflammation, 6-OAP (5−20 mg·kg(−1)·d(−1), ip, for 7 days before LPS injection) dose-dependently inhibited the production of inflammatory cytokines, the activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway, and the expression of inflammatory enzymes in brain tissues. 6-OAP pretreatment significantly ameliorated the activation of microglia and astrocytes in the brains. 6-OAP at a high dose caused a much stronger antineuroinflammatory effect than dexamethansone (DEX). Furthermore, we demonstrated that 6-OAP pretreatment could inhibit LPS-induced neurite and synaptic loss in vitro and in vivo. In conclusion, our results demonstrate that 6-OAP exerts antineuroinflammatory effects and can be considered a novel drug candidate for the treatment of neuroinflammatory diseases.

title: Mechanisms of disease: pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating vascular disorder linked to pulmonary haemodynamic changes and consequent right ventricular failure. This disease is associated with high mortality, end-organ damage and functional disability mostly due to its delayed diagnosis. Changes in molecular pathways are considered as the main cause for such disease progression and this article seeks to identify those pathways that prove relevant in the development of PAH diseases progression. Using clinical studies, genetic deciphering tools, biochemical analyses and animal models, we will review existing data on the mechanisms of pathogenesis involved in PAH progressions; discussing their implications on preclinical strategies for diagnostics as well as potential targets for novel therapies. Our aim is to provide an up-to-date overview of critical findings concerning the molecular basis related to PAH mechanism which could improve current management options available for these patients.

title: Dissecting Response to Cancer Immunotherapy by Applying Bayesian Network Analysis to Flow Cytometry Data
abstract: Cancer immunotherapy, specifically immune checkpoint blockade, has been found to be effective in the treatment of metastatic cancers. However, only a subset of patients achieve clinical responses. Elucidating pretreatment biomarkers predictive of sustained clinical response is a major research priority. Another research priority is evaluating changes in the immune system before and after treatment in responders vs. nonresponders. Our group has been studying immune networks as an accurate reflection of the global immune state. Flow cytometry (FACS, fluorescence-activated cell sorting) data characterizing immune cell panels in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA) patients were used to analyze changes in immune networks in this setting. Here, we describe a novel computational pipeline to perform secondary analyses of FACS data using systems biology/machine learning techniques and concepts. The pipeline is centered around comparative Bayesian network analyses of immune networks and is capable of detecting strong signals that conventional methods (such as FlowJo manual gating) might miss. Future studies are planned to validate and follow up the immune biomarkers (and combinations/interactions thereof) associated with clinical responses identified with this computational pipeline.

title: Functional and topographical analyses of epitopes on bovine herpesvirus type 1 glycoprotein IV
abstract: This study describes the functional and topographical analyses of epitopes on bovine herpesvirus type 1 glycoprotein IV (BHV-1 gIV). Employing strategies such as ELISA, ferritin staining, molecular modeling and gelatin zymography, the aim was to evaluate the immunogenic potential of BHV-1 gIV. Data showed that a total of eight linear epitopes had strong immunogenicity in response to four monoclonal antibodies in sheep red blood cell lysates. Furthermore, four conformational epitope bindings were detected on detergent-solubilized antigen with IgG from infected cattle serum by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Additionally, circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed a highly conserved secondary structure for the studied protein associated with reasonable thermostability. In conclusion, this novel research advances our understanding about the functionality and localization of BHV-1 gIV derived peptides useful for their use as antigens potentially leading towards developing new efficacious vaccines against this pathogen.

title: DNA transducer-triggered signal switch for visual colorimetric bioanalysis
abstract: This paper introduces a ground-breaking study on the potential of DNA transducer technology to power an innovative signal switch able to support visual colorimetric bioanalysis. While traditionally this type of biosensing requires microscopes and bulky laboratory instrumentation, advances in the development and characterization of DNA transducers opened up the possibility for developing a miniaturized analytical device triggered by sensitive electrical signals that could be applicable in a broad range of biomedical analyses. Herein we describe how careful manipulation of plasmid DNA sequences can generate nanoscale conductors with Ag/Au nanoparticle anchors receptive to redox interactions, allowing our team to fabricate field-effect transistor (FET) switches which can drive localized, real-time chromoprotic reaction visualization directly on Kapton substrate with optical resolution capabilities similar or improving current state-of-the art techniques when operating under biologically reactive conditions. This research findings pave the way towards miniaturization strategies for designing smart sensors adapted for point-of care device diagnostics.

title: The receptor for Bacillus thuringiensis CrylA(c) delta‐endotoxin in the brush border membrane of the lepidopteran Manduca sexta is aminopeptidase N
abstract: This study investigates the role of aminopeptidase N (APN) in discriminating binding sites for Bacillus thuringiensis CrylA(c) delta-endotoxin during hormonal signaling between Manduca sexta lepidopteran larvae and their host plants. Previous studies have suggested that a receptor other than APN is involved in transmitters binding to brush border membrane along different points throughout larval growth, however this hypothesis had not been rigorously tested. Through careful examination of manducan larvae at varying stages of development, we found significant evidence supporting APN as the true receptor for Bt Cry1Ac toxin binding within the brush border membrane. A novel fluorescent assay demonstrated significantly greater affinity towards Bt toxin when APN was present in comparison to control conditions lacking the peptidase enzyme which provided further evidence confirming our hypothesis. title: Efficiency of prompt quarantine measures on a susceptible-infected-removed model in networks
abstract: This paper examines the efficiency of prompt quarantine measures on a susceptible-infected-removed (SIR) model in the context of networks. In response to a variety of contagious diseases which can rapidly spread among populations, effective and timely prevention strategies are required from public health authorities to safeguard large clusters of susceptible individuals from infection. The SIR model has been fundamental in providing an understanding as to how infectious disease spreads within a given population and has thus become an important tool for policy makers wishing to investigate preventative methods, such as quarantine protocols. Herein, we analyze the effectiveness of various types of quarantines applied at different rates throughout randomly generated networks under conditions inspired by real world examples, examining the resulting outbreak size and peak timing. Comparisons between network structures further highlight their respective strengths when used together with prompt quarantine procedures.

title: Vaping induced pneumonitis: a small community hospital’s case series and analysis
abstract: Vaping induced pneumonitis has been established as a newly identified systematic illness that can have potentially serious effects on human health, characterized by inflammation and consolidation in the lung parenchyma. This article presents an analysis of a case series evaluation conducted in 2018 at AC Memorial Hospital (ACMH) to qualitatively analyze clinically diagnosed cases of Veping Induced Pneumonitis seen within its community during a one-year duration. The primary outcome considered was correlation between reported vaping behaviors with clinical manifestation of Veping Induced Pneumonitis and the second outcome studied was patient demographics including age, employment status and general lifestyle information. Upon completion of results, data shown were statistically analyzed using SPSS software version 24 with 95% confidence intervals for hypothesis testing. Instances observed indicated notable correlations with self-reported vaping habits as possible risk indicator for development of Veping Induced Pneumonitis among hospitalized patients within ACMH’s service area over the study period; thus suggesting public health concerns may be present from frequent long-term use or abuse attempts involving such products .

title: Important Databases Related to Genomes
abstract: Genome databases are the locations, which permits storing, sharing, retrieving and comparison of the information related to the genomes of various individuals and organisms. Traditionally the databases were confined to the updated information of certain vital model organisms. Rapid development of technology and high speed internet facilities have created an explosion of databases resulting in the development of specific databases of almost all model organisms and a group of organisms with a common specificity. In the present chapter, details of the databases related to the genomes of viruses, archaea, bacteria, cell organelle, invertebrates, vertebrates, plants, and human beings are provided in a table format which provides an instant information, about different databases and their URLs.

title: An Ultrasensitive Mechanism Regulates Influenza Virus-Induced Inflammation
abstract: Influenza viruses present major challenges to public health, evident by the 2009 influenza pandemic. Highly pathogenic influenza virus infections generally coincide with early, high levels of inflammatory cytokines that some studies have suggested may be regulated in a strain-dependent manner. However, a comprehensive characterization of the complex dynamics of the inflammatory response induced by virulent influenza strains is lacking. Here, we applied gene co-expression and nonlinear regression analysis to time-course, microarray data developed from influenza-infected mouse lung to create mathematical models of the host inflammatory response. We found that the dynamics of inflammation-associated gene expression are regulated by an ultrasensitive-like mechanism in which low levels of virus induce minimal gene expression but expression is strongly induced once a threshold virus titer is exceeded. Cytokine assays confirmed that the production of several key inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin 6 and monocyte chemotactic protein 1, exhibit ultrasensitive behavior. A systematic exploration of the pathways regulating the inflammatory-associated gene response suggests that the molecular origins of this ultrasensitive response mechanism lie within the branch of the Toll-like receptor pathway that regulates STAT1 phosphorylation. This study provides the first evidence of an ultrasensitive mechanism regulating influenza virus-induced inflammation in whole lungs and provides insight into how different virus strains can induce distinct temporal inflammation response profiles. The approach developed here should facilitate the construction of gene regulatory models of other infectious diseases.

title: Deep-learning-assisted detection and segmentation of rib fractures from CT scans: Development and validation of FracNet
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diagnosis of rib fractures plays an important role in identifying trauma severity. However, quickly and precisely identifying the rib fractures in a large number of CT images with increasing number of patients is a tough task, which is also subject to the qualification of radiologist. We aim at a clinically applicable automatic system for rib fracture detection and segmentation from CT scans. METHODS: A total of 7,473 annotated traumatic rib fractures from 900 patients in a single center were enrolled into our dataset, named RibFrac Dataset, which were annotated with a human-in-the-loop labeling procedure. We developed a deep learning model, named FracNet, to detect and segment rib fractures. 720, 60 and 120 patients were randomly split as training cohort, tuning cohort and test cohort, respectively. Free-Response ROC (FROC) analysis was used to evaluate the sensitivity and false positives of the detection performance, and Intersection-over-Union (IoU) and Dice Coefficient (Dice) were used to evaluate the segmentation performance of predicted rib fractures. Observer studies, including independent human-only study and human-collaboration study, were used to benchmark the FracNet with human performance and evaluate its clinical applicability. A annotated subset of RibFrac Dataset, including 420 for training, 60 for tuning and 120 for test, as well as our code for model training and evaluation, was open to research community to facilitate both clinical and engineering research. FINDINGS: Our method achieved a detection sensitivity of 92.9% with 5.27 false positives per scan and a segmentation Dice of 71.5%on the test cohort. Human experts achieved much lower false positives per scan, while underperforming the deep neural networks in terms of detection sensitivities with longer time in diagnosis. With human-computer collobration, human experts achieved higher detection sensitivities than human-only or computer-only diagnosis. INTERPRETATION: The proposed FracNet provided increasing detection sensitivity of rib fractures with significantly decreased clinical time consumed, which established a clinically applicable method to assist the radiologist in clinical practice. The funding sources played no role in the study design; collection, analysis, and interpretation of data; writing of the report; or decision to submit the article for publication .

title: Ten-year outcomes of antivascular endothelial growth factor therapy in neovascular age-related macular degeneration
abstract:
The Ten-year Outcomes of Antivascular Endothelial Growth Factor Therapy in Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) is a debilitating retinal disorder that impacts the elderly population and the leading cause of blindness among those aged 65 years or older. In order to reduce visual impairment caused by neovascular AMD, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy has been implemented as an effective treatment approach. With this in mind, we sought to study the 10 year outcomes evaluating anti-VEGF therapies administered for wet AMD compared to conventional treatments currently used. title: Implications of Human Microbiome Research for the Developing World
abstract: The human microbiome refers to all of the species that inhabit the human body, residing both on and in it. Over the past several years, there has been a significantly increased interest directed to the understanding of the microorganisms that reside on and in the human body. These studies of the human microbiome promise to reveal all these species and increase our understanding of the normal inhabitants, those that trigger disease and those that vary in response to disease conditions. It is anticipated that these directed research efforts, coupled with new technological advances, will ultimately allow one to gain a greater understanding of the relationships of these species with their human hosts. The various chapters in this book present a range of aspects of human microbiome research, explain the scientific and technological rationale, and highlight the significant potential that the results from these studies hold. In this chapter, we begin to address the potential and long-term implications of the knowledge gained from human microbiome research (which currently is centered in the developed world) for the developing world, which has often lagged behind in the benefits of these new technologies and their implications to new research areas.

title: A Systems Approach to Refine Disease Taxonomy by Integrating Phenotypic and Molecular Networks
abstract: This paper presents a Systems Approach to refine disease taxonomy by integrating phenotypic and molecular networks of diseases. By leveraging innovation in systems biology, we demonstrate how the integration of phenomic and genomic datasets can be used to provide more robust classifications than currently applied. At the same time, this approach also allows for efficient identification and characterization of “clinically relevant” genes/loci that may contribute or associate with complex trait-diseases. This study demonstrates a unique application of system wide criteria, such as gene regulatory networks, protein-protein interactions (PPI), gene co-expression patterns, and pathophysiological pathways associated with the obtained emergence scores to identify underlying deficits linked to different diseases. Through the integration of multiple levels of data including transcriptomics, genomics & metabolomics into databases suitable for systems level analysis is expected to enable deeper investigations into biodiverse traits known clinically expressed as complex disorders. The results provide new insights into identifying clinical paths from which we hope therapeutic interventions be developed from these better defined genetic taxonomies.

title: Immune regulation of the unfolded protein response at the mucosal barrier in viral infection
abstract: This paper presents an exploration of the role of immune regulation in the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) at mucosal barriers during viral infection. Recent advances have revealed a complex interplay between the antiviral response and UPR, suggesting that dedicated processes coordinate these two seemingly divergent pathways. Drawing on insights from various levels, including gene expression profiling and proteomic mapping assays, this article will explore the physiological significance of these regulatory mechanisms at mucosa barrier points during viral infections by analyzing protein-protein interactions as well as responses to small molecule inhibitors/activators. The findings from this research will provide novel perspectives into how our bodies respond to and fight against virus infections at gene and biochemical level, thereby deepening our understanding about immunity defense strategies for improving medical care treatments in relevant scenarios.

title: The European Classical Swine Fever Virus Database: Blueprint for a Pathogen-Specific Sequence Database with Integrated Sequence Analysis Tools
abstract: The European classical swine fever virus (CSFV) is a widespread yet rarely reported viral infection within the pig population. It has been estimated that millions of pigs are infected with CSFV annually, in Europe and beyond. In order to better monitor and mitigate transmission of this pathogen, it is essential to start building dedicated databases which hold genomic sequences of the virus associated with medically-relevant information regarding geographical origin and host species. This paper presents 'The European Classical Swine Fever Virus Database', a blueprint for such a database with integrated sequence analysis tools aimed at providing comprehensive surveillance capabilities. The proposed system encompassed key components required by epidemiologists: advanced data storage solutions; efficient structured query language (SQL); automated sequence alignment tools and combination features able to identify new variants quickly; as well as visualisation and statistical functions intended to facilitate comparison between disparate geographic areas or other contextual factors. In conclusion, by pursuing the construction of this specific database on CSFV it will be possible not only to deliver an up-to-date map but also offer great potential for aiding public health initiatives related to improved pathogen identification methods in real-time scenarios

title: Assessing the Methods, Tools, and Statistical Approaches in Google Trends Research: Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review critically evaluates the methods, tools and statistical approaches employed in Google Trends research and discusses the associated strengths and weaknesses. The purpose of this study is to provide evidence-based insight into how current research can best be undertaken using Google Trends. A comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify published studies related to this topic that were limited to those written in English between 2010 and 2020. Thirty-six articles met criteria for inclusion in a detailed assessment of their methodological approach, statistical tool(s) utilized, results findings, and any limitations reported. title: Viral-associated Ventilator-associated Pneumonia
abstract: Nosocomial pneumonia is the most commonly acquired infection in intensive care units (ICUs). Its frequency is approximately 10 cases/1000 admissions; however, the incidence may increase to 20 times that number in patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation [1–3]. The overall incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) may range between 15 % to 20 % [2–6]. This complication prolongs the length of hospital stay, increases healthcare costs and may increase mortality [4, 5, 7, 8].

title: Exploring Leptospiral proteomes to identify potential candidates for vaccine design against Leptospirosis using an immunoinformatics approach
abstract: Leptospirosis is the most widespread zoonotic disease, estimated to cause severe infection in more than one million people each year, particularly in developing countries of tropical areas. Several factors such as variable and nonspecific clinical manifestation, existence of large number of serovars and asymptomatic hosts spreading infection, poor sanitation and lack of an effective vaccine make prophylaxis difficult. Consequently, there is an urgent need to develop an effective vaccine to halt its spread all over the world. In this study, an immunoinformatics approach was employed to identify the most vital and effective immunogenic protein from the proteome of Leptospira interrogans serovar Copenhageni strain L1-130 that may be suitable to stimulate a significant immune response aiding in the development of peptide vaccine against leptospirosis. Both B-cell and T-cell (Helper T-lymphocyte (HTL) and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)) epitopes were predicted for the conserved and most immunogenic outer membrane lipoprotein. Further, the binding interaction of CTL epitopes with Major Histocompatibility Complex class I (MHC-I) was evaluated using docking techniques. A Molecular Dynamics Simulation study was also performed to evaluate the stability of the resulting epitope-MHC-I complexes. Overall, this study provides novel vaccine candidates and may prompt further development of vaccines against leptospirosis.

title: Interleukin-1β decreases HLA class II expression on a glioblastoma multiforme cell line
abstract: This research article summarizes the findings of a study conducted to investigate the effects of Interleukin-1β (IL-1β) on HLA class II expression in an established glioblastoma multiforme cell line. Despite its importance as a regulator of humoral and cellular immunity, little is known about how IL-1β modulates immunoexpression of surface molecules like human leucocyte antigen class 2 (HLA-II). Our experiments demonstrate that incubation with IL-1β decreases the expression levels of HLA class II both at the surface and intracellularly, confirming our hypothesis that this cytokine can direct T cells towards B7 for antigen presentation by downregulating co-stimulatory HLA class II. We also analyse another possible role for IL-1α: decreasing proliferation capacity by expressing IL receptors in some cancer cell lines such as glioblastomae multiforme. This finding suggests that targeting immune cells with high concentrations of carefully designed IL analogues could provide novel alternatives to therapies based entirely on antibody recognition or antiinflammatory factors over time. In summary, our results imply that manipulating lymphocyte responses through biologic agents could serve as an effective tool against more aggressive forms of tumorigenesis due to their ability to modulate gene activation pathways within increasingly resistant malignant environments surrounding classical treatments.

title: Effect of Liraglutide on Cardiometabolic Risk Profile in People with Coronary Artery Disease with or without Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Background: Whether liraglutide use improves cardiometabolic risk factors in different subsets of subjects with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains unclear. In a systematic review and meta-analysis, we quantified the effects of liraglutide on cardiometabolic risk profile in subjects with CAD with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D). Methods: Online database searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science, Cochrane library, and Google Scholar from incept up to 15th January 2021. We identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing the effects of liraglutide compared to placebo on cardiometabolic risk profile. We used the random- or fixed-effect models to pool the weighted mean differences (WMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Out of a total of 7,320 citations, six articles (seven RCTs) with 294 subjects with CAD (mean age, 61.21 years; 19% women) were included. Our findings presented as WMD and 95% CI showed a statistical significant decrease in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) [−0.36%; −0.47; −0.26, p < 0.001; I (2) = 0.0% (with 6 RCTs)], body mass index (BMI) [−0.61 kg/m(2); −1.21; −0.01, p = 0.047; I (2) = 72.2% (with five RCTs)], and waist circumference [−2.41 cm; −3.47; −1.36, p < 0.001; I (2) = 0.0% (with three RCTs)]. Through a set of subgroup analyses, we found a significant reduction in BMI in CAD patients with T2D [WMD = −1.06; 95% CI, −1.42, −0.70, p < 0.001; I (2) = 0.0% (with three RCTs)] compared to CAD only patients [WMD = −0.08; 95% CI, −0.45, 0.29, p = 0.66; I (2) = 0.0% (with two RCTs)] in the liraglutide group compared with the placebo group. No significant changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were observed. Conclusions: Among people with established CAD, liraglutide significantly improved HbA1c, BMI, and waist circumference values. The effect of liraglutide on BMI was more robust in individuals with T2D compared to those without.

title: Pleura: Anatomy, Physiology, and Disorders
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of the anatomy and physiology of the Pleura, examining common disorders associated with this body structure. The Pleura is located within the thoracic cavity and serves as a double-layered membrane which surrounds and separates the lungs from other mediastinal structures. This protective layer allows for maintenance of ventilation while also providing an additional level of shock absorber against foreign bodies entering or bouncing within the chest cavity. Additionally, pleural fluid functions to reduce friction between opposing surfaces during expansion and contraction of lung tissue during breath cycles. Consequently, any aberration in either structure or function can lead to pathological changes such as pulmonary infection, pneumothorax, chylothorax or certain malignancies prohibiting compromised breathing sensation. title: The social benefits of private infectious disease-risk mitigation
abstract: This paper seeks to establish the social benefits of private infectious disease-risk mitigation as a viable strategy for public health management. Emerging viral and bacterial infections represent a formidable challenge facing society. Too often countermeasures are triggered too late, or not at all due to inadequate information dissemination, delays in implementation of preventive strategies, and lack of resources among vulnerable populations whose risk is most heavily affected by negative outcomes associated with infection outbreaks. We propose that pro-active targeted approaches may be an important part of mitigating ongoing contacts by those identified as being at risk. Our study posits that enabling individuals’ access to resources pertinent to their circumstances can play a major role in reducing rates of transmission while potentially providing wider economic and medical benefits elsewhere in society. In this article we examine available data regarding the effects of private infectious disease-risk mitigation on public health prevention outcomes through literature review and survey research methods drawn from existing international settings where such measures have been tested for efficacy against known acknowledged risks. Our goal is identify potential shortfalls in current policies related to epidemic crisis management illustrated specifically through considerations employed within the context of pandemic planning guidelines along with prosocial applications towards future deployment scenarios across risky population subsets global .

title: Coronavirus, humanpathogenes
abstract: This research paper explores the emergence of Coronavirus as a human pathogen and presents new insights into its defining characteristics. This investigation reveals that Coronavirus is able to cause major acute respiratory symptoms in humans, leading to high mortality rates amongst infected individuals. A closer examination of this virus also establishes it as an alpha-group coronavirus capable of infecting many parts of the respiratory system through direct contact with commercially available animal products carrying any remaining traces. The findings demonstrate significant implications for disease prevention measures adopted by international health authorities including awareness campaigns about exotic trades and implementation of stronger quarantine policies within various markets worldwide. Finally, the aim is to develop more effective countermeasures against the viral strain and safeguard public safety in a post coronavirus era.

title: A Survey of Recent Adenoviral Respiratory Pathogens in Hong Kong Reveals Emergent and Recombinant Human Adenovirus Type 4 (HAdV-E4) Circulating in Civilian Populations
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of current human adenoviral respiratory pathogens in Hong Kong, revealing an emergent recombinant strain known as human adenovirus type 4 (HAdV-E4). Given the impact of respiratory viral infections on global health, it is important to understand the prevalence and dynamics of these pathogens. A population-based survey was employed using samples from clinically symptomatic patients attending hospital outpatient services for suspected respiratory illness over five years. The results revealed that HAdV-E4 was circulating among susceptible civilian populations in Hong Kong during the period under review. This study highlights the need for ongoing surveillance efforts and effective public health interventions to monitor and control emerging viruses at their respective source locations.

title: Protective role of antigenic sites on the envelope protein of Hantaan virus defined by monoclonal antibodies
abstract: This study aims to examine the protective role of antigenic sites located on the envelope protein of Hantaan virus (HTNV) by employing single-domain monoclonal antibodies. It has long been recognized that HTNV can cause potentially severe hemorrhagic fever among humans, and understanding how its envelope protein may be targeted by immune defense systems is essential for furthering our knowledge about this pathogen. To date, few studies have investigated the ability of antibody binding to these sites as a means for protecting against HTNV infection. Through application of single-domain monoclonal antibodies, this experiment will explore if recognition of these antigenic sites serves an immune protective role in mice infected with HTNV. Such an analysis will provide much needed insight into strategies which could be employed towards fighting infections from this virus.

abstract: In 2003, the Utah State Department of Health received funding from the Health Resources and Services Administration to develop a medical surge plan to increase the number of available hospital beds in the state by 1250 beds, including 125 beds for burn or critical trauma patients. title: Clinical characteristics and predictors of mortality in 67 patients with primary pyomyositis: a study from North India
abstract: Primary pyomyositis is infection of the skeletal muscles in the absence of adjacent skin, soft tissue, and bone infection. This study was undertaken to look at the spectrum of clinical presentations, therapeutic interventions, and their outcomes and also to evaluate the association of various risk factors with mortality. This was a retrospective study in which the patients admitted with the diagnosis of primary pyomyositis from January 2000 to June 2007 were included. Their demographic details, clinical and laboratory data, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score at presentation, treatment instituted, complications encountered, and hospital outcome were recorded. Sixty-seven patients (42 males and 25 females) with a diagnosis of primary pyomyositis were included. Median age at the time of presentation was 37 years (interquartile range = 25–50 years). Common presenting symptoms were myalgias [50 (74.62%)] and fever [49 (73.13%)]. Twenty-six patients had underlying predisposing medical conditions. The commonest muscle group involved was iliopsoas muscles in 31 (46.26%) patients. Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus was the commonest organism isolated from the pus. Twenty-eight patients developed sepsis and seven died. On univariate analysis, there was a statistically significant association between higher SOFA score, lower Glasgow coma scale, higher pulse rate, lower blood pressure, raised blood urea, raised serum creatinine, higher serum glutamic pyruvate transaminase, raised total bilirubin at presentation, and development of sepsis during hospital stay with mortality. In our study, the patients were seen almost a decade later than those seen in other studies from the region. Evidence of organ dysfunction at presentation and sepsis was associated with increased mortality.

title: Primates, Pathogens, and Evolution: A Context for Understanding Emerging Disease
abstract: This journal article explores the implications of primates as reservoirs for emerging pathogens and their role in disease evolution. Primate ecology, behavior and evolutionary biology are discussed in relation to host-pathogen interactions. The primary focus is on the ways in which native primate species interact with novel pathogenic agents and serve as critical amplifying hosts; playing a key role in the emergence of new diseases. Additionally, this paper evaluates how landscape changes through human activities can impact both primate systems and transmission pathways between primate populations and humans, leading to further risk of emergence or spillover events. Such insights provide crucial frameworks for understanding why some zoonoses emerge more readily than others, thus enabling us to better anticipate future outbreaks or pandemics related to wildlife/primates sources.

title: Exposure of p19 matrix protein of human T-cell leukemia virus type I (HTLV-I) on the surface of MOLT-4#8 cells after virus adsorption
abstract: This research paper reports the findings of an experiment conducted to assess the exposure of p19 matrix protein on the surface of MOLT-4#8 cells after being subjected to human T-cell leukemia virus type I (HTLV-I). Using indirect immunofluorescence assay and advanced image analysis techniques, it was discovered that upon binding HTLV-I particles, a significant increase in the amount and intensity of exposed p19 matrix proteins occurred. Moreover, differences between infection and noninfection samples were attained by measuring cell size changes. Results suggest that virus adsorption affects key parameters related to membrane events associated with HTLV-I infection; further experiments are proposed to address other aspects related to this phenomenon such as expression shift patterns or dynamical behaviors observed during particle assembly/disassembly.

title: Solidarity, vulnerability and mistrust: how context, information and government affect the lives of women in times of Zika
abstract: This study investigates the multifaceted impacts of Zika virus outbreaks on women’s health in multiple contexts and how trust, vulnerability, and support networks shape complex interactions between information agents, healthcare providers, and governmental authorities. Through interviews across nine different countries affected by Zika spread to explore underlying dynamics between elements of knowledge about the disease; access to vital medical information; state responses such as public campaigns or preventive measures; gender roles related to health care burdens; and associational relationships within communities. Results indicate that isolation caused by mistrust among community members impaired effective actions against Zika diffusion while a lack of interconnection among public entities led to vast instances of uncoordinated decision-making procedures inside which women were largely left out from key decisions. title: Bacterial survival in evaporating deposited droplets on a teflon-coated surface
abstract: This study investigates the ability of bacterial cells to survive in evaporating droplets deposited onto a teflon-coated surface. In particular, this research is geared towards determining if the physical properties of the substrate enable bacteria to resist dying off due to water stress. To test these hypotheses, samples were collected from different concentrations of Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus epidermidis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa at evaporation rates across temperature ranges and compared against controls without a teflon coating. The results show that survival depends on both evaporation rate and species composition, with E. coli having the highest survival rate regardless of temperature conditions; meanwhile S. epidermidis exhibited greater resistance in higher temperatures when compared against P. aeruginosa under the same conditions. These findings demonstrate that there are significant advantages in deploying microorganisms on surfaces coated with teflon for their protection during periods of drought or reduced water availability which could serve beneficial applications in microbial induced corrosion prevention as well as industrial water remediation techniques relying on such materials as part of their design features .

title: Interleukin-1β induces human cementoblasts to support osteoclastogenesis
abstract: Injury of the periodontium followed by inflammatory response often leads to root resorption. Resorption is accomplished by osteoclasts and their generation may depend on an interaction with the cells in direct contact with the root, the cementoblasts. Our study aimed to investigate the role of human cementoblasts in the formation of osteoclasts and the effect of interleukin (IL)-1β hereupon. Extracted teeth from healthy volunteers were subjected to sequential digestion by type I collagenase and trypsin. The effect of enzymatic digestion on the presence of cells on the root surface was analyzed by histology. Gene expression of primary human cementoblasts (pHCB) was compared with a human cementoblast cell line (HCEM). The pHCBs were analyzed for their expression of IL-1 receptors as well as of receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL) and osteoprotegerin (OPG). In a co-culture system consisting of osteoclast precursors (blood monocytes) and pHCBs, the formation of osteoclasts and their resorptive activity was assessed by osteo-assay and ivory slices. The cells obtained after a 120 min enzyme digestion expressed the highest level of bone sialoprotein, similar to that of HCEM. This fraction of isolated cells also shared a similar expression pattern of IL-1 receptors (IL1-R1 and IL1-R2). Treatment with IL-1β potently upregulated RANKL expression but not of OPG. pHCBs were shown to induce the formation of functional osteoclasts. This capacity was significantly stimulated by pretreating the pHCBs with IL-1β prior to their co-culture with human blood monocytes. Our study demonstrated that cementoblasts have the capacity to induce osteoclastogenesis, a capacity strongly promoted by IL-1β. These results may explain why osteoclasts can be formed next to the root of teeth.

title: Electronic application to improve management of infections in low-income neonatal units: pilot implementation of the NeoTree beta app in a public sector hospital in Zimbabwe
abstract:
This study investigates the effect of implementing an electronic application, named NeoTree beta app, to manage infections in neonatal units (NUs) located within low-income settings. The intervention was tested through a pilot implementation at Parirenyatwa Hospital in Zimbabwe. Results demonstrated that the use of this innovative system could improve preventive measures for infection control and management for NUs with limited resources more efficiently than tradition methods. 

In recent years, increased attention has been given to the need for comprehensive strategies aimed at improving healthcare systems' ability to deliver cost-effective interventions on a global scale. title: Oxidative Stress in Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma Cells Induced by an Infection with Canine Distemper Virus Led to a Dysregulation of HIF-1α Downstream Pathway Resulting in a Reduced Expression of VEGF-B In Vitro
abstract: Oxidative stress plays a vital role in mediating the pathophysiological responses to many diseases, such as histiocytic sarcoma (HS). Recent evidence indicates that dogs suffering from HS show an impaired response to infection with canine distemper virus (CDV), leading to aberrant expression of tumorigenic markers and growth factors. This study conducted an in vitro assay of CDV-infected canine HS cells, which aimed to determine whether oxidative stress induced by CDV could dysregulate hypoxia inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1α) downstream targets. The results revealed that exposure to CDV significantly increased intracellular reactive oxygen species concentration, while HIF-1αcytoplasmic activity was found decreased substantially compared with non infected controls. Concurrently, changes in HIF-1α signaling pathways were observed resulting in reduced expression of vascular endothelial growth factor B (VEGFB) gene transcriptional levels compared with those of controls. Taken together, these findings suggest that oxidative stress caused by parasitic infections such as CDV induces aberrations within the normal regulation process mediated by HIF/VEGF axis during histiocytosis development precluding functional reoxygenation and triggering tumorigenesis features associated with canine HS progression.

title: Targeted Profiling of Immunological Genes during Norovirus Replication in Human Intestinal Enteroids
abstract: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide. The pathogenesis of norovirus and the induced immune response remain poorly understood due to the lack of a robust virus culture system. The monolayers of two secretor-positive Chinese human intestinal enteroid (HIE) lines were challenged with two norovirus pandemic GII.4 Sydney strains. Norovirus RNA replication in supernatants and cell lysates were quantified by RT-qPCR. RNA expression levels of immune-related genes were profiled using PCR arrays. The secreted protein levels of shortlisted upregulated genes were measured in supernatants using analyte-specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Productive norovirus replications were achieved in three (75%) out of four inoculations. The two most upregulated immune-related genes were CXCL10 (93-folds) and IFI44L (580-folds). Gene expressions of CXCL10 and IFI44L were positively correlated with the level of norovirus RNA replication (CXCL10: Spearman’s r = 0.779, p < 0.05; IFI44L: r = 0.881, p < 0.01). The higher level of secreted CXCL10 and IFI44L proteins confirmed their elevated gene expression. The two genes have been reported to be upregulated in norovirus volunteer challenges and natural human infections by other viruses. Our data suggested that HIE could mimic the innate immune response elicited in natural norovirus infection and, therefore, could serve as an experimental model for future virus-host interaction and antiviral studies.

title: Advances in molecular phytodiagnostics – new solutions for old problems
abstract: Molecular phytodiagnostics (MPD) is an emerging field that uses genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to diagnose plant diseases. For decades scientists have tried to find effective solutions for challenging plant diseases caused by fungi, viruses, nematodes or bacteria which cause serious losses in crop yields. In recent years a swift development occurred in MPD research due to significant advances of sequencing technologies as well as bioinformatics and computer science methods which made the identification of pathogens easier than ever before. This review focuses on current breakthroughs in this exciting field that represent powerful solutions for existing problems in agricultural production processes: new diagnostic capabilities such as PCR-based assays; the use of efficient mobile applications; automation systems enabling more cost-effective diagnostics; genome editing techniques allowing us to detect pathogens efficiently from early stages. The paper also outlines potential benefits coming from increased accuracy of molecular tests leading to improved prevention strategies against devastating crops failures and lower economic losses associated with them. Enhancing disease control workflows through comprehensive approaches relying on accumulated knowledge about genetic composition poses great challenges but also promises immense rewards for future sustainable agriculture making it a valuable target for continued investigation and discussion among researchers working at the forefront of developments in MPD today.

title: Human lung extracellular matrix hydrogels resemble the stiffness and viscoelasticity of native lung tissue
abstract: Chronic lung diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are associated with changes in extracellular matrix (ECM) composition and abundance affecting the mechanical properties of the lung. This study aimed to generate ECM hydrogels from control, severe COPD [Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) IV], and fibrotic human lung tissue and evaluate whether their stiffness and viscoelastic properties were reflective of native tissue. For hydrogel generation, control, COPD GOLD IV, and fibrotic human lung tissues were decellularized, lyophilized, ground into powder, porcine pepsin solubilized, buffered with PBS, and gelled at 37°C. Rheological properties from tissues and hydrogels were assessed with a low-load compression tester measuring the stiffness and viscoelastic properties in terms of a generalized Maxwell model representing phases of viscoelastic relaxation. The ECM hydrogels had a greater stress relaxation than tissues. ECM hydrogels required three Maxwell elements with slightly faster relaxation times (τ) than that of native tissue, which required four elements. The relative importance (R(i)) of the first Maxwell element contributed the most in ECM hydrogels, whereas for tissue the contribution was spread over all four elements. IPF tissue had a longer-lasting fourth element with a higher R(i) than the other tissues, and IPF ECM hydrogels did require a fourth Maxwell element, in contrast to all other ECM hydrogels. This study shows that hydrogels composed of native human lung ECM can be generated. Stiffness of ECM hydrogels resembled that of whole tissue, while viscoelasticity differed.

title: An Overview of Brevinin Superfamily: Structure, Function and Clinical Perspectives
abstract:
The Brevinin family is a diverse group of polypeptides which are highly conserved among animal species. In this article, we provide an overview of the structure and function of these peptides as well as their potential clinical implications. Our review culminates with an investigation into future directions for research in this field. 

Brevinins are small pairs of cysteine-rich proteins organized in a disulfide pair pattern featuring two N-terminal domains divided by a loop region at its center. These compact domains have been found to display multiple biochemical activities; they inhibit serine proteases and hydrolyze both protein and lipid substrates amidst numerous other functions dependent on the sequence motifs present in each domain. Biochemical data suggests that Brevinins may interact with particular types of cells or tissue while playing important roles throughout development, immunity, metabolism and host defense against parasites and microbial pathogens due to their complexity and wide range of functions even when produced individually rather than within organisms that produce it cognately across evolutionary lineages. 

Indeed, there has been increasing evidence suggesting that Brevinin peptides may be clinically relevant biomarkers for various diseases such as stroke or cancer due to alterations in expression levels under different pathophysiological conditions. title: Clinical characteristics of refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children treated with glucocorticoid pulse therapy
abstract: The clinical characteristics and treatment effectiveness of glucocorticoid pulse therapy (GPT) for refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) in pediatric patients is explored in this study. Mycoplasma pneumoniae has been responsible for considerable morbidity among children, yet RMPP remains a challenge to manage. Despite the reported efficacy of GPT in adults with non-severe community acquired pneumonia associated with M.pneumoniae, its value as an adjuvant therapy for RMPP remains uncertain among pediatric patients due to the lack of well-designed studies on its usage. In order to clarify its clinical correlates and efficacy, this study evaluated 117 consecutive cases from three tertiary care centers over a 6 year period from 2012–2018. Clinical symptoms including age of onset, medical imaging examination results, laboratory findings and treatments outcomes were collected and analyzed retrospectively at discharge point or final follow up visit. The observed data associating GPT with improved clinical signs offered encouraging evidence on possible benefits it may offer these young patients affected by severe respiratory diseases caused by Mycoplasma species infections.

title: Potential factors that influence usage of complementary and alternative medicine worldwide: a systematic review
abstract: This systematic review seeks to identify and analyze the potential factors that influence usage of Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) worldwide. CAM is an increasingly prevalent practice in many countries, yet there remains a lack of cohesive understanding regarding what influences its global adoption. Applying rigorous qualitative techniques with a standardized methodology, this paper will analyze extant literature covering the range of sociodemographic, cultural, psychological and environmental elements potentially related to CAM utilization across the world. Through evaluating each factor separately as well as their collective impact, this research endeavors to provide a clearer picture of how different populations experience complementary treatments within varying contexts; ultimately illuminating consistent findings for health providers worldwide.

title: Metatranscriptomic Analysis of Virus Diversity in Urban Wild Birds with Paretic Disease
abstract: Wild birds are major natural reservoirs and potential dispersers of a variety of infectious diseases. As such, it is important to determine the diversity of viruses they carry and use this information to help understand the potential risks of spillover to humans, domestic animals, and other wildlife. We investigated the potential viral causes of paresis in long-standing, but undiagnosed, disease syndromes in wild Australian birds. RNA from diseased birds was extracted and pooled based on tissue type, host species, and clinical manifestation for metagenomic sequencing. Using a bulk and unbiased metatranscriptomic approach, combined with clinical investigation and histopathology, we identified a number of novel viruses from the families Astroviridae, Adenoviridae, Picornaviridae, Polyomaviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Parvoviridae, and Circoviridae in common urban wild birds, including Australian magpies, magpie larks, pied currawongs, Australian ravens, and rainbow lorikeets. In each case, the presence of the virus was confirmed by reverse transcription (RT)-PCR. These data revealed a number of candidate viral pathogens that may contribute to coronary, skeletal muscle, vascular, and neuropathology in birds of the Corvidae and Artamidae families and neuropathology in members of the Psittaculidae. The existence of such a diverse virome in urban avian species highlights the importance and challenges in elucidating the etiology and ecology of wildlife pathogens in urban environments. This information will be increasingly important for managing disease risks and conducting surveillance for potential viral threats to wildlife, livestock, and human health. IMPORTANCE Wildlife naturally harbor a diverse array of infectious microorganisms and can be a source of novel diseases in domestic animals and human populations. Using unbiased RNA sequencing, we identified highly diverse viruses in native birds from Australian urban environments presenting with paresis. This research included the clinical investigation and description of poorly understood recurring syndromes of unknown etiology: clenched claw syndrome and black and white bird disease. As well as identifying a range of potentially disease-causing viral pathogens, this study describes methods that can effectively and efficiently characterize emergent disease syndromes in free-ranging wildlife and promotes further surveillance for specific pathogens of potential conservation and zoonotic concern.

title: Inferring R(0) in emerging epidemics—the effect of common population structure is small
abstract: When controlling an emerging outbreak of an infectious disease, it is essential to know the key epidemiological parameters, such as the basic reproduction number R(0) and the control effort required to prevent a large outbreak. These parameters are estimated from the observed incidence of new cases and information about the infectious contact structures of the population in which the disease spreads. However, the relevant infectious contact structures for new, emerging infections are often unknown or hard to obtain. Here, we show that, for many common true underlying heterogeneous contact structures, the simplification to neglect such structures and instead assume that all contacts are made homogeneously in the whole population results in conservative estimates for R(0) and the required control effort. This means that robust control policies can be planned during the early stages of an outbreak, using such conservative estimates of the required control effort.

title: Genetic polymorphisms in malaria vaccine candidate Plasmodium falciparum reticulocyte-binding protein homologue-5 among populations in Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccines are the most reliable alternative to elicit sterile immunity against malaria but their development has been hindered by polymorphisms and strain-specificity in previously studied antigens. New vaccine candidates are therefore urgently needed. Highly conserved Plasmodium falciparum reticulocyte-binding protein homologue-5 (PfRH5) has been identified as a potential candidate for anti-disease vaccine development. PfRH5 is essential for erythrocyte invasion by merozoites and crucial for parasite survival. However, there is paucity of data on the extent of genetic variations on PfRH5 in field isolates of Plasmodium falciparum. This study described genetic polymorphisms at the high affinity binding polypeptides (HABPs) 36718, 36727, 36728 of PfRH5 in Nigerian isolates of P. falciparum. This study tested the hypothesis that only specific conserved B and T cell epitopes on PfRH5 HABPs are crucial for vaccine development. METHODS: One hundred and ninety-five microscopically confirmed P. falciparum samples collected in a prospective cross-sectional study of three different populations in Lagos, Nigeria. Genetic diversity and haplotype construct of Pfrh5 gene were determined using bi-directional sequencing approach. Tajima’s D and the ratio of nonsynonymous vs synonymous mutations were utilized to estimate the extent of balancing and directional selection in the pfrh5 gene. RESULTS: Sequence analysis revealed three haplotypes of PfRH5 with negative Tajima’s D and dN/dS value of − 1.717 and 0.011 ± 0.020, respectively. A single nucleotide polymorphism, SNP (G → A) at position 608 was observed, which resulted in a change of the amino acid cysteine at position 203 to tyrosine. Haplotype and nucleotide diversities were 0.318 ± 0.016 and 0.0046 ± 0.0001 while inter-population genetic differentiation ranged from 0.007 to 0.037. Five polypeptide variants were identified, the most frequent being KTKYH with a frequency of 51.3%. One B-cell epitope, 151 major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II T-cell epitopes, four intrinsically unstructured regions (IURs) and six MHC class I T-cell epitopes were observed in the study. Phylogenetic analysis of the sequences showed clustering and evidence of evolutionary relationship with 3D7, PAS-2 and FCB-2 RH5 sequences. CONCLUSIONS: This study has revealed low level of genetic polymorphisms in PfRH5 antigen with B- and T-cell epitopes in intrinsically unstructured regions along the PfRH5 gene in Lagos, Nigeria. A broader investigation is however required in other parts of the country to support the possible inclusion of PfRH5 in a cross-protective multi-component vaccine.

title: Compositional Associations of Sleep and Activities within the 24-h Cycle with Cardiometabolic Health Markers in Adults
abstract: This article examines the link between activities within the 24-h cycle, sleep and cardiometabolic health markers in adults. Over recent years there has been an increase in evidence that measures of activity vary throughout the day, with underlying biological rhythms known to be modulated by light–dark cycles and other factors such as age, sex or occupation. This study investigates whether certain types of daily activities are associated with particular aspects of a person’s metabolic health profile including parameters such as blood pressure, lipids and BMI. Moreover, by delving into information collected from previous research on sleeping patterns across populations this article aims to determine whether disruptions in sleeping habits have concomitant effects on a person’s overall physiological condition over time. With data provided from a cross‐sectional sample of adult patients aged 25–75 this systematic review presents novel insights into potential correlations between circadian behaviors and metabolic indicators which can be further used towards developing meaningful interventions aimed at improving long‐term healthiness within human populations. 'Compositional Associations of Sleep and Activities within the 24-h Cycle with Cardiometabolic Health Markers in Adults'.

title: Whole-Transcriptome Analysis of Dermal Fibroblasts, Derived from Three Pairs of Monozygotic Twins, Discordant for Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: This study examines the role of genetic and epigenetic factors in Parkinson’s Disease (PD) using a novel whole-transcriptome analysis to identify potential biomarkers that distinguish similarly aged monozygotic twins who differ in terms of PD discordance. Whole Transcriptome Analysis of Dermal Fibroblasts, Derived from Three Pairs of Monozygotic Twins, Discordant for Parkinson’s Disease presents findings related to how genetics and epigenetics may contribute to PD by examining global gene expression levels looking at differences between siblings. The results are compared between affected individuals with PD alongside their healthy twin whose transcriptomics remained unchanged, indicating non-genetic drivers as possible predictors for this disease. The team identified several differentially expressed genes associated with numerous processes such as cytoskeleton organization, response to extrinsic stimuli, calcium ion transport which might be indicative suggesting molecular signatures stemming from gene regulatory changes rather than genomic mutations may be correlated with an increased risk of developing PD. Ultimately this research introduces further clinical implications concerning diagnosis and prognosis methods pertinent or specific to monozygotic twins so that healthcare providers can better understand the idiosyncrasies of managing this potentially debilitating disorder.
