title: STAT2 Limits Host Species Specificity of Human Metapneumovirus
abstract: The prevalence of emerging human infections has been rapidly increasing over the past several decades, leading to a greater need to understand host species-specific viruses and how they may impact different species. Herein, we study the molecular determinants for host range restriction in human Metapneumovirus (hMPV) using mammalian cell systems as an effective model host system. This research reveals that STAT2 proteins play critical roles in limiting hMPV replication within multiple speciest by regulating Interferon Stimulated Genes (ISGs). Additionally, we identify point mutations within NJ43/R26 stem loop II—a region present in all existing strains of hMPA—that abolishes STAT2 binding and increases viral cytopathic effects in vitro without impacting replicative fitness among other parameters. Our results demonstrate clear evidence that STAT2 protein can limit virus infection specificity among multiple hosts, highlighting it as a viable target for antiviral drug discovery or possible deployment of recombinant vaccines.

title: Finding and identifying the viral needle in the metagenomic haystack: trends and challenges
abstract: Finding and identifying the viral needle in the metagenomic haystack: trends and challenges. The field of metagenomics is preparing to undergo a major shift, as the development of new tools designed to detect viruses has enabled us to survey complex microbial populations at unprecedented depths. This paper examines current developments in order to present an overview of existing approaches for detection and identification, both existing and ongoing ones. Additionally, this article aims to unveil latest advancements in sample preparation techniques employed for isolating viral nucleic acids from diverse environments; such technologies have been key enablers for precision diagnostics as well as related informatics processes which supplement downstream applications aimed at revealing the identities of unknown yet potentially pathogenic agents. To maintain accurate insight into methods behind successful diagnoses of peculiar strains – often radiating beyond species level recognition performances – insightful perspectives on computational benefits assisting this endeavor will be discussed here too. Finally, we will illustrate potential directions that could benefit our understanding towards thus far unresolved questions within metavirome exploration circles, mostly focusing on areas compatible with recent inherent complexities quickly rising at scale levels too large to manual or canonical bioinformatics tactics alone can readily address convincingly enough by themselves.

title: Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever: transmission to visitors and healthcare workers
abstract: This paper investigates the risk of transmission of Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) to visitors and healthcare workers. It focuses on epidemiological data, surveillance information and prevention strategies in order to find effective ways to reduce these risks and protect such individuals from contracting CCHF. The results are further discussed in light of modern health systems, their policies and their implications for managing the virus in endemic areas.

title: Characterization of a Bowman–Birk type trypsin inhibitor purified from seeds of Solanum surattense
abstract: A Bowman–Birk type trypsin inhibitor protein (SSTI) from seeds of the medicinal plant Solanum surattense was isolated, purified and characterized. SSTI showed a single band on SDS-PAGE corresponding to 11.4 kDa molecular weight. It is a glycoprotein (2.8% glycosylation) that differentially interacted with trypsin and chymotrypsin in a concentration-dependent manner. Its peptide sequence is similar to other Bowman–Birk type protease inhibitors found in Glycine max and Phaseolus acutifolius. The inhibitory activity was stable over a wide range of pH (1–10) and temperatures (10–100° C). Far-UV Circular Dichroism (CD) studies showed that SSTI contains β sheets (~ 23%) and α helix (~ 6%) and demonstrated structural stability at wide pH and high temperature. The kinetic analysis revealed a noncompetitive (mixed) type nature of SSTI and low inhibitor constant (Ki) values (16.6 × 10(−8) M) suggested strong inhibitory activity. Isothermal titration calorimetric analysis revealed its high affinity towards trypsin with dissociation constant (K(d)) 2.28 µM.

Its peptide sequence is similar to other Bowman–Birk type protease inhibitors found in Glycine max and Phaseolus acutifolius. The inhibitory activity was stable over a wide range of pH (1–10) and temperatures (10–100° C). Far-UV Circular Dichroism (CD) studies showed that SSTI contains β sheets (~ 23%) and α helix (~ 6%) and demonstrated structural stability at wide pH and high temperature. The kinetic analysis revealed a noncompetitive (mixed) type nature of SSTI and low inhibitor constant (Ki) values (16.6 × 10(−8) M) suggested strong inhibitory activity. Isothermal titration calorimetric analysis revealed its high affinity towards trypsin with dissociation constant (K(d)) 2.28 µM.

title: Performance of Zoster Vaccine Live (Zostavax): A Systematic Review of 12 years of Experimental and Observational Evidence
abstract: This systematic review examines the performance of Zostavax, an inactivated live herpes zoster vaccine (HZV) developed to protect against shingles and the associated complications. An effective herpes zoster vaccine should reduce the incidence, severity and associated burden of disease due to this highly contagious viral infection. We conducted a comprehensive search of 12 years' worth of literature regarding observational data as well as experimental studies that have investigated both efficacy outcomes and safety profiles related to Zostavax vaccination against shingles. Findings include that observational evidence demonstrated higher efficacy rates with increasing age at immunization; while reliable results from clinical trials suggest a sustained protection for up to 6 years but no further protection beyond 9-12 years post vaccination, when measured by incident cases or seropositivity compared to placebo effectiveness. Furthermore, notable adverse effects such as local injection site reactions were observed throughout all studies reviewed within the systematic review. This systemic appraisal provides healthcare providers with valuable insight into informed decision making on various aspects including expected benefits and uncertain risks when recommending Zostavax for their patients who are candidates for HZV immunization.

title: Post-Transcriptional Control of Type I Interferon Induction by Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus in Its Natural Host Cells
abstract: This article aims to demonstrate the hitherto unrecognised role of post-transcriptional control in modulating the induction of Type I interferon (IFN) by Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus (PRRSV) in its natural host cells. We sought to ascertain if infection with PRRSV increased IFN levels beyond those associated with conventional transcriptional regulation, and further determine the underlying molecular mediators responsible for this process. Furthermore, our findings provide new insights into previously uncovered mechanisms governing antiviral response following PRRS exposure. Our study presents evidence that suggest a distinct contribution of post-transcriptional pathways in driving IFN receptor expression upon recognition of viral threat from PRRSV, which significantly contributes towards determining an effective overall immune defence outcome against virus propagation.

title: The autophagy elongation complex (ATG5-12/16L1) positively regulates HCV replication and is required for wild-type membranous web formation
abstract: This study focuses on the role of autophagy elongation complex (ATG5-12/16L1) in the positive regulation of human hepatitis C virus (HCV) replication and its involvement in wild-type membranous web formation. Autophagosomes are double membrane vesicles with critical roles in protein degradation, energy metabolism and innate antiviral defense mechanisms. ATG proteins constitute an evolutionarily conserved family that plays a pivotal role during autophagosome formation, maturation, and fusion. The aim of this research was to investigate how ATG5-12/16L1 influences HCV replication within hepatocytes by manipulating expression at the level of transcription or translation using siRNA or small molecules. We also aimed to dissect its mechanism involved in wild type membranous webs formation. Our results indicated that ATG5-12/16L1 positively regulates HCV replication through multiple pathways involving E2 ubiquitin ligase activity; furthermore it is required for wild Type membranous webs morphology confirming a direct functional link between autophagic events and endomembrane modifications to support productive viral infection.

title: A Survey of Recent Adenoviral Respiratory Pathogens in Hong Kong Reveals Emergent and Recombinant Human Adenovirus Type 4 (HAdV-E4) Circulating in Civilian Populations
abstract: Human adenovirus type 4 (HAdV-E4), which is intriguingly limited to military populations, causes acute respiratory disease with demonstrated morbidity and mortality implications. This respiratory pathogen contains genome identity with chimpanzee adenoviruses, indicating zoonotic origins. A signature of these “old” HAdV-E4 is the absence of a critical replication motif, NF-I, which is found in all HAdV respiratory pathogens and most HAdVs. However, our recent survey of flu-like disease in children in Hong Kong reveals that the emergent HAdV-E4 pathogens circulating in civilian populations contain NF-I, indicating recombination and reflecting host-adaptation that enables the “new” HAdV-E4 to replicate more efficiently in human cells and foretells more potential HAdV-E4 outbreaks in immune-naïve civilian populations. Special attention should be paid by clinicians to this emergent and recombinant HAdV-E4 circulating in civilian populations.

title: Improved phylogenomic sampling of free-living nematodes enhances resolution of higher-level nematode phylogeny
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nematodes are among the most diverse and abundant metazoans on Earth, but research on them has been biased toward parasitic taxa and model organisms. Free-living nematodes, particularly from the clades Enoplia and Dorylaimia, have been underrepresented in genome-scale phylogenetic analyses to date, leading to poor resolution of deep relationships within the phylum. RESULTS: We supplemented publicly available data by sequencing transcriptomes of nine free-living nematodes and two important outgroups and conducted a phylum-wide phylogenomic analysis including a total of 108 nematodes. Analysis of a dataset generated using a conservative orthology inference strategy resulted in a matrix with a high proportion of missing data and moderate to weak support for branching within and placement of Enoplia. A less conservative orthology inference approach recovered more genes and resulted in higher support for the deepest splits within Nematoda, recovering Enoplia as the sister taxon to the rest of Nematoda. Relationships within major clades were similar to those found in previously published studies based on 18S rDNA. CONCLUSIONS: Expanded transcriptome sequencing of free-living nematodes has contributed to better resolution among deep nematode lineages, though the dataset is still strongly biased toward parasites. Inclusion of more free-living nematodes in future phylogenomic analyses will allow a clearer understanding of many interesting aspects of nematode evolution, such as morphological and molecular adaptations to parasitism and whether nematodes originated in a marine or terrestrial environment. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (10.1186/s12862-019-1444-x) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

title: Dietary supplementation with Withania somnifera root powder ameliorates experimentally induced Infectious Bursal Disease in chicken
abstract: Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD) is an economically important, immunosuppressive viral disease of chicken. Withania somnifera, a well-known Indian medicinal plant and functional food, finds extensive ethnomedicinal and ethnoveterinary use in the subcontinent. Root extracts of Withania somnifera have been shown to inhibit IBD virus (IBDV) in vitro. The effect of dietary supplementation with whole root powder of Withania somnifera was studied in chicken experimentally infected with IBDV. Dietary supplementation with the root powder improved erythrocytic indices, biochemical parameters, bursal weight index, and lymphocyte stimulation indices, and reduced histopathological insult in the infected birds. Viral load decreased to less than one-fourth in the birds receiving dietary supplementation with Withania somnifera root powder. It could be concluded that continued supplementation of IBDV-infected chicken with Withania somnifera root powder alleviated virus-induced stress and histological and immunological alterations and reduced viral persistence in the host.

title: Ventilatory support and mechanical properties of the fibrotic lung acting as a “squishy ball”
abstract: This study examines the relationship between mechanical properties of the fibrotic lung and its capacity to receive ventilatory support. Utilizing a combination of computational modelling, ex vivo measurements and in vivo observations, it is hypothesized that the stiffness dichotomy between healthy lungs and those affected by fibrosis can explain at least part of the observed differences in ventilation outcomes for people with debilitating respiratory illnesses. By exploring how altered pulmonary turbulence affects gas exchange as well as examining the tissue changes responsible for restricting airflow dynamics during subsaturation levels of inspiration, this paper seeks to provide insight into therapeutic strategies related to lung injury rehabilitation.

title: Optimistic Bias, Food Safety Cognition, and Consumer Behavior of College Students in Taiwan and Mainland China
abstract: This paper examines the effects of optimistic bias, food safety cognition, and consumer behavior of college students in Taiwan and mainland China. Previous studies have indicated that Taiwanese consumers usually prefer safe food with a low risk perception due to cultural differences between the two countries. The present study used a questionnaire survey to assess Taiwanese and Chinese undergraduate students´ perceptions about risks related to eating out/food delivery services such as cooking practices, hygiene facilities, ingredient sources etc., and their buying behaviors when faced with different kinds of food safety-related products including fresh produce, processed foods, ready-to-eat meals. Variables like gender, age group were also examined to determine if they affected naive optimism when possessing information concerning potential hazards associated with those items. Furthermore factors affecting the belief which guide an individual’s decisions while responding to his uncertainty were analyzed to understand how motivated optimism can lead people into either under confidence or overconfidence towards hazardous situations even after being informed via cues on product labels or news regarding occasional contamination incidents around them. Results highlighted important implications for policymakers aiming at improving consumer education programs targeting young adults as well as providing structural regulations represent restrictions or economic incentives for O2O businesses during pandemics or other unforeseen disasters.

title: Green Synthesis of Selenium and Tellurium Nanoparticles: Current Trends, Biological Properties and Biomedical Applications
abstract: The synthesis and assembly of nanoparticles using green technology has been an excellent option in nanotechnology because they are easy to implement, cost-efficient, eco-friendly, risk-free, and amenable to scaling up. They also do not require sophisticated equipment nor well-trained professionals. Bionanotechnology involves various biological systems as suitable nanofactories, including biomolecules, bacteria, fungi, yeasts, and plants. Biologically inspired nanomaterial fabrication approaches have shown great potential to interconnect microbial or plant extract biotechnology and nanotechnology. The present article extensively reviews the eco-friendly production of metalloid nanoparticles, namely made of selenium (SeNPs) and tellurium (TeNPs), using various microorganisms, such as bacteria and fungi, and plants’ extracts. It also discusses the methodologies followed by materials scientists and highlights the impact of the experimental sets on the outcomes and shed light on the underlying mechanisms. Moreover, it features the unique properties displayed by these biogenic nanoparticles for a large range of emerging applications in medicine, agriculture, bioengineering, and bioremediation.

title: Laboratory epidemiology of respiratory viruses in a large children's hospital: A STROBE-compliant article
abstract: This article presents the findings of a laboratory-based epidemiological study on respiratory viruses among children treated at a large hospital in an urban setting. To assess the prevalence, transmission and clinical dynamics of various respiratory viruses associated with these patients, nasopharyngeal swab specimens were collected from 377 pediatric patients aged three months to eighteen years over a 12 month period. Using polished culture media, conventional enzyme immunoassay tests and real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assays for diagnostics purposes, it was possible to identify 285 positive samples belonging to 15 different species from five clades: orthomyxoviruses; paramyxoviruses; enteroviruses; adenoviruses; and coronaviridae. Of these infections, 13% were symptomatic while 87% were asymptomatic or not considered clinically relevant when comparing incidence rates based on virus type with age strata of patient cohorts between twelve weeks postnatal vs >twelve weeks old stratified by areas of residence. The report is structured according to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology – Checklist (STROBE). Key findings elucidate significant associations between RT-PCR test results correlating directly to prevailing population healthcare challenges related underlying pediatric conditions such as chronic pulmonary disease or bronchial asthma exacerbations requiring primary medical attention leading global health initiatives emphasizing intensive management strategies addressing infectious diseases among infant care populations particularly vulnerable within underserved subpopulations.

title: Thorax
abstract:
Thorax: Investigating the Impact of Exercise on Chest Expansion and Its Implications for Patients’ Wellbeing 
The primary objective of this research is to gain insight into how regular exercise influences chest expansion in patients with respiratory diseases, such as asthma and cystic fibrosis. This study aims to provide further evidence on whether improved chest expansion contributes to better patient health outcomes. A comprehensive evaluation of current literature underpins our investigation, which also includes interviews with four medical practitioners specialising in pulmonary medicine. Our novel findings reveal that due to physical resistance and greater ventilation gained from consistent exercising, patients display higher thoracic mobility—leading towards an enhanced quality of life. The implications discuss how larger thoracic volumes associate with lower breathlessness during activity or at rest and aid physicians when prescribing treatment for a range of lung ailments.

title: Characterization of the Sendai virus V protein with an anti-peptide antiserum
abstract: The Sendai virus V protein, which is a fusion of the P and V ORFs of the P gene, was characterized with antisera to a portion of the V ORF and compared to the P protein. The only property found in common with P is that V is also highly phosphorylated, and this is so even when these proteins are expressed independently of the other viral proteins. Otherwise, V was not found in virions, was not strongly associated with viral nucleocapsids like P, and anti-V had no effect on viral RNA synthesis in vitro under conditions where anti-P was highly inhibitory. The available evidence suggests that V may playa role in RNA synthesis, but it is not an essential one like that of the P protein.

title: Lipid peroxidation in Gram-negative bacteremia modulates the risk for septic shock and infections by resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae
abstract: Controversies in outcomes with the parenteral administration of antioxidants as adjuvant therapies led to the measurement of malondialdehyde (MDA), a product of lipid peroxidation, in serum collected from 120 patients with primary Gram-negative bacteremia during the first 24 h from sepsis onset. MDA was measured by the thiobarbiturate assay, followed by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. After receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, patients were divided into those with high levels of MDA and low levels of MDA. The primary endpoint was the association of the level of MDA with septic shock. The level of MDA as an index of neutrophil function and associations with outcome and with infections by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae were the secondary endpoints. In total, 63 patients had high and 57 had low MDA levels; 27% and 49.1%, respectively, had septic shock (p = 0.015). The rate of the concentration of MDA to the total neutrophil count was used as an expression of neutrophil function; this was lower among patients with septic shock. The odds ratio (OR) for death among patients without septic shock and low level of MDA was 4.00; this was 0.48 for patients with septic shock (p = 0.020 between the two ORs). The OR for resistance to carbapenems among patients with bacteremia by K. pneumoniae and low level of MDA was 7.50 (p = 0.011 compared to patients with bacteremia by other pathogens). Low level of circulating MDA is associated with susceptibility to septic shock and infections by carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae.

title: Measurement and Comparison of Melt-Blowing Airflow Fields: Nozzle Modifications to Reduce Turbulence and Fibre Whipping
abstract: The present study examines the airflow fields generated by melt-blowing production processes and their effect on turbulence, fibre whipping and other crucial temperature control factors. Using novel nozzle modifications, this research aims to reduce turbulent airflows as well as increase consistency of polypropylene fibres across a given area. To achieve these goals, measurement was conducted via Particle Imaging Velocimetry (PIV) analysis at various working pressures and temperatures along with the application of sophisticated Finite Element Analysis software Tools (FEAT). Comparison with theoretical predictive models was then used to assess differences in resulting airflow development. Ultimately, it is envisioned that findings from this research could be deployed for manufacturing parameters optimisation for better process control.

title: Pre-Travel Medical Preparation of Business and Occupational Travelers: An Analysis of the Global TravEpiNet Consortium, 2009 to 2012
abstract: This paper discusses the global findings of the TravEpiNet Consortium's investigation on pre-travel medical preparations and their importance in limiting risks associated with business and occupational travel. Utilizing a large, international cohort study from 2009 to 2012 for reference, this article evaluates predominant trends in pre-travel medical care and provides insight into possible areas for increased awareness among travelers. The mechanism by which preventive approaches can guard against potentially hazardous environmental exposures is also outlined. We anticipate these results will aid policy makers in better informing travelers about potential health risks during incarceration abroad and provide strategies for preventing negative outcomes due to inadequate knowledge about current protection measures available.

title: Outcomes and management approaches of resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta based on the income of countries
abstract: The title of this article is 'Outcomes and Management Approaches of Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta based on the Income of Countries'. Over recent years, endovascular techniques have been increasingly employed for treating complex aortic injuries. They offer better results compared to conventional surgical techniques due to their minimally-invasive nature. As beneficial as these techniques may be in general, fewer studies have sought to explore whether there are any discrepancies among countries with different levels of income when applying such techniques for tackling traumatic aortic transections (TATs). This article seeks to investigate outcomes and management approaches concerning resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion methods used in treating TATs from low-, middle-, and high-income countries (MIC & HIC) by analyzing previous research articles. Moreover, other associated factors likely having an influence on clinical outcomes before/after sophisticated interventions will be addressed. In sum, through evaluating international outcome trends related to modern therapeutic measures developed over time, recommendations can be established that would eventually help improve patient quality recovery regardless across all three economic demarcations.

title: Challenges for Microelectronics in Non-Invasive Medical Diagnostics
abstract: Microelectronics is emerging, sometimes with changing fortunes, as a key enabling technology in diagnostics. This paper reviews some recent results and technical challenges which still need to be addressed in terms of the design of CMOS analog application specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and their integration in the surrounding systems, in order to consolidate this technological paradigm. Open issues are discussed from two, apparently distant but complementary, points of view: micro-analytical devices, combining microfluidics with affinity bio-sensing, and gamma cameras for simultaneous multi-modal imaging, namely scintigraphy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The role of integrated circuits is central in both application domains. In portable analytical platforms, ASICs offer miniaturization and tackle the noise/power dissipation trade-off. The integration of CMOS chips with microfluidics poses multiple open technological issues. In multi-modal imaging, now that the compatibility of the acquisition chains (thousands of Silicon Photo-Multipliers channels) of gamma detectors with Tesla-level magnetic fields has been demonstrated, other development directions, enabled by microelectronics, can be envisioned in particular for single-photon emission tomography (SPECT): a faster and simplified operation, for instance, to allow transportable applications (bed-side) and hardware pre-processing that reduces the number of output signals and the image reconstruction time.

title: The Hemagglutinin A Stem Antibody MEDI8852 Prevents and Controls Disease and Limits Transmission of Pandemic Influenza Viruses
abstract: This article explores the efficacy of MEDI8852 – a monoclonal antibody based on the hemagglutinin A stem of an influenza virus – in preventing and controlling disease caused by pandemic influenza viruses. Developed by Medigene AG, MEDI8852 has demonstrated unprecedented activity in pre-clinical models when used as either preventative or therapeutic treatment against novel influenzas, including H5N1 and H7N9. Our research builds on these discoveries to examine how well it can not only be used to ensure decreased morbidity and mortality in humans with existing heavy viral loads, but also offers the promise of reducing pathogenicity through protection from infection and transmission among contacts. We conducted studies using laboratory cultures infected with commonly circulating strains belonging to group 1 subtype B3 lineages from multiple regions that were treated with varying concentrations of MEDI8852. The results are presented herein along with a discussion about future potential for controlling viral spread during pandemics.

title: Coronavirus Infection in Acute Lower Respiratory Tract Disease of Infants
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between Coronavirus Infection and Acute Lower Respiratory Tract Disease (ALRTD) in infants. To understand how COVID-19 infection manifests in this population, we compared a cohort of hospitalized ALRTD patients and SARS-CoV-2 positive infants to assess clinical and laboratory features associated with primary viral infections as well as severity of illness from both groups. Our results indicate that SARS-CoV-2 virus is an important factor presenting similar characteristics to other respiratory viruses causing severe presentations in vulnerable populations such as infants who suffer from poor airway clearance capacity leading to increased hospitalization rates, mechanical ventilation support, higher mortality risk and overall worse prognosis without aggressive management strategies. The aim of this study is to enhance understanding surrounding infectious diseases caused by emerging pathogens such as coronaviruses thereby providing insight into best practices for managing these cases when presented in critically ill infant population.

title: Estimating the Potential Effects of a Vaccine Program Against an Emerging Influenza Pandemic—United States
abstract: Background. Human illness from influenza A(H7N9) was identified in March 2013, and candidate vaccine viruses were soon developed. To understand factors that may impact influenza vaccination programs, we developed a model to evaluate hospitalizations and deaths averted considering various scenarios. Methods. We utilized a model incorporating epidemic curves with clinical attack rates of 20% or 30% in a single wave of illness, case hospitalization ratios of 0.5% or 4.2%, and case fatality ratios of 0.08% or 0.53%. We considered scenarios that achieved 80% vaccination coverage, various starts of vaccination programs (16 or 8 weeks before, the same week of, or 8 or 16 weeks after start of pandemic), an administration rate of 10 or 30 million doses per week (the latter rate is an untested assumption), and 2 levels of vaccine effectiveness (2 doses of vaccine required; either 62% or 80% effective for persons aged <60 years, and either 43% or 60% effective for persons aged ≥60 years). Results. The start date of vaccination campaigns most influenced impact; 141 000–2 200 000 hospitalizations and 11 000–281 000 deaths were averted when campaigns started before a pandemic, and <100–1 300 000 hospitalizations and 0–165 000 deaths were averted for programs beginning the same time as or after the introduction of the pandemic virus. The rate of vaccine administration and vaccine effectiveness did not influence campaign impact as much as timing of the start of campaign. Conclusions. Our findings suggest that efforts to improve the timeliness of vaccine production will provide the greatest impacts for future pandemic vaccination programs.

title: More than Meets the ISG15: Emerging Roles in the DNA Damage Response and Beyond
abstract: Maintenance of genome stability is a crucial priority for any organism. To meet this priority, robust signalling networks exist to facilitate error-free DNA replication and repair. These signalling cascades are subject to various regulatory post-translational modifications that range from simple additions of chemical moieties to the conjugation of ubiquitin-like proteins (UBLs). Interferon Stimulated Gene 15 (ISG15) is one such UBL. While classically thought of as a component of antiviral immunity, ISG15 has recently emerged as a regulator of genome stability, with key roles in the DNA damage response (DDR) to modulate p53 signalling and error-free DNA replication. Additional proteomic analyses and cancer-focused studies hint at wider-reaching, uncharacterised functions for ISG15 in genome stability. We review these recent discoveries and highlight future perspectives to increase our understanding of this multifaceted UBL in health and disease.

title: Outcomes of Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 Virus Infection: Results from Two International Cohort Studies
abstract: This study seeks to examine the outcomes of infection with the Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus in two international cohort studies, an important expansion on existing research literature. The H1N1pdm09 virus is associated with significant morbidity and mortality, especially among high-risk populations such as pregnant women, yet little is known about its effects when compared between different patient groups from distinct geographic regions. In order to better understand how clinical factors and geographical variations impact influenza severity, this study analyses data collected by two large prospective cohorts of infected patients across three continents; Europe, Asia, and North America. By processing these extensive patient records with epidemiological and statistical methods such as chi-squared tests and Kaplan-Meier analysis we are able to identify potential preventative measures or determinants that could help decrease the burden posed by influenza globally. This comparative assessment will benefit clinicians treating a wide range of viral infectious diseases worldwide.

title: Fluorescence cross-correlation spectroscopy using single wavelength laser
abstract: This article presents a novel approach to the analysis of submicron particles using Fluorescence Cross-correlation Spectroscopy with single wavelength laser. We provide an experimental calculation of the time interval between two fluorescence photons collected from selected emitting particles while they are exposed to interleaved and stopped laser excitation fields generated by a single wavelength femtosecond laser. This comprehensive study evaluated data accuracy as well as measuring dynamic parameters, such as diffusion constants and rotational relaxation times, in polydisperse suspensions ranging from fluorescent proteins up to nanometers. The results revealed high correlation values obtained both independently of concentrations and absolute sizes of emitted quantum dots used in this investigation. These findings may introduce robust technique for measurements even at low concentration level range allowing valuable insights into small particle collisions dynamics whenever these occur during fluctuations among freely diffused objects or between driven chemical reactions at thermal equilibrium conditions.

title: Platelet aggregation inhibitor prescription for newly diagnosed peripheral arterial disease in the Netherlands: a cohort study
abstract:
This study evaluates the antithrombotic pharmacotherapy among patients newly diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) in the Netherlands. Data was collected from a large cohort of patients to investigate trends in prescription for platelet aggregation inhibitors (PAI) and their factors associated with prescription.
Based on available information, this observational retrospective cohort study provides an insight into prescribing habits following diagnosis of PAD that may help guide clinical management decisions in future patient cases. 
In total, 8963 diagnoses made between 1st January 2017 and 31st December 2018 were included on the basis of their International Classification of Diseases 9th Revision codes related to PAD within two Dutch nationwide linked databases: Pharmetrics Claims Database (PCD) and Longitudinal Ageing Study Amersfoort (LASA). 
Results indicate PAIs were prescribed during eleven per cent of patient encounters post diagnosis over a two year period; prescriptions increased amongst those aged 70 or above but disagreed based upon gender as males received more than females did by 15%. Additionally, risk stratification tools showed decreased odds ratio at moderate-to-high levels while comorbidities involving cerebral vascular insufficiency obtained higher inclusion rates compared to other associated pathologies. 
The findings from this paper provide significant insights into PAI prescription practices for peripheral arterial disease based upon demographic considerations and potential risk alongside low frequency usage overall which could have implications for regional adaptation learning protocols. title: Label-Free Electrochemical Diagnosis of Viral Antigens with Genetically Engineered Fusion Protein
abstract: We have developed a simple electrochemical biosensing strategy for the label-free diagnosis of hepatitis B virus (HBV) on a gold electrode surface. Gold-binding polypeptide (GBP) fused with single-chain antibody (ScFv) against HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), in forms of genetically engineered protein, was utilized. This GBP-ScFv fusion protein can directly bind onto the gold substrate with the strong binding affinity between the GBP and the gold surface, while the recognition site orients toward the sample for target binding at the same time. Furthermore, this one-step immobilization strategy greatly simplifies a fabrication process without any chemical modification as well as maintaining activity of biological recognition elements. This system allows specific immobilization of proteins and sensitive detection of targets, which were verified by surface plasmon resonance analysis and successfully applied to electrochemical cyclic voltammetry and impedance spectroscopy upto 0.14 ng/mL HBsAg.

title: Lack of a 5.9 kDa Peptide C-Terminal Fragment of Fibrinogen α Chain Precedes Fibrosis Progression in Patients with Liver Disease
abstract: This journal article examines the potential connection between changes in a 5.9 kilo Dalton (kDa) peptide fragment of fibrinogen α chain and fibrosis progression in patients with liver disease.  Using clinical observations from 12 cases, the authors explored whether clots formed by this peptide may offer biochemical evidence that is associated with early onset of fibrotic processes common to cirrhosis development. Results suggest that a lack of this C-terminal fragment may be correlated more directly with an increased risk for developing advanced stages of hepatic cirrhosis than previously thought. Through identifying theoretical relationships between patient conditions and clustering enzyme activities, the findings create greater insight into some factors at play during the course production process leading to liver pathology.

title: DeepVISP: Deep Learning for Virus Site Integration Prediction and Motif Discovery
abstract: Approximately 15% of human cancers are estimated to be attributed to viruses. Virus sequences can be integrated into the host genome, leading to genomic instability and carcinogenesis. Here, a new deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model is developed with attention architecture, namely DeepVISP, for accurately predicting oncogenic virus integration sites (VISs) in the human genome. Using the curated benchmark integration data of three viruses, hepatitis B virus (HBV), human herpesvirus (HPV), and Epstein‐Barr virus (EBV), DeepVISP achieves high accuracy and robust performance for all three viruses through automatically learning informative features and essential genomic positions only from the DNA sequences. In comparison, DeepVISP outperforms conventional machine learning methods by 8.43–34.33% measured by area under curve (AUC) value enhancement in three viruses. Moreover, DeepVISP can decode cis‐regulatory factors that are potentially involved in virus integration and tumorigenesis, such as HOXB7, IKZF1, and LHX6. These findings are supported by multiple lines of evidence in literature. The clustering analysis of the informative motifs reveales that the representative k‐mers in clusters could help guide virus recognition of the host genes. A user‐friendly web server is developed for predicting putative oncogenic VISs in the human genome using DeepVISP.

title: Impact of sampling depth on pathogen detection in pit latrines
abstract: Wastewater based epidemiology (WBE) is increasingly used to provide decision makers with actionable data about community health. WBE efforts to date have primarily focused on sewer-transported wastewater in high-income countries, but at least 1.8 billion people in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) use onsite sanitation systems such as pit latrines and septic tanks. Like wastewater, fecal sludges from such systems offer similar advantages in community pathogen monitoring and other epidemiological applications. To evaluate the distribution of enteric pathogens inside pit latrines–which could inform sampling methods for WBE in LMIC settings unserved by sewers–we collected fecal sludges from the surface, mid-point, and maximum-depth of 33 pit latrines in urban and peri-urban Malawi and analyzed the 99 samples for 20 common enteric pathogens via multiplex quantitative reverse transcription PCR. Using logistic regression adjusted for household population, latrine sharing, the presence of a concrete floor or slab, water source, and anal cleansing materials, we found no significant difference in the odds of detecting the 20 pathogens from the mid-point (adjusted odds ratio, aOR = 1.1; 95% confidence interval = 0.73, 1.6) and surface samples (aOR = 0.80, 95% CI = 0.54, 1.2) compared with those samples taken from the maximum depth. Our results suggest that, for the purposes of routine pathogen monitoring, pit latrine sampling depth does not strongly influence the odds of detecting enteric pathogens by molecular methods. A single sample from the pit latrines’ surface, or a composite of surface samples, may be preferred as the most recent material contributed to the pit and may be easiest to collect.

title: The Establishment and Validation of the Human U937 Cell Line as a Cellular Model to Screen Immunomodulatory Agents Regulating Cytokine Release Induced by Influenza Virus Infection
abstract: This study presents the establishment and validation of the Human U937 cell line as a cellular model to screen immunomodulatory agents regulating cytokine release induced by influenza virus infection. The aim of this work was to evaluate whether U937 cells, activated with a combination of phorbol-12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) and ionomycin (Io), could be used in vitro as a tool for high throughput screening, providing evidence on identifying modulators acting in cellular metabolism following stimulation with an Influenza Virus Infection. For validating their functional response profile compared to PBMCs from healthy volunteers, both cell types were stimulated by PR8 strain of influenza virus A/Aichi/2/68 (H3N2). The results indicated that U937 clones uniformly expressed proinflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, IL1βand IL6 after viral challenge comparable with PBMCs from three independent donors. Moreover miRNA profiling suggested common patterns between both tested cell types being MIR424 iMIR200a upregulated. Ultimately these studies demonstrate that Human U937 can reproduce leukocyte functions upon stimulation when challenged with an acutely cytocidal agent like influenza viruses thereby confirming its suitability for identification and development of novel strategies against infectious diseases due to its ability to serve as surrogate system reducing time and costs while improving efficacy when it comes providing information regarding drug candidates effectiveness before testing them in animal models or clinical trials.

title: Six-minute walking test in children with ESRD: discrimination validity and construct validity
abstract:
The purpose of this paper is to assess the validity of using a Six-minute Walking Test (6MWT) in children with End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD). This study aims to evaluate medical research data which demonstrate the discrimination, criterion and construct validity for the 6MWT in measuring physical function over time for pediatric patients suffering from ESRD. Through a review of relevant literature, evaluation instruments and questionnaires, reliability testing was conducted among 30 children being treated at an acute care hospital. A range of demographic variables were taken into consideration along with potential confounding factors such as age, gender and prior monitoring tests results. The results concluded that although there were variations that influence levels of performance across different 6MWT studies due to differing methods used by each investigator; overall it represented good test/retest reliability leading to high discrimination and construct validations. This suggests that an accurate assessment can be made regarding progression or regression in activity through repeat trials amongst patients dealing with ESRD making this method suitable for long term tracking when combined with other dimensions such as diet and lifestyle choices.

title: Rab5-mediated VE-cadherin internalization regulates the barrier function of the lung microvascular endothelium
abstract: This study examines the role of Rab5-mediated VE-cadherin internalization in regulating the barrier function of lung microvascular endothelial cells (MVECs). The current understanding is that cadherins are adhesion molecules, important for intercellular junctions and maintaining cell–cell contacts. Disruption of these molecules consequently results in altered physiological processes including transendothelial permeability and impairment of vascular homeostasis. Additionally, aberrant uptake or trafficking of junctional proteins can also lead to abnormal interendothelial tightness. Here, we demonstrate how Rab5-encoded GTPases and its effector have an impact on VE-cadherin dynamics with downstream effects on MVEC paracellular transport. Employing in vitro time lapse imaging protocols and immunocytochemistry along with electrophysiology approaches, this work shows that Rab5 activity impacts the membrane localization at adherens junctions leading to changes in transepithelial ion fluxes responsible for controlling tissue barrier properties. Ultimately these findings provide new insights into appropriate therapeutic interventions aimed at improving endothelium health particularly targeting increased metabolic compartmentalization within MVECs  as a novel strategy against barriers malfunctions associated with pulmonary diseases like bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) .

title: Human Ebola virus infection in West Africa: a review of available therapeutic agents that target different steps of the life cycle of Ebola virus
abstract: The recent outbreak of the human Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) epidemic is spiraling out of control in West Africa. Human EBOV hemorrhagic fever has a case fatality rate of up to 90%. The EBOV is classified as a biosafety level 4 pathogen and is considered a category A agent of bioterrorism by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with no approved therapies and vaccines available for its treatment apart from supportive care. Although several promising therapeutic agents and vaccines against EBOV are undergoing the Phase I human trial, the current epidemic might be outpacing the speed at which drugs and vaccines can be produced. Like all viruses, the EBOV largely relies on host cell factors and physiological processes for its entry, replication, and egress. We have reviewed currently available therapeutic agents that have been shown to be effective in suppressing the proliferation of the EBOV in cell cultures or animal studies. Most of the therapeutic agents in this review are directed against non-mutable targets of the host, which is independent of viral mutation. These medications are approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of other diseases. They are available and stockpileable for immediate use. They may also have a complementary role to those therapeutic agents under development that are directed against the mutable targets of the EBOV. ELECTRONIC SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: The online version of this article (doi:10.1186/2049-9957-3-43) contains supplementary material, which is available to authorized users.

title: Interferon Lambda: Opportunities, Risks, and Uncertainties in the Fight Against HCV
abstract: Innate immunity is key to the fight against the daily onslaught from viruses that our bodies are subjected to. Essential to this response are the interferons (IFNs) that prime our cells to block viral pathogens. Recent evidence suggests that the Type III (λ) IFNs are intimately associated with the immune response to hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. Genome-wide association studies have identified polymorphisms within the IFN-λ gene locus that correlate with response to IFNα-based antiviral therapy and with spontaneous clearance of HCV infection. The mechanisms for these correlations are incompletely understood. Restricted expression of the IFN-λ receptor, and the ability of IFN-λ to induce IFN-stimulated genes in HCV-infected cells, suggest potential roles for IFN-λ in HCV therapy even in this era of directly acting antivirals. This review summarizes our current understanding of the IFN-λ family and the role of λ IFNs in the natural history of HCV infection.

title: Design and Synthesis of Multi-Functional Superparamagnetic Core-Gold Shell Nanoparticles Coated with Chitosan and Folate for Targeted Antitumor Therapy
abstract: Intensifying the effects of chemotherapy treatments in cancer therapy has become a major focus within medical research. This has encouraged vigorous studies into the implementation of nanotechnology advancements and new drug delivery systems, both of which are essential elements for effective targeted antitumor therapies. This study focused on designing and synthesizing multifunctional superparamagnetic core-gold shell nanoparticles coated with chitosan and folate (MFGNPs) to create a safe, noninvasive method for administering these drugs at tumor sites. With potent cytotoxicity confirmed against tumor cells such as HeLa and MCF-7 cell lines, our experiments achieved positive results that declared MFGNPs to be effective agents in anti-cancer treatments. Successful outcomes could pave the way towards more advances within medical science that can eventually provide better outcomes in treating neoplasms with minimized damage to healthy tissue or organs associated with traditional surgery methods.

title: Identification of type-specific and cross-reactive neutralizing conformational epitopes on the major capsid protein of human papillomavirus type 31
abstract: This abstract presents a landmark study that identified specific neutralizing epitopes on the major capsid protein of human papillomavirus (HPV) type 31. By employing cutting-edge methods, a panel of 21 serum samples from patients infected with HPV type 31 were analyzed to differentiate between conformational epitopes and cross-reactivity with other HPV types. Our results uncovered three previously unrecognized immunogenic domains within the HPV-31 capsid protein that could form an informational basis for antigenic analysis in future vaccine design strategies against this virus subtype. These findings will prove invaluable in helping allocate resources toward developing vaccines targeting both type-specific and distinguished common antigens across HPVs to prevent infection among at risk populations worldwide.

title: A Method to Identify p62's UBA Domain Interacting Proteins
abstract: The UBA domain is a conserved sequence motif among polyubiquitin binding proteins. For the first time, we demonstrate a systematic, high throughput approach to identification of UBA domain-interacting proteins from a proteome-wide perspective. Using the rabbit reticulocyte lysate in vitro expression cloning system, we have successfully identified eleven proteins that interact with p62’s UBA domain, and the majority of the eleven proteins are associated with neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease. Therefore, p62 may play a novel regulatory role through its UBA domain. Our approach provides an easy route to the characterization of UBA domain interacting proteins and its application will unfold the important roles that the UBA domain plays.

title: Unraveling the deep learning gearbox in optical coherence tomography image segmentation towards explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of advancements in deep learning-based optical coherence tomography (OCT) image segmentation for explainable artificial intelligence (AI). This analysis comes amidst ongoing discussions on the usage and interpretation of complex AI models, the need for interpretability has gained momentum. To this end, elaborate exploration into leveraging various facets of OCT to accurately detect abnormalities through an effective automated solution is necessary. A novel approach will be taken by examining different aspects of deformable convolutional networks with addition layers dedicated to handling illumination artifacts and improving texture features from gray-scale OCT images. Lastly, a dataset with pathological biomolecular rules will be used as metrics to adequately train the model while methods like importance scoring and adversarial removal sampling strategies are explored to enable better understanding at both global and local levels. Results suggest viable solutions that prioritize pathologic tissue segmentation clarity while enhancing pre-existing components towards attaining maximum interpretability thus further augmenting applications of this technology in healthcare sciences

title: Nogo-B protects mice against lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute lung injury (ALI) is a deadly, yet common phenomenon in mammals. In this study, we investigate the protective effects of Nogo-B in mice to LPS-induced ALI. Our results demonstrated that Nogo-B blocked the inflammatory response and oxidative destruction caused by LPS inhalation via its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties respectively; thus reducing mortality rate significantly compared to the control group. Furthermore, this paper presents information on how modulating key molecules between inflammation and oxidative damage has potential therapeutic implications for treating ALI caused by environmental toxins including airborne pollutants such as smoke particles. This research provides preclinical evidence that promoting the expression of Nogo Receptor B improves pulmonary function thereby decreasing mortality due to severe lung diseases in natural or artificially induced conditions. Such outcomes imply a promising future for treating ALI cases with drugs targeting critical pathways involved in cellular protection against toxic insults which are dysregulated during inflammation and free radical generation.

title: Genomic diversity of Escherichia coli isolates from backyard chickens and guinea fowl in the Gambia
abstract: This paper examines the genomic diversity of Escherichia coli (E. coli) isolates found in backyard chickens and guinea fowls kept in The Gambia, a low-income country located on the west coast of Africa. The recent emergence of antimicrobial resistant E. coli poses a serious risk to animal health leading to increased morbidity and mortality among both human and animal populations, although limited studies have been conducted describing these strains for this region. Genomic sequencing was performed using isolate samples from six flocks, five chicken caged farms and one village based flock with an average sample size of 15 colonies per site obtained from cloacal swabs collected across three seasons between 2015–2017.. Results showed that 78 distinct multilocus sequence types (STs) were identified out of the total 112 E. coli isolates analysed by multi locus sequence typing PCR assays combined with phylogenetic analyses  showing high genetic diversity amongst bacterial taxa colonization multiple avian hosts from backyard poultry reared under different environmental conditions in The Gambia. This study provides new insights into important aspects such as how host behavior affects disease transmission amongst local domesticated animals as well as public health significance associated with interactions between humans diseased livestock at community level in developing countries likeThe Gambia

title: Apoptosis in brain-specific autoimmune disease
abstract: This scientific journal article investigates the role of apoptosis in brain-specific autoimmune disease. Autoimmune diseases are characterised by an immune system response against endogenous molecules, resulting in inflammation around affected areas and potential tissue damage. Recent studies have suggested that a particular subset of these conditions – brain-specific autoantibodies – cause neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment by triggering an increased rate of cell death via apoptosis in neural tissues. To explore this hypothesis, we will utilise experimental techniques such as immunohistochemistry, Western Blotting, flow cytometry and ELISA to analyse the effects of cytokine release on the regulation of programmed cell death pathways specifically in the context of including different concentrations for various autoantibody types. Our goal is to contribute new insights into understanding how autoimmune pathogenesis may affect neuronal health under varying physiological environments.

title: Current Status of the Immunomodulation and Immunomediated Therapeutic Strategies for Multiple Sclerosis
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the current status of immunomodulatory and immunomediated therapeutic strategies for treating Multiple Sclerosis (MS). An in-depth review is provided on the physiological principles and mechanisms underlying cognitive, physical, sensory and neurobehavioral changes resulting from dysregulation of the immune system. The complex network of interactions between host immunity, inflammation, axonal damage and remyelination are explored. Furthermore, current trends in research to develop novel classes of drugs targeting myeloid cells as well as reprogramming lymphocyte's activity through modulation of signalling pathways is evaluated. Recent progress made in optimizing these new therapies is critically discussed with a focus on safety parameters such as long term effects and possible side effects due to prolonged use. Emerging treatment regimens designed to target lifestyle related traits shared by individuals living with MS are also addressed along with potential future directions for combatting this disabling condition.

title: Comparative Analysis of Host Cell Entry of Ebola Virus From Sierra Leone, 2014, and Zaire, 1976
abstract: The ongoing Ebola virus (EBOV) disease (EVD) epidemic in Western Africa is the largest EVD outbreak recorded to date and requires the rapid development and deployment of antiviral measures. The viral glycoprotein (GP) facilitates host cell entry and, jointly with cellular interaction partners, constitutes a potential target for antiviral intervention. However, it is unknown whether the GPs of the currently and previously circulating EBOVs use the same mechanisms for cellular entry and are thus susceptible to inhibition by the same antivirals and cellular defenses. Here, we show that the GPs of the EBOVs circulating in 1976 and 2014 transduce the same spectrum of target cells, use the same cellular factors for host cell entry, and are comparably susceptible to blockade by antiviral interferon-induced transmembrane proteins and neutralizing antibody KZ52. Thus, the viruses responsible for the ongoing EVD epidemic should be fully susceptible to established antiviral strategies targeting GP and cellular entry factors.

title: Humanized Mice for Live-Attenuated Vaccine Research: From Unmet Potential to New Promises
abstract: Live-attenuated vaccines (LAV) represent one of the most important medical innovations in human history. In the past three centuries, LAV have saved hundreds of millions of lives, and will continue to do so for many decades to come. Interestingly, the most successful LAVs, such as the smallpox vaccine, the measles vaccine, and the yellow fever vaccine, have been isolated and/or developed in a purely empirical manner without any understanding of the immunological mechanisms they trigger. Today, the mechanisms governing potent LAV immunogenicity and long-term induced protective immunity continue to be elusive, and therefore hamper the rational design of innovative vaccine strategies. A serious roadblock to understanding LAV-induced immunity has been the lack of suitable and cost-effective animal models that can accurately mimic human immune responses. In the last two decades, human-immune system mice (HIS mice), i.e., mice engrafted with components of the human immune system, have been instrumental in investigating the life-cycle and immune responses to multiple human-tropic pathogens. However, their use in LAV research has remained limited. Here, we discuss the strong potential of LAVs as tools to enhance our understanding of human immunity and review the past, current and future contributions of HIS mice to this endeavor.

title: Developmental Regulation of Angiotensinogen Gene Expression in Sheep
abstract: This study investigates the developmental regulation of angiotensinogen gene expression in sheep. Analysis was performed on RNA samples derived from sheep liver at different ages, ranging between mid-gestation and adulthood, to determine whether changes occurred in levels of specific angiotensinogen transcripts over development. Results indicate that all investigated stages showed differential expression of some isoforms but significant differences were apparent only in comparison between birth and adulthood. Expression patterns of postnatal hepatic angiotensinogen mRNAs revealed dramatic age-dependent increases around parturition which appeared to be largely driven by transcription factor APF1/Sp3 activity. The results demonstrated ontogenic sensitivity to Sp3 occupancy during development may underlie large increases observed during early postnatal life and point towards a role for APF1/Sp3 regulating tissue-specific gene expression processes related to Ang II production with potential implications for homeostasis maintenance.

title: Brain abscess in seven cats due to a bite wound: MRI findings, surgical management and outcome
abstract: PRESENTATION AND LESION LOCALISATION: Seven adult domestic shorthair cats were presented with a 1- to 6-day history of progressive neurological signs. A focal skin puncture and subcutaneous swelling over the dorsal part of the head were detected on physical examination. Neurological examination indicated lesion(s) in the right forebrain in four cats, multifocal forebrain in one cat, left forebrain in one cat, and multifocal forebrain and brainstem in the remaining cat. In all cats, magnetic resonance imaging revealed a space-occupying forebrain lesion causing a severe mass effect on adjacent brain parenchyma. CLINICAL APPROACH AND OUTCOME: All cats were managed with a combination of medical and surgical treatment. At surgery a small penetrating calvarial fracture was detected in all cats, and a tooth fragment was found within the content of the abscess in two cats. The combination of surgical intervention, intensive care and intravenous antimicrobials led to a return to normal neurological function in five cats. PRACTICAL RELEVANCE: As this series of cases indicates, successful resolution of a brain abscess due to a bite injury depends on early recognition and combined used of antimicrobials and surgical intervention. A particular aim of surgery is to remove any skull and foreign body (tooth) fragments that may represent a continuing focus of infection.

title: Treatment Options for Motor and Non-Motor Symptoms of Parkinson’s Disease
abstract:
This paper presents an overview into the current treatment landscape for motor and non-motor symptoms of Parkinson’s Disease. Despite the complexity associated with treating these symptoms, research continues to expand and provide clinicians with scientifically supported therapies for this debilitating condition. Drawing attention to the advances made in using new medications, medical devices and physical interventions such as deep brain stimulation, this article reviews the advantages and disadvantages of each treatment strategy. Additionally, contributing factors including delayed diagnosis, patient adherence to techniques and lifestyle management are discussed in depth. By reviewing existing literature in keeping up with developments within this field of research, it is hoped that patients will have greater access to evidence-based treatments capable of improving their long term quality of life when suffering with Parkinson’s Disease.

title: Vaccines for caseous lymphadenitis: up-to-date and forward-looking strategies
abstract: This paper aims to provide an in-depth review of the available vaccines for caseous lymphadenitis. With up-to-date information on anti-CL strategies that have been used historically and currently, as well as a forward-looking outlook on potential new direction should highlight any discoveries, this document provides valuable insight for those in the medical field about the current state of vaccine research for this condition. Research data sourced from international journals and opinions from knowledgeable practitioners both within and outside academia provide critical perspectives from all angles of enquiry surrounding CL vaccination. The ultimate goal is to form strategic directions that tap into rapidly changing science and technology to help inform future decisions regarding improved methods to limit or eradicate caseous lymphadenitis infection levels. This document offers a comprehensive review ensuring readers are kept abreast with key developments relating to existing and upcoming medications when it comes implementing effective approaches against this contagious disease.

title: Structure of the type VI secretion system TssK–TssF–TssG baseplate subcomplex revealed by cryo-electron microscopy
abstract: Type VI secretion systems (T6SSs) translocate effectors into target cells and are made of a contractile sheath and a tube docked onto a multi-protein transmembrane complex via a baseplate. Although some information is available about the mechanisms of tail contraction leading to effector delivery, the detailed architecture and function of the baseplate remain unknown. Here, we report the 3.7 Å resolution cryo-electron microscopy reconstruction of an enteroaggregative Escherichia coli baseplate subcomplex assembled from TssK, TssF and TssG. The structure reveals two TssK trimers interact with a locally pseudo-3-fold symmetrical complex comprising two copies of TssF and one copy of TssG. TssF and TssG are structurally related to each other and to components of the phage T4 baseplate and of the type IV secretion system, strengthening the evolutionary relationships among these macromolecular machines. These results, together with bacterial two-hybrid assays, provide a structural framework to understand the T6SS baseplate architecture.

title: Potential biomarkers of immune protection in human leishmaniasis
abstract: This study seeks to uncover potential biomarkers of immune protection in human leishmaniasis. Leishmaniasis is a tropical infection caused by the parasite Leishmania, spread through the bite of an infected sandfly. The second most common parasitic vector-borne infectious disease after malaria, it affects both humans and animals with some species causing severe disfigurement from lesions on the face and limbs. After decades of research, there are still gaps in our understanding as to why certain individuals develop immunity to prevent or control this infection whereas others do not. This review will discuss recent advances in progress made towards identifying potential biomarkers for predicting susceptibility or level of protection against leishmaniasis epidemics among at-risk populations worldwide. title: Viral-associated Ventilator-associated Pneumonia
abstract: This article is a comprehensive review of research studies on the topic of viral-associated ventilator-associated pneumonia. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is one of the most common complications among patients receiving mechanical ventilation in intensive care units, and its etiology involves multiple viral pathogens as well as bacteria. Studies show that both bacterial and viral infections contribute to morbidity and mortality outcomes for VAP; however, there has been little exploration into how these agents interact during VAP development. This article discusses recent advances in our understanding of the interaction between virus infection and VAP progression, identifying areas for future research geared towards ameliorating clinical effects due to this silent killer.

title: Factors associated with development of early and late pulmonary hypertension in preterm infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with the development of early and late pulmonary hypertension (PH) in preterm infants diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Preterm babies are especially susceptible to BPD, yet little is known about its long-term impacts. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify factors that may contribute to the development of PH among these preterm infants with BPD. In total, 9 studies were included meeting the inclusion criteria; 7 observational cohort studies and 2 case­control studies were analyzed for evidences regarding risk factors for early (<2 weeks postnatal age) or late (>2 weeks postnatal age) onset of PH in these populations. Factors related to antenatal characteristics, delivery complications and neonatal management/postnatal care were assessed together with adjusted risk estimates from each study provided where possible. Results from our analysis suggest important implications for clinical practice when managing high-risk pregnancies involving preterm babies who might develop BPD in future.

title: Hybrid Basketball Game Outcome Prediction Model by Integrating Data Mining Methods for the National Basketball Association
abstract: The sports market has grown rapidly over the last several decades. Sports outcomes prediction is an attractive sports analytic challenge as it provides useful information for operations in the sports market. In this study, a hybrid basketball game outcomes prediction scheme is developed for predicting the final score of the National Basketball Association (NBA) games by integrating five data mining techniques, including extreme learning machine, multivariate adaptive regression splines, k-nearest neighbors, eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and stochastic gradient boosting. Designed features are generated by merging different game-lags information from fundamental basketball statistics and used in the proposed scheme. This study collected data from all the games of the NBA 2018–2019 seasons. There are 30 teams in the NBA and each team play 82 games per season. A total of 2460 NBA game data points were collected. Empirical results illustrated that the proposed hybrid basketball game prediction scheme achieves high prediction performance and identifies suitable game-lag information and relevant game features (statistics). Our findings suggested that a two-stage XGBoost model using four pieces of game-lags information achieves the best prediction performance among all competing models. The six designed features, including averaged defensive rebounds, averaged two-point field goal percentage, averaged free throw percentage, averaged offensive rebounds, averaged assists, and averaged three-point field goal attempts, from four game-lags have a greater effect on the prediction of final scores of NBA games than other game-lags. The findings of this study provide relevant insights and guidance for other team or individual sports outcomes prediction research.

title: Assay for screening for six antimalarial drugs and one metabolite using dried blood spot sampling, sequential extraction and ion-trap detection
abstract:
This paper presents the development of a novel assay and methodology for screening six antimalarial drugs, artemether (AM), arthemisinin (AH) and its metabolite dihydroarthemisinin (DHA), lumefantrine (LF), sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) and piperaquines Tartrate in dried blood spot sampling. The assay was conducted using sequential extraction followed by ion-trap detection. 
The rationale for designing this method originates from research into malaria diagnosis which has demonstrated that DBS offers certain advantages over venous blood samples such as less pain to the patient and better transportation opportunities making it more suitable for developing countries with limited resources. Therefore, assays developed based on DBS could potentially provide greater accessibility to quality healthcare services related to malaria diagnosis. 
The study evaluated the extraction performance of buffer solution in terms of 90% limit of detection for each drug compound under particle assisted liquid–liquid microextraction technique before it is combined with LC/MS analysis using an ion trap mass spectrometer detection system at an optimized pH value ranging between 5 – 7 obtained through spiked samples exploration. Results are expected to significantly impact the current methodological practices involved in conducting mass screenings within developing nations where malaria poses a high risk health problem among populations living in rural areas thus providing essential antimalarial treatment support especially during public health outbreaks in resource deprived settings.

title: Advancing UK Regulatory Science Strategy in the Context of Global Regulation: a Stakeholder Survey
abstract:
In the United Kingdom, recent discussions have focused on how advances in regulatory science can help meet the challenges posed by global regulations. This paper presents a stakeholder survey’s results in order to investigate current UK approaches for advancing regulatory science strategies amidst an evolving international regulatory framework. The survey, comprising interviews of 12 stakeholders from across four sectors (academia, industry, government and health), was conducted to assess opinions and experiences regarding the potential of a more integrated approach towards tackling global regulation with greater emphasis on progress from internal UK resources. 

The study identified three main areas which were important when considering implementation of future advancements in this field: 1) collaboration between government institutions and external stakeholders; 2) education/ training opportunities tailored to specific regulatory science needs; 3) developing existing or creating new initiatives that facilitate an increased span between academic initiatives and public policy priorities informed by effective stakeholder engagement mechanisms. By analysing these findings within their socio-political context it is possible to gain clarity into how innovation may drive change through improved regulatory science strategies aimed at balancing long-term market investments with societal requirements. 

Overall, this paper provides useful insight around adapting existing governance structures so as to move forward indispensable technological advancement whilst ensuring careful consideration remains at the core of all policy making decisions especially when it comes to matters that invoke national security concerns where traditional methods are no longer suitable. It is hoped ‘Advancing UK Regulatory Science Strategy in the Context of Global Regulation: A Stakeholder Survey’ will offer relevant recommendations about novel measures for development during difficult times propelled by rapid transformation instigated both domestically and internationally..

abstract: This study explores the efficacy of screening for gastric cancer in Japan. title: Cause and predictors of neonatal mortality among neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units of public hospitals in eastern Ethiopia: a facility-based prospective follow-up study
abstract: BACKGROUND: The first month is the most crucial period for child survival. Neonatal mortality continues to remain high with little improvement over the years in Sub-Saharan Africa, including Ethiopia. This region shows the least progress in reducing neonatal mortality and continues to be a significant public health issue. In this study setting, the causes and predictors of neonatal death in the neonatal intensive care units are not well documented. Hence, this study aimed to determine the causes and predictors of neonatal mortality among infants admitted to neonatal intensive care units in eastern Ethiopia. METHODS: A facility-based in prospective follow-up study was conducted among neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units of public hospitals of eastern Ethiopia from November 1 to December 30, 2018. Data were collected using a pre-tested structured questionnaire and a follow-up checklist. The main outcomes and causes of death were set by pediatricians and medical residents. EpiData 3.1 and Statistical Package for Social Sciences Version 25 software were used for data entry and analysis, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify the predictors of facility-based neonatal mortality. RESULTS: The proportion of facility-based neonatal mortality was 20% (95% CI:16.7–23.8%). The causes of death were complications of preterm birth (28.58%), birth asphyxia (22.45%), neonatal infection (18.36%), meconium aspiration syndrome (9.18%), respiratory distress syndrome (7.14%), and congenital malformation (4.08%). Low birth weight, preterm births, length of stay of the neonatal intensive care unit, low 5 min APGAR score, hyperthermia, and initiation of feeding were predictors of neonatal death among infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care units of public hospitals in eastern Ethiopia. CONCLUSIONS: The proportion of facility-based neonatal deaths was unacceptably high. The main causes of death were preventable and treatable. Hence, improving the timing and quality of antenatal care is essential for early detection, anticipating high-risk newborns, and timely interventions. Furthermore, early initiation of feeding and better referral linkage to tertiary health facilities could lead to a reduction in neonatal death in this setting.
