title: The effect of dexamethasone-induced immunosuppression on the development of faecal antibody and recovery from and resistance to rotavirus infection
abstract: The title of this study is 'The Effect of Dexamethasone-Induced Immunosuppression on the Development of Faecal Antibody and Recovery from and Resistance to Rotavirus Infection'. Rotavirus is an enteric pathogen responsible for severe diarrhoea in children lacking effective immunisation, presenting a significant burden around the world. The current study aimed to investigate if dexamethasone-induced immunosuppression impacts faecal antibody levels, recovery from rotaviral infection, and protection against re-infection with rotavirus. Utilising a murine model, rodents were administered dexamethasone prior to screening for fecal antibodies specific to the common P[8] strain of group A rotaviruses. Results revealed that animals exposed both pretreatment with dexamethasone showed significantly reduced concentrations in serum and faeces IgA levels compared with control groups. Furthermore post treatment; animals did not demonstrate clear evidence of either increased susceptibility or resistance towards reinfestation by P[8]. This suggests that while down regulation may reduce mucosal intake vaccine antibody titres; environmental exposures may be impacted primarily as a result alteration local milieu influences during bouts symptomatic disease rather than through initiation primary immune response or impact innate protection barriers. Collectively these findings suggest further studies into how prednisolonemia alters host defence mechanisms in infectious gastroenteritis should be investigated more fully if therapeutic strategies based upon modulating inflammatory responses are pursued as viable measures combating existing enteropathogens within human populations

title: Prospective epidemiological study of common colds and secretory otitis media
abstract: This study aims to investigate common colds and their association with secretory otitis media. Recent evidence has suggested that infection with a member of the coronavirus family, Characterized as upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs), might be a risk-factor for both common colds and secretory otitis media among children aged from 2-5 years old in particular. The purpose of this prospective epidemiological study is to determine the strength between URIs and the development or exacerbation of either condition in population samples aged from 2-5 years old within two geographically distinct regions over a pre-defined time period. This paper presents a systematic review assessing existing data sources pertaining to URTIs, common colds and secretory otitis media including demographic information, primary medical records focusing on recent exposure to viral agents correlated with these conditions are considered as part fo our hypothesis testing procedure.

title: What about lay counselors’ experiences of task-shifting mental health interventions? Example from a family-based intervention in Kenya
abstract: This article explores the experience of lay counselors in task-shifting mental health interventions. A qualitative study from a family-based intervention within Kenya was conducted to investigate this phenomenon, with data collected through semi-structured interviews and field observations. Findings suggest that lay counselors have positive experiences with task-shifting mental health interventions, although varying levels of knowledge and comfortability towards the practice exist among them. As potential pitfalls are identified which must be addressed for successful implementation as well as improved patient outcomes. These results not only provide new insights into existing supportive services in developing countries but also inform policy makers on how to effectively respond to increasing demands for accessible health care at lower levels of cost both domestically and internationally.. Additionally, conclusions presented herein lay out areas where further research may be required in order to expand the evidence base concerning alternative provisions for mental health treatments globally.

title: Organic Cation Transporters in the Lung—Current and Emerging (Patho)Physiological and Pharmacological Concepts
abstract: Organic cation transporters (OCT) 1, 2 and 3 and novel organic cation transporters (OCTN) 1 and 2 of the solute carrier 22 (SLC22) family are involved in the cellular transport of endogenous compounds such as neurotransmitters, l-carnitine and ergothioneine. OCT/Ns have also been implicated in the transport of xenobiotics across various biological barriers, for example biguanides and histamine receptor antagonists. In addition, several drugs used in the treatment of respiratory disorders are cations at physiological pH and potential substrates of OCT/Ns. OCT/Ns may also be associated with the development of chronic lung diseases such as allergic asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and, thus, are possible new drug targets. As part of the Special Issue “Physiology, Biochemistry and Pharmacology of Transporters for Organic Cations”, this review provides an overview of recent findings on the (patho)physiological and pharmacological functions of organic cation transporters in the lung.

title: Bioorganometallic Chemistry and Malaria
abstract: This article focuses on the fundamental mechanisms behind bioorganometallic chemistry and its potential application in combating malaria. Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, resulting in an estimated 219 million cases yearly with particularly disproportionate effects in certain parts of the world. In recent years, research has emerged regarding organometallic compounds as candidates for antimalarial drugs due to their stability and broader target spectra when compared to organic molecules. The present document synthesizes this multidisciplinary body of literature and provides further insights into how bioorganometallics could be utilized to battle against one of humanity's oldest foes.

title: Angiogenin and tRNA fragments in Parkinson’s disease and neurodegeneration
abstract: This study presents the results of an investigation into the potential role that angiogenin and tRNA fragments can play in Parkinson’s disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. Recent advances in our understanding of transcriptome variability have illuminated a complex network of interactions between molecules, pathways, environmental factors, and genetic predispositions; this research explores how angiogenin and its downstream effector - tRNA fragmenst - may contribute to these disorders. We examined gene expression levels related to inflammation, oxidative stress, amyloid deposition, enzyme activity regulation and apoptosis of different brain regions affected by neurodegeneration to examine their correlation with angiogenic activity. Results showed that changes in angiogenin levels were associated with significant decreases in certain enzymes involved in neuronal cell death mechanisms as well as notable increases in inflammatory markers which are known precursors for progression Parkinson's symptoms. These findings demonstrate a possible link between modulation of these biomolecules within the aging brain culminating on increased risk for macroscopic tissue injury during development or manifestation stages from chronic neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's.

title: ExoU-induced redox imbalance and oxidative stress in airway epithelial cells during Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumosepsis
abstract: This paper investigates the molecular mechanism underlying the role of the virulence factor ExoU in Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumosepsis and how it induces redox imbalance and oxidative stress in airway epithelial cells. Recent studies have suggested that this pathogen is associated with altered redox homeostasis, which can lead to cellular damage if not efficiently counteracted. In order to elucidate how ExoU mediates its effects on host cells, and further understand a possible contribution of oxidative stress in P. aeruginosa-induced diseases, cytotoxicity measurements were performed by measuring levels of superoxide anion (O2•−), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) as well as markers for oxidative damage such as TBARS assay and protein carbonylation analysis. Our results indicate that exposure to ExoU leads to increased O2•− production followed by enhanced H2O2 release while also promoting formation of reactive oxygen species at increased levels compared to untreated control cells under similar culture conditions. Furthermore, treatment with N-acetylcysteine prevents or significantly lowers occurrence of both cellular injury indicators detected during exopolysaccharide stimulation indicating involvement of relieving ROS/RNS-mediated cytotoxic events by providing more reducing power into cellular environment. Thus we conclude that disruption induced by ExoU onto cell's oxidant balance indicates high susceptibility towards debilitating disease states originating from aberrant immune system responses requiring rapid action upon detection through proper adjustment strategies aimed at restoring preferred equilibrium ratio between oxidants/antioxidants required for healthy outcomes when facing potentially severe infection scenarios caused by this particular bacterium strain presenting itself within affected individual's domain.

title: Emergency treatment and nursing of children with severe pneumonia complicated by heart failure and respiratory failure: 10 case reports
abstract: This paper examines the effective strategies of emergency treatment and nursing of children with severe pneumonia complicated by heart failure and respiratory failure. 10 case reports are used to demonstrate how hospital teams were able to successfully identify appropriate treatments, provide vital nursing interventions and improve the long-term outcomes of these often critically ill patients. The findings illustrate the crucial roles that comprehensive physical examinations play in reaching an accurate diagnosis as well as their relevance for designing specialized treatment plans for children affected by a multitude of serious medical conditions. By expanding our understanding on how clinical practice can be tailored differently depending on individualized criteria, this research offers important guidance on establishing improved care protocols for pediatric patients worldwide who present symptoms of severe pneumonia, congestive heart or respiratory failure.

title: Methods for studying naturally occurring human pain and their analogues
abstract: Methods for investigating human pain have been developed over the last 100 years. Typically, researchers focus on people with clinical pain, or on healthy participants undergoing laboratory-controlled pain-induction techniques focussed mostly on exogenously generated skin nociception. Less commonly investigated are acute pain experiences that emerge naturally. Six common painful complaints were identified: headache, muscular pain, visceral pain, menstrual pain, dental pain, and pain associated with upper respiratory tract infection. Methods used to recruit participants with the natural occurrence of each pain complaint were identified, and features of their use reviewed. Also reviewed were experimental analogues designed to mimic these pains, with the exception of menstrual pain. Headache and menstrual pain appear to be most effectively researched in their naturally occurring form, whereas muscle and dental pain may be more easily induced. Upper respiratory tract infection and abdominal pain provide further challenges for researchers. Summary guidance is offered, and directions for methods development outlined.

title: What is a Hotspot Anyway?
abstract: This article seeks to discuss the idea of 'hotspots' and why it is important to modern day data science technology. A hotspot can be defined as an area of concentrated activity, usually related with mobile area networking or where digital information exchange takes place through wireless portals. This phenomenon has gained a great amount of attention in recent times due to its relevance for numerous fields, such as cloud computing, urban planning, architecture and marketing analytics. The increasing prevalence of hotspots will have deeply profound implications for how we interact with our physical environment, creating opportunities for better understanding usage patterns that could lead to improved service provision and potentially influencing behavioural patterns in both private residential areas and public spaces. Through this study we want explore what makes up a hotspot today, identify the existing trends in their development and investigate potential future insight into their continued useability within a range of disciplines moving forward.

title: Bacteriological study of calf colisepticemia in Alage Dairy Farm, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study was designed to estimate the prevalence of E. coli which is the main cause of colisepticemia and the potential risk factors associated with the disease. A total of 74 calves less than 6 months age were selected for this study. For isolation and identification of E. coli, bacterial culture and biochemical tests were used. RESULT: Out of 74 calves selected for this study, 6 (8.11%) were positive for septicemic E. coli. Higher prevalence of 5 (8.93%) was recorded in Holstein Friesian breed than Boran breed 1 (5.56%). However, breed showed no significant difference on E. coli infections (P > 0.05). Higher prevalence of E. coli revealed below age of 30 days (17.39%) than calves aged between 30 and 90 days (8.33%) and above 90 days (0.00%). However, statistical association showed no difference (P > 0.05). Parity showed a significant difference in prevalence of E. coli (P < 0.05) in which infection increased with number of parity. Sex of the animal showed no association with infection of the calves (P > 0.05). Diarrheic calves showed higher prevalence (33.3%) than non-diarrheic calves (4.62%) with strong statistical association (P < 0.05). The present study showed a high prevalence of septicemic E. coli in the farm and intervention is strongly recommended.

title: 2,500-year Evolution of the Term Epidemic
abstract: This article examines the evolution of the word epidemic over a span of 2,500 years from its Greek origin in Homer’s Iliad. Drawing on etymology, linguistics, and history this research intends to map out how the term has been used to describe epidemics across different regions throughout time. By describing changes in nomenclature within both medical and general vocabulary over this period, we will reveal why it is necessary for language use to adjust with changing circumstances. Furthermore, implications that arise regarding our current understanding of pandemics are strengthened by an overview of modern linguistic applications of 'epidemic'. Finally, conclusions drawn from this study attempt to inform doctors and policy-makers alike by contextualizing their language choices appropriately when conversing about public health threats.

title: Phylogeography of the diamond turbot (Hypsopsetta guttulata) across the Baja California Peninsula
abstract: This study investigates the phylogeography of the diamond turbot (Hypsopsetta guttulata) across the geographic extent of Baja California Peninsula, a region characterized by its profound biogeographic complexity. The aim is to explore potential genetic diversity associated with this species across relevant spatial scales and correlate it with local ecological features in order to identify possible evidence for gene flow discontinuity according to spatial distributions. This paper presents findings from an extensive sequence analysis-based phylogeographic approach, analyzing mitochondrial DNA markers as well as environmental variables data that are valuable sources of information on population-level processes. In conclusion, this new biogeographical study will improve our understanding of novel patterns governing gene development in fish inhabiting dynamic marine environments such as those found in Baja California Peninsula.

title: Modelling the Economic Impact of Reducing Loneliness in Community Dwelling Older People in England
abstract: Loneliness has been associated with poor mental health and wellbeing. In England, a 2018 national strategy on loneliness was published, and public health guidelines recommend participation in social activities. In the absence of existing economic evidence, we modelled the potential cost effectiveness of a service that connects lonely older people to social activities against no-intervention. A 5-year Markov model was constructed from a health and social care perspective. Parameters were drawn from the literature, with the intervention structure based on an existing loneliness alleviation programme implemented in several settings across England. Univariate and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were undertaken. The total expected cost per participant in the intervention group is £7131 compared to £6783 in the usual care group with 0.45 loneliness free years (LFY) gained. The incremental cost per LFY gained is £768; in the probabilistic sensitivity analysis the intervention is cost saving in 3.5% of iterations. Potentially such interventions may be cost-effective but are unlikely to be cost-saving even allowing for sustained effects and cumulative adverse health and social care events averted. Empirical studies are needed to determine the cost-effectiveness of these interventions, ideally mapping changes in loneliness to the quality of life, in order to allow the key metric in health economic studies, cost per quality adjusted life year to be estimated.

title: Applications, challenges, and needs for employing synthetic biology beyond the lab
abstract: This paper presents an overview on the current applications, challenges and needs for further exploiting synthetic biology outside of the lab. It reflects on how recent developments in the field have facilitated work out of traditional laboratory setups, especially with regard to deployment in environments such as space or disaster scenarios. Challenges like containment strategies and infrastructure considerations are discussed along with safety protocols while potential applications that would benefit from a move away from lighted labs are analyzed. Finally, commercially viable opportunities and critical needs for utilizing synthetic biology beyond classic academic domains are proposed.

title: Development of a rapid recombinase polymerase amplification assay for the detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae in whole blood
abstract: BACKGROUND: Streptococcus pneumoniae is an important cause of microbial disease in humans. The introduction of multivalent vaccines has coincided with a dramatic decrease in the number of pneumococcal-related deaths. In spite of this, at a global level, pneumococcal infection remains an important cause of death among children under 5 years of age and in adults 65 years of age or older. In order to properly manage patients and control the spread of infection, a rapid and highly sensitive diagnostic method is needed for routine implementation, especially in resource-limited regions where pneumococcal disease is most prevalent. METHODS: Using the gene encoding leader peptidase A as a molecular diagnostics target, a real-time RPA assay was designed and optimised for the detection of S. pneumoniae in whole blood. The performance of the assay was compared to real-time PCR in terms of its analytical limit of detection and specificity. The inhibitory effect of human genomic DNA on amplification was investigated. The potential clinical utility of the assay was investigated using a small number of clinical samples. RESULTS: The RPA assay has a limit of detection equivalent to PCR (4.0 and 5.1 genome equivalents per reaction, respectively) and was capable of detecting the equivalent of <1 colony forming unit of S. pneumoniae when spiked into human whole blood. The RPA assay was 100 % inclusive (38/38 laboratory reference strains and 19/19 invasive clinical isolates) and 100 % exclusive; differentiating strains of S. pneumoniae species from other viridans group streptococci, including S. pseudopneumoniae. When applied to the analysis of a small number (n = 11) of clinical samples (blood culture positive for S. pneumoniae), the RPA assay was demonstrated to be both rapid and sensitive. CONCLUSIONS: The RPA assay developed in this work is shown to be as sensitive and as specific as PCR. In terms of reaction kinetics, the RPA assay is shown to exceed those of the PCR, with the RPA running to completion in 20 minutes and capable generating a positive signal in as little as 6 minutes. This work represents a potentially suitable assay for application in point-of-care settings.

In order to properly manage patients and control the spread of infection, a rapid and highly sensitive diagnostic method is needed for routine implementation, especially in resource-limited regions where pneumococcal disease is most prevalent. METHODS: Using the gene encoding leader peptidase A as a molecular diagnostics target, a real-time RPA assay was designed and optimised for the detection of S. pneumoniae in whole blood. The performance of the assay was compared to real-time PCR in terms of its analytical limit of detection and specificity. The inhibitory effect of human genomic DNA on amplification was investigated. The potential clinical utility of the assay was investigated using a small number of clinical samples. RESULTS: The RPA assay has a limit of detection equivalent to PCR (4.0 and 5.1 genome equivalents per reaction, respectively) and was capable of detecting the equivalent of <1 colony forming unit of S. pneumoniae when spiked into human whole blood. The RPA assay was 100 % inclusive (38/38 laboratory reference strains and 19/19 invasive clinical isolates) and 100 % exclusive; differentiating strains of S. pneumoniae species from other viridans group streptococci, including S. pseudopneumoniae. When applied to the analysis of a small number (n = 11) of clinical samples (blood culture positive for S. pneumoniae), the RPA assay was demonstrated to be both rapid and sensitive. CONCLUSIONS: The RPA assay developed in this work is shown to be as sensitive and as specific as PCR. In terms of reaction kinetics, the RPA assay is shown to exceed those of the PCR, with the RPA running to completion in 20 minutes and capable generating a positive signal in as little as 6 minutes. This work represents a potentially suitable assay for application in point-of-care settings.

title: Remote monitoring of chronic heart failure patients: invasive versus non-invasive tools for optimising patient management
abstract: This paper examines the efficacy of invasive and non-invasive tools for remote monitoring of chronic heart failure patients, evaluating their impact on patient management. An increasing number of physicians are realising that regular monitoring not only improves long-term prognosis but also allows for better control over symptoms as well as improved medication use. Studies have revealed that remote monitoring holds a significant potential to improve clinical outcomes in this population, with certain technologies offering more reliable results than others. In particular, we compare the accuracy and efficiency associated with invasive versus non-invasive tools used in such activities, considering factors like cost effectiveness and convenience. Supervised by both medical professionals and care providers alike, the selected strategies were tested on an extensive sample group comprised mostly of WCHF (Wandering Chronic Heart Failure) patients recruited from across Europe; according to a variety of methodological characteristics including demographic information supplied voluntarily at each stage. The aim is to assess any advantages presented by technological advances when it comes to managing patients remotely who suffer from chronic heart failure conditions – ultimately providing insight into which method could represent a viable solution for optimising long term treatment plans utilised by doctors around the world.

title: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase deficiencies in search of common themes
abstract: PURPOSE: Pathogenic variations in genes encoding aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) are increasingly associated with human disease. Clinical features of autosomal recessive ARS deficiencies appear very diverse and without apparent logic. We searched for common clinical patterns to improve disease recognition, insight into pathophysiology, and clinical care. METHODS: Symptoms were analyzed in all patients with recessive ARS deficiencies reported in literature, supplemented with unreported patients evaluated in our hospital. RESULTS: In literature, we identified 107 patients with AARS, DARS, GARS, HARS, IARS, KARS, LARS, MARS, RARS, SARS, VARS, YARS, and QARS deficiencies. Common symptoms (defined as present in ≥4/13 ARS deficiencies) included abnormalities of the central nervous system and/or senses (13/13), failure to thrive, gastrointestinal symptoms, dysmaturity, liver disease, and facial dysmorphisms. Deep phenotyping of 5 additional patients with unreported compound heterozygous pathogenic variations in IARS, LARS, KARS, and QARS extended the common phenotype with lung disease, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, and renal tubulopathy. CONCLUSION: We propose a common clinical phenotype for recessive ARS deficiencies, resulting from insufficient aminoacylation activity to meet translational demand in specific organs or periods of life. Assuming residual ARS activity, adequate protein/amino acid supply seems essential instead of the traditional replacement of protein by glucose in patients with metabolic diseases.

title: Identification of a novel Getah virus by Virus-Discovery-cDNA random amplified polymorphic DNA (RAPD)
abstract: This paper presents the identification of a novel Getah virus by combining PCR and Virus-Discovery-cDNA random amplified polymorphic DNA (RAPD). Recent years have seen an alarming increase in the prevalence of vector-borne diseases caused by arboviruses. Of these, Getah and its associated vector, mites, is a major health hazard of global significance. To address this challenge, we utilized Virus-Discovery-cDNA RAPD to generate cDNAs from two pools of mite species collected from various locations worldwide. These were then subjected to PCR for virus detection and subsequent cloning into plasmid vectors for further analysis. Our results revealed that one pool had significantly higher viral titers than another pool. Sequencing analyses further confirmed the presence of seven different types of Getah viruses along with full length sequences on each sample type showing considerable variation in gene organization and size suggesting distinct evolutionary pathways as well as diversity among members within each group. Altogether our findings demonstrate utilization of modern molecular techniques such as cDNA RAPD can be harnessed to detect diverse strains/variants in vitro which may aid future design strategies for rapid diagnosis and relief treatment options against emerging pestiferous arbovirus threats like Getah that threaten global public health safety standards uniformly across all nations globally.

title: Melatonin receptor agonist ramelteon attenuates mouse acute and chronic ischemic brain injury
abstract: The impact of ramelteon, a melatonin receptor agonist, on mouse models of acute and chronic ischemic brain injury was examined in this study. It has been long established that oxidative stress plays an important role in the pathology of stroke-related brain injuries; however, its potential as a therapeutic target is still uncertain. This research investigated the efficacy of using ramelteon to reduce harmful expression levels caused by intense oxygen deprivation in both subacute and sustained cerebral infarction conditions. Brain tissue samples were obtained from C57BL/6 male mice for examination under physiological parameters. Results indicated consistent protection against cerebrovascular cytotoxicity from dosing via intraperitoneal injection with near absolute attenuation at higher dosages after two weeks post-induction under subacute ischemia scenarios. Ramelteon also provided beneficial effects towards reducing apoptotic cell death when faced with severe hypoxia observed through greater neuronal preservation within cortical regions serving as a promising indication for its use as an effective neuroprotective treatment against both short-term and prolonged pathological conditions associated with neurological disorders.

title: The Impact of Nonpharmacological Interventions on Patient Experience, Opioid Use, and Health Care Utilization in Adult Cardiac Surgery Patients: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study
abstract:
Abstract:

The aim of this research is to explore the impact of nonpharmacological interventions on patient experience, opioid use, and health care utilization in adult cardiac surgery patients. To investigate this relationship a mixed methods study will be conducted consisting of quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews. Those eligible to participate are adults aged 18-90 years old who have undergone cardiac surgery at least 12 weeks prior; both preoperative and postoperative data will be gathered to compare effects within the same individual over time. The proposed design involves the development and implementation of an education program regarding self-managed strategies for mitigating pain during recovery followed by individuals completing patient satisfaction questionnaires as well as quality-of-life (QOL) assessments while using 24-hour urine collections to analyze opioid usage. Interviews with hospital staff will provide insights into changes in healthcare utilization trends based on participants’ responses or perceived improvements among observed change agents following intervention implementation since baseline measures were established. Understanding these relationships may identify potential solutions for addressing gaps in quality management systems that can help guide process improvements leading to better outcomes related to reducing opioid overdose rates from inappropriate prescribing practices or misuse among recipients following their stay inhospital care facilities.

title: Bronchial inflammation and the common cold: a comparison of atopic and non‐atopic individuals
abstract: Bronchial inflammation, spearheaded by upper respiratory infections such as the common cold, is a widespread and complex condition with interesting characteristics in atopic individuals compared to non-atopic persons. This study aimed to evaluate potential differences between these two populations regarding bronchial inflammation when triggered by viral infection. The results shown will contribute to our present understanding of this pathological state in order to develop targeted therapies directed towards its resolution. A total of 280 participants diagnosed with the common cold (at or within one week of symptom onset) were included in this prospective cohort study, stratified according to their atopy status;143 considered atopic and 137 being non‐atopic (assessed via skin prick test). Bronchial inflammation was measured using induced sputum assessment up until 14 days after symptom onset for both subgroups. Results indicated that there was no statistically significant difference between both groups concerning median levels of inflammatory markers but did display higher values for some individual components particularly related to increased necrotic debris accumulation at t=14 days among the non-atopic group. In conclusion, recipients of Upper Respiratory Infections may demonstrate distinctive immune responses indicative of varied degrees bronchial inflammation regardless of their previous sensitization from general allergies which should be taken into account when developing clinical interventions during treatment management decision making processes..

title: Structures of the four Ig-like domain LILRB2 and the four-domain LILRB1 and HLA-G1 complex
abstract: This paper examines the Structures of the four Ig-like domain LILRB2 and the four-domain LILRB1 and HLA-G1 complex. Members of the Leukocyte Immunoglobulin-Like Receptor (LIR) family regulate innate immunity via interactions with Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules. To date, several structures have been determined from this family but none have revealed details on how MHC ligands interact with their receptors. By presented herein, we provide a detailed view of two distinct members in this family, LILRB2 and LILRB1/HLA-G1 complexes, which reveal interesting features about their contacts that occur at specific sites burried between domains. In addition to identifying structurally conserved regions of contact that appear to be important for recognition events in both molecules, our results suggest how MHC binding could promote or disrupt signaling depending on its combination heterogeneity or nature as they describe various configurations observed within each ligand pair system studied here. Overall these data point towards a more complete understanding into how different families of receptors can differentiate between self vs nonself while allowing fine modulation by highly versatile modes present across complexes formed by this particular receptor -ligand combination.

title: Synthesis and Glycosidase Inhibition Properties of Calix[8]arene-Based Iminosugar Click Clusters
abstract: This paper presents the development of a new novel class of calix[8]arene-based iminosugar click clusters and their use for glycosidase inhibition. Inspired by ongoing studies in drug design, the synthesis and application of these compounds was studied to better understand their structural characteristics and inhibitory potential against carbohydrate processing enzymes. The versatility of this scaffold provides an opportunity to expand our understanding as well as potentially creating new therapeutic compounds with enhanced properties compared to what is currently available in the market. Thus, this paper seeks to investigate the synthesis process and evaluate its relevance as anti-glycosidases consisting of differentially protected sugars bound together via copper catalysed 1,3 dimethylimidazolium chemistry (CuAAC). Ultimately elucidating how this new significant structure-activity relationship can be beneficial in further drug applications.

title: Lactic Acidosis in a Newborn With Adrenal Calcifications
abstract: A patient is reported who presented in the newborn period with an unusual combination of congenital lactic acidosis and bilateral calcifications in the adrenal medulla, visible on standard abdominal x-ray and ultrasound examination. At birth, the proband was hypotonic and dystrophic. She developed respiratory insufficiency, cardiomegaly, and hepatomegaly and died at the age of 38 d. Examination of postmortem heart muscle revealed multiple areas of myocardial infarction with dystrophic calcifications. In the medulla of the adrenal glands, foci of necrosis and calcifications, and in the liver, multiple zones of necrosis and iron deposition were detected. Biochemical analysis in heart muscle revealed a decreased activity of complex IV of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and in liver a combined deficiency involving the complexes I, III, IV, and V. The findings were suggestive of a defect in biosynthesis of the mitochondrially encoded subunits of the OXPHOS complexes. Extensive analysis of the proband's mitochondrial DNA revealed neither pathogenic deletions and point mutations nor copy number alterations. Relative amounts of mitochondrial transcripts for the ribosomal mitochondrial 12S rRNA (12S) and mitochondrial 16S rRNA (16S) were significantly increased suggesting a compensatory mechanism involving the transcription machinery to low levels of translation. The underlying molecular defect has not been identified yet.

title: Influenza virus assays based on virus‐inducible reporter cell lines
abstract: The emergence of new virulent strains due to the increasing ability of influenza viruses to develop mutations has necessitated rapid and accurate assays for the detection and surveillance of these infections in both the human and animal populations. This study evaluates an innovative approach to this problem based on virus-inducible reporter cell lines (VIRCLs) that have been engineered with fluorescent protein markers which upon infection, produce a fluorescent output proportional to infecting viral titers. Results from validation experiments demonstrate that VIRCL‐based assays are highly sensitive and may offer a step change in our ability to predict accurately under real-world conditions, particularly concerning their use as a diagnostic tool or for assessing vaccine efficacy. Overall, this work demonstrates that VIRCLs provide an effective platform for quickly detecting changes in targeted pathogens, allowing us greater insight into understanding how flu vaccination strategies can be optimised within humans or animals in order to protect against rapidly evolving viral strains.

title: Inhibition of protein glycosylation is a novel pro-angiogenic strategy that acts via activation of stress pathways
abstract: Endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is thought to be one of the driving forces for angiogenesis. Here we report the identification of the hexosamine D-mannosamine (ManN) as an EC mitogen and survival factor for bovine and human microvascular EC, with an additivity with VEGF. ManN inhibits glycosylation in ECs and induces significant changes in N-glycan and O-glycan profiles. We further demonstrate that ManN and two N-glycosylation inhibitors stimulate EC proliferation via both JNK activation and the unfolded protein response caused by ER stress. ManN results in enhanced angiogenesis in a mouse skin injury model. ManN also promotes angiogenesis in a mouse hindlimb ischemia model, with accelerated limb blood flow recovery compared to controls. In addition, intraocular injection of ManN induces retinal neovascularization. Therefore, activation of stress pathways following inhibition of protein glycosylation can promote EC proliferation and angiogenesis and may represent a therapeutic strategy for treatment of ischemic disorders.

title: Inhibiting APOBEC3 Activity with Single-Stranded DNA Containing 2′-Deoxyzebularine Analogues
abstract: This article investigates an innovative approach to halt the activity of APOBEC3, a cellular protein involved in innate antiviral defense mechanisms. Our objective is to evaluate the effectiveness and specificity of single-stranded DNA containing 2′-Deoxyzebularine analogues in inhibiting APOBEC3's mutagenic effects mediated by deamination of double-stranded cytosines from genomic DNA. Using molecular dynamics simulation and enzymatic assays, we seek to identify motifs within these analogue molecules that can effectively interact with APOBEC3, possibly leading toward new design paradigms for compounds that could inhibit virus replication or gene editing. We presuppose our findings will expand current knowledge on essential biological pathways related to innate immunity as well as aid in discovering novel therapeutic strategies against cancer and viral infection.

title: Biological effects of HBV X protein on hepatocellular carcinogenesis in association with cellular factors
abstract: This study presents evidence of the biological effects of hepatitis B virus X (HBV X) protein on hepatocellular carcinogenesis in association with cellular factors. To further understand human pathways related to HBV-associated malignancies, we sought to characterize the role of this viral protein and its interactive pathway between host cell machinery. The results allowed us to gain a more thorough understanding of physiological and biochemical processes related to hepatocarcinogenesis via HBV infection, providing critical information for future preventive measures.

title: Clonal spread of multi-resistant Gallibacterium anatis isolates among Iranian broilers and layers
abstract: Gallibacterium anatis is a common cause of reproductive tract infection in chickens, which leads to reduced egg production and increased mortality. This study was undertaken to investigate prevalence of G. anatis in 12 poultry flocks originating from Iranian provinces with leading chicken production and to determine genetic diversity, antimicrobial resistance, and the presence of major antigens of the isolates investigated. Out of the 120 chicken tracheal samples collected and tested, 84 (70%) were positive for G. anatis. Genotyping by Pulse Field Gel Electrophoresis and genome sequencing revealed a total of 24 pulsotypes for 71 strains (at a 87% similarity level) and seven genome clusters comprising 21 strains (97% similarity level), respectively. The combination of the two typing methods confirmed the presence of several genotypes originating from a common ancestor affecting poultry yet also suggested that identical clones were shared among chickens within farms and between different farms. The latter finding is to our knowledge the first example of clonal presence of G. anatis in epidemiologically unrelated farms. The 21 sequenced strains were characterized against a panel of commonly used antibiotics and showed lowered sensitivity to tetracycline (76.2%) and enrofloxacin (90.5%). The widespread presence of multiresistant G. anatis isolates calls for non-antibiotic prophylactics. Three major immunogen genes, gtxA, Gab_1309 and Gab_2312 were detected in the isolates indicating these antigens likely represent effective vaccine targets. A conserved sequence of the gtxA gene across a range of epidemiologically independent strains suggests the use of GtxA for future vaccine development purposes.

title: Control of acute virus diseases of calves in the Federal Republic of Germany
abstract: This article focuses on the control of acute virus diseases of calves in the Federal Republic of Germany, providing an overview and analysis of current practices. In view of the economic importance for farmers and animal health policy makers, it explores measures taken to control viral infections by analyzing them from a historical perspective as well as by investigating their effectiveness at present. Through this systematic investigation we intend to provide valuable information as to how these diseases are addressed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

title: H2 influenza A virus is not pathogenic in Tmprss2 knock-out mice
abstract: This study investigates the pathogenic potential of H2-subtype Influenza A Virus (H2-IAV) in Tmprss2 knock-out mice. Five cohorts of animals, made up of male and female wild type and Tmprss2 knock out (KO) mice, were intranasally inoculated with a fixed dose of genetically engineered influenza virus on day 0. title: Habitat structure is more important than vegetation composition for local‐level management of native terrestrial reptile and small mammal species living in urban remnants: A case study from Brisbane, Australia
abstract: Abstract As urban areas continue to expand and replace natural and agricultural landscapes, the ability to manage and conserve native wildlife within urban environments is becoming increasingly important. To do so we first need to understand species' responses to local‐level habitat attributes in order to inform the decision‐making process and on‐ground conservation actions. Patterns in the occurrence of native terrestrial reptile and small mammal species in 59 sites located in remnant urban habitat fragments of Brisbane City were assessed against local‐level environmental characteristics of each site. Cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling ordination, and principal axis correlation were used to investigate relationships between species' occurrences and environmental characteristics. Native reptiles were most strongly associated with the presence of termite mounds, a high amount of fallen woody material, and a moderate amount of weed cover. Native small mammals were most strongly associated with the presence of grass trees (Xanthorrhoea spp.), and both reptiles and small mammals were negatively influenced by increased soil compaction. Significant floristic characteristics were considered to be important as structural, rather than compositional, habitat elements. Therefore, habitat structure, rather than vegetation composition, appears to be most important for determining native, terrestrial reptile and small mammal species assemblages in urban forest fragments. We discuss the management implications in relation to human disturbances and local‐level management of urban remnants.

title: A Clinical Bridge between Family Caregivers and Older Adults: The Contribution of Patients’ Frailty and Optimism on Caregiver Burden
abstract: The association between caregiver burden and the physical frailty of older adults has been the object of previous studies. The contribution of patients’ dispositional optimism on caregiver burden is a poorly investigated topic. The present study aimed at investigating whether older adults’ multidimensional frailty and optimism might contribute to the burden of their family caregivers. The Caregiver Burden Inventory was used to measure the care-related burden of caregivers. The multidimensional frailty status of each patient was evaluated by calculating a frailty index, and the revised Life Orientation Test was used to evaluate patients’ dispositional optimism. The study involved eighty family caregivers (mean age 64.28 ± 8.6) and eighty older patients (mean age 80.45 ± 7.13). Our results showed that higher frailty status and lower levels of optimism among patients were significantly associated with higher levels of overall burden and higher burden related to the restriction of personal time among caregivers. Patients’ frailty was additionally associated with caregivers’ greater feelings of failure, physical stress, role conflicts, and embarrassment. Understanding the close connection between patient-related factors and the burden of caregivers appears to be an actual challenge with significant clinical, social, and public health implications.

title: A Virulent PEDV Strain FJzz1 with Genomic Mutations and Deletions at the High Passage Level Was Attenuated in Piglets via Serial Passage In Vitro
abstract: Highly virulent porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) strains re-emerged and circulated in China at the end of 2010, causing significant economic losses in the pork industry worldwide. To understand the genetic dynamics of PEDV during its passage in vitro, the PEDV G2 strain FJzz1 was serially propagated in Vero cells for up to 200 passages. The susceptibility and adaptability of the FJzz1 strain increased gradually as it was serially passaged in vitro. Sequence analysis revealed that amino acid (aa) changes were mainly concentrated in the S glycoprotein, which accounted for 72.22%–85.71% of all aa changes. A continuous aa deletion ((55)I(56)G(57)E → (55)K(56)Δ(57)Δ) occurred in the N-terminal domain of S1 (S1-NTD). To examine how the aa changes affected its virulence, FJzz1-F20 and FJzz1-F200 were selected to simultaneously evaluate their pathogenicity in suckling piglets. All the piglets in the FJzz1-F20-infected group showed typical diarrhea at 24 h postinfection, and the piglets died successively by 48 h postinfection. However, the clinical signs of the piglets in the FJzz1-F200-infected group were significantly weaker, and no deaths occurred. The FJzz1-F200-infected group also showed a lower level of fecal viral shedding and lower viral loads in the intestinal tissues, and no obvious histopathological lesions. Type I and III interferon were induced in the FJzz1-F200 infection group, together with pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-8. These results indicate that the identified genetic changes may contribute to the attenuation of FJzz1 strain, and the attenuated FJzz1-F200 may have the potential for developing PEDV live-attenuated vaccines. title: Practical guide for safe central venous catheterization and management 2017
abstract: The present article provides a systematic summary of fundamental best practices for central venous catheterization and management. Clinical evidence from 2017 has been reviewed to identify current developments in the field with particular attention given to safe insertion methods and potential complications associated with use. This practical guide aims to inform healthcare providers on relevant topics such as ideal catheter selection, the significance of site marking, and tips for avoiding thermal or mechanical injury. Additionally, advanced strategies for efficient vascular access are discussed along with useful recommendations for preventing infection during catheter maintenance and removal.

title: Lyophilized Matrix Containing Ready-to-Use Primers and Probe Solution for Standardization of Real-Time PCR and RT-qPCR Diagnostics in Virology
abstract: Real-time molecular techniques have become the reference methods for direct diagnosis of pathogens. The reduction of steps is a key factor in order to decrease the risk of human errors resulting in invalid series and delayed results. We describe here a process of preparation of oligonucleotide primers and hydrolysis probe in a single tube at predefined optimized concentrations that are stabilized via lyophilization (Lyoph-P&P). Lyoph-P&P was compared versus the classic protocol using extemporaneously prepared liquid reagents using (i) sensitivity study, (ii) long-term stability at 4 °C, and (iii) long-term stability at 37 °C mimicking transportation without cold chain. Two previously published molecular assays were selected for this study. They target two emerging viruses that are listed on the blueprint of the WHO as to be considered for preparedness and response actions: chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and Rift Valley fever phlebovirus (RVFV). Results of our study demonstrate that (i) Lyoph-P&P is stable for at least 4 days at 37 °C supporting shipping without the need of cold chain, (ii) Lyoph-P&P rehydrated solution is stable at +4 °C for at least two weeks, (iii) sensitivity observed with Lyoph-P&P is at least equal to, often better than, that observed with liquid formulation, (iv) validation of results observed with low-copy specimens is rendered easier by higher fluorescence level. In conclusion, Lyoph-P&P holds several advantages over extemporaneously preparer liquid formulation that merit to be considered when a novel real-time molecular assay is implemented in a laboratory in charge of routine diagnostic activity.

abstract: We report here two genome sequences of a newly designated rhinovirus genotype, RV-C56, which were obtained from respiratory specimens of three patients with acute respiratory illness in 2016 and 2017. To our knowledge, these sequences represent the first near-complete genomes for RV-C56 strains.

title: Evidence-Based Support for Nutrition Therapy in Head and Neck Cancer
abstract: This article examines the scientific evidence for nutrition therapy for head and neck cancer (HNC). Recent research has demonstrated that appropriate dietary support and interventions can improve clinical outcomes of patients with HNC. This paper aims to review existing research on the effects of specific micronutrient supplementation, nutrient-based dietary strategies, timing of nutritional therapies and individualized patient approaches in this population. Studies focusing on individuals at a higher risk of complications or those having undergone critical treatments are particularly highlighted. Furthermore, potential implications related to these findings as well as areas requiring future investigations are discussed. The results of this analysis should provide healthcare professionals with updated evidence on maximizing both survival rates and overall quality of life for their HNC patients through nutrition-related interventions.

title: Cell type- and replication stage-specific influenza virus responses in vivo
abstract: Cell type- and replication stage-specific influenza virus responses in vivo presents the new findings of an extensive study conducted to understand the impact of host cell types and stages of viral replication on co-existing influenza viruses. This research focused on testing a range of properties, from intracellular kinetics and extracellular spreading potential via binding affinity for swine respiratory epithelial cells, using multiple infection sites at different time points within mouse models in vivo. The results demonstrate that influenza virus responses vary based upon both cell type and stage of infection. Of particular significance was the finding that nonstructural (NS) segments produce higher levels of viral replication than structural (S) or matrix segments for each microenvironment tested, which suggest S strains are more sensitive to environment changes than NS strains during growth. Overall this work provides fresh insights into how environmental context can shape influenzavirus survival strategies by affecting its entry/exit mechanisms thereby informing future studies seeking to manipulate these pathways to generate vaccine leads as well as therapeutics against emerging pandemic threats.

title: Combined Resection and Radiofrequency Ablation for Advanced Hepatic Malignancies: Results in 172 Patients
abstract: This study presents the results of combined resection and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in 172 patients with advanced hepatic malignancies. This multicenter prospective clinical trial set out to determine whether preoperative RFA provides any Inoperable/Unresectable lesions a viable treatment option, along with tumor size reduction for surgical candidates and an overall improved outcome for those undergoing surgery. Outcomes were assessed based on physical examinations, laboratory tests, computed tomography scans and pathology reports from post-operative biopsies. The author observed that significantly better long-term outcomes are achievable after combining two minimally invasive techniques:radio frequency ablation and liver tumour excision. Moreover our data suggests that this method can provide potential access to aspects of curative treatments which were unavailable due to advanced stage of disease prior to the introduction of RNA technology. Our results support evidence that RFA may be effective in triage selection as well as providing complete resectioning possibilities regardless of tumour burden thus increasing patient's possibility for Oncological cure or at least improving their prognosis when applied alone or in combination with other therapies such as chemoembolization/targeted therapy availability.

title: Efficient functional screening of a cellular cDNA library to identify severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus entry factors
abstract: The identification of host cell factors for virus entry is useful for the molecular explanation of viral tropisms and often leads to a more profound understanding of virus-induced diseases. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging infectious disease caused by SFTS virus. No countermeasures against the disease exist. In this report, we show an efficient method using virus-like particles for the functional screening of a cellular cDNA library to identify SFTS virus entry factors. Two variants encoding dendritic cell-specific ICAM-3 grabbing non-integrin related (DC-SIGNR), a calcium-dependent lectin known to enhance SFTS virus infection, were successfully identified from a human liver cDNA library. We will discuss applications for yet unidentified factor(s) for SFTS virus entry and for entry factor(s) for other viruses related to SFTS virus.

title: Angiotensin II type-1 receptor A1166C polymorphism is associated with increased risk of ischemic stroke in hypertensive smokers
abstract:
This study aims to determine the association between angiotensin II type-1 receptor A1166C single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) and ischemic stroke in hypertensive smokers. Hypertension, smoking, and genetic variations are known risk factors for cardiovascular diseases such as coronary artery disease or ischemic stroke. Despite several studies suggesting an association between gene polymorphisms of the renin-angiotensin system including angiotensinogen and angiotensin II type 1 receptors with these diseases, there are still many unknowns related to the role of these mechanisms on ischemic stroke susceptibility especially in subgroups such as smokers who have higher risks of developing this medical condition. 

In order to better understand the influence of A1166C SNP on a person's predisposition towards ischemic stroke among individuals presenting hypertension due to smoking habits, we carried out a case-control study involving two matched cohorts from four hospitals in Portugal comprising 257 subjects: 103 cases, composed by smokers diagnosed with myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accident; and 154 controls composed by non-smokers also suffering from hypertension but free from myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accidents up until sampling date. We observed that those carrying 1166CC genotype had a significantly increased odds ratio for having developed an acute ischemic event when compared with 1166AA homozygotes [OR 2.78 (95% CI 1.18–6.57); p=0.<0028]. Therefore our results suggest that A1166C polymorphism at AT1R gene might modulate risk of acute cerebral events associated with long term tobacco use in hypertensive patients highlighting its importance as predictive biomarker for this serious medical condition.

title: The M-current works in tandem with the persistent sodium current to set the speed of locomotion
abstract: The speed of locomotion is a fundamental part of the daily lives of many animals, allowing them to escape danger, forage for food and cover large distances with great efficiency. The persistent sodium current (I$_{NaP}$) has been studied for its role in regulating a variety of motor behaviors such as motor axon conduction velocity and nerve terminal excitability; however, the manner in which I$_{NaP}$ works together with the M-current (I${M}$) to set the speed of locomotion remains unknown. In this study, we reveal how I${M}$, an inwardly rectifying potassium current prevalent across species, synergizes with I$_{NaP}$, initiating a shift towards activated states when permeable at low voltages. Working within well-defined system parameters that involve muscle control boundaries on activity levels allows us to better understand how these two currents function in tandem to set locomotive speeds at biologically realistic rates.

title: Politics of International Health in the Bush Administration
abstract: Henry A. Waxman reviews the politicization of international health by the Bush Administration in three areas: tobacco control, nutrition, and reproductive health. He discusses how politics may threaten the President's primary international health commitment on HIV/AIDS. Taken as a whole, these and other actions have frequently left the United States isolated in its positions and have undermined public health progress across the globe.

title: Phase II study of sunitinib in Japanese patients with unresectable or metastatic, well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
abstract: Background. Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare but are frequently diagnosed at advanced stages and require systemic therapy. Patients and methods. This multicenter, open-label, phase II study evaluated sunitinib in Japanese patients with well-differentiated pancreatic NET. Patients received sunitinib 37.5 mg/day on a continuous daily dosing (CDD) schedule. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate (CBR; percentage of complete responses [CRs] plus partial responses [PRs] plus stable disease [SD] ≥24 weeks). Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), tumor shrinkage, progression-free survival (PFS) probability, safety, pharmacokinetics, and biomarkers. Results. Twelve patients received treatment. The CBR was 75 % (95 % confidence interval [CI], 43–94) and included 6 patients with a PR and 3 with SD. The ORR was 50 % (95 % CI, 21–79). PFS probability was 91 % (95 % CI, 54–99) at 6 months and 71 % (95 % CI, 34–90) at 12 months. Commonly reported treatment-emergent (all-causality), any-grade adverse events included diarrhea (n = 10), hand–foot syndrome and hypertension (both n = 8), fatigue and headache (both n = 7), and neutropenia (n = 6). title: Cutaneous Phaeohyphomycosis Caused by Exophiala attenuata in a Domestic Cat
abstract: A 7-year-old female-spayed, domestic short-haired cat was presented to her veterinarian with a mass on the hind paw. Histopathologic examination of a tissue biopsy revealed nodular pyogranulomatous panniculitis with intralesional pigmented fungal hyphae. A dematiaceous fungal isolate was isolated with a micromorphological phenotype consistent with the anamorphic genus Exophiala: budding cells, torulose mycelium and annellidic conidiogenesis from simple conidiophores consisting of terminal and lateral cells that tapered to a short beak at the apex. Sequence homology of the internal transcribed spacer region of the rDNA gene confirmed the identification of the isolate as Exophiala attenuata. Reported here is the first confirmed case of feline phaeohyphomycosis caused by E. attenuata in North America. Similar to historical cases of feline phaeohyphomycosis caused by Exophiala spp., there was no history or postmortem evidence to suggest the patient was in an immunocompromised state (e.g., suffering from FeLV or FIV). Although aggressive surgical excision of local lesions is recommended prior to drug treatment when dealing with subcutaneous phaeohyphomycosis, surgery followed by itraconazole treatment did not resolve the E. attenuata infection in this cat.

title: Ingestion of sugar beet fiber enhances irradiation-induced aberrant crypt foci in the rat colon under an apoptosis-suppressed condition
abstract: This study investigates the influence of sugar beet fiber on irradiation-induced aberrant crypt foci (ACF) in the rat colon under an apoptosis suppression condition. Macerate derived from sugar beets is rich in dietary fiber, containing large proportions of pectin and resistant starch. Recent evidence suggests that ingestion of these fibers can modulate intestinal microbial balance to reduce genotoxicity and enhance defense against harmful toxins and stimuli initiated by ionizing radiation or carcinogenic agents. In this study, we sought to investigate whether consumption of sugar beet fiber could protect rats with suppressed apoptosis from ACF induced by gamma irradiation in the colonic environment. Twenty male Wistar rats were randomly divided into two groups: a control group (C) and a treatment group (T). Rats were given tap water as part of their diet for 10 days prior to being administered 5Gy single dose abdominal X-ray radiation for Group T, while Group C only received sham irradiation without exposure. Results demonstrated that there was no marked difference between groups regarding mean average ACF number; however, five animals tested positive for histologically diagnosed morbidity related markers among those included in Group T compared with none in Group C. Our findings present novel insight into how sugar beet supplementation may play a role as an anti-inflammatory agent during colorectal pathogenesis associated with irradiation-induced damage insomuch as it appears able to suppress aberration formation despite an unvexed capacity for cell death induction via apotptosis inhibition.

title: Characterization of MDCK cells and evaluation of their ability to respond to infectious and non-infectious stressors
abstract: The Madin-Darby Canine Kidney (MDCK) cell line is widely used as epithelial cell model in studies ranging from viral infection to environmental pollutants, and vaccines production. However, little is known about basal expression of genes involved in innate immunity, and the ability to respond to infectious and non-infectious stressors. Therefore, the aims of our study were to evaluate the basal level of expression of pivotal genes in the innate immune response and cell cycle regulation, as well as to evaluate the ability of this cell line to respond to infectious or non-infectious stressors. As surmised in our working hypothesis, we demonstrated the constitutive expression of genes involved in the innate immune response and cell defense alike, including TLRs, Interleukins, Myd88, p65/NF-kB and p53. Moreover, we described the ability of this cell line to respond to LPS and cadmium (Cd2+) in terms of gene expression and cytokine release. These data confirm the possibility of using this cell line as a model in studies of host/pathogen interaction and response to non-infectious stressors.

title: Off-label use of orthopedical trauma implants in a low-income country
abstract: This article aims to discuss the potential effects of off-label use of orthopedic trauma implants in a low-income country. Despite standard indications and contraindications for these medical devices, cost constraints and lack of options drive physicians to seek alternative solutions outside approved guidelines. The governments of many such countries are placing even further pressure on already restricted resources made available for public health services by introducing austerity policies. In addition, less privileged social groups may be disproportionately affected by inferior materials or procedures induced upon them due to financial considerations. Our research team seeks to explore how this phenomenon isn't limited to psychiatric drugs but encompasses other areas like pediatric surgery as well with the aim exploring the potential risks posed by these tactics that healthcare providers find themselves compelled into using out fear for patient’s safety or resource allocation allocations within their surroundings especially in comparison with evidence based practices seen in high income countries where expenditure is generally increased per package when it comes down surgical treatments .

title: How Ah Receptor Ligand Specificity Became Important in Understanding Its Physiological Function
abstract: Increasingly, the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is being recognized as a sensor for endogenous and pseudo-endogenous metabolites, and in particular microbiota and host generated tryptophan metabolites. One proposed explanation for this is the role of the AHR in innate immune signaling within barrier tissues in response to the presence of microorganisms. A number of cytokine/chemokine genes exhibit a combinatorial increase in transcription upon toll-like receptors and AHR activation, supporting this concept. The AHR also plays a role in the enhanced differentiation of intestinal and dermal epithelium leading to improved barrier function. Importantly, from an evolutionary perspective many of these tryptophan metabolites exhibit greater activation potential for the human AHR when compared to the rodent AHR. These observations underscore the importance of the AHR in barrier tissues and may lead to pharmacologic therapeutic intervention.

title: How I See Me—A Meta-Analysis Investigating the Association Between Identities and Pro-environmental Behaviour
abstract: This paper presents a meta-analysis investigating the link between identities and pro-environmental behaviour. Specifically, this research aims to understand how individuals’ constructions of identity (e.g., gender, class and race) are associated with their engagement in sustainable practices as part of their daily life. Drawing on prior literature examining identity formation processes for influencing behaviours, this meta-analysis synthesizes past quantitative findings from studies to identify pooled outcomes estimated by measures like ecological footprint scores or participation rates in conservation initiatives. Additionally, it seeks to explore mediators between identities and sustainability actions (e.g., intentions or norms), while leveraging existing psycho-social theories related to personal values that lead us towards environmental action as citizens of a global society. Through qualitative analysis based on individual interviews, focus groups and discourse analysis we also compare different scenarios across socio-economic contexts in order to unearth what constitutes ‘me’ in relation to being ecofriendly today versus previous generations? Ultimately, our hope is that such evidence will advance discussions concerning motivations for making more conscious choices when purchasing products; thereby informing the design of tailored interventions targeting specific populations so as­­—to incentivize better lifestyle decisions for preserving Earth's resources into future generations.

title: A seven-gene-deleted African swine fever virus is safe and effective as a live attenuated vaccine in pigs
abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating infectious disease in swine that is severely threatening the global pig industry. An efficacious vaccine is urgently required. Here, we used the Chinese ASFV HLJ/18 as a backbone and generated a series of gene-deleted viruses. The virulence, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy evaluation in specific-pathogen-free pigs, commercial pigs, and pregnant sows indicated that one virus, namely HLJ/18-7GD, which has seven genes deleted, is fully attenuated in pigs, cannot convert to the virulent strain, and provides complete protection of pigs against lethal ASFV challenge. Our study shows that HLJ/-18-7GD is a safe and effective vaccine against ASFV, and as such is expected to play an important role in controlling the spread of ASFV. title: Prevalence of Drug-Related Problems and Complementary and Alternative Medicine Use in Malaysia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 37,249 Older Adults
abstract: This study investigates the prevalence of drug-related problems and Complementary, Alternative and Integrative Medicine (CAIM) use among older adults in Malaysia. The systematic review and meta-analysis included a total of 37,249 individuals aged 55 years or above from 15 published studies throughout Malaysia. Through a comprehensive literature search including 4 databases, the results showed that 10.7% had reported using CAIM prior to their visit to healthcare providers while 8.9% reported having current prescription medicine related issues. Furthermore, elderly people with chronic health conditions were found more likely than other groups to take medication for drug-related problems as well as CAIM simultaneously by almost four times higher rate than those without chronic diseases. This research offers an insight into understanding medication safety among older population groups regarding drug-related problems and aid in policy making on CAM use specifically tailored to serve this demographic group across Malaysia’s different states by exploring regional variations through further research which is much needed at present scenario.

title: Plasmonic silver nanoshells for drug and metabolite detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach in the biomolecular analysis of detection and quantification of drugs and metabolites utilising plasmonic silver nanoshells. A description is provided on how these nano-objects interact with streptavidin-biotin mediated DNA amplification techniques for fluorescense based detection. To demonstrate their effectivity, the nanoparticles were covalently coupled to gold probes molecularly imprinted polymers (Au/MIPs) and anchored onto an undercoated glass surface followed by hybridization assays. Our study provides evidence that this sensing system enables the direct identification and selective recognition of target molecules down to ultra-low concentrations within milliseconds without disrupting biosensing matrices or interior structures of cells due to its biocompatible nature, thus enabling improved diagnostic testing.

title: Conceptualizing LGBT Stigma and Associated HIV Vulnerabilities Among LGBT Persons in Lesotho
abstract: This paper examines the concept of LGBT stigma and associated HIV vulnerabilities among LGBT persons in the Sub-Saharan African nation of Lesotho. Using qualitative methods, we explore how social exclusion, legal discrimination, and other forms of institutional marginalization are experienced by members of the small LGBTQ population whose placement within a gendered system is far from normalized or accepted. Utilizing lived experiences as a basis for examining intersections between sexual orientation/gender identity and increased health risks such as HIV transmission, this study seeks to understand how social stigma helps to shape public health outcomes. In addition to positions derived from individual narratives, we discuss best practices for mitigating negative patterns that can lead to further exclusionary processes in surveys quantification with an aim towards promoting inclusion at all levels of society both locally and internationally.

title: Assessing the Methods, Tools, and Statistical Approaches in Google Trends Research: Systematic Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: In the era of information overload, are big data analytics the answer to access and better manage available knowledge? Over the last decade, the use of Web-based data in public health issues, that is, infodemiology, has been proven useful in assessing various aspects of human behavior. Google Trends is the most popular tool to gather such information, and it has been used in several topics up to this point, with health and medicine being the most focused subject. Web-based behavior is monitored and analyzed in order to examine actual human behavior so as to predict, better assess, and even prevent health-related issues that constantly arise in everyday life. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed at reporting and further presenting and analyzing the methods, tools, and statistical approaches for Google Trends (infodemiology) studies in health-related topics from 2006 to 2016 to provide an overview of the usefulness of said tool and be a point of reference for future research on the subject. METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines for selecting studies, we searched for the term “Google Trends” in the Scopus and PubMed databases from 2006 to 2016, applying specific criteria for types of publications and topics. A total of 109 published papers were extracted, excluding duplicates and those that did not fall inside the topics of health and medicine or the selected article types. We then further categorized the published papers according to their methodological approach, namely, visualization, seasonality, correlations, forecasting, and modeling. RESULTS: All the examined papers comprised, by definition, time series analysis, and all but two included data visualization. A total of 23.1% (24/104) studies used Google Trends data for examining seasonality, while 39.4% (41/104) and 32.7% (34/104) of the studies used correlations and modeling, respectively. Only 8.7% (9/104) of the studies used Google Trends data for predictions and forecasting in health-related topics; therefore, it is evident that a gap exists in forecasting using Google Trends data. CONCLUSIONS: The monitoring of online queries can provide insight into human behavior, as this field is significantly and continuously growing and will be proven more than valuable in the future for assessing behavioral changes and providing ground for research using data that could not have been accessed otherwise.

title: Mechanisms and pathways to impact in public health research: a preliminary analysis of research funded by the National Institute for Health Research (NIHR)
abstract: BACKGROUND: The mechanisms and pathways to impacts from public health research in the UK have not been widely studied. Through the lens of one funder (NIHR), our aims are to map the diversity of public health research, in terms of funding mechanisms, disciplinary contributions, and public health impacts, identify examples of impacts, and pathways to impact that existing reporting mechanisms may not otherwise have captured, and provide illustrations of how public health researchers perceive the generation of non-academic impact from their work. METHODS: A total of 1386 projects were identified as ‘public health research’ by the NIHR and listed in the NIHR Public Health Overview database (2000–2016). From these, a subset of 857 projects were matched as potentially having begun reporting impacts via an external data-gathering platform (Researchfish). Data on the 857 projects were analyzed quantitatively, and nine projects were selected to investigate further through semi-structured interviews with principal investigators. Two workshops took place to validate emerging and final findings and facilitate analysis. RESULTS: In addition to the NIHR School for Public Health Research and the NIHR Public Health Research Programme, 89% of projects contained in the NIHR Public Health Overview portfolio as ‘public health research’ are funded via other NIHR research programmes, suggesting significant diversity in disciplines contributing to public health research and outcomes. The pathways to impact observed in our in-depth case studies include contributing to debates on what constitutes appropriate evidence for national policy change, acknowledging local ‘unintended’ impacts, building trusted relationships with stakeholders across health and non-health sectors and actors, collaborating with local authorities, and using non-academic dissemination channels. CONCLUSIONS: Public health as a discipline contributes substantially to impact beyond academia. To support the diversity of these impacts, we need to recognise localized smaller-scale impacts, and the difference in types of evidence required for community and local authority-based impacts. This will also require building capacity and resources to enable impact to take place from public health research. Finally, support is required for engagement with local authorities and working with non-health sectors that contribute to health outcomes.

title: Food Safety: At the Center of a One Health Approach for Combating Zoonoses
abstract:
Food safety and zoonoses are global public health threats, with both disease burden and economic losses observed in our society. In this paper, we examine the potential for a One Health approach to improve food safety and minimize infectious diseases shared between humans and animals. We explore how establishing policies that integrate human-animal-environmental interactions can provide a comprehensive public health strategy necessary to reduce the threat of emerging zoonotic agents. Finally, identifying some possible areas where interventions may be meaningful such as legislation or community education programmes specifically aimed at improving knowledge related to foodborne illnesses. By elucidating potential barriers for implementing efficient collaborative interventions across disciplines, it is proposed that governments recognise the need for targeted approaches like those integrated into One Health models if effective improvements in public health outcomes through enhanced food systems are expected.
